## D-161 · 2026-10-06 · A longjmp or a fiber switch in translated code goes on in the interpreter

Assassin's Creed crashed after its disclaimer, in a task thread, with registers r27-r31 and LR zero (run 099). Its
job system runs jobs as fibers, switching with its libc's setjmp/longjmp (0x10AA544: r1, r2, r13-r31, LR, CR, the
FPRs and the VRs loaded from a buffer). Translated code turns a guest function into a host C function and `blr` into
a C return, so the translated longjmp returned to its C caller instead of to the other fiber's setjmp, and the caller
went on with the other fiber's r1, restoring its registers from someone else's stack. The interpreter follows LR and
r1 and was always right.
- The lifter: a function's plain return (bclr to LR, no link) checks that r1 is what it was at the function's entry,
  as every return the ABI allows leaves it. When it is not, the code makes a pseudo-syscall marked by cia 0xFFFFFFF0
  (no guest register is touched, so the differential tests stay exact) and the kernel throws lv2::NonLocalJump.
- lv2::run_guest, the only caller of the executor (a thread's entry, call_guest's callbacks), catches it and goes on
  in the interpreter from the context the jump restored (cia = LR), translated callees still called as such, until
  the code returns where the call would have: for a thread, to kThreadReturnAddress at any r1 (RunOptions::
  stop_any_sp). Another jump in translated code lands there again: the host stack never grows with fiber switches.
- The cost: one compare per translated return; after a jump the frames above the jump target run interpreted until
  they return (Assassin's Creed: its job loop).
- The interpreter now remembers its last taken branch to address 0, and a translated function that came back with LR
  0 (the fault report names it): what found 0xCF6CD4, the game's "switch to fiber".
Libraries prepared by older lifters lack the check: a translator generation (prepare::kTranslatorGeneration, 2 now)
goes into each manifest, and library_is_current prepares a library of an older generation again, where an ordinary
translator change only leaves a note. Result (run 099): Assassin's Creed plays its intro and reaches its title
screen (NEW / CONTINUE) on the Mac. Test: jmp_set / jmp_long / jmp_deep / jmp_test, lifted and interpreted, the same
context; a manifest without the generation is not current.

## D-162 · 2026-10-06 · Disc images: the Joliet tree when there is one

Assassin's Creed, after NEW on its title screen, opens /dev_bdvd/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/dataps3_flashback_paradise.forge,
was told it does not exist, and showed "There's a problem with the disc you're using" for ever (a dialog without
buttons, so a black screen here). The image's primary ISO 9660 tree cuts names to 31 characters
(DATAPS3_FLASHBACK_PARADISE.FORG;1); its Joliet supplementary tree (volume descriptor 17, escape sequence %/E) holds
the whole names in UCS-2, as the disc's UDF tree does on a PS3. runtime/disc reads the Joliet tree whenever the image
has one (type 2 with %/@, %/C or %/E), its names as UTF-8, lookups still ignoring case; the volume name stays the
primary descriptor's. RPCS3's Loader/ISO.cpp reads the last of the two as well. Test: a synthetic image with a cut
primary name and the whole Joliet name.

## D-163 · 2026-10-06 · 24-bit depth textures from memory are decoded, and HILO and Y16_X16_FLOAT

Assassin's Creed's first level samples DEPTH24_D8 textures from memory that no depth buffer the backend drew covers
(a buffer the CPU or a copy filled): "texture format DEPTH24_D8 is not decoded yet", 264,615 times in 330 s (run
099), each such draw left without its texture. Both 24-bit depth formats now decode, on the CPU and in the compute
decoder, to R32Float read in every channel as DEPTH16 already was (RPCS3 VKFormats.cpp get_component_mapping):
DEPTH24_D8 as the top 24 bits unsigned normalized (the stencil byte dropped), DEPTH24_D8_FLOAT as the 24-bit float
there, `bits << 7` into a float (RPCS3 ShuffleBytes.glsl d24f_to_f32). Depth buffers the backend drew are still
sampled directly (D-106). Three more formats no game could use before decode the same way, with RPCS3's channel
mappings ((A, R, G, B) = {R, G, R, G}): COMPRESSED_HILO8 (RG8, LO in red as RPCS3's R8G8 upload of the big-endian
word), COMPRESSED_HILO_S8 (signed, kept in RGBA16F) and Y16_X16_FLOAT (RG16F). Still not decoded: DEPTH16_FLOAT and
the 4:2:2 formats (COMPRESSED_B8R8_G8R8, R8B8_R8G8), which RPCS3 itself marks untested. Tests: the CPU decoder's values
for each, and the compute decoder against it.

## D-164 · 2026-10-06 · The time left starts from the game's own speeds, else the device's PPU speed

Assassin's Creed's SPU code compiled 6 times faster than the cost model predicts (rate 0.16-0.19), GTA V's at about
the model (1.13 of it), and the model cannot tell them apart from the text (a 1.3 MB GTA V program takes 170 s, a
3.2 MB Assassin's Creed one 18 s; run 099). The app started each preparation from the last game's per-kind rates,
so one game's SPU code skewed the next game's first estimate (GTA V after Assassin's Creed would have started 5
times low). prepare::prior_rates: this game's own last preparation when there is one (re-preparing after a lifter
fix, D-161: the same code on the same device); else the device's speed measured on the last game's PPU code (0.84-1.0
across both games) for PPU and SPU alike, and its table rate; each from the heat it was measured at to the heat now.
pspocket-prepare on the Mac uses the game's own manifest the same way. Test: the three cases and the heat.

## D-165 · 2026-10-06 · L.A. Noire's first stops: encrypted SDATA files, a workload attribute, GCM handlers

L.A. Noire (BLES00933), prepared on the phone (61,666 PPU functions, no SPU programs in its executable), stopped before
its first frame (phone log 2026-10-06 05:53): cellFsSdataOpen of its fragment programs (programs.fp.ps3.sdat) was
missing, so were its SPURS workload (cellSpursAddWorkloadWithAttribute) and eleven smaller calls; its SPURS then waited
for work for good. All fourteen now follow RPCS3, each with a test (tests/hle/test_la_noire.cpp, test_spurs_run.cpp):

- **Encrypted SDATA files.** recomp::NpdFile (recomp/common/npd.cpp) ports RPCS3's EDATADecrypter and its LZ decoder
  (Crypto/unedat.cpp, lz.cpp): blocks of the NPD file, each key the file key's AES of the dev hash and block number,
  AES-128-CBC with the header's digest as IV, the AES-CMAC or HMAC-SHA1 of the encrypted bytes checked, compressed
  blocks decoded; the last block read is cached. The SDAT key is the header's dev hash XOR SDAT_KEY; the keys
  (SDAT_KEY, EDAT_KEY_0/1, EDAT_HASH_0/1, EDAT_IV) come from RPCS3's key_vault.h at build time (scripts/self-keys.py,
  build directory only). lv2 sys_fs_open with the SDATA or EDATA type argument on an "NPD\0" file opens it through
  the opener the HLE process installs (Kernel::set_npd_opener): a read-only file of its plain bytes, fstat the plain
  size, as RPCS3's lv2 wraps it; cellFsSdataOpen is RPCS3's (read-only, the type argument {0x180, 0x10}). Differences:
  EDATA (PSN content) needs the game's klicensee, which nothing keeps yet: refused with a log, as before. RPCS3's LZ
  decoder returns 0 for a block stored plain (a first byte above 0x80), which would read nothing: the copied length is
  returned. Damaged input cannot read or write past the buffers (the range decoder's input is bounds-checked, offsets
  and lengths are checked before a copy), where RPCS3's could. Tests: RFC 4493's AES-CMAC examples, synthetic SDATA
  files in thirteen layouts (flags 0x02, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, compressed, debug data; NPD versions 1 to 4) read whole and
  in pieces across blocks, a damaged block, wrong keys, EDATA, LZ noise; the lv2 open on an image and a host directory;
  cellFsSdataOpen with the build's keys.
- **SPURS.** _cellSpursWorkloadAttributeInitialize, cellSpursWorkloadAttributeSetName and
  cellSpursAddWorkloadWithAttribute (a custom policy module, run by the native scheduler as cellSpursAddWorkload's,
  D-051, with the attribute's names and shutdown hook in wklH1/wklF1 and event bit 2);
  cellSpursAttributeEnableSpuPrintfIfAvailable (the flag); cellSpursAttributeEnableSystemWorkload (RPCS3's checks and
  fields). An instance initialized with the system workload is now accepted: it lends SPUs to the system, and there is
  no system here, as RPCS3's add_default_syswkl is a TODO. cellSpursSetGlobalExceptionEventHandler keeps the handler
  (BUSY the second time); SPU exceptions still stop a native worker with a log rather than reach it.
- **GCM.** cellGcmInitSystemMode: mode 1 makes the IO address space 512 MB (lv2's and cellGcmSys's main_mem_size, as
  RPCS3's _cellGcmInitBody). cellGcmSetFlipHandler and cellGcmSetUserHandler: the interrupt thread now waits for the
  vblank on an lv2 event queue of its own, where the RSX thread's flip listener and its new user-command listener
  (Kernel::set_rsx_user_command_listener, GCM_SET_USER_COMMAND) post an event; it calls the flip handler with head 1
  and the user handler with the command's argument, on itself, as RPCS3's interrupt thread does.
- **Smaller ones.** sys_ppu_thread_once (under a "_lv2ppu" lv2 mutex, init called on the calling thread, the control
  word set to 1), cellRtcGetCurrentClock, sceNpInit (np_init, offline as after sceNp2Init), lv2 syscall 254
  sys_spu_thread_group_log (the on/off switch).

The phone run after this shows L.A. Noire's next stops (its SPU code comes from its data files and runs interpreted in
the first session).

## D-166 · 2026-10-06 · The engine resolves what a game calls by itself, as a PS3: the plan, and lv2's null syscalls

The user's direction (2026-10-06): system functions, graphics features and the rest should be found and handled by
the engine itself, as a PS3 runs any game, not added game by game; the PS3 system software is installed in Settings;
speed comes later from runs. Research on the engine and RPCS3 (five audits, 2026-10-06) set the work, in this order:

1. **Kernel.** lv2 answers every syscall RPCS3 answers (149 of RPCS3's 451 implemented ones are here): first the
   null_func slots (below), then SPU thread groups, threads and images with the SPU side of them (stop codes 0x100,
   0x101, 0x102, 0x110, 0x111; interrupt-mailbox events, event flag bits), the rest of sys_fs, the PRX syscalls,
   interrupts and raw SPU (problem-state access through a fault handler).
2. **System libraries, linked as a PS3 links them.** Per game and per firmware module, at boot: the native module
   when it implements every function the game imports from it; else the firmware's own module when it and everything
   it needs resolves (its imports, its variables, its syscalls); else the native one with what it lacks listed.
   Always native: liblv2, libsysmodule, libsre (D-037), libgcm_sys, libaudio, libvoice, libio, libfs, libnet,
   libnetctl, libsysutil and libsysutil_*, the device modules. sysPrxForUser (33 of liblv2's 157 functions) comes
   first: every firmware module imports from it. Then cellSpurs up to libsre's API (52 of 149) and the other native
   modules as RPCS3 has them.
3. **Graphics.** The RSX audit's list: the fragment program opcodes that make a draw be skipped (LIT, LIF, DST, REFL,
   DP2A, PKG, UPG, BEM, TEXBEM, TXPBEM), the texture control bits (unsigned remap, signed channels, gamma, alpha
   kill) and sRGB output, primitive restart, scaled NV3089 blits, state changes inside BEGIN/END, point sprites,
   fog, clip planes, two-sided colour, the present (insets, FP16 buffers, gamma), MSAA's sample layout.
4. **Speed**, later, from runs.

First step here: lv2's syscall table answers each of the 299 slots RPCS3's table answers with null_func (named or
not) as RPCS3 does, a log of the first call and CELL_OK, unless pspocket implements it
(runtime/lv2/src/syscall_null.inc, generated by runtime/lv2/scripts/gen_null_syscalls.py from RPCS3's lv2.cpp); unused
slots still return CELL_ENOSYS and count as unimplemented. sys_fs_fcntl's unknown operations return CELL_OK with an
error log, as RPCS3's do (31 of its operations are no-ops). Test: a named, a debug and an unnamed null slot return
CELL_OK, an unused one ENOSYS.

## D-167 · 2026-10-06 · SPU thread groups: games run SPU programs on lv2 directly, as on a PS3

Until now SPU code ran only inside the native SPURS (D-037); lv2 had none of the SPU thread group syscalls, so a game
(or a firmware library) that creates its own SPU threads stopped at the first one (the kernel audit of 2026-10-06:
the largest gap). lv2 now has them as RPCS3 has them (rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_spu.cpp; the SPU side from SPUThread.cpp
stop_and_signal and set_ch_value), in runtime/lv2/src/spu.cpp:

- **Images.** sys_spu_image_open (a file through the VFS; an SPU SELF decrypts with the build's keys through a hook
  the HLE layer installs), sys_spu_image_open_by_fd, _sys_spu_image_import, _sys_spu_image_close, the information and
  segment calls: RPCS3's kernel image (the segment table and a copy of the ELF in user memory, 64 KB pages, an image
  object 0x22000000, the guest's sys_spu_image {KERNEL, ID, 0, 0}). sysPrxForUser's side (runtime/hle/src/sys_spu_.cpp):
  sys_spu_image_import (PROTECT through the syscall, DIRECT as a user image whose segments point into the ELF),
  sys_spu_elf_get_information and get_segments (an SCE header followed to its ELF), and the SPU printf server's
  callbacks (_sys_spu_printf_*).
- **Groups and threads.** create (RPCS3's types, the SPU limits shared with sys_spu_initialize, the memory charged to
  the default or given container), destroy, initialize (user segments checked as RPCS3 does; thread IDs (index << 24)
  | group ID), set_argument, get_exit_status, start (each image copied into its local store, the context reset as
  RPCS3's cpu_init: ps_spu_thread_reset keeps the inbound mailbox and signal registers; arguments in $3..$6's preferred
  doublewords, $1 = 0x3FFF0; the run event), suspend, resume, yield, terminate (refused while a thread waits on an SPU
  queue), join (cause: group exit, all threads exited, terminated), priorities, read_ls/write_ls, write_spu_mb,
  write_snr, spu_cfg (signal OR modes), thread and group events, bind/unbind of SPU queues, connect_event_all_threads,
  cooperative victims and syscall 253 (checked, as RPCS3's TODO).
- **The SPU side,** through the context's hooks: stop 0x110/0x111 (receive/tryreceive an event from a bound SPU queue
  into the inbound mailbox), 0x101 (group exit: the first one decides cause and status; the others are stopped), 0x102
  (thread exit with its status), 0x100 (yield), 0x001/0x002; interrupt-mailbox codes 0..63 send_event (answered),
  64..127 throw_event, 128/192 event flag bits. Each SPU thread has a parked host thread of its own (8 MB stack); the
  lifted program for each image is attached at start (ImageKind::Thread, found by hash as SPURS's images are;
  otherwise the interpreter runs it). Process exit stops every SPU thread and aborts its waits.

Differences from RPCS3: while a thread waits on an SPU queue its group is WAITING, but the group's other threads go on
(RPCS3 suspends them); a suspend stops threads at their next attention check; local stores are host memory (the PPU
uses read_ls/write_ls, the group's threads the 0xF0000000 DMA window, spu_num below 8); halts, SPU exceptions and
unknown stop codes end the thread with an error log (an abort when the SPU miss policy aborts), without the exception
event; raw and isolated SPUs, SPU page faults and asynchronous interrupts are not implemented. Two bugs this found in
the SPU runtime: a signal-notification write did not wake an SPU already blocked reading it (fixed:
ps_spu_write_signal notifies); RPCS3's check for a terminate before a thread starts to wait on its queue was needed
here too. Tests (tests/hle/test_spu_threads.cpp, synthetic SPU ELFs on the interpreter): arguments, exit status and a
restart; images; RPCS3's refusals; group exit stopping a spinning sibling; suspend, resume, terminate; the inbound
mailbox, send_event to a PPU queue and receive_event from an SPU queue (and terminate refused while it waits); event
flag bits, signal OR mode, local store access, the run event; SPU-to-SPU DMA and a signal through the group window;
the process ending while a thread waits.

## D-168 · 2026-10-06 · sysPrxForUser: the C library, heaps, lwcond, mempool and the rest, as RPCS3 has them

D-166's second step starts with sysPrxForUser, which every firmware module imports from: the 50 functions RPCS3
implements there that pspocket lacked, each from the RPCS3 source its comment names, each tested for its behaviour and
error codes (tests/hle/test_sysprx_libc.cpp, 20 cases). sysPrxForUser now has 83 of liblv2's 157 functions; the SPU
printf, SPU image and ELF, raw SPU, interrupt thread and PRX ones are another change's. Where pspocket differs from
RPCS3, and why:

- **Pointers** are checked before use (D-042), where RPCS3 would fault: functions that write refuse a range that is not
  all guest memory and write nothing; scans (strlen, strcmp, strchr, memchr, memcmp) check each page as they reach it,
  so they fail only where RPCS3's would. A refusal is logged with the call site and returns what the function returns
  for nothing found (0, NULL, the destination), or CELL_EFAULT where the function returns an error code.
- **C library** (runtime/hle/src/sysPrxForUser_libc.cpp, from sys_libc_.cpp): memset, memcpy, memmove, memcmp,
  memchr, the str functions, ctype with RPCS3's table, as RPCS3. A guest char is unsigned (the PPU's): strncasecmp
  folds 'A'..'Z' and compares bytes from 0x80 as they are, where RPCS3's _sys_tolower aborts on its host's negative
  chars; a ctype argument outside -1..127 has no class or case (a warning the first time) where RPCS3 aborts.
  _sys_memcpy copies overlapping ranges as memmove.
- **printf, sprintf, snprintf**: RPCS3's ps3_fmt (Utilities/cfmt.h over the ABI's argument slots): its parsing (flags,
  width, precision and length in any order; an unknown sequence printed as written, the rest of the format untouched),
  its conversions (d i u o x X c s p, its b B, and f F e E g G a A by the host's snprintf on the double in the
  argument's GPR or stack slot, where a variadic call puts it) and its sizes (long and size_t 4 bytes). C99, which
  liblv2 follows, where RPCS3 departs from it: %d takes an int, not the whole 64-bit slot; precision 0 prints no digits
  only for 0 ("%.0d" of 5 is "5"); "%#x" and "%#o" of 0 print "0" (RPCS3 "00"); %lf is %f (RPCS3 stops formatting at
  it). Arguments after the eighth are read at r1 + 0x30 + 8n, where the caller puts them; RPCS3 reads each one slot
  low (a 0-based index into its 1-based get_stack_arg). A null %s prints "(null)"; one that is not guest memory prints
  nothing, logged. Widths and precisions stop at 65,536. _sys_printf goes to sys_tty_write on channel 0 in pieces of up
  to 1 KB on the caller's stack (RPCS3 puts the whole text there). _sys_snprintf returns the bytes written and 0 for a
  count of 0, as RPCS3, not C99's whole length.
- **qsort**: a merge sort of the elements' indices; the guest comparator (call_guest) gets the elements' addresses
  where they lie, then the array is written in its order: stable, about n log2 n comparisons, and a comparator that is
  not consistent cannot make it leave the array. RPCS3 runs the host's std::qsort, whose comparison order depends on
  the host.
- **malloc and heaps** (sys_heap.cpp): vm::alloc in the main area as RPCS3 (MainMemory: first fit, at least 64 KB
  aligned, zeroed); an alignment that is not a power of two returns NULL with a log (RPCS3 aborts); free(NULL) does
  nothing. Heaps are names under idm's IDs (1..1023, each new one first, then the lowest free); _sys_heap_malloc
  ignores the heap, as RPCS3's.
- **lwcond** (sys_lwcond_.cpp, without hle_lwmutex): over lv2's _sys_lwcond_* (lw.cpp), the signal modes by who owns
  the lwmutex (1 owner, 2 another thread, 3 taken free and handed to the waiter; a RETRY lwmutex always 2), the
  waiter count and owner words kept as RPCS3 keeps them, and sys_lwcond_wait's recursion count and its CELL_OK, ESRCH,
  EBUSY, ETIMEDOUT and EDEADLK paths. An lwcond or lwmutex that is not guest memory, or an lwmutex not 8-byte aligned
  as its atomics need, is CELL_EFAULT; where RPCS3 throws (an owner free or dead after a handover, an unexpected kernel
  result) pspocket aborts (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
- **mempool** (sys_mempool.cpp): blocks handed out from the chunk's end, given-back ones first, each pool with an lv2
  mutex and condition variable ("mp_m<ID>", "mp_c<ID>") that sys_mempool_allocate_block waits on. RPCS3's vector of
  free blocks is kept as a count of chunk blocks not taken yet under the returned ones, so a chunk of many small blocks
  costs no host memory. Differences: block size 0 is CELL_EINVAL (RPCS3 divides by it); destroy removes the condition
  variable before the mutex (in RPCS3's order lv2 refuses the mutex, a condition variable still bound to it, and it
  stays); try_allocate looks again under the mutex (RPCS3 can pop an empty vector); out of IDs is CELL_EAGAIN and a
  mutex or condition variable that cannot be made returns lv2's error (RPCS3 crashes or throws).
- **atexit** (sys_ppu_thread_.cpp): eight slots for the process (EPERM for one registered already, a null one matching
  a free slot; ENOMEM when full; ESRCH to unregister one not there), run in slot order by every sys_ppu_thread_exit
  before its TLS goes. The guard is a recursive lv2 mutex "atexit!" made at the first registration, where RPCS3's
  sys_initialize_tls makes an lwmutex; a function that is not guest memory is skipped with a log.
- **Smaller ones**: console_putc and console_write (sys_tty_write on channel 0; console_write returns CELL_OK whatever
  it returned), sys_process_get_paramsfo (the syscall), sys_mmapper_allocate_memory_from_container (the shared memory
  syscall from a container, without an IPC key), sys_get_random_number (CELL_EINVAL past 4096 bytes; RPCS3 then calls
  lv2's sys_ss_random_number_generator, which lv2 here does not have yet, so the library fills the buffer from the
  host's std::random_device itself), sys_game_process_exitspawn2 (sys_game_process_exitspawn's parameter block, now
  shared, with RPCS3's flags: top bits 0 or 1 kept, else cleared; the atexitspawn handler runs for 0 and the
  at_Exitspawn one for 1 before the process ends, D-031).

The synthetic executable's loader test (test_hle.cpp) now counts _sys_printf among its implemented imports.

## D-169 · 2026-10-06 · cellSync and cellRtc complete, as RPCS3 has them

Every function RPCS3 implements in the two libraries is now native: 33 more in cellSync (the mutex's Lock; the
barrier, the reader-writer buffer and the queue, five, five and nine functions; the lock-free queue's thirteen) and 32
in cellRtc. Each follows RPCS3's rpcs3/Emu/Cell/Modules/cellSync.cpp or cellRtc.cpp, cited per function; cellSync was
compared with libsre (fw 4.92, the reference, D-046) function by function as well. Where pspocket differs, and why:

- **Atomicity.** Every cellSync structure lies in one 128-byte line, and every update of it is one reservation_op
  (D-160), never a host atomic. The lock-free queue is the whole line, so each pass of RPCS3's loops is one update: what
  the pass reads is one snapshot, and it stores only if nothing in the line changed since, as libsre's lwarx/stwcx. on
  the line give. The second compare-and-swap of a completion (push3/pop3), which RPCS3 ensures and libsre asserts
  nobody changed in between, therefore cannot fail. cellSyncLFQueueInitialize's claim of `init`, the set-up and its
  end are one update too: nobody sees the queue half set up.
- **Waiting.** Where RPCS3 spins (Lock, Notify, Wait, Read, Write, Push, Pop, Peek, Clear, the blocking pointer calls,
  a completion waiting for an SPU waiter to leave), the thread sleeps until the line changes (ps_res_wait_change: an
  HLE update, a stwcx., a PUTLLC or PUTLLUC, a DMA PUT), and looks again every 1 ms for plain guest stores, which don't
  move the line's version. The end of the process unwinds it (ThreadExit), where RPCS3 returns 0. A thread waiting
  300 ms in Lock used under 50 ms of CPU. A contended Lock hands over through a wake-up: 24,000 handovers among six
  threads took 0.08 to 9.4 s over 15 runs on a Mac loaded by other builds (load average above 100); a spin before the
  sleep waits for a game that needs it (rule 8).
- **libsre where RPCS3 differs.** cellSyncLFQueueInitialize ends with init = 2: RPCS3 stores 0, after which a second
  Initialize of the queue is STAT, where libsre's accepts the same arguments again (the SPU side initializes the same
  queue). The push completion stops only when var2 + var4 is above 16, libsre's assertion (RPCS3 ensures below 16).
- **Fatal where RPCS3 throws or ensures and libsre asserts (D-047):** a queue whose next or count is beyond its depth;
  the lock-free queue's receive from its lv2 event queue failing; `16 - var2 <= 1` in a completion; a completion with
  an SPU waiter to wake and no signal function, which is what PushBody and PopBody pass, in RPCS3 and in libsre.
- **Not here:** RPCS3's todo stubs that return CELL_OK: the ANY2ANY functions (_cellSyncLFQueue*Pointer2) and
  _cellSyncLFQueueAttach/DetachLv2EventQueue stay unimplemented (rule 4); PushBody and PopBody refuse an ANY2ANY queue
  with CELL_SYNC_ERROR_NOSYS, where RPCS3 copies an entry at a pointer nothing handed out.
- **Checks (D-042).** Objects, entries, buffers and signal functions that are not guest memory are FAULT with the call
  site logged, the structure left as it was. The four pointer functions, which check nothing in RPCS3 and libsre, also
  refuse a queue that is not 128-aligned (ALIGN): Initialize sets none up there.
- **cellRtc sets no clock.** cellRtcSetCurrentTick and cellRtcSetConf go through lv2's sys_time_set_current_time and
  sys_time_set_timezone (CELL_ENOSYS without root, nothing changed), as RPCS3; cellRtcSetCurrentSecureTick returns
  CELL_OK and keeps nothing, as RPCS3's sys_ss_secure_rtc stub. cellRtcGetCurrentSecureTick is the host's UTC time in
  whole seconds: RPCS3's stub answers with the timebase counter, which its arithmetic turns into a date 150 years
  further per minute of running. CheckValid and CompareTick refuse a bad pointer with INVALID_POINTER and a log, where
  RPCS3 ensure()s it. Sums wrap at 32 or 64 bits, as the PS3's, where RPCS3's signed ones would overflow.
- **A fix in the date parser.** A year RPCS3's cellRtcGetTick refuses (0, or 0xFFFF for a cellRtcParseRfc3339 string
  that doesn't start with digits) writes no tick, and the offset is added to what the tick held, as RPCS3 does
  (cellRtcGetTick, then cellRtcTickAddMinutes); cellRtcParseDateTime computed a tick from year 0 before.

Tests: tests/hle/test_sync.cpp (25 cases): every NID; each function's checks in RPCS3's order and its effect byte for
byte; blocking calls woken by other threads and by SPU-style GETLLAR/PUTLLC, and unwound at exit; the mutex hammered
with Lock and with TryLock against a PPU's lwarx/stwcx. and an SPU's tickets; barrier rounds; readers of the rwm never
seeing half a buffer; queue producers and consumers; the lock-free queue's layout, out-of-order completions, a waiter
signalled through a guest function, the lv2 event queue wait, and a PPU pushing (popping) 3,001 entries against an SPU
popping (pushing). tests/hle/test_rtc.cpp (10 cases): every function's values (from Python's datetime) and errors.

## D-170 · 2026-10-06 · cellGcmSys complete, as RPCS3 has it

libgcm_sys is always native (D-166), so it now has every function RPCS3's cellGcmSys.cpp implements: the 36 it
lacked, each from RPCS3 (and RPCS3's sys_rsx.cpp where the firmware goes through lv2), with RPCS3's error codes and a
comment citing RPCS3's function. Where pspocket differs, and why:

- **IO mapping.** cellGcmMapEaIoAddress, cellGcmMapMainMemory (RPCS3's first fit over the offset table's eaAddress
  half, below the reserved MBs; CELL_GCM_ERROR_NO_IO_PAGE_TABLE without room), cellGcmUnmapIoAddress and
  cellGcmUnmapEaIoAddress (a mapping is unmapped from where it starts: RPCS3's IoMapTable, the size of each mapping by
  its first EA MB, is kept beside the table), cellGcmReserveIoMapSize, cellGcmUnreserveIoMapSize,
  cellGcmGetMaxIoMapSize (256 or 512 MB less the reserve; 0 before cellGcmInit, as RPCS3's renderer),
  cellGcmGetOffsetTable, cellGcmGetNotifyDataAddress, cellGcmMapLocalMemory (once, before cellGcmInit, which then keeps
  that local memory). Every map and unmap changes lv2's IO map and both halves of the offset table together.
  Differences: an EA range at or past 3 GB, an IO offset past 512 MB and an unmapped one are CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE,
  where RPCS3 reads or writes past its tables; before cellGcmInit a map gets CELL_EINVAL, as lv2 answers RPCS3 then.
- **Flips.** cellGcmGetFlipStatus, cellGcmResetFlipStatus, cellGcmSetFlipStatus, cellGcmGetCurrentDisplayBufferId and
  cellGcmGetLastFlipTime read and change head 1 of lv2's driver information, where the firmware keeps them; RPCS3's
  HLE keeps them in its renderer. lv2 sets the flip-done bit of flipFlags, the time and the buffer at each flip (the
  bit atomically now), and its package 0x10a, as RPCS3's (flipFlags = (flipFlags & a4) | a5; LV1_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER_VALUE
  past head 7, CELL_EINVAL for heads 2 to 7 where RPCS3 aborts), resets and sets it. The status is DONE from
  cellGcmInit on (RPCS3 rsx::thread::init). cellGcmGetLastFlipTime is the flip's time in microseconds on the guest's
  system-time clock; RPCS3 returns its host clock less one second, which no guest clock matches. cellGcmGetVBlankCount
  counts the interrupt thread's vblanks.
- **Queue handler.** cellGcmSetQueueHandler: RPCS3 calls the handler with head 1 from its HLE flip command, before the
  flip handler. The RSX's GCM_FLIP_COMMAND now queues the buffer on head 1 before it flips, on the path a
  GCM_DRIVER_QUEUE method takes: lv2 notes the queue in the driver information as RPCS3's 0x103 does
  (lastQueuedBufferId, the queued bits), then a new listener (Kernel::set_rsx_queue_listener) posts it to the GCM
  interrupt thread, which calls the handler with the head. A GCM_DRIVER_QUEUE a game writes itself calls the handler
  too, as lv1's queue event does through the firmware's interrupt thread; RPCS3's HLE does not.
- **Command words.** cellGcmSetPrepareFlip (returns the id; cellGcmSetFlip now shares RPCS3's gcmSetPrepareFlip with
  it), cellGcmSetUserCommand and cellGcmSetWaitFlipUnsafe write RPCS3's words, with its room check and callback.
- **Z-cull.** cellGcmBindZcull returns lv2's result (LV1_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER_VALUE past region 7). lv2's 0x301 now checks
  a region it binds as RPCS3's lv2 does: the cull range not empty, not wrapping and inside the 3 MB of Z-cull RAM, the
  offset inside local memory, else CELL_EINVAL; cellGcmSetZcull meets the same checks (logged). The packed words reach
  the game's CellGcmZcullInfo array only when lv2 took them. cellGcmUnbindZcull: CELL_GCM_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE past 7,
  else the region keeps its settings, unbound (RPCS3 clears its renderer's bound flag; lv2 gets the last words with
  status1 0).
- **The rest.** cellGcmGetDisplayInfo, cellGcmGetTileInfo and cellGcmGetZcullInfo (the arrays), _cellGcmFunc12 (the
  local report area), cellGcmGetDefaultCommandWordSize and cellGcmGetDefaultSegmentWordSize with
  cellGcmSetDefaultCommandBufferAndSegmentWordSize (only while put and get are both 0x1000; the sizes are only read
  back, as in RPCS3), cellGcmSetDefaultCommandBuffer, cellGcmSetDebugOutputLevel (levels 1 to 3 kept, read by nothing,
  as in RPCS3), cellGcmSetSecondVFrequency (logged), cellGcmInitDefaultFifoMode, cellGcmSetDefaultFifoSize and
  cellGcmTerminate (CELL_OK). cellGcmSetFlipImmediate checks the id (past 7 CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE); RPCS3's TODO
  passes the id to cellGcmSetFlipMode as the mode (vsync for buffer 2), which is not what the call means: here nothing
  changes and the first call is logged, since nothing is flipped outside the command buffer yet.
- Pointers these functions write through are checked (D-042): CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE, or a log for the void ones,
  where RPCS3 would fault. Before cellGcmInit, calls that need the context refuse or log where RPCS3 writes address 0.

Not done: RPCS3's bare TODO and UNIMPLEMENTED stubs (the cursor and GPAD functions, the "2" variants,
cellGcmSetVBlankFrequency, cellGcmSetSecondVHandler, cellGcmSetGraphicsHandler, cellGcmSortRemapEaIoAddress,
cellGcmGetDisplayBufferByFlipIndex, cellGcmGetLastSecondVTime, cellGcmSysGetLastVBlankTime, cellGcmGetCurrentField,
cellGcmDumpGraphicsError, cellGcmSetInvalidateTile, _cellGcmFunc1/2/3/4/13/38, _cellGcmSetFlipCommand2) stay
unimplemented, logged with CELL_ENOSYS, until a game calls one. Tests: tests/hle/test_gcm_sys.cpp (every name resolves
by its NID; before cellGcmInit; mapping, first fit, reserves and unmapping against lv2's IO map; 512 MB; the flip state
from the driver information; lv2's 0x10a and queue notes; the queue handler's head and order on the interrupt thread,
in guest code under the interpreter; the command words; the default buffer's sizes; Z-cull and the arrays; the small
ones) and the flip command's queue in tests/rsx/test_methods.cpp.

## D-171 · 2026-10-06 · cellSpurs up to RPCS3's API, on the native scheduler

Every function RPCS3's cellSpurs.cpp implements now runs on the native SPURS (D-037): the 58 pspocket lacked
(initialize and SPURS2, the information and thread IDs, the SPU GUID, workload priorities, contention, idle SPU
requests, signals, data and ready counts, the second flag receiver, shutdown, wait and remove with the
shutdown-completion hook, the exception handler flags, traces, CellSpursTaskset2 and the taskset accessors, the event
flag getters, clear and try-wait, the barrier's taskset, the LF queue, the old job chain API, the job chain getters,
exception handlers, guards, grab limit and urgent call). Each cites RPCS3's function and was compared with libsre (fw
4.92, the reference, D-046); where the two differ, or RPCS3 has a TODO, libsre's behaviour is taken ("as libsre" in the
comments), as in D-047 and D-054. Updates of CellSpurs line 0 (ready counts, contention, signals, the flag receiver,
the system service message bits) are one reservation_op each, so idle workers waiting on the line wake (D-073).

- **SPURS2.** cellSpursInitializeWithAttribute2 makes an instance of 32 workloads (8 KB, SAF_SECOND_VERSION, flags1's
  SF1_32_WORKLOADS), and the native scheduler runs it with kernel 2's selection (RPCS3 spursKernel2SelectWorkload):
  contention and maximum contention in nibbles (byte wid & 15, low nibble for 0..15, high for 16..31), the ready
  counts of 16..31 in wklIdleSpuCountOrReadyCount2, signals in wklSignal2, the second state, status and event tables,
  and the information, F and H tables at 0x1000, 0x1200 and 0x1A00; the weight is the priority and the current
  workload's tie-breaker only. A game's policy module on SPURS2 is entered as kernel 2 calls it, from 0x834 ($0 and
  [0x1E0] are 0x838). Every workload function, the job chain policy's ready count and its error path's shutdown use
  the second tables for 16..31. cellSpursRequestIdleSpu is STAT on SPURS2 (its byte is a ready count there), as libsre.
- **Shutdown-completion hooks.** RPCS3 creates the event helper thread at initialize; natively it exists for the hooks
  only, created with the first workload whose attribute has one: an lv2 PPU thread "<prefix>SpursHdlr1" at the
  instance's PPU priority, waiting on the "_spuPrv" queue (42 entries) attached to a dynamic SPU port and a local event
  port, as RPCS3's. A completed shutdown sends it the workload's bit (data3); it calls the hook (spurs, wid, arg) once
  the workers have left the workload (D-136) and sets event bit 0x20, which cellSpursWaitForWorkloadShutdown waits for
  where RPCS3 waits on the semaphore the helper posts. cellSpursFinalize stops it (the end event, the join, the port,
  SPU port and queue). Its entry is an internal function the loader links (_pspocket_spurs_event_helper, NID
  0x8A1D254E); without it a hook is logged, not called. A shutdown an SPU starts (a job chain's error) is completed by
  the waiter, which sends the completion as the system service would.
- **libsre where RPCS3 differs.** cellSpursGetSpuGuid decodes the .SpuGUID section's four `ila $2` instructions (RPCS3
  writes nothing). cellSpursCreateJobChain makes the old API's chain with libsre's checks (entry, a grab limit of 1 to
  16, tags up to 31, priorities, descriptors of 64, 128 or 256 bytes), revision 1 from SDK 1.5, else 0; RPCS3's checks
  attribute fields the old API has not and always fails. cellSpursKickJobChain gives a chain with autoReadyCount ready
  count 1 if it had none (compare-and-swap 0 to 1) and one without it the count given (ReadyCountStore); RPCS3 has the
  two the other way round. A job guard keeps its chain as a u64 at 0x08 (RPCS3 reads a u32 there, the high word); the
  last notify kicks a revision 0 or 1 chain with the requested SPU count, runs a later one that waits on the guard.
  cellSpursGetJobChainInfo also gives the grab limit (0x44) and takes the name from the workload's information;
  cellSpursJobSetMaxGrab writes the limit at 0x72, where libsre keeps it (RPCS3's layout: 0x70), and the policy keeps
  a limit changed during a visit. cellSpursJobChainGetError refuses a NULL cause and writes it only with an error;
  cellSpursJobChainGetSpursAddress and the taskset accessors refuse a workload ID past 31 (RPCS3 checks none, or 15,
  which a SPURS2 taskset passes); the event flag and barrier getters check alignment before the output's NULL and
  sign-extend direction and clear mode; _cellSpursLFQueueInitialize refuses a taskset whose workload ID is past 31;
  _cellSpursTaskAttribute2Initialize clears all 256 bytes; cellSpursRequestIdleSpu answers with the policy module's
  codes and accepts a count of 8 (RPCS3: the core's, and 8 is INVAL). cellSpursCreateTaskset2 (RPCS3: a TODO after
  the first two steps) adds the Task2 and exit-code handler descriptors, two lv2 event flags "taskset2" and the task
  name buffer, cleared.
- **Fixes (rule 7).** _cellSpursWorkloadFlagReceiver clearing for a workload that is not the receiver is PERM and
  changes nothing; it returned CELL_OK and reset the flag. cellSpursReadyCountStore: a value above 255 is INVAL before
  SRCH, as RPCS3 and libsre.
- **What a native SPURS has not.** No SPU thread group or SPU threads: cellSpursGetSpuThreadGroupId,
  cellSpursGetSpuThreadId, cellSpursGetInfo and the trace header give their IDs as 0, an ID lv2 refuses (logged
  once); a memory container from cellSpursAttributeSetMemoryContainerForSpuThread is kept and not used (logged). No
  system service: a trace keeps its buffer, mode and per-SPU start indices and gets no packets; GetInfo's deadline
  counters are 0. The exception handlers (global, taskset, job chain) are kept and cellSpursEnableExceptionEventHandler
  sets the flag, but an SPU exception still stops its worker with a fatal log (rule 5). The job memory check
  (cellSpursJobChainAttributeSetJobTypeMemoryCheck, a descriptor's jobType bit 1) is not done: logged once, the jobs
  run without it, where the policy stopped with a fatal log before.

Not done: RPCS3's UNIMPLEMENTED stubs for CellSpursTaskset2's own tasks (cellSpursCreateTask2, JoinTask2,
TryJoinTask2, DestroyTaskset2, CreateTask2WithBinInfo) and cellSpursGetWorkloadInfo (a TODO in RPCS3) stay
unimplemented (rule 4); tasks made with cellSpursCreateTask run in a Taskset2 as in any taskset. Tests:
tests/hle/test_spurs_api.cpp (11 cases): the 58 names by NID and the internal helper; initialize, the container, the
information and thread IDs; the GUID decoder; priorities, contention, idle SPU requests, signals, data and ready counts;
the flag receivers (the PERM regression); shutdown, wait and remove with a hook run by guest code on the event helper,
and without the helper; traces and the exception handler flags; Taskset2 and the accessors, a task running in it; event
flags, the barrier and the LF queue; a SPURS2 instance whose taskset (workload 16) runs a task and whose policy module
(workload 17) is entered as kernel 2 does. tests/hle/test_spurs_jobchain.cpp (3 more cases): the old API made and
kicked; IDs, errors, information, handlers, grab limits, urgent calls and the memory check; guards that run and kick
chains. The synthetic executable's loader test (test_hle.cpp) counts cellSpursInitialize among its implemented imports.

## D-174 · 2026-10-06 · Fragment program opcodes and texture controls that skipped or spoiled draws

An audit of the RSX translation against RPCS3 (upstream 431b169: Program/FragmentProgramDecompiler.cpp, the
GLSLSnippets/RSXProg files, RSXTexture.cpp, Common/TextureUtils.cpp, RSXThread.cpp) found features games use that
pspocket refused, which skipped the whole draw, or decoded and never applied, which spoiled it. Each now follows RPCS3;
where pspocket differs, the reason is given.

- **Fragment program ops.** LIT (RPCS3 _builtin_lit), LIF (_builtin_lif), DST, REFL (GLSL reflect(src0, src1);
  NV_fragment_program's RFL reflects src1 about src0 instead, RPCS3's reading is kept), DP2A, PKG and UPG (PKB and UPB
  through linear_to_srgb and srgb_to_linear, on all four components), BEM (NV_fragment_program's X2D) and TEXBEM and
  TXPBEM (BEM's result as the coordinate of a TEX or TXP; RPCS3 marks them untested). LIT, LIF and REFL are not
  precision-clamped (SetDst). TXP on a cube map divides the direction by w (TEX3D_PROJ); TXD on a shadow map is the
  plain comparison (TEX2D_SHADOW). Still refused, as RPCS3's decompiler has nothing for them: CAL, POW, BEMLUM and
  TIMESWTEX.
- **Loops.** LOOP and REP run their count (SRC1 bits 2-9) times, as RPCS3's decompiler does and NV_fragment_program2
  defines ("the x, y, and z components ... specify the initial values for the loop count, loop index, and loop index
  increment"). pspocket ran `for (i = init; i < count; i += increment)`, as RPCS3's interpreter does: wrong whenever
  the initial index is not 0 or the increment not 1, and a REP encoded with all three fields the count, as nouveau's
  nv40_fp_rep encodes it after NVIDIA's compilers, never ran. A loop whose condition never holds is skipped (RPCS3:
  `if (false) for`; pspocket ran its body once), and a BRK outside any loop does nothing (it ended the program).
- **Indexed inputs** (SRC2.use_index_reg, refused before): texture coordinate A0.x + addr_reg (NV_fragment_program2's
  fragment.texcoord[A0.x + n]). In a LOOP, A0.x is init + k * increment (the increment signed 8-bit); RPCS3 indexes by
  its 0-based counter, the same for the {n, 0, 1} loops compilers emit for `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)`. A REP leaves
  the index (NV_fragment_program2); with no LOOP around it, its own counter is used, as RPCS3. The coordinate comes
  from a table of the ten with each one's 2D control applied (RPCS3 reads them as they are and logs the case); past
  TEX9 it is (0, 0, 0, 1), as RPCS3's _indexed_load. Outside loops the input is TEX(addr_reg); past SSA the program is
  refused (RPCS3: invalid ucode, nothing drawn).
- **ARL** keeps floor (only its comment changed): NV_vertex_program2 defines ARL as floor and ARR (vector op 0x17) as
  round, and nouveau emits Gallium's floor ARL as op 0x0d. RPCS3 now truncates (`ivec4($0)`; it used `$ifloor`
  before); only a negative fractional address tells them apart.
- **Texture controls**, decoded in state.cpp and never applied. texture_control() (texture.cpp) makes each unit's word
  as RPCS3's format_ex: what the format allows (get_format_features: the 8-bit formats everything; the depth formats,
  X16 and HILO8 the biased remap only; Y16_X16 signed and biased, in 16-bit steps; the float formats and HILO_S8
  nothing), signed channels (TEXTURE_FILTER bits 28-31) through the remap (shuffle_mask_bits, with RPCS3's remap for
  X16, Y16_X16, HILO and the float formats), gamma (ADDRESS bits 20-23, R G B A in the register, A R G B in the word,
  not remapped) on the channels not signed, and the biased unsigned remap (ADDRESS bits 12-15 = 1: (x - 128) / 127 in
  the bytes' steps) on the rest. The fragment shader applies it to the sampled texel (rsx_texel, RPCS3's
  _process_texel), after the alpha kill (CONTROL0 bit 2: alpha below 1e-6 discards the fragment). Units that convert or
  alpha-kill are compiled in (FpOptions masks, in the program key), as RPCS3's TEXTURE_FORMAT_CONVERT and
  TEXTURE_ALPHA_KILL; the word reaches the shader in MslFsParams::tex_control. Gamma decodes after filtering, as
  RPCS3's shader path does; its GL and Vulkan backends sample an sRGB view instead when the remap is the identity and
  gamma covers R, G and B (decoding before filtering), not done here.
- **_bx2** expands only formats with biased renormalization, on the channels the remap reads (a channel forced to 0 or
  1 stays), as 2x - 1, and replaces gamma (RPCS3 _enable_texture_expand). Before, it expanded every channel of every
  texture, float formats and shadow lookups included.
- **LOD bias** (TEXTURE_FILTER bits 0-12, signed 4.8). Metal samplers have none, so the shader adds it: TEX and TXP
  sample with bias(b), TXB adds b to its own bias, TXL to its level (GL and Vulkan, whose samplers RPCS3 gives the
  bias, add it to an explicit LOD too), TXD's derivatives grow by 2^b. It applies to textures with more than one level
  whose min filter reads mipmaps, as RPCS3 sets it on the sampler only then; shadow lookups take none.
- **The ROP**, in RSXROPEpilogue.glsl's order. NV4097_SET_SHADER_PACKER turns the colour outputs' RGB to sRGB
  (linear_to_srgb) on 8-bit targets with 16-bit exports (RSXThread.cpp). Alpha to coverage
  (NV4097_SET_ANTI_ALIASING_CONTROL bit 4) discards a fragment whose alpha is not above RPCS3's _rand of its pixel
  (targets have one sample here, as RPCS3 emulates it without hardware support). The alpha test reads colour 0's alpha
  before the B8 and G8B8 channel moves, and runs without colour targets too ("This stage always runs even without a
  color output"): depth-only passes of alpha-tested geometry, shadow maps, were drawn solid.
- **The shader cache.** Program records now start with the translation's version (shader::kTranslationVersion, 2);
  records of another version are skipped, since they hold the old translation under keys the new one makes too. The
  Mac and the phone compile their programs again once; the shaders the app is seeded with need a new Mac run.

What changes for programs that already translated (GTA V's frames): loops that start their index elsewhere than 0 or
step by other than 1, and REPs; _bx2 on float formats, on remaps with a constant channel and on shadow lookups;
mipmapped textures with a LOD bias; textures with gamma, signed or biased-remap bits; alpha kill; alpha-tested draws
without colour targets or onto B8 and G8B8 targets; the sRGB packer; alpha to coverage. Everything else gives what it
gave (the samples gain `bias(fp.tex_bias[n])`, 0 for them). Assassin's Creed's washed-out Abstergo lab (status.md)
may be gamma textures or the sRGB packer; that is for the next run to show.

Not done: TXL and TXB still take their level and bias from src0.w (nouveau's NV40 compiler puts them there too); RPCS3
reads src1.x. That is outside this audit and changes nothing that worked; a game's TXL would settle it. The border
colour of signed textures (RPCS3 border_color re-encodes it) is not converted: pspocket's three Metal border colours
are approximate anyway. RPCS3's RENORMALIZE (its hosts' precision for 16-bit formats) does not apply: pspocket decodes
those formats to 8 bits as RPCS3's CPU path does.

Tests: tests/rsx/test_shader.cpp (each new op's MSL and RPCS3's helpers; precision exemptions; TXP on a cube map and
TXD on a shadow map; loops: counts, LOOP's index, REP inside and outside a LOOP, a negative increment, a never
condition, BRK outside loops, indexed inputs in and out of loops and past SSA; per-unit conversions, alpha kill and LOD
bias; the ROP order and the alpha test without colour outputs), tests/rsx/test_texture.cpp (texture_control: format
features, the register orders, signed over gamma over the remap, remaps with constant channels, X32_FLOAT, DEPTH24_D8,
Y16_X16's remap), and tests/rsx/test_metal.mm, run on the GPU against values worked out from RPCS3's formulas: LIT,
LIF, DST, REFL, DP2A, BEM, PKG and UPG; loop counts and indexed coordinates; TEXBEM and TXPBEM; ARL's floor through
c[A0.x + n]; gamma, signed channels and the biased remap; _bx2 by format and remap; alpha kill; LOD bias between two
mipmap levels; the sRGB packer; the alpha test in a depth-only pass; alpha to coverage's share of pixels; every
texture op on every texture kind compiles, with and without conversions.

## D-175 · 2026-10-06 · System libraries chosen per game, as a PS3 links them

Before, a firmware module ran as it is (LLE, D-157) only when the host implemented none of its libraries. A library
the host implemented only in part stayed on the host, and the game's calls to the missing functions failed. Now the
loader chooses per game, before it links the executable's imports (LleModules::decide, runtime/loader/src/lle.cpp):

- **Host or firmware.** A library goes to the host when the host implements every function the game imports from it
  and the game imports none of its variables (the host exports none). Otherwise its firmware module runs as it is.
- **Always native.** Some module files never run as they are. These are the process runtime (liblv2*), module loading
  (libsysmodule), SPURS (libsre, D-037), the RSX (libgcm_sys), audio, voice, input (libio), files (libfs), the network
  (libnet, libnetctl), sysutil and everything built on it (libsysutil*), and devices (camera, mic, gem, usbd,
  usbpspcm). pspocket must own what they do.
- **Linking a chosen module.** Its imports link as RPCS3 links a module (PPUModule.cpp ppu_load_imports): from another
  chosen module, else the host, else a firmware module that can join.
  - A function none of these has links to the host's unimplemented stub, which logs and fails when called (rule 4).
    The same goes for a syscall lv2 does not answer. Both are listed (gaps()).
  - A variable must come from a chosen module. A module whose imported variable no module exports is refused, and its
    libraries stay on the host; refusals can cascade.
  - The choice is a fixpoint over module files. Only the modules the game's libraries reach are kept.
- **The log.** It names the modules chosen and what each lacks, the modules refused and why, and the functions the
  host lacks for libraries left on it. That is the list of what to implement next.
- **The index.** The module index (lle-index.txt) moves to format 2. For each module file it lists the libraries, the
  functions and variables each exports, what the file imports, and the syscalls its code makes (an `sc` with
  `li r11,N` in the eight instructions before it). An old index is rebuilt.
- **Modules loaded while the game runs (D-159).**
  - A game's own PRX gets the same choice for its imports (LleModules::extend). What was chosen stays chosen, since it
    is linked, and more modules may join.
  - A library something already linked to the host stays on the host, so a library has one implementation.
  - Firmware modules loaded for the PRX start before its module_start, on the thread that starts it
    (ModuleLoader::take_dependency_starts).
  - A firmware module loaded by its path runs as it is when it was chosen, or when the host implements none of its
    libraries.
  - A module start runs once (take_starts marks each start as run).

Probed against the user's 4.92 firmware (144 modules), assuming a game needs something the host lacks in each library:

- **Would run as they are:** libdmux, libdmuxpamf, libpamf, libpngdec, libjpgdec, libgifdec, libfont (with libfontFT
  and libfreetype), libl10n, libresc, libsync2 (with libfiber and libspurs_jq), libatrac3plus, libatrac3multi,
  libvpost, libsail (with its 15 decoders), libkey2char, librudp, libhttp (with libssl).
- **Refused: libadec.** It imports a variable of the DTS-HD core decoder that no module exports, so cellAdec needs a
  native implementation.
- **Host functions those modules lack, which they log when called:** cellSpursQueuePushBody, cellSpursQueueSize,
  cellSpursSendWorkloadSignal, cellSpursDestroyTaskset2, cellGcmGetLastSecondVTime, _sys_vsnprintf,
  _sys_heap_get_total_free_size, cellSysmoduleUnloadModuleInternal and cellKbGetConfiguration, among others.

Tests (tests/hle/test_lle.cpp):

- The choice: host-covered, partial, native list, gaps, variable refusal, the game's variables, extend, host-bound
  libraries, forced libraries. Each runs twice, the second time from the cached index.
- A game PRX loaded while the game runs, whose firmware dependency joins and starts first, once.

## D-176 · 2026-10-06 · The PS3 system software analysed: what it holds and how each part meets the engine

The user asked for the system file (PS3UPDAT.PUP 4.92, already installed on the Mac) to be taken apart and its useful
parts connected to the iOS-native engine, "like analysing a car engine and making it work for another car". It is
Sony's closed software, free to download but not open source, under a licence that allows reverse engineering only
as far as the law does. That covers interoperability, which is what this is. Two lines hold:

- Nothing from the file enters the repository or the app's code. The analysis output stays in inventory/ (rule 1).
- pspocket uses the user's own copy on the user's own device.

The tools (none holds firmware content):

- `pspocket-firmware --decrypt DEV_FLASH OUT` writes every module of sys/external and sys/internal as an ELF.
- `pspocket-boot --hle-list` prints every function the host implements.
- `scripts/firmware-report.py` runs both and ps3inspect, reads RPCS3's g_prx_list, and writes report.md and
  report.json under inventory/firmware/analysis/.

docs/firmware.md is the committed summary. The firmware holds 179 modules, 206 libraries, 5,385 exported functions
and 188 SPU programs, plus 35 system fonts, 60 root certificates, keyboard dictionaries, the XMB, a Blu-ray player and
three emulators. The host implements 607 of the functions.

Each part gets one of five plans:

- **Ours on iOS** (77 modules): lv2, SPURS, RSX to Metal, audio, input, files, network, sysutil and everything on it,
  devices. These never run as they are (D-175).
- **iOS framework** (24 modules): ImageIO for image decoding and encoding, VideoToolbox for H.264, Metal/vImage and
  AudioConverter for post-processing.
- **Sony's code, translated once per firmware** (75 modules): media front ends and decoder cores without an iOS
  counterpart, movie containers and players, fonts with FreeType, text conversion, cellSync2/fibers/job queue,
  cellResc, HTTP/SSL/RUDP, encoders.
- **Data kept**: fonts and certificates.
- **Not used**: debug modules, the XMB, the Blu-ray player, the emulators, the dictionaries.

The order of work:

1. Link like a PS3 and keep only what games use (D-177).
2. Translate Sony's modules and their SPU programs once per firmware, at fixed addresses, Mac first; then on the
   phone.
3. iOS frameworks behind cellPngDec/cellJpgDec/cellGifDec, cellVdec (H.264) and cellAdec (AAC, MP3, AC-3), each
   measured against the translated original.
4. The parts that are ours, filled in from what games call.

## D-177 · 2026-10-06 · Firmware modules linked as a PS3 links them; the phone keeps only what games use

The first step of D-176's plan.

- **sys/internal is indexed too.**
  - cellAdec's codec cores partly live there: DTS-HD, MPEG-2 AAC, AAC 2ch, MP3 surround and TrueHD, among 37
    modules.
  - LleModules keys a module by its file name for sys/external and "internal/NAME" for sys/internal. libvpost.sprx is
    in both, as different modules. sys/external's exports win when both export a library.
  - The index (lle-index.txt) is format 3 and is rebuilt when either folder changes.
  - Loading a module by its path (sys_prx_load_module, D-159) accepts both folders.
  - The always-native list also covers sys/internal's audio and voice services (sys_audio, sysvoice_modules,
    libvoice_internal) and the file utilities (libfs_utility*).
- **An imported variable no module exports no longer refuses a module.**
  - lv2 leaves such an import unlinked on a PS3. libadec imports the WMA Pro, WMA Lossless, DTS and DTS-HD core
    decoders, which are in no retail firmware, and still decodes every other format.
  - The variable is listed in the module's gaps (with the functions and syscalls nothing implements) and stays
    unlinked.
  - D-175 refused libadec over it, which left cellAdec on the host, which has none of it. Only a module missing from
    the index is refused now.
- **The phone keeps only what games use.**
  - install_firmware writes sys/, data/font and data/cert (recomp::firmware_path_used). It leaves out the XMB, the
    Blu-ray player, the PS1/PS2/PSP emulators and the keyboard dictionaries: 150 of 4.92's 188 MB. FirmwareInstall
    counts what it left out.
  - An install from before this is pruned once when a game starts on the phone (recomp::prune_firmware, game.mm).
  - The Mac's copy in inventory/ is left whole for analysis (pspocket-boot does not prune).

Checked against the user's 4.92 firmware: 177 modules indexed, 198 libraries. Assassin's Creed still takes all of its
140 imports from the host (no firmware module chosen). Its ATRAC audio comes from sys/external/flashATRAC.pic, an SPU
program its audio library loads itself, as GTA V loads flashMP3.pic.

Tests:

- tests/common/test_firmware.cpp: install skips vsh; firmware_path_used; prune once.
- tests/hle/test_lle.cpp: an unlinked variable is a gap; a sys/internal core serves the sys/external module that
  needs it; both run twice, the second time from the cached index.

## D-178 · 2026-10-06 · The PS3 system software's modules translated once: the system library

The second step of D-176's plan. The firmware modules a game gets (D-175) ran under the interpreter (D-157). Now they
are translated once per firmware, as a game is, and shared by every game.

- **Fixed addresses.**
  - Every module the index holds has a fixed place in the PRX region (PS_MEM_PRX_BASE, 256 MB). The region was
    reserved in lv2's map and unused until now.
  - The modules are laid out in key order (sys/internal's, then sys/external's), each PT_LOAD at a 64 KB boundary,
    as RPCS3 allocates segments (recomp::prx_fixed_layout). 4.92's 177 modules fit.
  - A module's code is the same bytes in every game. Placement and relocation are one function,
    recomp::place_prx, which the loader copies into guest memory and the preparation translates.
  - None of the modules translated patch code when they are linked. Code patched by function references exists only
    in the modules pspocket serves itself (45 sysutil modules and libnetctl). Variable references patch data only.
  - The index (format 4) keeps each module's PT_LOAD sizes and its file's SHA-256, so the layout costs nothing at
    boot.
  - A game's own PRX modules still go to main memory.
- **The library.**
  - prepare_system (runtime/prepare/src/system.cpp) places every module that is not native (100 of 177; 77 are
    pspocket's own) and seeds the analysis with every exported function's descriptor and each module's descriptor
    table, read relocated. It analyses them as one program and lifts them with the game lifter.
  - prepare_game's compile, link and sign steps then make game.dylib in the folder "system" beside /dev_flash.
  - identity.txt (LleModules::identity_text: each module's key, file SHA-256 and addresses) is what it was made
    from; the library holds its SHA-256.
  - modules.txt has each translated module's code segments and their SHA-256 as placed.
  - pspocket-prepare --system DEV_FLASH --game-dir DIR makes it on the Mac.
- **Loading.**
  - loader::SystemLibrary loads it, before the executable's imports are linked, when it was made for the installed
    modules (game::load_library with an expected SHA-256 and no D-098 samples) and this runtime.
  - Its functions go to a second dispatch table, for the PRX region, sorted by address
    (pspocket/ppu/prx_dispatch.hpp). ps_ppu_dispatch_register(_table) routes there; the miss stub, ps_ppu_jump_miss
    and ps_ppu_dispatch_find look there first.
  - The first table keeps to the game's range; its one-range limit would otherwise have been 3/4 GB away.
  - Each firmware module that loads (LleModules' load hook) is checked: its code segments' SHA-256 in guest memory
    against modules.txt. Its range is enabled only on a match; else it runs under the interpreter, logged.
  - The library ABI is unchanged (the new header is host-only), so no game needs preparing again.
- **The phone.** Before the first game after the system software is installed (or after an update that translates
  differently), the app prepares the system library with the game's "Preparing…" overlay
  (ps_prepare_system_check/_start, LibraryModel.armBoot). game.mm loads it from beside /dev_flash. pspocket-boot
  does the same (--system-library DIR|none).

Results on the user's 4.92:

- 100 modules translated: 18,962 functions, 1.26 million instructions, none unsupported, one illegal word reached (now
  logged).
- 105 files compiled in 33 s on the M4 into an 18.8 MB library.
- Booting Assassin's Creed with five libraries forced in (cellPngDec, cellFontFT, cellL10n, cellSync2, cellAdec):
  each "runs translated", and their module_starts ran with no interpreter fallback at a firmware address.
- GTA V's gate passes unchanged.

A bug found on the way: in 38 modules the first PT_LOAD reserves more than its file part, past the second's vaddr
(libpngdec: 0x50000 bytes from 0, its data at 0x40a00). An analysis address there belongs to the later segment.

Not yet:

- The modules' 188 SPU programs. They are found at run time as a game's are (D-117) and translated into that game's
  library at its next preparation.

Tests:

- tests/common/test_prx_place.cpp: layout and placement at fixed addresses; native, translated and identity lines.
- tests/ppu/test_dispatch.cpp: the second table, its enabling, a call through the miss stub with no miss.
- tests/game/test_system_library.cpp: a synthetic firmware module translated with the device's compiler, placed,
  checked, its module_start run translated with no miss; changed code refused; another firmware not current.

## D-179 · 2026-10-06 · Internal module IDs, two small imports, and what the phone run of 2026-10-06 showed

Run 100 and the phone sessions after it (Sniper: Ghost Warrior, L.A. Noire, in a copy of the app with no system
software installed) showed gaps in pspocket's own modules.

- **cellSysmodule's internal module IDs, as RPCS3.**
  - Its table of 87 internal modules (0xF000 + index) and their dependencies, generated from cellSysmodule.cpp.
  - LOADABLE_INTERNAL_MODULES says which the public calls take. LOADABLE_INTERNAL_MODULES_EX says which the Ex calls
    take.
  - cellSysmoduleLoadModuleInternal, UnloadModuleInternal, IsLoadedEx, LoadModuleEx and UnloadModuleEx are new.
  - 0xF035 is CELL_SYSMODULE_SYSUTIL_NP_TROPHY, which lv2 counts as loaded from SDK 3.3 on (DEFAULT_MODULES) and
    many games load. Sniper: Ghost Warrior got CELL_SYSMODULE_ERROR_UNKNOWN for it.
  - 0xF020, 0xF024 and 0xF03E (VC-1, WMA, the ASF parser) need flags in the PARAM.SFO buffer that lv2 leaves zero, so
    they are refused, as in RPCS3.
- **cellGcmSetGraphicsHandler**: noted and not kept, as RPCS3.
- **sceNpDrmIsAvailable2**: the same check as sceNpDrmIsAvailable, as RPCS3.
- **Job chain stops.** Every job chain stop now first reports what the SPU read of the job at hand, what memory holds,
  who wrote over it and the commands around pc (D-138's report). Run 100's stop came through the job binary's fetch,
  which stopped without it.
- **The app warns when the system software is missing.** It says so in the game's info when no system software is
  installed. A copy of /dev_flash pushed from the Mac holds only the sound decoders games load themselves, and the
  app had used it without a word. LleModules no longer reports an empty firmware as "does not fit".

The direction after this (the user, 2026-10-06): any PS3 game on iOS-native infrastructure, no emulation, no
interpreting. Every library a game calls is to be pspocket's own (docs/firmware.md's "iOS framework" and "Sony's code,
translated once" families become "ours"). D-178's system library stays only as a fallback for what is not written yet.
Every SPU and PPU function is to be translated before the game runs.

Tests (tests/hle):

- test_sysPrxForUser.cpp: internal IDs (the trophy module, dependencies through internal IDs, the Ex lists, the
  refused codecs).
- test_np.cpp: sceNpDrmIsAvailable2.

## D-180 · 2026-10-06 · cellResc on the host: the game's frame goes to the screen as it is

The first of the libraries D-179 moves to pspocket's own. On a PS3, libresc (the resolution scaler) has the RSX draw the
game's frame (a "source", cellRescSetSrc) into colour buffers of its own at the TV's resolution and mode (PAL 50/60,
interlacing, letterbox), then flips those. Here the display is the iPhone's screen, and Metal already shows any
display buffer scaled to it, so cellRescSetConvertAndFlip flips the source as it is:

- **The flip.** The source becomes a display buffer (cellGcmSetDisplayBuffer, with its index as the buffer id, again
  only when its geometry changes), and cellGcmSetFlip's command goes into the game's command buffer. The RSX flips it
  in command order, and the Metal backend presents it.
- **No conversion pass.** None runs, and the colour buffers the game gives libresc are kept and unused.
- **Handlers and status.** Flip and vblank handlers, flip status and the last flip time are GCM's.

Where a game can see the difference, libresc is matched. RPCS3 runs Sony's libresc by default, and its own functions
only check arguments, so its checks are taken. The rest comes from reading the firmware's libresc.sprx for
interoperability (D-176):

- **cellRescGetNumColorBuffers**: six buffers for PAL 60 interpolated from 576 lines, three for PAL 60 dropped, else
  two.
- **cellRescVideoOutResolutionId2RescBufferMode**: 1080 to 1920x1080, 720 to 1280x720, 480 to 720x480, 576 to
  720x576.
- **cellRescGcmSurface2RescSrc**:
  - a pitch A8R8G8B8 surface is texture 0xA5 (0x85 swizzled); W16Z16Y16X16 float is 0xBA/0x9A; another format is
    0xFF;
  - with a 24- or 28-byte configuration, 2x multisampling doubles the width and 4x doubles both sides.
- **cellRescGetBufferSize**:
  - libresc's 384 bytes of vertices and its largest shader (0x300);
  - colour buffers per destination mode: the pitch given (cellRescSetDsts) times the mode's height aligned as asked,
    times its buffer count;
  - the display mode's with MINIMUM_VRAM, the largest supported mode's otherwise.
  - The game's memory is therefore laid out as on a PS3, though the buffers stay unused.

Kept and not applied: the aspect ratio, the PAL flex ratio and the register count of libresc's shader. The interlace
table is checked and not written, since the screen is progressive. Sniper: Ghost Warrior showed frames only through
cellResc (phone run of 2026-10-06).

Also: the SPU DMA write log's size is PSPOCKET_DMA_LOG (2,048 entries per thread by default). Run 100's descriptor
overwrite on the Mac found no writer among the last 2,048, which is a few milliseconds of EDGE traffic.

Tests: tests/hle/test_gcm_sys.cpp (cellResc). Covers the checks before and after init, libresc's tables and sizes,
the surface conversion with 4x multisampling, a source flipped through the command buffer and shown (display buffer 0
holds its geometry, the RSX counts the flip), the buffer address alignments, float arguments in f1 and f2, and the PAL
combination.

## D-181 · 2026-10-06 · FFmpeg's decoders for pspocket's own media libraries

To run any game with no PS3 firmware file (D-179's direction), video and audio decoding must be pspocket's own. RPCS3
decodes with FFmpeg in its own cellVdec (H.264, MPEG-2, MPEG-4) and cellAtracXdec (ATRAC3plus), and swscale converts
the pictures. pspocket's versions of those libraries follow RPCS3's, so they use FFmpeg too.

- **The build.** scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh builds FFmpeg 7.1.1 from the unmodified release tarball, SHA-256 pinned and
  not kept in the repository (the build needs no network), for macOS arm64 (build/ffmpeg/macos: the Mac's tests and
  pspocket-boot) and iOS arm64 (build/ffmpeg/ios: the app).
- **What goes in.** libavcodec with the decoders the PS3's formats need (H.264, MPEG-1/2 video, MPEG-4 part 2; ATRAC3,
  ATRAC3plus and their AL forms, MP1/2/3, AAC, AC-3, E-AC-3, PCM) and their parsers, plus libswscale, libswresample
  and libavutil. Nothing else: no formats, devices, filters, network or autodetected system libraries.
- **Licence.** Configured --disable-gpl --disable-nonfree --disable-version3, so only LGPL-2.1-or-later code, which
  combines with pspocket's GPLv2 (D-001). Recorded in third_party/README.md.
- **Size and time.** About 5 MB of static libraries per platform (libavcodec 3.1 MB), built in 69 s for both on the
  M4.
- **Wiring.** CMake makes pspocket::ffmpeg (an INTERFACE target defining PSPOCKET_HAVE_FFMPEG=1) from build/ffmpeg/macos
  or -DPSPOCKET_FFMPEG_DIR. scripts/ios.sh and app/ios/project.yml add build/ffmpeg/ios's headers and libraries to
  the app. Without them the media libraries build with their decoders left out (#if PSPOCKET_HAVE_FFMPEG), and
  decoding fails, logged.
- **Hardware decoding later.** VideoToolbox (H.264 in hardware) and AudioToolbox can take over a format later, measured
  against these first (rule 8).

## D-182 · 2026-10-06 · Functions RPCS3 leaves as stubs are answered as RPCS3 answers them

A library pspocket always serves itself (recomp::firmware_module_native, D-175) has no firmware fallback. A
function the host lacks there returns CELL_ENOSYS to the game. RPCS3 also serves most of these libraries itself
(g_prx_list in rpcs3/Emu/Cell/lv2/sys_prx.cpp says HLE for them). Many of its functions there are stubs: a log line,
then a constant, nearly always CELL_OK. Games run on RPCS3 with those answers. pspocket now gives the same answers,
as D-166 did for lv2's null syscalls:

- **The table.** runtime/hle/scripts/gen_rpcs3_stubs.py reads RPCS3's module sources and writes
  runtime/hle/src/rpcs3_stubs.inc. A function counts as a stub when its body is nothing but log statements and
  `return X;`, with X a constant. 296 functions in 28 libraries qualify, among them:
  - cellSysutil's web browser and packet functions;
  - cellCamera's async calls;
  - the netctl GameInt calls;
  - sceNp's commerce getters;
  - cellSysutilAvc2/AvcExt, cellPrint, cellRemotePlay, cellVideoPlayer, cellDtcpIp, cellPesm, cellBgdl;
  - sys_io's sys_config calls.
- **Which libraries.** Only those whose firmware file pspocket keeps native *and* RPCS3 serves itself:
  - every libsysutil* library, the NP libraries among them;
  - libsysmodule, libaudio, libvoice, libio, libcamera, libmic, libgem, libnetctl and libfs_utility_init.

  Left out are liblv2, libsre, libgcm_sys, libfs, libnet, libusbd and libusbpspcm. RPCS3 loads those from the
  firmware by default, so its stubs there are not what games meet on RPCS3.
- **The answer.** HleProcess links an import to the registry's implementation when there is one, else to the stub's
  answer (LinkedFunction::stub), else to the unimplemented stub (CELL_ENOSYS).
  - A stub call logs `STUB module::name (NID) ... -> 0x0 as RPCS3`, for the first 8 calls and then every 1024th.
    It counts apart from the gaps (HleProcess::stub_calls), so the log still names what is not implemented.
  - --stop-at-first does not stop on a stub.
  - A real implementation added to the registry always wins; the table does not need regenerating for that.
- **What the user sees.**
  - pspocket-boot lists the stubbed calls apart from the unimplemented ones, at the end of a run.
  - `--imports` marks stubs with ~.
  - The phone's boot line counts the stubs.
  - LleModules' list of what the host lacks counts how many of those are stubs.
- **D-175's choice is unchanged.** A stub is not an implementation: a library that is not always native still goes to
  its firmware module when the host lacks one of its imported functions.

Also: the Linux host build is warning-free again with -DPSPOCKET_WERROR=ON. Apple-only helpers and options are marked
unused, sys/sysctl.h is used on Apple only, and test_firmware's using-directives moved out of its Apple-only block.
ctest passes on Linux x86, apart from the SPU float fuzz, which needs AArch64 (D-027).

Tests (tests/hle/test_hle.cpp):

- every stub's NID matches its name or its REG_FNID;
- a stub answers CELL_OK, and cellMicIsAttached answers 1;
- stub calls are counted apart from the gaps;
- an implemented function is linked to its implementation, not to its stub.

## D-183 · 2026-10-06 · The sysutil family, input, audio and devices as RPCS3 has them; dialogs answered as their cursor starts

The two HLE batches that stopped at a usage limit (status.md). Sysutil and everything built on it is
always native (D-175), so a function missing there fails the game outright.

**cellSaveData: every function RPCS3 registers (40)**

The new functions sit on the existing savedata_op:

- **The variants:** List{Save,Load}[2], Fixed{Save,Load}[2], Auto{Save,Load} and ListAutoSave.
- **The cellSaveDataUser\* variants.** Each takes a user ID:
  - 0 is the current user (00000001).
  - Another user's /dev_hdd0/home/NNNNNNNN/savedata must exist, else CELL_SAVEDATA_ERROR_NOUSER.
  - Above 99999999 is parameter error 91.
- **The rest:** ListDelete, Delete, UserGetListItem, Enable/GetEnableOverlay, and the import and export functions.
  For the last, RPCS3 checks the arguments (error 137), then returns CELL_OK without doing anything; so does pspocket.
- **The list step, as RPCS3's:**
  - funcList sees the list.
  - Its listSet is checked (parameter errors 34 to 46).
  - Its fixedList filters what is shown; an empty one shows nothing, as RPCS3's (games copy the listing into it).
  - newData offers a new save.
  - focusPosition puts the cursor: DIRNAME, HEAD, TAIL, LATEST, OLDEST or NEWDATA.
- **ListDelete's '\*' prefix** lists the game's own saves, as RPCS3.

**No dialog UI: the user answers as the cursor starts.** cellMsgDialogOpen2's dialogs are already answered at once
with their default button (show_msg_dialog). Save data's own dialogs now follow the same rule:

- **The YES/NO confirmations** of the fixed variants (CELL_SAVEDATA_OPTION_NONE) and of a list choice are answered YES.
  Before, they failed with CELL_SAVEDATA_ERROR_INTERNAL, as RPCS3 does when it cannot open a dialog. A game that saves
  with OPTION_NONE could not save at all.
- **The save list.** The user picks the save funcList focused. Failing that, the new save when there is one, else the
  first save shown. With nothing to pick, CELL_CANCEL.
- **The delete lists** (Delete, Delete2, ListDelete) are left at once: CELL_CANCEL, nothing deleted. Accepting one
  would delete the saves one by one with nobody choosing.

Every such answer is logged as a warning. A dialog UI (the app) replaces these answers with the user's own.

**cellSysutil, cellMsgDialog, cellVideoOut, cellAudioOut, cellSysutilAvconfExt: every function RPCS3 implements**

These are 41 more functions.

- **The message dialog.**
  - cellMsgDialogOpen (Open2 under its older name).
  - OpenErrorCode: an OK dialog with RPCS3's English text for the error code, then the code.
  - OpenSimulViewWarning.
  - The progress bars: SetMsg, Reset, Inc.
  - cellMsgDialogClose(delay): the dialog closes with CELL_MSGDIALOG_BUTTON_NONE at the first
    cellSysutilCheckCallback after the delay. RPCS3 closes it from a thread of its own, but the end of the drawing and
    the callback reach the game only at a check either way.
- **cellSysutil.**
  - The callback dispatchers, 32 slots, kept as RPCS3 keeps them.
  - The game exit functions (cellSysutilGameDataExit and its _I wrappers).
  - cellSysutil_E1EC7B6A.
  - Background music Ex: the fade times are checked and kept; Status2.
- **Video out.**
  - GetNumberOfDevice.
  - GetConfiguration: the configured mode, else the display's 720p at 4 bytes a pixel.
  - GetConvertCursorColorInfo (full range).
  - ConvertCursorColor: RPCS3's gamma conversion. Gamma comes in f1; the integer arguments keep r3 to r8, as RPCS3's
    binder counts them.
  - GetGamma, GetScreenSize (VALUE_IS_NOT_SET: no 3D display), SetCopyControl, SetXVColor, SetupDisplay, Configure2.
- **Audio out.**
  - GetNumberOfDevice.
  - GetDeviceInfo: HDMI, 13 ms latency, the output's modes.
  - GetSoundAvailability2.
  - Register/SetDeviceMode/GetDeviceInfo2 and the "2" configurations, with RPCS3's checks.
- **Audio in.** There is no microphone, as RPCS3 with none configured:
  - available devices: 0, each entry disconnected (device number 0xff);
  - device info and registering a device: DEVICE_NOT_FOUND after RPCS3's checks;
  - the device mode is kept.

**cellGame and cellSysutil's game functions: every function RPCS3 registers (20 more)**

- **cellGame.**
  - cellGameGetParamInt: PARENTAL_LEVEL, RESOLUTION, SOUND_FORMAT.
  - cellGameSetParamString: the titles, into game data the session may create.
  - cellGameGetSizeKB: the checked directory, files rounded up to 1 KB, as RPCS3's fs::get_dir_size.
  - cellGamePatchCheck: NOTPATCH unless the game booted from a patch (category GD).
  - cellGameDeleteGameData: refused while a session may write the data, and for what isn't game data.
  - cellGameGetDiscContentInfoUpdatePath and cellGameGetLocalWebContentPath: nothing written, as RPCS3.
  - cellGameThemeInstall and cellGameThemeInstallFromBuffer: to /dev_hdd0/theme/<title ID>_<SHA-256>.p3t, once.
- **cellSysutil.**
  - HddGameCheck2 and DataCheckCreate are their newer twins.
  - HddGameGetSizeKB sizes the booted directory, a disc image included.
  - GameDataGetSizeKB sizes the last checked game data.
  - The system version checks ("04.8300").
  - The disc change callbacks under both names, and unregistering them.
  - The "exit broken" dialogs: logged, then CELL_SYSUTIL_REQUEST_EXITGAME to the game, as RPCS3's dialog does when it
    closes.
- **Kernel::vfs_tree_size.** The size of a guest directory, on a host mount or inside a disc image.

**cellOskDialog and cellOskExtUtility: every function RPCS3 registers (23 more)**

- **cellOskDialogGetInputText** serves the text last copied, by an unload or cellOskDialogExtUpdateInputText. Its
  result is OK with that text, else NO_INPUT_TEXT, as RPCS3's getText.
- **GetSize**: RPCS3's 1 x 1, width 0 for separate windows.

All of these are reset at the unload, as RPCS3's osk_info::reset.

**The small sysutil libraries (sysutil_misc.cpp, 52 functions)**

All are as RPCS3 has them with no device, service or overlay:

- **cellUserInfo.**
  - The current user (00000001, "User") is made on first use, as RPCS3 makes it at boot.

- **cellScreenShotUtility**: the titles and overlay are kept, with RPCS3's checks.
