## D-510 · 2026-10-08 · The C99 math library, under sys_libm and sys_libc

RPCS3 names nearly the same list under sys_libm and sys_libc (1,071 names shared) and implements neither; no firmware
module has them (a game links its C library into itself), so there is no Sony code to compare with. The math half is
pspocket's own now (runtime/hle/src/sys_libm.cpp, from the library work's draft): 522 functions registered under both
libraries and the 38 variables of Dinkumware's math (_Inf, _Nan, _Eps, _Flt, _Dbl, ... in sys_libc; _Erf_one,
_Gamma_big, _Fenv0, ... in sys_libm). Each is the C99 function (Annex F's special values, Annex G's complex ones)
computed by the host's libm, with the PS3 SDK's conventions where they differ from the host's:
- long double is double on the PPU (every `l` form is the double one); long is 32 bits (lrint, lround, scalbln).
- FP_ILOGB0 is INT_MIN and FP_ILOGBNAN INT_MAX (Dinkumware's math.h); an infinity's ilogb is INT_MAX.
- lrint, lround and their long long forms convert as fctiw/fctid: saturated, a NaN to the minimum; rint, nearbyint,
  lrint and llrint round as the guest's FPSCR[RN] says; the fenv functions keep FPSCR as the architecture has it.
- The SIMD functions (vector float in v2, v3) work lane by lane and flush denormals as VMX does with VSCR[NJ] set;
  complex values are two FPRs, the real part first; the fast float forms give the precise results.
- Dinkumware's internals (_Dtest, _Exp, _Sin, _Atan, ...) as its xmath.h uses them; four whose signatures are unknown
  (_Eadd, _Emul, _Esub, _Etentox) log the call and answer an error.
Tests (tests/hle/test_libm.cpp, 8,056 checks): every one-argument function and its float and long double forms at 23
points (zeros, denormals, infinities, NaN, large and small values) and every two-argument one over a grid, called
through the guest's registers as the PowerPC ABI passes them, equal to the C99 results; the conventions above; SIMD
lanes and the denormal flush; complex values; the variables.

## D-511 · 2026-10-08 · The C library under sys_libc and sys_libm, part 1: strings, ctype, stdlib, random numbers

The C half of the list RPCS3 names under both libraries (D-510 has the math), pspocket's own and registered under
both, each function's NID computed from its name at registration (recomp::nid_of). No firmware module has it, so it is
written to C99 and Dinkumware's documented choices (the SDK's C library is Dinkumware's), on guest memory checked
before use (D-042). Shared parts from the library work's drafts: libc_guest.hpp (checked guest access, the PPC64
variadic arguments, a per-thread block of 256 bytes for errno, conversion states, strtok's place and static results)
and libc_format.hpp (C99 integer and float parsing, printf and scanf engines for later parts).
Part 1 (runtime/hle/src/sys_libc.cpp):
- string.h: the copies, concatenations, searches, strtok (its place per thread) and strtok_r, strerror (its text in the
  thread's block), strcoll and strxfrm in the "C" locale; comparisons give -1, 0 or +1 (Dinkumware's memcmp.c,
  strcmp.c), POSIX's strcasecmp the difference; Sony's memcpy16, memset_vmx, _memset_int and the _ascii forms.
- ctype.h in the "C" locale: ASCII only, nothing past 127 or for EOF.
- stdlib.h: abs to imaxabs, div to imaxdiv through the caller's buffer in r3 (the 64-bit ABI returns aggregates in
  memory), strtol to strtoumax (long 32 bits, ERANGE clamping, the end pointer), strtod/strtof/strtold and atof/atoff
  (the host's correctly rounded parse in the "C" locale), qsort (a stable merge sort through the guest's comparator,
  one of the orders the standard allows) and bsearch.
- rand and srand as Dinkumware's rand.c (a linear congruential seed, RAND_MAX 0x7FFF). Sony's TT800 functions:
  Matsumoto and Kurita's TT800 with mt19937ar's interface (init by seed or array, int32, int31, three reals), the _
  forms on a state the caller gives, the others on the variable __TT800 (25 words and a position). No reference to
  compare their seeding with: the public mt19937ar initialization, said so here.
Tests: tests/hle/test_libc.cpp (6,769 checks: every behaviour above, a guest comparator for qsort and bsearch).

## D-513 · 2026-10-08 · The C library, part 3: malloc and its family, the mspaces, strdup

Part 3 of D-511 (runtime/hle/src/sys_libc_malloc.cpp) on libc_malloc.hpp (the library work's draft: malloc's heap a
pool of liblv2-style dlmalloc 2.8.3 mspaces, lv2_heap.hpp, D-502), under sys_libc and sys_libm.

  dlmalloc without REALLOC_ZERO_BYTES_FREES; a block that still fits and wastes at most half or 256 bytes stays),
  memalign (a boundary that is not a power of two rounds up, as internal_memalign), Sony's reallocalign(ptr, size,
  boundary), valloc and pvalloc (4 KB pages), malloc_usable_size; requests of MAX_REQUEST (0xFFFFFFC0) or more fail
  first. errno is lv2's CELL_ENOMEM.

  lines to the TTY, malloc_footprint, malloc_trim (the empty mspaces after the first back to lv2), mallopt
  (M_TRIM_THRESHOLD and M_MMAP_THRESHOLD accepted with nothing to act on, M_GRANULARITY a power of two of a page at
  least, the pool's growth step), independent_calloc and independent_comalloc (each element a block of its own).

  growing; mspace_destroy (the bytes given back to lv2), mspace_malloc, calloc, memalign, realloc, reallocalign, free
  (the mspace from the block's footer), malloc_usable_size, malloc_stats, Sony's mspace_is_heap_empty.

  back), their _lv2 forms (the same), _init_malloc_lock and _init_malloc_lock0 (nothing: the lock is a host mutex),
  _allocate_mapped_pages (pages from lv2, MFAIL when none: an assumption, its signature is not known beyond its name).
  The variable _malloc_limit (0: no cap) caps malloc's pool.

Shared: range_ok and a TTY writer (tty_out) moved into libc_guest.hpp.

## D-514 · 2026-10-08 · The C library, part 4: stdio and the POSIX file functions

Part 4 of D-511 (runtime/hle/src/sys_libc_stdio.cpp), under sys_libc and sys_libm, over lv2's file system and TTY.
- A FILE is 128 bytes of guest memory, cleared but for its first word, which holds its own address: the getc/putc
  macros of Dinkumware's headers compare buffer pointers in it and so always call the functions, and code that takes
  the variables _Stdin, _Stdout and _Stderr for FILE pointers rather than FILEs (Dinkumware's newer headers declare
  them as FILEs, `#define stdin (&_Stdin)`) still finds the stream. The rest of a stream lives on the host; data moves
  through a 4 KB staging buffer of the stream's in guest memory (lv2 reads and writes guest memory), large freads and
  fwrites go straight between lv2 and the caller's memory.
- The console: descriptors 0..2 (lv2's own start at 3). stdout to the TTY line buffered, stderr unbuffered; lv2's TTY
  gives no input (sys_tty_read fails), so stdin is at its end at once (read(0) returns 0).
- C99's choices where the library has one: a sticky end-of-file indicator, any number of bytes pushed back, no seek
  needed between reading and writing (the library repositions itself), fgets with n of 1 or less NULL (Dinkumware's
  fgets.c), fpos_t Dinkumware's (64-bit offset, 8-byte state), setvbuf's buffer unused (the mode kept), tmpnam's names
  "/dev_hdd1/tNNNN" (short enough for any L_tmpnam), tmpfile's file removed at fclose, remove choosing rmdir for a
  directory, freopen with no path keeping the file when the new mode asks for no access it lacks.
- printf, scanf and their f, s, sn, v and wide forms on libc_format.hpp's engines; a wide stream's characters are the
  "C" locale's bytes (EILSEQ past 255). swprintf is negative when the text does not fit (C99).
- POSIX: open (lv2's O_* values), close, read, write, lseek (32-bit off_t, EOVERFLOW) and lseek64, stat and fstat
  (lv2's CellFsStat), unlink, mkdir, rmdir, chmod, truncate(64), ftruncate(64), fsync, utime (NULL: now), link
  (lv2's syscall 810 as it answers), fcntl (F_GETFD/SETFD/GETFL/SETFL), getpid, kill (no signals in lv2: ENOSYS),
  opendir/readdir/closedir (a DIR holds the descriptor and a CellFsDirent), _wremove, _wrename, __rename.
- Dinkumware's and Sony's stdio internals with their known signatures: _Fofind, _Fopen (its _M bits), _Foprep,
  _Frprep, _Fwprep and the wide forms, _Fgpos, _Fspos, _Lockfilelock/_Unlockfilelock (the stream's recursive lock),
  _fs_initialize, _fs_finalize, _close_all_FILE, _filep_close_it, _Vacopy; the variable _FILE_P_Head (an empty list).
  Not done: _get_fd and _put_fd (nothing known of them but the names), and the formatter internals that take
  Dinkumware's _Pft/_Sft structures (_Putfld, _Getfld and their kin), whose layouts are not known.
- Fixed on the way: guest_strnlen with a limit of "no limit" (the %s of printf without a precision) overflowed its end
  address and claimed a string of 2^64 bytes.
Tests: tests/hle/test_libc_stdio.cpp (streams on mounted host directories, the TTY, the string forms, POSIX).

## D-515 · 2026-10-08 · The C library, part 5a: time, the "C" locale's tables, Dinkumware's conversions

Part 5a of D-511 (runtime/hle/src/sys_libc_time.cpp), under sys_libc and sys_libm.
- time.h: time_t is 64 bits (the SDK's CellFsStat and CellFsUtimbuf hold it in 64-bit fields) from 1970, lv2's clock.

  the summer offset is not 0. gmtime, localtime, mktime (normalizing, tm_isdst > 0 the summer offset, < 0 lv2's

  conversions in the "C" locale, the host's strftime as the test's reference; %Z empty: no zone names), clock in
  microseconds from its first call (POSIX's CLOCKS_PER_SEC; the SDK's value is not known).
- Plauger's time internals with his semantics: _Daysto (leap days since 1900 and the month's first day), _Ttotm,
  _Isdst (lv2's summer time), _Gettime (a delimited field and its length).
- locale.h: setlocale knows the "C" locale only ("C", "POSIX", ""; NULL asks: "C"), categories 0..6; localeconv's
  struct lconv in Dinkumware's C99 layout (seven monetary strings, fourteen chars at CHAR_MAX, decimal_point "." at
  +44, then grouping, thousands_sep and Dinkumware's five strings, all "").

  C99 class bits, _XB for isblank on tab) with _Getpctype, _Getptolower and _Getptoupper, and newlib's __ctype_ptr
  (257 chars of its bits). Each variable holds the pointer to entry 0, as Plauger's `const short *_Ctype =
  &ctyp_tab[1]`, the table after it.
- Dinkumware's conversion internals: _Stoul, _Stoull, _Stoll and the x forms (_Stolx ... _Stoullx, a range error in
  *perr), the wide _WStoll, _WStoul, _WStoull; _Stod, _Stof, _Stold (scaled by 10^pten with one rounding: the decimal
  exponent moved before converting) and their x and wide forms; _Strcollx, _Strxfrmx, _Wcscollx, _Wcsxfrmx,
  _CStrxfrm, _CWcsxfrm (the "C" locale's code order whatever table they get); _Strerror.

## D-516 · 2026-10-08 · The C library, part 5b: exit and atexit, assertions, locks, SPU printf, _Printf and _Scanf

Part 5b of D-511 (runtime/hle/src/sys_libc_process.cpp), under sys_libc and sys_libm.
- exit runs the functions atexit, __cxa_atexit (with its argument) and Dinkumware's _Atexit registered, last first
  (one registered meanwhile runs too; Sony's __call_functions_registered_with_atexit runs them alone), flushes stdio and
  ends the process through liblv2's sys_process_exit (its own exit list, then lv2). _Exit and abort end it at once
  (abort with EXIT_FAILURE, its call site logged); exitspawn and _Exitspawn are exit's and _Exit's way into
  sys_game_process_exitspawn. environ is an empty list.
- _Assert prints Dinkumware's "<message> -- assertion failed" on stderr and ends the program; _Nonfatal_Assert prints
  it and returns; Sony's _SCE_Assert prints the strings among its first four arguments and ends the program.
- The library's locks: Dinkumware's _Mtxinit/_Mtxdst/_Mtxlock/_Mtxunlock as host recursive mutexes keyed by the guest
  object's address (nothing written into it, whatever its size), _Locksyslock/_Unlocksyslock (eight numbered locks),
  _Initlocks and _Clearlocks (nothing to set up), _Once on Dinkumware's flag word (0, 1 while running, 2 done). The
  variables _Mutex_attr and tls_mutex_attr: sys_mutex_attribute_t for a recursive priority-ordered mutex.
- SPU printf with the SDK's protocol (Newcastle University's PS3 SPU tutorial shows the official server: SPU port 1, a
  user event whose data3 is the arguments' LS address, spu_thread_printf(spu, data3), the result back through
  sys_spu_thread_write_spu_mb): spu_printf_initialize(prio, handler) makes the queue (127, FIFO) and an lv2 thread
  running the library's server (an internal function), and registers the attach and detach callbacks with liblv2's
  _sys_spu_printf_initialize (internal descriptors); attach_group connects port 1 of every thread
  (connect_event_all_threads with only port 1 allowed), attach_thread connects it; finalize destroys the queue, which
  ends the server, and joins it. A handler, when given, gets each text instead of the TTY.
- spu_thread_printf/sprintf/snprintf and raw_spu_printf, spu_raw_sprintf/snprintf: the arguments are quadwords in the
  SPU's local store, the format's LS address in the first one's preferred word, then one argument per quadword (word 0
  for 32 bits, doubleword 0 for 64-bit integers and doubles), as the SPU ABI keeps variadic arguments: an assumption
  of the layout, the SDK's spu_printf not being available to read. An SPU thread's store is read through
  sys_spu_thread_read_ls, a raw SPU's at 0xE0000000 + 0x100000 * id. %n is not written into an SPU's memory. The
  printf engine gained FormatSource::next_int(bits) for such sources, where a 32-bit value is not in a 64-bit slot's
  low word.
- _Printf, _WPrintf, _Scanf and _WScanf: the engines with the caller's pfn (output pieces of up to 512 characters,
  each call returning the next arg, NULL stopping it; input as pfn(arg, 0, 1) to get and pfn(arg, c, 0) to push back).
- Not done (signatures not known): the TLS functions (TlsGetValue, TlsSetValue, _Tlsalloc, _Tlsfree, _Tlsget, _Tlsset,
  _Destroytls), _Once_ctor/_Once_dtor, _Atrealloc, setjmp and longjmp (an engine question: lifted code's native frames
  would have to unwind), the raw_spu_/spu_thread_ read and write families and the __*_printf/putfld/puttxt internals.
Tests: tests/hle/test_libc_process.cpp (exit's order, assertions, locks, _Once, _Printf/_Scanf through guest code, an
SPU program's spu_printf through the server and spu_thread_snprintf on its store).

## D-517 · 2026-10-08 · cellL10n, libl10n's character-set conversions, the same as Sony's

cellL10n made pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/cellL10n.cpp), each function read from the firmware's libl10n and
compared with it on the same inputs (tests/hle/test_l10n.cpp, PSPOCKET_TEST_DEV_FLASH): answers, every byte written and
the lengths reported, over every value where a sweep is possible (all 16-bit codes, every one- and two-byte sequence,
every 8F sequence) and random strings with every source length and short destinations. Its conventions are libl10n's:
a character function answers the units it read or wrote (0: cannot convert); a string function answers 0, 1 (an
illegal or unconvertible character: *src_len the units left from it) or 2 (the destination full), *dst_len the units
written before; the multibyte decoders and UTF8stoUCS2s refuse a character read past *src_len, the others read on.
Guest pointers are checked (D-042): libl10n would fault where pspocket refuses and logs.
- The tables (runtime/hle/src/l10n_tables.hpp) come from public mapping data only, scripts/l10n/ (Python's codecs:
  cp932, euc_jp, cp949, gbk, gb2312, gb18030, cp950, ISO 8859 and the DOS/Windows code pages; libaribcaption's ARIB
  additional-symbol table, ISC licence); the comparison found the few cells Sony reads otherwise, patched there by
  name (JIS X 0212 A2B7/A2C3 as Microsoft's EUC-JP, KS X 1001 A2E8, GB18030-2000's A8BF, Big5 without ETEN's C6A1-FE,
  three ARIB cells). An IBM extension's EUC-JP code is its character's NEC-selected cell, else its NEC row 13 cell,
  else its JIS X 0208 cell (FA54 is FCFB, FA5B ADDA, as Sony's).
- Part 1: the Unicode family (UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32, UCS-2: 24 functions), the 35 single-byte code pages (8: the code
  numbers 5..23, 28, 29, 38..51), and the Japanese codes' core (42: EUC-JP, Shift-JIS and cp932 to and from UCS-2 and
  UTF-8, EUC-JP and Shift-JIS to each other, and the kuten, JIS, EUC-JP and Shift-JIS number conversions). Over 4.4
  million comparisons, none differing.
- Part 2: Korean (20: EUC-KR and cp949's UHC, KS X 1001 then cp949's extension, UHC's extension cells read without an
  FFFF check as libl10n does) and Chinese (32: EUC-CN, GBK with the euro sign at 80, GB18030 with its own rows, A8-A9,
  D7 and FE cells and CJK Extension A's four-byte cells, Big5). Two million comparisons more, none differing.
- Part 3: the Japanese text tools (18): half- and full-width forms both ways (Sony's full-width backslash is A1C0),
  isEucJpKigou and isSjisKigou, hiragana and katakana, upper and lower case, and the voiced marks: a kana followed by
  a half-width voiced or semi-voiced mark is written as the one full-width kana (ｳﾞ as ヴ), split back the other way.
- Part 4: ISO-2022-JP (8: to and from EUC-JP, Shift-JIS, UCS-2 and UTF-8; ESC ( B, ( J, $ @, $ B and $ ( D, JIS X
  0212 read as libl10n reads it) and HZ (4: RFC 1843, "~\n" a newline; the UCS-2 and UTF-8 forms' differing lengths
  kept).
- Part 5: ARIB STD-B24, the Japanese caption code (4): four graphic sets G0..G3 (kanji, alphanumerics, hiragana,
  katakana), the locking and single shifts, the designations libl10n knows (kanji, JIS kanji plane 1, the additional
  symbols, alphanumerics, hiragana, katakana; the others refused); kanji rows 1..3 ARIB's own (its non-spacing marks as
  combining characters), the additional symbols from the public table; the encoders write alphanumerics after LS1,
  hiragana in GR, katakana after SS3, kanji and symbols after ESC $ B or ESC $ ; as needed. jstrchk and jstrnchk (2):
  which Japanese encodings a string could be in (ASCII 2, JIS 4, EUC-JP 8, Shift-JIS 16, UTF-8 32, unknown 1): 7-bit
  text read as ISO-2022-JP, then from the first 8-bit byte three machines for Shift-JIS, EUC-JP and UTF-8 each ruling
  its encoding out. The converter dispatch (5: L10nConvert, L10nConvertStr, l10n_get_converter, l10n_convert,
  l10n_convert_str): libl10n's 52 x 52 converter table written as its rule (every encoding to and from UCS-2 and UTF-8,
  the Unicode forms among themselves, EUC-JP, Shift-JIS and ISO-2022-JP among themselves, EUC-KR and UHC; nothing for
  UCS-4), the character form's *dst_len per function kind, no character form for ARIB, HZ and ISO-2022-JP (-1).
  Quirks kept: ARIBstoUCS2s checks the room for an additional symbol before counting it (one unit past *dst_len is
  written, a full destination reports one less), ARIBstoUTF8s reports one unit less at an invalid one-byte character,
  and the two report a different *src_len at an unassigned kanji.
- All 165 of libl10n's functions are pspocket's own; the comparison makes about 10.9 million checks (5.4 million calls
  on each side, 2.5 minutes), none differing, and a deliberately wrong converter table fails it.

## D-518 · 2026-10-09 · sys_fs complete: libfs's other 34 functions, and the kernel calls behind them

The 34 sys_fs functions pspocket lacked are its own (runtime/hle/src/sys_fs.cpp), each read in libfs.sprx (4.92) and
compared with it (tests/hle/test_fs_compare.cpp: the same scripts in two fresh processes over the same file tree, one
calling pspocket's functions and one Sony's module; every answer, every byte written and the file tree afterwards the
same, 4,907 checks). RPCS3 implements none of them.
- **libfs's path layer.** libfs asks lv2 (sys_fs_fcntl 0xC0000006) whether a path's file system wants its names
  converted (FAT long names to and from a code page registered with cellFsRegisterConversionCallback) and then sends
  the call as an fcntl with the converted name. lv2 here answers that none does (CELL_ENOTSUP, as RPCS3), so the
  functions take libfs's direct way: the system call with the path as it is. The conversion table itself is kept as
  libfs keeps it (32 slots, a code page's first registration wins, CELL_EAGAIN when full; cellFsUnregisterL10nCallbacks
  removes code pages 437, 850, 866, 932, 948, 950 and 936).
- **What libfs does with each.** Plain system calls: cellFsAccess (816), AclWrite (824), Link (810), SymbolicLink (833),
  Chown (835), Fcntl (817), Truncate2 (847), LsnGetCDASize/GetCDA/Lock/Unlock (825-828). With checks: AclRead copies
  4 bytes from its stack on success; FGetBlockSize2 and GetBlockSize2 check three pointers (GetBlockSize2 copies its
  stack out even after a failure: uninitialised there, zeros here); MappedAllocate rounds to 4 KB pages; LsnRead maps a
  buffer for offset + size, reads the sectors into it and copies size bytes from offset; LsnRead2 reads straight in.
  Fcntl blocks: the by-fd size calls (0x80000006..8 with the size), the by-path ones (0xE0000016 and 0xE0000018, a
  0x28-byte path block like 0xE0000017's), cellFsSdataOpenWithVersion (0xE0000025), the I/O buffer calls (0xC0000008:
  SetDefaultContainer, SetIoBuffer, and SetIoBufferFromDefaultContainer, which before answered CELL_OK for any open
  file), SetDiscReadRetrySetting (0xC000001A: none or 99 retries), ArcadeHddSerialNumber (0xC0000007). cellFsOpen2 is
  cellFsOpen with the mode given (-1 is cellFsOpen's: 0600 when creating). cellFsSetAttribute opens a /dev_hdd0 path
  (or its directory) and sends fcntl 1 with the CellFsStat; elsewhere it is CELL_ENOTSUP. cellFsGetDirent and
  cellFsGetDirentCount are not in libfs: the count 0, CELL_ENOSYS.
- **The kernel side.** lv2's calls behind them were RPCS3's stubs answering CELL_OK; they are pspocket's own now, with
  readings of their own where nothing documents them: sys_fs_link (a hard link on one writable mount; FAT has none),
  sys_fs_access (exists; W_OK needs a writable file system), sys_fs_acl_read/write (a 4-byte word per path, 0 until
  written, kept for the process), sys_fs_symbolic_link (the target a guest path, relative ones from the link's
  directory, stored as the host path so a link never leads out of the mounts), sys_fs_chown (as sys_fs_chmod: checked,
  nothing changes), sys_fs_lsn_get_cda (no areas), sys_fs_lsn_read/write ({lsn, offset, size}: the file's sectors of the
  mount's sector size from lsn, offset + size bytes), sys_fs_mapped_allocate/free (kernel-kept user memory per file,
  freed at close), sys_fs_truncate2 (ftruncate's). fcntl gains 1, 0x80000004 (RPCS3's), 0x80000006..8, 0xC0000006,
  0xC0000007, 0xC0000008 (RPCS3's container accounting: a file's buffer taken from a container and given back at close),
  0xC000001A, 0xE0000016, 0xE0000018 and 0xE0000025. tests/lv2/test_fs.cpp checks each. The kernel's error names now
  cover every CELL_E code.
- sys_fs is 100% pspocket's own (82 of 82); 12 more kernel calls are pspocket's own.

## D-519 · 2026-10-09 · cellGcmSys complete, compared with libgcm_sys running on pspocket's lv2

The 33 cellGcmSys functions pspocket lacked are its own (runtime/hle/src/cellGcmSys.cpp, the D-519 section), each read
in libgcm_sys.sprx (4.92); RPCS3 leaves them as stubs. The comparison (tests/hle/test_gcm_compare.cpp) runs Sony's
module for real: lv2's RSX calls 668, 670 and 672 to 675 are now bound to their numbers (they were called only by
pspocket's own cellGcmSys), so libgcm_sys's _cellGcmInitBody initialises on pspocket's kernel, and every script runs in
two fresh processes, one initialised by each side. Answers, the bytes written, lv2's driver information (heads and the
event mask) and every RSX call into lv2 with its arguments (a new test hook, Kernel::set_syscall_observer) are the same,
over seven scenarios: the getters, flip status, flip mode, vblank frequencies and handlers, the hardware cursor, tiles,
sorting the IO mappings, immediate flips, flip command 2 and the flip ring.
- **What libgcm_sys keeps.** A context record (memory handle, local memory, context ID, DMA control, driver
  information, reports), head 1 as the head it drives, the handlers with their bits in the driver information's event
  mask (vblank 1/2, flip 8/0x10, queue 0x20/0x40, user 0x80, second vblank 0x400/0x800), the ring of 8 buffers
  cellGcmSetPrepareFlip queued (cellGcmGetDisplayBufferByFlipIndex, cellGcmSetFlipImmediate), the tile word each
  cellGcmSetTile sent (cellGcmSetInvalidateTile sends it without its location bits), the cursor state.
- **The new functions.** _cellGcmFunc1 (GPU version), 2 (0), 3 (a table of 16 magic numbers), 4 (package 0x106), 13
  (the notify area), 38 (driver information + 0x12F0); the head-0 ("2") variants of flip status, flip mode, vblank
  count, last flip time, flip handler, flip immediate and flip command; cellGcmGetCurrentField, GetLastSecondVTime,
  SysGetLastVBlankTime (lv2's words as they are), SetVBlankFrequency (0x108 then VSYNC), SetSecondVHandler (called
  with the vblank once cellGcmSetSecondVFrequency enabled it), SetInvalidateTile, DumpGraphicsError (CELL_OK),
  SortRemapEaIoAddress (unmap all past IO MB 0, pack the offset table's entries into the holes, map again), the cursor
  (InitCursor, Enable, Disable, Position, ImageOffset, Update: libgcm_sys's dirty flags and lv2 packages 0x10B/0x10C/
  0x10D). The three GPAD functions are in no retail module (Sony's GPU capture tool): no capture, CELL_OK.
- **Existing functions made libgcm_sys's.** _cellGcmInitBody now sets the FIFO at 0x1000 (package 0x001), both heads'
  flip status done and the head-1 vblank bit, as libgcm_sys; cellGcmSetFlipStatus leaves only the flip-done bit
  (libgcm_sys's 0x10a with a4 0); cellGcmSetFlipMode goes through sys_rsx_attribute 2 and 0x101 as libgcm_sys (VSYNC is
  lv2's 2 unless the display reports 59.94 Hz); cellGcmSetSecondVFrequency sends 0x108; cellGcmSetFlipImmediate flips
  the ring's buffer through lv2's 0x102 (before, nothing); the handler setters set their event bits; the RSX calls go
  through lv2's syscall table.
- **The kernel side.** sys_rsx packages 0x102 (display flip: the RSX thread runs it as a GCM_FLIP_HEAD,
  Rsx::request_flip, even while its FIFO waits), 0x103 (display queue), 0x108 (vblank frequencies), 0x10B/0x10C (the
  cursor, kept for an overlay). Flip and vblank times in the driver information are timebase ticks, as lv2's (they were
  nanoseconds); cellGcmGetLastFlipTime converts them as libgcm_sys does (the same microseconds as before). 0xFED also
  keeps the second vblank's time.
- **Left as they were (deviations kept).** pspocket's cellGcmSetFlip and SetPrepareFlip still write RPCS3's
  GCM_FLIP_COMMAND (queue and flip at once) and return the buffer id, where libgcm_sys writes GCM_DRIVER_QUEUE, flips
  from its interrupt handler and returns the ring slot; changing the flip path is engine work of its own (GTA V and
  Assassin's Creed run on it). A full flip ring drops its oldest slot instead of failing. Head 0 never flips here.
- GTA V's prologue gate passes unchanged (29.8 fps median, no new messages). cellGcmSys is 100% pspocket's own; 6
  more kernel calls are bound.

## D-520 · 2026-10-09 · liblv2's internal variables under RPCS3's names, holding pspocket's state

RPCS3 registers eight hidden variables in sysPrxForUser (sys_ppu_thread_.cpp, sysPrxForUser.cpp, sys_mmapper_.cpp)
for liblv2's own data, and the chart counts them. They are now pspocket's host variables (guest memory laid out by the
HLE process), and the state lives in them: g_ppu_atexit (the eight thread atexit functions) under the recursive
"atexit!" lwmutex g_ppu_atexit_lwm (an lv2 mutex before), g_ppu_once_mutex ("_lv2ppu", sys_ppu_thread_once),
g_ppu_exit_mutex (liblv2's "exitprc", sys_process_exit), g_ppu_prx_lwm ("_lv2prx", which RPCS3 makes and nothing
locks), g_ppu_atexitspawn and g_ppu_at_Exitspawn (the exitspawn handlers), s_shared_memory_area (0: nothing here asks
for the shared memory area). As RPCS3, sys_initialize_tls makes the four objects; a call before it (tests) makes them
at first use. sys_raw_spu_load and sys_raw_spu_image_load wait for lv2's raw SPUs (kernel work).

## D-521 · 2026-10-09 · sys_lv2dbg as a retail system's liblv2dbg

A retail system's debugger library is liblv2dbg_for_cex.sprx, which denies everything: all 35 functions answer
CELL_LV2DBG_ERROR_DEOPERATIONDENIED (0x8001042C), and sys_dbg_vm_get_page_information first clears the page
information entries it was given. pspocket's sys_lv2dbg is that (runtime/hle/src/sys_lv2dbg.cpp), compared with the
module call for call (tests/hle/test_lv2dbg.cpp). RPCS3 answers CELL_OK with a todo for each (a debug kernel's answer).

## D-522 · 2026-10-09 · USB as a console with no device: lv2's sys_usbd, libusbd and libusbpspcm pspocket's own

pspocket runs where no USB device reaches the game (an iPhone), so the model is a PS3 with nothing plugged in, built
from the bottom and compared with Sony's modules on it.

- **lv2 (runtime/lv2/src/usbd.cpp, tests/lv2/test_usbd.cpp).** Every named sys_usbd call is bound (530..551, 556, 558,
  559). sys_usbd_initialize gives RPCS3's handle; the device list is empty, and every call that names a device or a
  pipe (descriptors, pipes, transfers and their status, location, speed, attach, send_event, which libusbd's
  cellUsbdResetDevice calls) is CELL_EINVAL, as RPCS3 answers an unknown one. Drivers are kept by product name (a
  second registration CELL_EEXIST, unregistering an unknown one CELL_ESRCH; the names RPCS3 knows get their device
  IDs). sys_usbd_receive_event waits for the library's own events (sys_usbd_event_port_send) and finalisation wakes it
  with RPCS3's termination (4, 0, 0). Memory for transfers (sys_usbd_allocate_memory, RPCS3 todo) is user memory in
  64 KB pages the kernel keeps until sys_usbd_free_memory or finalisation. The unnamed calls libusbd also makes (552,
  563 for composite drivers, 565 memory from a container, 567..569 shared memory) stay RPCS3's CELL_OK with nothing
  written: the name table has no entry to bind them to.
- **cellUsbd (runtime/hle/src/usbd.cpp), 29 functions, as libusbd.sprx.** cellUsbdInit makes libusbd's event queue
  "_ubdorg" with a local port and its two threads (libusbd_callback_thread in sys_usbd_receive_event forwarding device
  events, libusbd_usbd_thread on the queue; priority 500, 4 KB stacks), lists the devices (none) and is the only call
  before which the others are not CELL_USBD_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED; cellUsbdEnd sends both threads event 4, joins them,
  destroys the objects and finalises. Thread priorities (type 0 kept for drivers, 1 and 2 the threads', lv2's errors
  as they are; SetThreadPriority2 needs ldd < usbd < callback and puts the usbd thread's back when the callback
  thread's fails). Drivers: the four CellUsbdLddOps pointers set, a name registered compared as the strings read now,
  unregistering by the four pointers as they are now (plain and extra by cellUsbdUnregisterLdd and
  cellUsbdUnregisterExtraLdd, which is the same function, composite by cellUsbdUnregisterCompositeLdd, which calls
  536). Devices and pipes are never found (DEVICE_NOT_FOUND, PIPE_NOT_FOUND, a null pointer for GetPrivateData and
  ScanStaticDescriptor) after libusbd's own argument checks. Memory: lv2's errors raw for AllocateMemory and
  AllocateSharedMemory, FATAL for FromContainer and FreeMemory, a null address FATAL.
- **cellUsbPspcm, 27 functions, as libusbpspcm.sprx.** CalcPoolSize is 8268·devices·connections + 128·devices +
  144·connections (32-bit); Init checks the parameters (size 32, 1..16 devices, connections > 0, a name of at most 63
  characters, the pool's size), starts the library's thread "cellUsbPspcm_Library" (the parameters' priority and stack
  plus 4 KB; lv2's error as it is) and registers its driver "cellUsbPspcm" with cellUsbd (its error as it is, so
  CELL_USBD_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED before cellUsbdInit); the pool's address is the initialised flag, as libusbpspcm's.
  With no PSP no device slot binds (CLOSED), no connection opens (CLOSED for transfers, resets and data waits,
  ALREADY for a close) and nothing is pending (INVALID for the polls, waits and cancels). The pool is the library's
  own memory: pspocket keeps its state on the host and leaves the pool alone.
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_usb_compare.cpp: scripts of every function with good and bad arguments in two fresh
  processes, Sony's modules (libusbpspcm on libusbd) and pspocket's: the answers, the bytes written outside the pool,
  and the lv2 calls the script's thread makes (the libraries' own `sc`: sys_usbd with its arguments and drivers'
  names, threads, events) all the same. Two things are not compared because libusbd answers from leftovers: an
  AllocateMemoryFromContainer past its checks (565 writes nothing, so libusbd reads its stack) and
  cellUsbdUnregisterLdd of a composite driver (it compares an entry's bytes its allocator reused).
- **Left out.** libusbd's seven exports with no known name (a Bluetooth helper among them) and its answer for ten titles
  that takes lv2 refusing a product registration as CELL_OK (pspocket's lv2 never refuses one libusbd lets through).
  A device arriving, a transfer completing or the driver being probed stops a dev build (rule 5): with a device model
  (an emulated portal or guitar, a PSP over the network) the attach and transfer paths are to be written and compared
  with libusbd on it.

## D-523 · 2026-10-09 · lv2's network calls in the kernel, libnet's own layer over them (sys_net, part 1)

sys_net was one HLE file that answered the sockets itself (RPCS3's lv2 behaviour, no lv2 call) and returned -1 with
errno in the thread's TLS (RPCS3's convention). It is now two layers, as on a PS3:

- **lv2 (runtime/lv2/src/net.cpp).** All 27 network calls are bound (700..726): the offline socket model that was in
  the HLE (sockets numbered from 24 as RPCS3's IDs, the loopback interface the only one, loopback UDP and TCP between
  the game's own sockets, connect/sendto elsewhere EADDRNOTAVAIL, blocking calls waiting for loopback data, a close,
  sys_net_abort or their timeout, select/poll, the socket information) with getsockopt, getpeername, recvmsg, sendmsg,
  poll, sys_net_abort (a socket's waiters EINTR, "all" closes every socket) and infoctl (6/11 the socket lists, 9/52
  the resolver configuration, empty with no link, 53 a thread's sync object) added; sysctl answers the routing
  socket's tables as empty (no interface, no route); the dumps, sys_net_control and eurus answer as RPCS3's stubs;
  ioctl keeps the test parameters. Each call answers a value or -SYS_NET_E*. A blocked call shows as a network wait.
- **libnet (runtime/hle/src/sys_net.cpp), Sony's libnet.sprx's logic.** sys_net_initialize_network_ex takes the
  game's memory pool (memory set, at least 8 KB, flags 0 or 1; a second call CELL_OK, or EBUSY with flag 1) and
  libnet's allocator runs over it exactly (first fit, 20-byte headers {next, prev, tag, line, size}, free and used
  lists in address order, neighbours merged; the lists survive a finalisation): __sys_net_lib_malloc, _free, _calloc,
  _realloc. Each thread gets a 3192-byte context in the pool at its first call (errno at +2928, h_errno at +2900, its
  sync object: an lv2 mutex and condition "_netsyc", told to lv2 with infoctl 53), freed at the thread's exit (an
  atexit function registered with sysPrxForUser) or by sys_net_free_thread_context (its flags as libnet's).
  Before initialisation (and when a context can't be made) the calls use libnet's static context, marked aborted with
  EBUSY (ENOMEM): SYS_NET_ERROR_EBUSY without reaching lv2. Every lv2 call goes through the context: a failure
  keeps the errno there and answers SYS_NET_ERROR_* (0x80010200 | errno), not -1, as libnet does. libnet's random
  generator (521-word lagged XOR, seeded from the clock), its sync objects (_sys_net_lib_sync_*), threads, usleep,
  system time, the socket list (TCP states mapped to SYS_NET_STATE_* in a list), the libnetctl queue calls, the
  resolver configuration (sys_net_set_resolver_configurations), the address conversions (libnet's own: inet_aton is
  BIND's with 32-bit parts, inet_pton for IPv4 is inet_aton in strict mode, so "0x" is 0 and white space ends an
  address; inet_pton6 is BIND 8's; inet_ntoa writes into the context), getifaddrs, sys_net_get_if_list and
  sys_net_show_ifconfig (which GTA V calls at start: "No interface found.", lv2's and libnet's memory, the packets and
  the thread contexts on the TTY).
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_net_compare.cpp with Sony's libnet running on pspocket's lv2: set-up, the pool and
  thread contexts (the pool's bytes block by block), the text conversions over 65 strings and 10 addresses, sockets
  and helpers, the interface report (its TTY text too); answers, memory, pool and lv2 calls the same, masking only
  what differs by construction (each module's own file-name pointers in block headers, lv2 IDs, the clock-seeded
  generator). The old HLE tests (tests/hle/test_net.cpp) now run on this kernel and libnet's conventions;
  tests/lv2 keeps sys_raw_spu_create as the unimplemented example (700 is bound now).
- **Not yet libnet's own (part 2).** gethostbyname is interim: it gives libnet's answers (a hostent in the context for
  an address or for libnet's /etc/hosts "127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.", HOST_NOT_FOUND, TRY_AGAIN otherwise) but not
  libnet's resolver work behind them (its hosts-file reads, res_init over lv2's resolv.conf, the DNS attempt, which
  offline opens a socket of family 0 and fails, and their pool allocations); its comparison waits, hidden. Still
  missing: gethostbyaddr, if_nametoindex, sys_net_if_ctl, the name-server, routing, netset, test-parameter, dump,
  ioctl/control wrappers and show_nameserver/show_route.

## D-527 · 2026-10-09 · Kernel calls as a retail console running a game: devices, system manager, services (part 1)

The kernel-calls chart counts 634 named lv2 calls; 339 were not pspocket's own (95 missing, 244 answered as RPCS3's
null or stub slots answer them, D-166/D-184). This decision makes them pspocket's own group by group, each from
RPCS3's lv2 code where it has one (cited in each file) and its syscall table's permission column (lv2.cpp: ROOT,
DBG, PM): those calls belong to system processes, so a game (Config::root false) gets CELL_ENOSYS, as pspocket's
sys_ss already answers its root-only packages and RPCS3's sys_sm_shutdown answers a game; a root process gets RPCS3's
answers. Which retail modules issue which calls was checked with scripts/firmware-syscalls.py: liblv2coredump (the
retail crash-dump library) uses the sys_dbg, crypto-engine and PRX-query calls, so those get real behaviour over the
process's own state in a later part, not a refusal.

Part 1 (runtime/lv2/src/devices.cpp, services.cpp; 78 calls):
- sys_gpio: no LEDs or DIP switches on a retail console: both read 0, the LEDs take a set, the switches refuse it.
- sys_io buffers: IDs from 0x44000000; each allocation is block_count * block_size bytes of user memory lv2 keeps in
  64 KB pages, freed with its buffer; freeing another address frees nothing (RPCS3's vm::dealloc fails quietly).
- sys_sm (377-397, 408, 409): all ROOT, DBG or PM. For a root process: no event (CELL_EAGAIN, outputs 0), RPCS3's
  parameters (0, 0, 0x200, 7), shutdown and reboot end the process (pspocket cannot start the system software
  again), the LPAR operations ENOTSUP; the services RPCS3 leaves as null_func answer CELL_OK with nothing written.
- sys_dbg_read/write_process_memory (904, 905): the process's own memory (pid 1); a write into the executable's area
  is logged, as code translated ahead of time does not change with it (RPCS3 recompiles the function there).
- HID manager (500-514): handles from 0x100; the ioctl's DualShock 3 descriptor and IDs RPCS3 recorded on real
  hardware; the focus is the game's. lv2 keeps no input state (pspocket's libio is native), so a root process reading
  it gets nothing.
- sys_config (516-525): the service registry, events to the handle's event queue as (1, handle, registered << 32 |
  event ID, size); the pad manager (0x11, 0x12) registered with one controller at the first open; a listener of 0x11
  hears of it only when its data starts with 1; ONCE listeners one event; no I/O error events.
- Raw storage (600-623): opening a device and the device queries are root-only; for root, RPCS3's 17 devices and
  their sizes, reads of zeros (no device contents), writes taken, asynchronous commands answered at once on the
  configured queue; the emulated speed is a debug kernel's (ENOSYS).
Tests: tests/lv2/test_devices.cpp, test_services.cpp (both permission sides, every answer above).

Part 2 (runtime/lv2/src/misc.cpp, rsx.cpp; 110 calls). RPCS3 answers these with todos or null slots; pspocket's
answers follow its console, and one correction to part 1's rule: a call RPCS3 marks ROOT that Sony's game-loadable
modules make (libatxenc's SPU group switching, 244-247) must work for a game, lv2 letting those modules run in it.
- Debug and test kernels' facilities: the lv1 trace (60-69, 77), the performance monitor and PC trace (960-967),
  DECI3 (880-899), the Blu-ray disc emulator (699), the RSX trace (968), and the USB/Bluetooth audio calls RPCS3 marks
  deprecated (640-647): CELL_ENOSYS, as RPCS3 answers the trace calls.
- The system software's: the Bluetooth module (583-597), its settings (635), the NP DRM key cache (470, 471), sys_ss's
  sunset flag, protected file database, virtual TRM and factory data (860-862, 869), the process calls RPCS3 marks
  ROOT or DBG (2, 4, 5, 21, 23, 27, 28), the RTC (119) and sys_console_write (398): CELL_ENOSYS for a game; for root
  no children (ESRCH), no spawning (ENOTSUP), the object count as sys_process_get_number_of_object, the RTC as the
  wall clock's seconds, the console text logged, CELL_OK otherwise.
- One process: sys_process_kill finds no child (ESRCH).
- Calls Sony's game-loadable modules make: CELL_OK with nothing to do here (group switching and start-on-exit, the
  shared-memory flag, attribute and access rights, the budget, the security framework, disc access control, media ID
  and ad signature, the file-system watch, the YCON gamepad interface and the LDD pads, which pspocket's libio serves).
  sys_bluetooth's 579 keeps RPCS3's checks. sys_console_write2 logs its text; sys_fs_sync has nothing to flush.
- sys_rsx: the device open and close, the attribute and the unmap answer CELL_OK; sys_rsx_context_free stops the RSX
  thread and forgets the context, after which a new one can be allocated; sys_rsx_memory_free gives the local memory
  back (with the context still allocated it is refused, CELL_EBUSY, where RPCS3 aborts).
Tests: tests/lv2/test_misc_calls.cpp (every call above on both sides), tests/hle/test_gcm.cpp (context and memory
freed, then allocated again with a new RSX thread); Sony's libgcm_sys still compares the same (test_gcm_compare).
Kernel calls own: 483 of 634.

Part 3 (runtime/lv2/src/prx.cpp, misc.cpp; 40 calls):
- The PRX calls (460-499) reach pspocket's module loader through lv2::ModuleHost, which HleProcess::set_module_loader
  gives the kernel (the same loader, lock and steps as liblv2's native sys_prx_* functions; firmware modules loaded
  for a module start in its start command, D-175). RPCS3's contract: _sys_prx_start_module's command 1 links the
  module and gives module_start (~0 none; no prologue), command 2 takes its result (0 resident; another value in its
  low word unloads it and is returned); _sys_prx_stop_module likewise (command 2: 0 stops, 1 CAN_NOT_STOP; 4 gives the
  entries, 8 is taken); loads by path, by descriptor (the file's path, `offset` in), on a memory container (none for
  modules) and by list (64-bit path pointers; a failure unloads the ones loaded and fills the list with -1); the list
  (only with flags bit 1, size 0x20) and the info (an option block of size 0x10 holding the info of size 0x48 or
  0x58); _sys_prx_register_module refuses a game the system software's stub registration
  (CELL_PRX_ERROR_ELF_IS_REGISTERED, not an error); the library todos answer CELL_OK; the debugger's lists are root's;
  without a loader the calls answer CELL_PRX_ERROR_NO_LIBLV2.
- Overlays (450-458): a process whose executable's ppc_seg is 0 (every game pspocket has seen) gets CELL_ENOSYS, as
  RPCS3; an overlay-enabled one would need its overlay placed at a fixed address in the 0x30000000 segment, which the
  loader does not do: logged, CELL_ENOEXEC. No overlay is ever loaded, so their queries find none (CELL_OK).
  lv2::Config::ppc_seg comes from the executable's sys_process_param.
- sys_ss_update_manager (863) and the AV manager's UART (367-370): root's (RPCS3 checks too); for root, RPCS3's update
  manager (the installed version as 0x492 << 40 for 4.92, its preset EEPROM cells, buffers of user memory, 3.40 as the
  applicable version) and a UART with no AV manager behind it (sends taken, nothing received).
Tests: tests/hle/test_lle.cpp (a module through the raw PRX calls: both start commands, list, info, lookups, stop,
unload, registration, overlays), tests/lv2/test_misc_calls.cpp. Kernel calls own: 523 of 634.

Part 4 (runtime/lv2/src/rsxaudio.cpp; 10 calls): sys_rsxaudio, the RSX's audio DMA as lv2 gives it to the system's
audio service, as RPCS3 has it: one context at a time (IDs from 0x60000000) with its 128 KB shared page (DMA regions
for the serial and two S/PDIF ports, a silence block, the control area: three ring buffers of 16 entries, the
client's three event queue IDs); create_connection takes the queues (all three must exist) and points the entries at
lv1's IO addresses (0x30000000 for the page); prepare makes the context the hardware's (-1 when another is); start
clears the active ring buffers, turns their DMA on and tells each queue (port name, port, 0, 0); stop turns it off;
get_dma_param gives the IO base (0) or ID (1). The hardware is a host thread that, once per block period (128 frames:
2.67 ms serial at 48 kHz, 2.90 ms S/PDIF at 44.1 kHz), stamps the entry playing and with DMA on retires a valid one,
telling the port's queue (port name, port, block index, timestamp) at each notify step by RPCS3's rule. pspocket's
console has no AV manager to enable an output (part 3's UART), so the samples are not played, as RPCS3 mutes a port
lv1 left disabled; the page has no protection to lock and unlock. Test: tests/lv2/test_rsxaudio.cpp (the context, the
queues, the DMA addresses, the start event and two notifications for three entries retired on schedule, stop,
finalize and a new context).

## D-528: Raw and isolated SPUs, interrupt threads, guest MMIO through faults (2026-10-09)

The last kernel calls without an answer: raw SPUs (150-154, 160, 161, 163, 196, 197, 199), isolated SPUs (230-240)
and interrupt threads (80, 81, 84, 88, 89). RPCS3 references: lv2/sys_spu.cpp, RawSPUThread.cpp, lv2/sys_interrupt.cpp,
SPUThread.h.

- Guest MMIO (runtime/core/mmio.hpp): guest code reaches guest memory directly, so a raw SPU's problem-state registers
  (0x40000 above its local store, 0xE0000000 + 0x100000 * index) are left without host pages; the platform's
  SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler (pspocket-boot, the iOS app) calls mmio_handle_fault, which decodes the faulting AArch64 load
  or store (LDR/STR in their unsigned, unscaled, pre/post-indexed and register-offset forms, sign-extending loads,
  LDP/STP/LDPSW, SIMD and FP registers of 8 to 128 bits, PRFM skipped), performs it on the range's device with the
  guest's big-endian values and resumes after the instruction. Apple AArch64 only (iOS, Apple-silicon macOS); elsewhere
  sys_raw_spu_create answers CELL_EAGAIN, as when the share is used up. Exclusive and atomic accesses stay faults.
- A raw SPU (raw_spu.cpp) is an SPUContext on its own host thread with its local store in committed guest memory (the
  PPU reads and writes it directly) and the plain one-entry interrupt mailbox (new hooks member plain_intr_mbox; each
  write raises class 2's mailbox bit through intr_mbox_written). SPU_RunCntl 1 runs from SPU_NPC (bit 0: interrupts
  on) and reads as running at once (RPCS3 try_start); 0 stops it and returns once it has. Every stop code stops it
  (stop-and-signal interrupt), as does a halt (halt interrupt); an exception logs and raises class 0's error bit. The
  MFC proxy runs a GET, PUT, SNDSIG or SDCRZ when the command status is read after its five writes (else
  MFC_PPU_DMA_CMD_SEQUENCE_ERROR), the S forms starting the SPU (ps_spu_proxy_dma); the mailbox status, the signal
  registers and the queue status are RPCS3's.
- Interrupt threads: a tag per raw SPU and class (0 or 2; IDs 0x0A000000), a service per establish (0x0B000000) whose
  host thread waits until class 2's status (with the mailbox bit set while the interrupt mailbox holds a value, as
  RPCS3's loop sets it) meets its mask, then runs the thread's entry with (arg1, arg2) from the top of its stack until
  sys_interrupt_thread_eoi; disestablish ends it and gives back its r13 (also for a thread never established, as
  RPCS3). Any thread not yet started may be established (RPCS3); it is then an interrupt thread.
- Isolated SPUs: the module image (a SELF through the process's decrypter, then an SPU ELF; else CELL_EAUTHFAIL) in a
  raw SPU's local store, r3..r6 the arguments in the preferred doublewords, the status marked isolated, started by
  sys_isolated_spu_start. RPCS3's table marks these root's but lets a game use them; so does pspocket.
- Process exit stops the raw SPUs and ends the interrupt threads (abort_all_waits); destroy ends a raw SPU's services,
  removes its tags, stops its host thread, unmaps its registers and decommits its local store.
Every named syscall slot now has a binding (test_dispatch checks it). Tests: tests/core/test_mmio.cpp (each decoded
form against a recording device with a real fault handler), tests/lv2/test_raw_spu.cpp (a synthetic SPU program
through the registers: mailboxes, status and NPC after a stop, interrupt status, a mailbox interrupt served by an
interrupt thread, a stop request on a spinning SPU, the MFC proxy both ways and its sequence error, destroy and a new
one; the errors). Kernel calls: 560 own, 74 answered as RPCS3's null or stub, of 634.

## D-529: sysPrxForUser's raw SPU loaders; sys_spu_segment's address at +0x10 (2026-10-09)

- sys_raw_spu_load and sys_raw_spu_image_load are pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/sys_spu_.cpp), read from liblv2: the
  local store is filled through the raw SPU's MFC proxy registers as liblv2 fills it (each COPY segment as GETs of up to
  16 KB on tag 0, its five registers written again until the command status takes it; each FILL segment a word at a
  time straight into the local store; other types skipped; then the tag query for tag 0, polled until it completes),
  the registers being guest MMIO answered by lv2's raw SPU (D-528). sys_raw_spu_load reads the file whole into
  liblv2's heap through sys_fs (open, fstat, read, close; a short read is CELL_ENOENT), gives the entry through
  sys_spu_elf_get_information and deploys sys_spu_elf_get_segments' table; sys_raw_spu_image_load takes a user
  image's table as it is or a kernel image's through lv2 (155, 159), then writes SPU_NPC (CELL_EINVAL for another
  image type). One deviation: a raw SPU that does not exist is CELL_ESRCH with an error logged (liblv2 would fault on
  its local store).
- Bug fixed: sys_spu_segment keeps its address or fill value as the first word of a doubleword-aligned union at +0x10
  (RPCS3 sys_spu.h; liblv2's loaders and libsre's cellOvis read it there); lv2 (spu.cpp) and sysPrxForUser's
  sys_spu_elf_get_segments wrote and read it at +0xC. The two agreed with each other, so the images pspocket made
  loaded, but a segment table a game wrote itself (a user image's own FILL for its bss, say) was loaded from the wrong
  addresses, and a table lv2 gave out was wrong for anything else that read it.
- A raw SPU's MFC proxy command whose EA is not guest memory is taken and copies nothing, with an error logged (the
  MFC would fault on it later; copying from there would fault inside the fault handler, which hangs).
Tests: tests/hle/test_lv2_compare.cpp "raw SPU loaders" (both functions against liblv2 on the same raw SPU: a program
file over two GETs with bss, a missing file, a file that is not an SPU program, a user image with every segment type
in the SDK's layout, an unknown image type, a kernel image: answers, the whole local store, NPC and the entry the
same); tests/hle/test_spu_threads.cpp (lv2's table layout, and a user image whose table the test wrote run in an SPU
thread group).

## D-524 · 2026-10-09 · cellHttp pspocket's own: libhttp's objects, laid out where libhttp lays them

cellHttp had six functions after RPCS3's (the set-up's and the cookie store's checks; online play was a non-goal,
D-024). It is now libhttp.sprx's logic, read from its code and compared with the module running on pspocket's lv2:
all 123 named functions and 46 of its 58 unnamed exports
(runtime/hle/src/cellHttp*.cpp, one file per part: set-up, clients, connections, transactions, cookies,
authentication cache, caches, HTTPS).

- **Laid out as libhttp's.** libhttp keeps every object in liblv2 heaps made over the game's pools (cellHttpInit's;
  cellHttpInitCookie's, a heap of its own) and its globals in its data. pspocket makes the same heap blocks, of the
  same sizes, in the same order, with the fields at libhttp's offsets (cellHttp.hpp: the client 224 bytes, its
  connection manager 168, a transaction 488, a connection 152 with its socket at +40, host records 64, header nodes
  20, cookies 64 and domain records 36, authentication entries 644, redirection records 96), so the IDs a game holds
  are the blocks' addresses and the pools' bytes are libhttp's; the globals are a block of pspocket's. Every ID is
  checked as libhttp checks it: sys_memory_get_page_attribute (351) on the address, then the object's pointer to
  itself. Locks are liblv2 lightweight mutexes with libhttp's names (_httsys, _httcln, _httcla, _httcmg, _htttrn,
  _htttna, _httrec, _httauc, _httcok, _httssl, _httvfy, _httcac, _httxca); a host record has an lv2 mutex and condition
  "_httsyn". libhttp's MD5 files cookies, redirection records and cache entries; the SDK version (syscalls 1, 25)
  picks limits and the default SSL version. Other libraries are called through the registry, as libhttp imports them
  (cellHttpUtil, sysPrxForUser, sys_net, cellRtc); the transaction state callback is called on the game's thread.
- **Offline.** A request goes as far as an offline console's: the state callback (1), the redirection records, the
  manager's host record (made), its limits, a connection with its socket, then libnet's resolver, which isn't
  pspocket's (D-523 part 2) and fails: CELL_HTTP_ERROR_NET_RESOLVER and h_errno, the connection destroyed (before
  sys_net_initialize_network the socket fails: 0x80710410). A transaction stays in state 0, so the response getters
  answer NO_REQUEST_SENT, the connection calls TRANS_NO_CONNECTION, polling NO_CONNECTION, as libhttp does there.
  libhttp's code past a made connection (connecting, sending, receiving and parsing, chunks, gzip, redirections,
  authentication, cookies and cache entries from responses, pipelines, waiting for a connection) is not pspocket's:
  where it would run, `unreachable()` logs the call site and answers CELL_HTTP_ERROR_INTERNAL. It is the next part,
  once the resolver is pspocket's, compared with libhttp against a loopback server.
- **HTTPS.** libssl is not pspocket's: cellHttpsInit loads no CA certificates (logged when given some) and then does
  what libssl's cellSsl_CC6A0CB5 does for libhttp, reading the title's PARAM.SFO (_sys_process_get_paramsfo); libssl's
  list of titles that get other verification flags is its data and isn't reproduced. cellHttpClientSetSslClientCertificate
  makes its checks, then answers CELL_HTTP_ERROR_INTERNAL; the SSL getters answer as libhttp does without a
  connection (UNAVAILABLE for HTTP, BAD_CONN for HTTPS).
- **Caches.** cellHttpInitCache's and the external one (cellHttp_009E4B77, 512-byte blocks in the game's buffer) are
  libhttp's, with their statistics, flushes and walks, and a transaction looks its URI up at creation; their entries
  come from responses, so offline they stay empty.
- **Where libhttp faults** (a pointer it dereferences unchecked: a URI, a header's name, an output), pspocket logs the
  call site and answers CELL_HTTP_ERROR_NO_BUFFER (D-042). libhttp's own slips are kept where they show: a failed
  transaction leaves its header copies, cellHttpTransactionSetUri its block on a failed copy, a failed creation
  unlocks a client lock it doesn't hold, cellHttpDestroyTransaction keeps the client's lock when its second check
  fails, cellHttpRequestGetAllHeaders counts 20 bytes for each header it adds.
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_http_compare.cpp (D-193's method, `[http]`): scripts in two fresh processes, Sony's
  libhttp (with libssl) and pspocket's: every answer, the scripts' memory, libhttp's pools (heap magic and footers,
  lv2 IDs and pointers to each side's globals set aside) and the lv2 calls the thread makes with their arguments, the
  same. Scripts: the authentication cache, the cookie store and its limits, clients, transactions (creation, every
  function on IDs that are not, headers both ways, sending with and without libnet set up, a proxy, HTTPS, cookies in
  requests), caches. A test without the firmware keeps libhttp's answers for the set-up and a client. The old RPCS3
  check of cellHttpInit/End in tests/hle/test_net.cpp went with this.
- **Left out.** libhttp's disk cache, twelve unnamed exports (0xE55FE254, 0xABC0EB57, 0x419C41D2, 0x4558639F,
  0xEBF753AB, 0xB6D70A87, 0xA01CC407, 0x17EDB7D0, 0xE9BE8A88, 0xA3981634, 0x03F1AEF6, 0x08924181: an index and
  response files through cellFs): not registered, so a game importing one gets the loader's CELL_ENOSYS; clients can't
  switch it on (DCACHE_NOT_INITIALIZED). cellHttp_F799F3EF with certificate 0 of none (libhttp faults) answers
  INVALID_VALUE.

## D-531 · 2026-10-09 · cellSync2 pspocket's own, libsync2's objects bit for bit

cellSync2 had no implementation (RPCS3's are todo stubs; libsync2.sprx ran LLE). All 32 functions and its 6 variables
are now pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/cellSync2.cpp), read from libsync2 (fw 4.92) and compared with it running on
pspocket (tests/hle/test_sync2.cpp).
- The objects (mutex, condition, semaphore, queue: 128 bytes, 128-aligned) are shared with the library's SPU side
  (SPURS tasks and jobs update them with GETLLAR/PUTLLC), so the layout is libsync2's to the bit and every update is the
  one libsync2 makes with the same lwarx/ldarx and stwcx./stdcx. pairs, through the reservation system as the PPU
  interpreter and lifted code make them (ps_res_acquire + ps_res_store_conditional): a store by any processor in
  between fails it, as on the hardware.
- Waiting goes through the caller's thread type, a table of callbacks (self, allocate a signal receiver, wait, free),
  and waking through the notifier of the waiter's thread type. The library's tables are its exported variables
  (gCellSync2CallerThreadTypePpuThread/PpuFiber, gCellSync2Notifier*), laid out as libsync2's with descriptors of
  internal functions: a PPU thread's receiver is a bit of one of two lv2 event flags (priority, several waiters, waited
  AND|CLEAR), a fiber's goes through cellFiber, a SPURS task's through _cellSpursSendSignal, a job queue job's through
  cellSpursJobQueueSendSignal (host imports, D-197, when the firmware's module gives them; pspocket's own otherwise).
  A call without a configuration takes the fiber caller when the object allows fibers and cellFiberPpuSelf() is not 0.
- Blocked callers wait in libsync2's waiter queue: a ring of 8-byte entries in the caller's buffer where waiters and
  wakers each claim the next entry of their own round (round bits in the header and in each entry), and a waker that
  comes first leaves a signal in the entry so the waiter does not sleep. The mutex is a hand-over lock (an unlock with
  waiters left keeps it locked and wakes the next waiter, who takes ownership) spinning spinWaitNanoSec first; the
  condition releases the whole recursive mutex while it waits; the semaphore with one waiter keeps the waiter's need
  in the object (its waiter entries inside the object at +0x48); the queue is a linked queue over depth + 1 entries
  (bitmap, next array, dummy head, counters of free entries and elements that reserve before taking, multiple-element
  TryPush).
- The tail of the queue moves one entry per call, as libsync2's (a first version walked it to the end: caught by the
  comparison).
- HleProcess::link_variable now runs a variable's initializer after its lock is released, so an initializer can link
  the module's internal functions (the callback tables).
Deviations: libsync2's assertions are fatal logs with its text; memory that is not the guest's is refused with
CELL_SYNC2_ERROR_INVAL and the call site logged (libsync2 would fault); the event flags are made at the first PPU
thread receiver instead of at module start, and a host mutex guards their bitmaps (libsync2: a lightweight mutex).
Tests: a 890-step one-thread script (attributes, every size range edge, each argument's errors, recursion, DEADLK,
NOMEM, AGAIN, STAT, BUSY, every object's bytes and buffers after each step) the same as libsync2's; objects made by
one implementation and used by the other, both ways, the same as all-Sony; four threads contending a mutex, waiters on
a condition, acquirers on a semaphore, two producers and two consumers on a queue, on each implementation.

## D-525 · 2026-10-09 · cell_FreeType2 pspocket's own: FreeType 2.2.1 on the host, shown to the guest as libfreetype

Sony's libfreetype.sprx (library cell_FreeType2_2_1) is FreeType 2.2.1 built for the PPU. All 155 functions of the
count, the two unnamed exports libfontFT imports, and FreeType itself now run natively; the firmware module is no longer
needed for a game that imports cell_FreeType2.

- **Sony's build, read from the module and its answers.** FreeType's default options (the structures' 32-bit sizes
  agree: FT_LibraryRec 0xC4, TT_FaceRec 0x334, TT_DriverRec 0x4C) with FT_CONFIG_OPTION_FORCE_INT64 (its FT_MulFix,
  FT_MulDiv and FT_DivFix multiply in 64 bits) and without zlib (FT_Stream_OpenGzip answers 7); FreeType's default module
  list without the PCF and BDF drivers (16 modules, no bytecode interpreter, so TrueType glyphs are autohinted); a
  system layer with no allocator (FT_New_Memory answers NULL, so FT_Init_FreeType answers FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature
  and games make libraries with FT_New_Library and an FT_Memory of their own) and files read through cellFsOpen,
  cellFsLseek and cellFsRead (a CELL_EIO or CELL_EFSSPECIFIC calls the handler set with cell_FreeType2_904CA41F).
  pspocket's FreeType (third_party/CMakeLists.txt, external/freetype-2.2.1) is built the same: runtime/hle/src/freetype
  holds the options, the module list and pspocket's own system layer (pspocket_ftsystem.c: FT_Stream_Open through the
  guest's cellFs calls, as Sony's makes them, on the calling thread).
- **Sony's own additions.** cellFreeType2Ex hands the system its fonts: for a CELL_FONT_TYPE_* in its list it writes
  a path FT_New_Face opens ("/:dev_font:/RD-R-LATIN.ttf", its NUL, 0xDE, then /dev_flash/data/font/SCE-PS3-....TTF
  XORed with 0xF2), one static buffer per font, NULL for others, 0x805400F2 for a bad argument. FT_Stream_Open opens such
  a path ("/:dev_font", one character other than ':' or none, ":/") by the hidden real path, any other path as it is,
  at most 1087 characters. cell_FreeType2_211248E7 writes the version (0x02020128) as a 64-bit word.
- **The guest's view (runtime/hle/src/freetype_bridge.*).** FreeType's objects stay the host's, in host memory; every
  object the public API shows gets a mirror in the game's FT_Memory, in FreeType 2.2.1's 32-bit big-endian layout
  (computed from FreeType's headers with clang -target powerpc): the library and its modules (with their classes as
  process-wide records), faces (names, fixed sizes, charmaps, the stream, the sizes list), sizes, the glyph slot (metrics,
  bitmap, outline, subglyphs), sfnt tables (the hhea/vhea metrics arrays too), glyph images, strokers and the cache's
  managers, caches, nodes, glyphs and small bitmaps. A mirror is rewritten after each call that changes its object (the
  `generic` fields stay the guest's: FreeType's finalizers call the guest's with the guest object); the guest's changes
  to a slot's outline are read back before FT_Render_Glyph. When the host frees an object, its memory manager releases
  the mirrors inside the freed block, so FT_Done_Face, FT_Done_Library and the cache's flushes take theirs with them.
  What the guest owns outright is worked on in its own memory as FreeType does, with the same FT_Memory calls: outlines
  (ftoutln.c ported; FT_Outline_New allocates twice the points, as 2.2.1), glyph images (ftglyph.c ported, a slot's
  bitmap going to FT_Get_Glyph's glyph), bitmaps (ftbitmap.c run over the guest's buffer with the game's memory behind
  it), lists, FT_Alloc/FT_Realloc/FT_Free. The fixed-point and trigonometric exports are FreeType's code for a 32-bit
  FT_Long as Sony's compiled it (64-bit products; fttrigon.c's 16-bit-halves downscale).
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_freetype_compare.cpp (harness: tests/hle/freetype_compare.hpp): 12 scripts in two
  fresh processes, Sony's libfreetype and pspocket's, with guest callbacks written by the PPU assembler (a logging bump
  allocator as FT_Memory, logging callbacks for lists, decomposition, spans and finalizers, a face requester calling the
  library's FT_New_Face, a stream reader): fixed point and trigonometry over 120 values, lists and the old memory calls,
  libraries and modules, six fonts' faces and tables, sizes and glyph loading in every load flag and render mode (Latin,
  Japanese and Korean fonts, embedded bitmaps), outlines, bitmaps and glyph images, the stroker, memory faces, guest
  streams and LZW, the cache, Windows FNT and Type 1 faces the test writes (with an AFM attached), cellFreeType2Ex and
  its paths. 18,945 observations, the same: answers, every field and pixel, outlines point by point, and for what the
  guest owns the FT_Memory calls. Found on the way: Sony's trigonometry downscales in 16-bit halves (fttrigon.c never
  sees FT_CONFIG_HAS_INT64), FT_CONFIG_OPTION_FORCE_INT64, no zlib, FreeType's reserved WinFNT bytes copied raw.
- **What differs by construction.** FreeType's own working memory is the host's: Sony's goes through the game's
  FT_Memory (a game sees fewer and smaller allocations; the stroker's arrays and a load's hint tables do not reach it),
  and the cache weighs its nodes with 64-bit sizes, so it flushes somewhat earlier for the same max_bytes. A file
  stream's `base` keeps the last frame FreeType extracted in Sony's (a FreeType quirk), 0 in pspocket's. FreeType 2.2.1
  writes the count of a Type 1 font's StdHW/StdVW/MinFeature over PS_PrivateRec's first byte: unique_id's high byte on
  the PPU, its low byte on the host. A face's slot is not rewritten after the cache loads glyphs through it.
- **Refused where Sony's would run the game's code or crash.** A module class or glyph class of the game's own
  (FT_Add_Module after FreeType's version checks, FT_Glyph_To_Bitmap): FT_Err_Unimplemented_Feature, logged. Calls that
  dereference a null or unknown handle in Sony's code (FT_Outline_Translate(NULL), FT_Bitmap_Copy(NULL library), a
  null cache) answer FreeType's error for a bad handle instead; FT_Get_Glyph_Name of glyph num_glyphs on a PostScript
  face (2.2.1 reads past its name table) is FT_Err_Invalid_Argument. The guest closing an open face's stream is logged
  and not done.
- **The firmware's modules.** libfontFT imports internals of libfreetype (FT_GlyphLoader_*, FT_Stream_*) that are not
  in the count; the loader keeps choosing libfreetype.sprx for libfontFT while libfontFT runs as Sony's (D-175), unless
  the game imports cell_FreeType2 itself, which now binds that library to the host: cellFontFT is next (D-526).

## D-526 · 2026-10-09 · cellFontFT and cellFont pspocket's own (part 1: cellFontFT, libfontFT over pspocket's FreeType)

Sony's libfontFT.sprx is the font library of libfont's FreeType type. cellFontInitLibraryFreeType hands libfont a
CellFontLibrary that is libfontFT's own static record (type 0xCFF00002, version 0x02020100 from FreeType's, a lock word
counting its users, a table of 34 functions libfont calls for everything it does with a font, the memory interface it
was given, a manager of one FT_Library); the FTManager_*, FTFaceH_* and FTCacheStream_* exports are the layer under
that table. All 43 functions of the count, the table and the callbacks libfontFT hands out now run natively
(runtime/hle/src/cellFontFT.cpp); libfont runs over it as Sony's until part 2.

- **On pspocket's cell_FreeType2, through its guest API.** libfontFT is C over libfreetype's API; pspocket's calls
  pspocket's cell_FreeType2 (D-525) the same way, with its records in guest memory in Sony's layout, allocated with
  the same FT_Alloc/FT_Free calls: the library record and the shared library record, face handles (256 bytes: the
  FT_Face, its FT_Open_Args, scale, DPI, effect weight and slant, the last code and composite codes, the last metrics),
  renderers (128 bytes: buffer, image place, sizes), cache streams (an FT_StreamRec, then owner, cache, block index,
  the file's own read, the lock interface). FreeType's objects are read where libfontFT reads them, in the guest
  mirrors (face, size, glyph slot, outline); where it reaches into FreeType's internals the host's objects are used:
  the slot's glyph loader (FT_GlyphLoader_Reset/CheckPoints/CheckSubGlyphs for cellFontAdjustGlyphExpandBuffer and
  its counts), the face's transform flags (cleared after an image, as libfontFT does instead of FT_Set_Transform),
  TrueType's maximum profile. libfont's own functions libfontFT imports (cellFontStatic, cellFontsetUSleep,
  cellFontGetRevisionFlags, cellFontControl) are host imports (D-197): the firmware's libfont's while it runs as it is.
- **Sony's arithmetic.** The getters' and the layouts' 32/64-bit steps (truncating shifts, sign and zero extensions:
  the em scale is used zero-extended, as libfontFT's lwz leaves it), the render buffer's sizing (bounding box, weight's
  widening, slant's lean, 4-byte rows, the margins), the vertical-writing shifts (the shift type's three fields), the
  glyph image's adjustments (em-box vertical metrics, weight, slant; composite codes' union) and the vertexes-glyph
  renderer's single-precision float steps, with fused multiply-adds only where Sony's code has fmadds/fmsubs (the file
  is compiled without contraction) and the weight's clamp constants bit for bit ((0.93f - 1) * 65536 and
  (1.04f - 1) * 65536). The file cache's 8 KB slots, round robin and eviction as libfontFT's cached read does them.
- **Sony's change to FreeType.** CELL_FONT_OPEN_MODE_IGNORE_VERTICAL_METRICS: libfontFT writes 0x01000000 into the
  FT_Library's debug_hooks[3], and Sony's sfnt_load_face then skips a face's vmtx after its vhea and sets face flag
  0x01000000 (no FT_FACE_FLAG_VERTICAL). pspocket's FreeType 2.2.1 stays as it is: the sfnt module's interface is
  wrapped (its class replaced by a copy, freetype_bridge.cpp patch_sfnt) and the flag read from the guest's record.
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_fontft_compare.cpp with Sony's libfontFT and libfreetype, both under Sony's libfont
  (the harness now runs a mix of the firmware's modules and pspocket's, linking host imports as the loader does): the
  FT layer called directly (managers and the shared library, memory, file and stream faces, every getter over three
  scales and twenty effect settings, metrics, images at three subpixel positions with effects and composite codes,
  kerning, a cache stream through six slots with its eviction, the open mode, closing) and libfont's API over it
  (libraries, fontsets, file and memory fonts, layouts, metrics and kerning, renderers with scissors and a small
  buffer, character images in all three directions, generated outlines with their environments and vertexes images
  in four styles, the open mode, closing, ending): 1,003 observations, the same (answers, metrics, image places and
  pixels, outline points).
- **Refused where Sony's would read through a null pointer**: closing a null face handle, an effect weight on a handle
  without a face, an image without a CellFontImageTransInfo (logged). An empty font file opened through the cache
  passes no stream where Sony's passes an unset one; the vertical glyph environment's shift words are 0 where Sony's
  reads them unset (shift type 0). libfontFT's unnamed exports that no game imports (other renderer and buffer entry
  points) are internal functions only.

## D-532 · 2026-10-09 · cellAtrac pspocket's own, libatrac3plus over pspocket's cellAdec

cellAtrac's 24 functions (RPCS3: answers without decoding) are now libatrac3plus.sprx's logic, read from its code and
compared with it running on pspocket (tests/hle/test_atrac.cpp). The handle (512 bytes, the game's) is laid out as
libatrac3plus's: a mutex and condition ("_a3pm00", "_a3pc00") around cellAdec's callback, cellAdec's type, attributes,
callback, resource and handle, the ATRAC3 and ATRAC3plus parameters, the work memory, and the stream state (play
range, loop, encoder delay, frames to decode before PCM is kept, how the file is held: whole, half loaded, streamed
through a ring, streamed with a loop, streamed with a second buffer for the loop's tail).
- SetDataAndGetMemSize reads the RIFF WAVE header as libatrac3plus does: fmt for ATRAC3 (0x270) or ATRAC3plus
  (WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE with its subformat GUID, config bytes giving the rate, channel configuration and frame size),
  fact (samples, first sample offset; a 4-byte offset adds the 184-sample delay later), smpl (the first loop), data;
  44.1 and 48 kHz only. The default first offset is 0x800 for ATRAC3plus, 0x400 for ATRAC3 (libatrac3plus computes it
  with a rotate, which a first version took for a shift: caught by the comparison). The memory it asks for is a
  frame's PCM (8 KB per channel for 1, 2, 6 or 8 channels; 4 KB per channel for ATRAC3) + cellAdec's + 1 KB.
- CreateDecoder/Ext open cellAdec (Open or OpenExt with the SPURS resource), start the sequence and decode the frames
  before the first kept sample; a failure deletes the decoder through DeleteDecoder as libatrac3plus does (its sync
  objects destroyed a second time, so that delete fails and the handle stays set, as on a PS3). Decode feeds one frame
  per call (cellAdecDecodeAu), waits for the callback's PCM-out on the condition, takes the PCM into the game's buffer
  or (a partial frame) into the work memory and copies the kept part, then moves the positions: loops back to the
  loop start, the ring, the switch to the second buffer past the loop's tail (the end of its last frame copied to the
  ring's front). GetBufferInfoForResetting decodes the pre-roll frames too, as libatrac3plus does.
- Remain-frame counts, vacant size, writable size and the read position of the stream are libatrac3plus's per state
  (-1 all in memory, -2 the rest of a stream without a loop, -3 of a looped one).
Tests: AT3+ files built here (silent frames that decode through pspocket's FFmpeg-based ATRAC3plus core) played whole,
half loaded, streamed (topped up and left to run dry), looped at the end and inside with a second buffer, reset, with
Create and CreateExt, fact chunks of both sizes, an odd unknown chunk, 44.1/32 kHz, a wrong GUID, a PCM tag, a read
larger than the buffer, a 12-byte header: every answer, output, the handle's bytes and the PCM the same as
libatrac3plus's (5,000-line log), over 150 decodes.
## D-530 · 2026-10-09 · cellSsl pspocket's own: libssl's set-up and the crypto library under it, as far as offline reaches

cellSsl had three functions after RPCS3's (cellSslInit/End, which only flipped a flag, and the certificate loader,
which cleared a buffer). It is now libssl.sprx's own logic, read from its code and compared with the module running
on pspocket's lv2: all 114 of libssl's exports are registered and native (runtime/hle/src/cellSsl.cpp, cellSslLib.cpp,
cellSslConn.cpp), the offline-reachable ones pspocket's own and the cryptographic core answering as libssl does where
it cannot run without a connection.

- **What libssl is.** RSA's SSL-C, an SSLeay/OpenSSL-0.9 descendant: the same LHASH, OBJ_NAME table, ERR queue, BIO,
  ASN.1/X509 objects and SSL state machine, over RSA's own crypto library (the "R_" functions and a context of
  resources). It keeps everything in a liblv2 heap made over the pool cellSslInit is given and its globals in its data
  segment. pspocket does the same (cellSslLib.cpp): every object is a heap block of libssl's size made at the same
  moment, its fields at libssl's offsets, so the pool's bytes are libssl's. What the pool points at that is not an
  object — the strings a function returns by value, the EVP method tables, the function ids an object names — lives in
  a guest block of pspocket's (ssl.hpp Lib::block), where a function libssl names by descriptor is an address of its
  own.
- **Set-up.** cellSslInit makes the heap "cellSsl_Library" over the caller's pool (liblv2's, D-502), the lightweight
  mutex "_sslsys" (recursive), installs SSL-C's memory functions and lock callback, builds the library context, seeds
  the random generator with 64 bytes from sys_get_random_number, and installs the time callback; it answers
  CELL_SSL_ERROR_NO_BUFFER for a null pool or size (RPCS3 checked neither), NO_MEMORY when the heap can't be made, and
  INITIALIZATION_FAILED on a later step. cellSslEnd frees the library context (OBJ_NAME_cleanup over the table, the
  error states and strings), deletes the heap and destroys the mutex. cellSslGetMemoryInfo reports the heap's free
  size and liblv2's mallinfo; it checks nothing (RPCS3: UNIMPLEMENTED), so with no heap it is liblv2's answer for heap
  0. The library context's resource list is libssl's: the digest and cipher aliases, then four ciphers and nine
  digests registered into OBJ_NAME in libssl's order, each OBJ name an object of standard names (PKCS #1, RFC 3279,
  NIST), the LHASH grown before it inserts and freed bucket by bucket as libssl's.
- **The error queue (ERR).** Each thread's ERR_STATE (a 332-byte ring of sixteen) is made at its first error and kept
  in an LHASH keyed by the thread id, which is always 0 (no id callback is set). ERR_get_error / ERR_peek_error read
  the ring; ERR_error_string formats "error:%08lX::lib(n) :func(n) :reason(n)" by number (liblv2's _sys_vsprintf),
  because libssl loads no error strings, so ERR_func_error_string and the string table are empty.
- **Conversions and names.** _cellSslConvertSslVersion, _cellSslConvertCipherId, SSL_alert_type_string_long,
  SSL_alert_desc_string_long and SSLCERT_OID_to_string are pspocket's own tables; the cipher and BIO accessors answer
  as libssl does for the null cipher or BIO a game has without a handshake. cellSsl_CC6A0CB5 (libhttp asks for a
  title's extra verification flag) reads the running title's PARAM.SFO as libssl does and returns the default: the
  list of titles libssl gives other flags is its data and is not reproduced (CLAUDE.md rule 1), so no title matches.
- **Surprises.** libssl's realloc takes the old size (it copies the smaller of the two). Its LHASH grows a bucket
  before it splits, and shrinks only past sixteen nodes. ERR_put_error writes only the code, file, line and data of a
  slot and leaves the rest of the slot's bytes as the ring held them. R_time_new always answers 0: it allocates a
