  time object, asks the installed callback to fill it, and the callback fills nothing, so it frees the object and
  returns 0. cellSslInit seeds the generator and installs the X509 and time method tables through a resource list
  whose cleanups run in order at cellSslEnd.
- **Left out (the next part).** The X509/ASN.1/RSA certificate parser (SSLCERT_from_binary and the method table it
  installs, the cellSslCert* queries, BER_read_item, EVP_PKEY_free, the PEM readers) and the TLS state machine
  (SSL_CTX_new, SSL_new, the handshake, read/write, the BIO memory and socket subsystem) are reached only around a
  TLS handshake, which pspocket's offline console can't complete (the boundary D-524 drew for cellHttp). Each is
  registered and native: it logs the call site and answers as libssl does with no certificate or connection (0, or
  the public cellSslCert* functions make libssl's init and pointer checks first, then UNRETRIEVABLE). It is the next
  part, compared against a loopback once the handshake is pspocket's. Because of this, libhttp's cellHttpsInit still
  loads no CA certificates (its loader calls cellSsl_9447404F, the PEM parser) and cellHttpClientSetSslClientCertificate
  still answers INTERNAL, as D-524 left them.
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_ssl_compare.cpp (D-193's method, `[ssl]`): scripts in two fresh processes, Sony's
  libssl and pspocket's, with every answer, the scripts' memory, libssl's pool (its heap, the same blocks at the same
  places, lv2 IDs and pointers to each side's globals set aside) and the lv2 calls the thread makes the same. Scripts:
  the set-up (init on a null and a small pool, the memory report and callback, re-init on a used pool), and the
  conversions, alert strings, cipher and BIO null answers, the title flag and the OID names (507 comparisons over the
  two, 0 differences). A test without the firmware keeps libssl's set-up answers. The certificate functions are driven
  by a hidden probe (made-up certificates from OpenSSL) that traces Sony's module to map the parser, not compared,
  since the parser is the next part. The old RPCS3 cellSsl check in tests/hle/test_net.cpp now expects Sony's set-up.

## D-533 · 2026-10-09 · sys_io's sys_config_* as libio's config service agent

sys_io's eight sys_config functions are pspocket's own, read from libio (sys_io.sprx, fw 4.92) and compared with it.
Before, sys_config_start/stop only kept a count and the other six were RPCS3's stubs; now all eight do what libio's
`config_service_agent` does over pspocket's lv2 sys_config (D-527).

- **The agent.** One 0x28-byte object on liblv2's heap (_sys_malloc), made at the first sys_config call under a spin
  guard (an atomic count; a second comer backs off with sys_timer_usleep(1000)): a recursive lwmutex "_io_mtx" at +0,
  the event queue at +0x18, lv2's sys_config handle at +0x1C (-1 until opened) and the I/O error handler at +0x20.
  Every call takes the lwmutex with a 4-second timeout and, as libio does, goes on without it when that fails (a
  diagnostic through _sys_printf). The last sys_config_stop deletes it (destroying the lwmutex) under the same guard,
  so sys_config_stop before any start makes and deletes an agent and answers CELL_EABORT.
- **Start and stop** count. The first start creates the queue ("_io_eq_", priority order, 32 deep), opens sys_config on
  it and starts "_cfg_ev_hndlr" (priority 512, 8 KB stack, joinable) through liblv2's sys_ppu_thread_create; on a
  failure it closes and destroys what it made and returns the error, leaving the count raised (libio does). The last
  stop frees every listener node, destroys the queue with the force flag (which wakes the thread with ECANCELED),
  closes the handle and joins the thread; a failure of any of these is printed and returned (the join's: printed,
  then 0). The thread's entry is an internal function, `_pspocket_sys_config_event_thread`.
- **Events.** The thread receives while the count is not zero. A service event (source 1: handle, registered << 32 |
  event ID, size) is read with sys_config_get_service_event into a buffer from the heap; its listener's callbacks
  get (service ID, user ID, verbosity, the data or NULL, its size) for a registered service and (service ID, user ID)
  for an unregistered one, under the lwmutex. An I/O error event (source 2) is read with sys_config_get_io_event and
  the handler gets (the first word, the rest, the rest's size). An event for another handle is printed and handled
  anyway; a failed read is printed and its buffer kept (libio leaks it); an unknown source is printed with the
  event's first datum. libio's diagnostics go out through _sys_printf with libio's text, as sys_net does with libnet's.
- **Listeners.** sys_config_add_service_listener(service ID, minimum verbosity, data, size, callbacks[2], type, u32*
  listener) refuses data with a negative service ID (CELL_EINVAL), makes lv2's listener, then a 20-byte node (next,
  previous, lv2's ID, the registered and unregistered callbacks) appended to libio's list; with no memory it removes
  lv2's listener and answers CELL_ENOMEM. Removing unlinks the node, removes lv2's listener (its answer is the call's)
  and frees the node after the lock. Register and unregister service pass straight to lv2 under the lock. The I/O
  error handler is one at a time (CELL_EEXIST), registered with lv2 first.
- **Surprise.** The callbacks' order in sys_config_add_service_listener comes before the listener type (r7, then r8),
  the reverse of lv2's call (type, then the listener's address).
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_config_compare.cpp: one script in two fresh processes (libio loaded in both), one
  calling libio's exports and one pspocket's: starts and stops (nested, before any start, again after the last), every
  listener case (bad data, the pad manager lv2 registers, the ONCE type, verbosity below the minimum, removal twice),
  services registered and unregistered, the I/O error handler twice, and events sent to the agent's queue through
  ports (I/O errors, a service event for another handle with no such event, an unknown source). The answers, the
  callbacks' arguments, the outputs and the lv2 calls of both threads (with their arguments, heap addresses kept) are
  the same; only the registers past a callback's arguments, which hold what each caller left there, are not
  compared. A test without the firmware runs pspocket's agent alone.

## D-526 (part 2) · 2026-10-09 · cellFont pspocket's own: libfont's code, its data read from the firmware's libfont

Sony's libfont.sprx is the PS3's font API. All 88 exports (the 85 of the count, cellFont_57E03823 (the initialization
without the system tables' set-up), cellFont_8D5094C4 and cellFont_47B70477 (a draw context's flags)) and the
callbacks libfont hands out (the file cache's lock and unlock to libfontFT, the composite-code lookup, the graphics
start cellFontExtend gives) now run natively (runtime/hle/src/cellFont.cpp), over pspocket's cellFontFT (part 1).

- **The code is pspocket's, the data the firmware's.** libfont's tables are data, not code: the system fonts (each
  font ID's file, cache size, scale, shift and weight factors), each fontset's fonts and its map of which font draws
  which code (range lists over trees of bitmaps, sorted code lists and code pairs), the per-code adjustments of the
  "capie" sets, the vertical forms, and the fonts' paths (XOR-encoded). They are not copied into the source: at the
  first call the module is read from dev_flash (/dev_flash/sys/external/libfont.sprx, decrypted with the build's SELF
  keys as the loader decrypts modules), its two segments placed and relocated in the main area (recomp::place_prx),
  and libfont's code ported to read them there. libfont's static records (its state and lock word, the revision, the
  system and user font tables, the library slots, the file cache's settings, the patch-works bits, the usleep and
  file-error slots) live in that data segment at libfont's own offsets, so libfontFT, which reads them through
  cellFontStatic, sees what it sees in Sony's. Only the libfont whose identity (recomp::prx_identity) is firmware
  4.92's is placed; another logs and the API answers as uninitialized.
- **Ported from Sony's code**: the locks (a word's top bit with a 1 ms nap through the game's usleep or
  sys_timer_usleep; bit 30 "open", the low bits the users, counted without the lock while others use an entry), the
  initialization and the file cache's layout, the fontsets' opening (the type's old and new Japanese names, every font
  of the set opened once in the system table, its path built as libfont builds it: the font server's hidden
  "/:dev_font:/" path or the game's font directory (cellFontControl 0x540000), the ".ccd" composite-code file beside
  it, the glyph buffer's expansion, on memory through the font library's file loader), file and memory fonts in the
  user table (one face per unique ID and library, E(0xd) when full), instances, closing with the last user's face
  closed and its buffers freed, the code-to-font walk with its fontset adjustments, metrics, kerning, layouts (the
  widest and deepest over a set's fonts), character images in three directions, generated glyphs and the vertical
  shift types, the renderers, draw contexts, scissors, cellFontDelete's dispatch on the record's magic, the
  extension queries, the patch works, and the outline walk of cellFontGlyphGetOutlineVertexes (moves, lines, conics
  and cubics halved until within the control distance, an S-shaped cubic halved at least once, 32 halvings at most,
  closes) with vertexes glyphs' headers and relocation. Single-precision steps as Sony's, fused only where its code
  has fmadds/fmsubs (no contraction in the file); libfont's float constants read from its data.
- **A fix in the FreeType bridge found here** (freetype_bridge.cpp): FreeType's reads of a guest stream and of a file
  went to the guest in 4 KB pieces; Sony's libfreetype reads a frame with one call (FT_Stream_Read; fread with one
  cellFsRead, libfreetype 0x14e64). With libfontFT's cache under the stream the pieces went through the game's cache
  slots one by one where Sony's reads a large frame straight from the file, leaving other blocks in the slots. One
  read now, into the buffer when it is guest memory, else through the guest stack (4 KB or less) or a block of the
  main area of its own (no allocation the game sees). The settings test compares the cache's slots.
- **Not made**: libfont's module_start (a cellSysutil call for SDKs before 1.40; pspocket's modules have no start), its
  dead code (a reserved-font list no export can set, file helpers nothing calls; cellFontPatchWorks' bit 4 that no
  function checks is set all the same). Paths over libfont's 1 KB buffers, which libfont overruns, are cut. The font
  library's functions libfont never calls (set_scale_point_dpi, setup_render_scale_dpi, alloc_memory, em_center: for
  the graphics libraries) are still not compared through libfont.
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_font.cpp with Sony's libfont, libfontFT and libfreetype against pspocket's three
  (the libfont script of part 1, now in tests/hle/font_scripts.hpp, runs over both): initialization and its errors,
  settings and controls, 18 fontset kinds by Unicode and by type, a fontset's open mode, fontsets on memory, instances,
  a game font directory, file fonts with shared entries and the full table, scaling, DPI, scales and effects with their
  clamps, null arguments, ending; draw contexts, the extension queries and the functions they give (a graphics start
  and end, cellFontEndGraphics, cellFontDelete of every kind), renderers bound to a font, the patch works turning
  functions off one by one; outline vertexes of made outlines (lines, conics, cubics, degenerate and malformed
  contours; three control distances) and of the fonts' glyphs (two), vertexes glyphs in enough and too little memory
  and relocated; composite codes from a ".ccd" made in the test beside a copy of a firmware font in a temporary
  directory (removed after). 1,432 observations, the same. How often the game's allocator is called is not compared
  (FreeType's own objects are the host's, D-525). The tests' font heap grew to 64 MB.

## D-535 · 2026-10-09 · cellAtracMulti pspocket's own: libatrac3multi as cellAtrac's code on its own layout

cellAtracMulti's 25 functions (RPCS3: answers without decoding) are now libatrac3multi.sprx's logic, compared with it
running on pspocket (tests/hle/test_atrac_multi.cpp). Read side by side, libatrac3multi is libatrac3plus's ATRAC3 path
(D-532) with four differences, so runtime/hle/src/cellAtrac.cpp now serves both modules: each export is a thin wrapper
over one body that takes a `Layout`.
- The handle (512 bytes) is laid out 0x14 bytes lower: the stream state from +0x5C (libatrac3plus +0x70), the work
  memory at +0x58 (+0x6C), the buffer for the frame cellAdec gets at +0x54, the track count at +0x40 and the file's
  channels at +0x50; the sync objects are named "_a3mpm0" and "_a3mpc0". Its errors are libatrac3plus's plus 0x800
  (0x80610Bxx), and every export first refuses a NULL handle or a NULL pointer it takes with 0x80610B91, before any
  other check (so does a track count outside 1..8 in SetDataAndGetMemSize).
- ATRAC3 only: the header parser is libatrac3plus's ATRAC3 branch plus one check, joint stereo must be 0; an ATRAC3plus
  (WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE) header is refused as an unknown format.
- Output tracks: SetDataAndGetMemSize takes the track count and an array naming, for each output track, the file
  channel it plays (NULL: the file's channels in order). Before each frame goes to cellAdec, libatrac3multi copies each
  track's block (the frame's bytes / the file's channels) from the named channel into its frame buffer, or a silent
  block (zeros, 0xA2 first: a sound unit with no spectrum) for an entry that names no channel of the file;
  ResetPlayPosition takes a new array. cellAdec's type is 31 (ATRAC3 multichannel), the firmware's core when the user's
  system software is installed.
- GetTrackArray is new (the count and the array back); the memory asked for counts the output tracks' PCM.
Tests: ATRAC3 files of four channels built in the test (silent frames whose blocks carry a per-channel, per-frame byte,
so a block shuffled wrong shows in the frame cellAdec gets) played whole, half loaded, streamed and run dry, with
fact chunks of both sizes, looped at the end and inside with a second buffer, with 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 tracks (picked
channels, silent entries, repeats), 0 and 9 tracks, joint stereo, an ATRAC3plus tag, 32 kHz, a read larger than the
buffer, a 12-byte header, and calls on a handle never set and with NULLs: every answer, output, the handle's bytes
(but the lv2 IDs, cellAdec's handle and the callback's descriptor), the shuffled frame and the PCM the same as
libatrac3multi's over the firmware's ATRAC3 multichannel core (2,517 checks, over 150 decodes). A test without the
firmware plays pspocket's side alone. cellAtrac's own comparison (D-532) still passes after the split into bodies.

## D-538 · 2026-10-09 · cellDaisy pspocket's own: libsre's cell::Daisy, both names of each

cellDaisy is the out-of-line part of the SDK's Daisy library (cell/daisy: pipes between PPU threads and SPU programs,
whose templates the game compiles in). libsre.sprx exports 26 functions, each under a _QN and a _ZN name (52 in the
count; RPCS3 has todo stubs). runtime/hle/src/cellDaisy.cpp is libsre's code, read from it (D-046):
- **Lock** (0x20 bytes: head and tail as u16 with a bitmap of completions past each, the next pointers to hand out,
  depth, state, open producers and consumers): initialize (depth below 0x8000; a second call with the same depth is
  fine), push/pop open and close (the last consumer closes it), the next head/tail pointer (DAISY_PTR_UNAVAILABLE when
  empty and producers may still come, full, or 16 under way; DAISY_PTR_TERMINATED when drained and the producers are
  gone; the pointer handed back is the moved one), and completions (with more than one open on that side, a bitmap of
  out-of-order completions, the end moving past every completion in a row). Plain loads and stores, as libsre's.
- **LFQueue2**: a cellSync LFQueue whose m_v1 counts open pushers and poppers, grown to 0x100 bytes by Daisy's fields
  (open pushers, state, close waiters with their IDs, pop waiters with their IDs and the pointers they wait for).
  GetPopPointer (SPU2PPU only; blocking needs an attached event queue; a closed queue with no pusher answers 3; a
  marked wait, m_h3, makes the call sleep on the lv2 event queue, clear the mark and take another pointer, which
  libsre really does), CompletePopPointer (cellSync's _cellSyncLFQueueCompletePopPointer, pspocket's own, then the first
  pop waiter whose pointer is in reach is signalled; cellSync's AGAIN/INVAL/BUSY become Daisy's 0x8041051x),
  PushOpen/PushClose (the last pusher signals every SPU waiter in the push side's ring), PopOpen/PopClose (the last
  popper closes the queue and signals the close waiters until a signal fails), HasUnfinishedConsumer.
- **ScatterGatherInterlock** over an AtomicInterlock (count, a waiting flag or the callback's argument + 1, an lv2
  event queue, an SPU port): the constructor with SPU threads makes the "_daiSGI" event queue and connects each SPU
  thread as a user event on the first port from the one given that the first thread accepts (one in use: the next);
  the callback constructor; proceedSequenceNumber; probe (waiting marks the flag and sleeps on the queue); release (to a
  waiting probe through an event port made and connected at the first such release; to the callback with its
  argument); the destructor undoes either.
- _snprintf is liblv2's _sys_snprintf on the variadic arguments (sysPrxForUser_libc.cpp's liblv2_snprintf_call).
Every lwarx/ldarx and stwcx./stdcx. pair of libsre's is a snapshot of the line through the shared reservation system
and a conditional store (as cellSync2's Reserve); lv2 calls are libsre's, with its arguments, the addresses in its
stack frames included. Deviations: libsre's assertions are fatal logs with their text; objects that are not guest memory
are refused with CELL_DAISY_ERROR_INVAL and the call site logged, where libsre would fault; release's "sreEventPortCreate
time out" (1,000 EAGAINs) is a log line.

Tests: tests/hle/test_daisy.cpp runs one script in two processes with libsre loaded, one calling libsre's exports and
one pspocket's: Lock initialize checks and 3,200 random operations at depths 1 to 0x7FFF; _snprintf with arguments in
registers and on the stack and four buffer sizes; LFQueue2 on SPU2PPU and PPU2SPU queues (each process's own cellSync
sets them up and completes pops, so cellSync's completion with an SPU waiter to signal is compared with libsre's too),
waits on a pre-sent event, ring wrap-around, failing signals; the interlock with a callback, with an event port, and
with two SPU threads of a group made in the test (ports taken); and a thread probing while another releases. About
6,500 lines of answers, bytes and callback arguments, and every lv2 call with its arguments, the same.

## D-539 · 2026-10-09 · sys_net, part 2: libnet's configuration calls, routes, interfaces, netsets and resolver

D-523 made libnet's core pspocket's own; this is the rest of what libnet.sprx exports but the resolver (part 4 below).
All in runtime/hle/src/sys_net.cpp, read from libnet's code and compared with it running on pspocket's lv2
(tests/hle/test_net_compare.cpp: the "configuration", "routes and interfaces", "netsets" and "netset configurations"
scripts; answers, the scripts' memory, libnet's pool byte for byte, every lv2 network call with its arguments and the
TTY the same).
- **Wrappers**: _sys_net_lib_ioctl (the 39 commands libnet passes to lv2, EINVAL for others and for a missing argument;
  two of them clear parts of their argument first), _sys_net_lib_bnet_control (sys_net_control), the packet dumps
  (lv2's 717..719).
- **Test parameters**: get/set, netemu (flags 1, version 0x101) and UDP-P2P, each an ioctl on a socket made for the
  call (a 528-byte block naming eth0), EINVAL without errno for a bad argument.
- **Name servers**: netset.c's resolv.conf text in the pool ("nameserver X" lines added with "nameserver add X", two
  lines at most), the library's own set (sys_net_set/get_lib_name_server), lv2's through infoctl 9 (read into the
  thread's context, outside the context's call wrapper) and 52, sys_net_show_nameserver's report.
- **Routes**: netset.c's route command interpreter ("route add|del|flushall" lines with -net, -host, -inet, gw,
  netmask, -prefixlen and up to three addresses; 0.0.0.1 stands for a caller's address), building version-3 routing
  messages (UP|STATIC, REJECT, HOST, GATEWAY; the next sequence number; sockaddrs rounded to 8 bytes) sent on a routing
  socket: _sce_net_set_default_gateway sends a 168-byte RTM_ADD; _sce_net_flush_route deletes what the routing table's
  dump lists; sys_net_get_routing_table_af and sys_net_show_route ("route: No routing table (0)").
- **Interfaces**: _sce_net_set_ip_and_mask (address, netmask, broadcast or destination ioctls),
  _sys_net_lib_if_nametoindex, and sys_net_if_ctl: lv2's memory (infoctl 8) and the pool's, the packet count
  (infoctl 10), the resolver cache flush (656), the wireless chip's two queries (eurus commands -1 and 153; the second's
  text from its first digit to a '('), route lookup 16 with its ICMP echo when no route is found, sys_net_control for a
  negative command, interfaces by index.
- **Netsets**: sys_netset_open's parser (up to five tokens a line; quotes; \ooo, \xHH, \a..\v and \( \) hex byte
  groups, their bytes counted for binary values; '#' and '\r' end a line; a last line without a newline is dropped;
  256 bytes of tokens a line), its keys (flags, mtu through libnet's own sscanf, strings, binary values, the resolver
  and route texts, the key table's values), close (the first netset's values become the key values; the last one
  clears lv2's resolver configuration), abort, get_status (the thread's last netset.c failure: what, line, arguments),
  get_key_value, get_if_id, if_up, if_down. Every netset.c failure is noted in the thread's context (+2904..+2920) as
  libnet notes it.
- **lv2 change**: an interface's ioctls (BSD's group 'i', but the test parameters) now answer ENXIO: pspocket's console
  has no interface with no link (D-523), and a missing interface's ioctls fail so on BSD. RPCS3's stub answered
  CELL_OK and wrote nothing, so libnet's if_up read its own stack's leftovers as interface flags. With it, if_up's
  first step (lo0 up, 127.0.0.1/8) fails; the netset goes back to state 0, status 9.
- Not reachable offline, so they stop with a fatal log naming what lv2 would have to have answered (as getifaddrs
  does, D-523): routing tables or interfaces lv2 lists, an interface ioctl lv2 accepts (if_up past lo0, DHCP, PPPoE
  and wireless set-ups, if_down of an interface that came up). The DHCP client is not needed: its first step, the
  interface's index, finds none.
- Deviations: sys_net_get_lib_name_server writes 0 for a server the library does not have (libnet copies its stack's
  leftovers); bad guest pointers are refused with errno EFAULT and the call site logged.

Part 4, **the resolver** (gethostbyname, now libnet's own, and gethostbyaddr, replacing D-569's interim one): FreeBSD's
gethnamaddr.c and nsdispatch over BIND 8's res_query, res_mkquery, res_comp and res_send, as Sony built them, their
statics in the thread's context (the hostent at +0xC0 with its address and alias pointers, text buffer and address;
BIND's __res_state from +0x988; res_send's socket at +0xB44). Compared with libnet in the "resolver" script: 44 lookups
by name (41 names) and 18 by address on two threads, the pool after each (with the DNS query each builds: the
generator's state is set the same in both processes first, which also checks _sys_net_lib_rand against libnet's) and
every lv2 call: 0 differences.
- Every step first reads lv2's resolver configuration again (infoctl 9: libnet never sets RES_INIT) and would run
  res_init when it changed; lv2 has none offline (D-523), so one gethostbyname makes up to six of these calls.
- A name that is an address gives a hostent of its own (digits and dots, or hex digits, colons and dots with a colon;
  not when it ends with a dot; HOST_NOT_FOUND when inet_pton refuses it). Any other name goes to the hosts source and
  then the DNS source (nsdispatch with no nsswitch configuration: the defaults).
- The hosts file is libnet's built-in "127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.\n", read through libnet's own FILE (88 bytes from
  the pool, "netset.c" 1698; at its end fgets sets errno EBADF; its rewind only marks the end). By name, every entry of
  the family whose name or an alias matches (case ignored) is gathered in a block from the pool ("gethnamaddr.c" 0x3DB)
  and copied back into the text buffer; by address, the first entry with the address.
- gethostbyaddr: link- and site-local IPv6 addresses are HOST_NOT_FOUND at once, IPv4-mapped and -compatible ones are
  looked up as IPv4; a length not the type's is EINVAL, another type EAFNOSUPPORT. Its DNS query is the address's
  in-addr.arpa or ip6.arpa name.
- DNS: res_search (ndots is 0 and the search list empty, since res_init never ran: every name is tried as it is),
  res_querydomain (a trailing dot dropped), res_query, res_mkquery (an ID from libnet's generator, also kept at +0x9C8;
  RD set), dn_comp (ns_name_pton into a 255-byte block from the pool, "res_comp.c" 0x345 — Sony's has no check for an
  empty label before the end, so "a.." is "a." —; each label looked up among the earlier names: errno ENOENT) and
  res_send. The context's one name server has no family: the DNS cache's hooks act on AF_INET servers only, lv2
  refuses socket(0, SOCK_DGRAM), the server is marked bad and the tries end: errno ECONNREFUSED, h_errno TRY_AGAIN
  (NO_RECOVERY when no query can be made: a name too long, a label over 63 bytes, a bad escape).
- Not pspocket's own, with a fatal log: res_init (reached only after _sce_net_set_name_server gave lv2 a
  configuration), RES_USE_INET6's mapped hostents (set only by res_init), the DNS cache and the exchange with a name
  server lv2 gives a socket for, and an answer's parsing (none comes offline).
- The comparison now also masks pointers into each module's hosts text, which stay behind in the pool (one with its
  low 4 bits cleared by res_query).

## D-562 · 2026-10-09 · cellSail pspocket's own, from libsail (part 1: the objects the game hands the player)

cellSail is Sony's media player framework, libsail.sprx (fw 4.92): 137 exports over a player that runs its own thread
and drives the PAMF reader, cellDmux, cellVdec, cellAdec, cellVpost and a SPURS instance, with the firmware's MP4 and
AVI libraries for those files. It is made pspocket's own part by part, read from libsail's code and compared with it
running on pspocket (tests/hle/test_sail.cpp: one script in two fresh processes, libsail loaded in both).

Part 1, the objects a game fills in and their calls into the player:
- **CellSailMemAllocator**: the two callbacks copied, the argument after them; any NULL is INVALID_ARG.
- **CellSailFuture** (0x18 bytes): an lv2 mutex and condition (priority, not recursive; both "_saifu0"), the state
  word (bit 31 the result is set, below it the waiters) and the result. Set twice is INVALID_STATE; Get counts itself
  a waiter, waits (the game's timeout) until the result is set and passes the wake-up on to the next waiter; Reset
  without waiting is INVALID_STATE while someone waits, else waits in 100 ms slices; IsDone answers 1 or 0.
- **CellSailSource** (0x80 bytes): the player, the argument, the 14 callbacks, 1 while initialized, a pending call's
  handle, a diagnostic handler. Its notifications go to the diagnostic handler (argument, kind 0-4, two values) when
  one is set, else as messages to the player's queue (codes 0x01 stream out, 0x17 input EOS, 0x20 session error with
  bit 31 cleared when terminated, 0x29 call completed, 0x2D media state); a call completed with a pending handle
  posts {0, result, handle} instead. NotifyStreamOut with any count but 1 is libsail's assertion: it stores to NULL
  (pspocket logs the call site and stops).
- **CellSailRendererAudio/Video**: the callbacks and argument, the wanted format copied from the attribute (version 8,
  else INVALID_ARG) or all 0xFF (video: its first byte 0); Finalize sets the state 9; the notifications are messages
  (audio 0x11, 0x12 frame done, 0x1D EOS, 0x33 completed; video 0x13, 0x14, 0x1E, 0x34). Two of them are exports
  RPCS3 does not name (cellSail_C00A450C, cellSail_3E9B9F80).
- **The player's queue** (at its +0x170): capacity, count, a ring of 16-byte messages, the write index, an lv2 mutex
  and condition; a post waits while the ring is full and wakes the player.
- **MP4 and AVI**: the calls go through the function tables libsail fetches from the firmware's MP4 library (internal
  module 0xF031, cellMp4) and AVI library (0xF039, cellSailAvi) when the player first opens such a file; before that
  libsail calls through NULL (pspocket logs and answers INVALID_STATE).
- Sixteen exports with no name answer -1. RPCS3 names five source notifications fw 4.92's libsail does not export
  (Open/Start/Stop/Read/CloseCompleted): they log and answer NOT_AVAILABLE.
Compared: 46 calls, the memory they touch (objects, the queue's ring, the callbacks' records) and every mutex and
condition call with its attributes: 0 differences.

Part 2, the player's life before it plays (runtime/hle/src/cellSailPlayer.cpp, cellSail.hpp):
- **Initialize** (player, mode, allocator, handler, handler argument, audio, video and user streams, messages: the
  first form builds the attribute from its arguments; it checks only the player and the allocator) and
  **Initialize2** (attribute and resource {SPURS, 0, 0, 0}: the attribute's +0x14/+0x18 and the resource's other words
  must be 0). The player (0x400 bytes): the version word 0x492000, the game's allocator copied, every event subscribed,
  one block from the allocator (boundary 8) for the audio, video and user slots (0x180, 0x238 and 0x88 bytes), the
  built-in source (0x138) and the message ring (16 bytes a message; 50 per stream and 50 when the game gives 0); the
  queue's and the player's lv2 mutex and condition pairs ("_saiqu0", "_saict0"); the AV-sync clock at +8 (200 bytes,
  lwmutex "_saiav0"; latencies 5333 us and, by mode, 16683 (0, 2), 33367 (3), 20000 (4), 40000 (5) or none; mode 7
  none at all); the built-in "x-cell-fs" source registered; the defaults (stream slots' indices and buffers, control
  thread priority 900 with 0x3000 bytes of stack, SPURS of 4 SPUs at priority 100 and PPU priority 300). Refused:
  mode 8 and up, no handler, no allocator, 16 audio or 4 video streams with an SDK of 4.0 or later.
- **Finalize**: INVALID_STATE once finalized; a booted player is told to stop (message 0xD1) and its control thread
  joined; then the source, the clock (its lwmutex destroyed, retried ten times 1 ms apart while busy), the pairs, the
  block.
- **Sources**: four protocols at most (FULLED), a name twice or NULL is INVALID_ARG. UnregisterSource never succeeds:
  libsail's test is inverted (index above the count), so it answers NOT_FOUND (0x80610710) every time.
- **Events and getters**: the event mask (types below 12, a parameter must be 0), ReplaceEventHandler (callable from
  inside the handler: the lock's EDEADLK is taken as held), descriptor count, current descriptor, paused, repeat mode
  (its 0x28-byte info when set), each stream's mute bit, under the player's lock.
- **Per-stream objects**: the audio renderer or sound adapter (one call in libsail), the video renderer or graphics
  adapter, the AU receiver: only before boot, index and NULL checks, USING when the slot has one; the object learns
  its index, the player and the clock.
- The built-in source's callbacks and file calls are internal functions that fail loudly until the player plays
  (part 3). Partly native cellSail does not mix with Sony's: a game importing any cellSail function pspocket lacks
  gets libsail whole (the loader chooses by library).
Compared: 2 scripts, 179 checks: answers, the player's bytes after Initialize, Initialize2 and every mode (each
side's own code addresses in the built-in source masked), the allocator's heap, and the lv2 calls: 0 differences.

Part 3, descriptors' fields and capabilities (runtime/hle/src/cellSailDescriptor.cpp): a descriptor (the player makes
it) holds the stream type (0 PAMF, 1 MP4, 2 AVI), URI, media info, flags, player, source, the audio, video and user
elementary stream tables (0x90, 0x78, 0x4C bytes each, a state byte first), a state byte and the stream's size.
GetStreamType/GetUri/GetMediaInfo read them; SetParameter (1 with 0 or 8: flag bit 0) and SetAutoSelection only while
the descriptor is new (INVALID_STATE after); ClearEs takes an elementary stream from state 1 back to 0 (the descriptor
open at most; INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE by the player's stream counts); DestroyDatabase answers UNSUPPORTED_STREAM past type
2. The capability bits: MP4 0xF0, AVI 0x70 with flag bit 0 else 0xF0, PAMF the source's GetCapabilities answer (asked
with the descriptor's type by GetCapabilities, with 0 by InquireCapability, which adds 0x80 when flag bit 0 is clear).
GetCapabilities turns them into the kind (1, or 0x75 without flag bit 0), start and seek flags and terminus (0xE with
bit 0x10, else 8); InquireCapability checks an inquiry (start, seek and terminus types, flags, count, positions)
against them and the stream's size, with libsail's whole decision tree, and on SDKs after 0x21FFF only for an open
descriptor (state 1, 3 or 5). Compared: 839 checks (700 inquiries from a fixed pseudo-random spread): 0 differences.

Part 4, the adapters' set-up, formats and AV sync (runtime/hle/src/cellSailAdapters.cpp): the sound adapter (0xD8
bytes) and graphics adapter (0x100) are libsail's own renderers (their renderer callback tables libsail's, here hidden
variables of internal functions that fail loudly until a later part plays) with the game's callbacks (3 and 5) and
argument, an lwmutex ("_saisa0", "_saiga0"), a state (7, 6 finalized; Finalize destroys the lwmutex again every 5 ms
while busy, ten times at most), the format they deliver (GetFormat: the sound one's +2 is 0x100) and the one the game
prefers, the first PTS (PtsToTimePosition: milliseconds from it, INVALID_STATE before one). UpdateAvSync feeds the
player's clock from the game's (frame, time) reports: audio's time per frame (in 1/256 when the clock has a latency)
first after 100 ms, then kept within a quarter of the last and smoothed by a quarter; video's after 8 frames, then
kept from 15001 to 149999 us; each with the record's frame mark giving the next frame's time. Compared on players of
modes 0 and 7: 107 checks (answers, the adapters' and the clock's bytes): 0 differences.

Part 5, the AU receiver's set-up and the player's parameters: AuReceiverInitialize takes no game callbacks in fw 4.92
(both optional arguments must be NULL, else INVALID_ARG): an lwmutex "_saiau0", libsail's 9 stream callbacks copied
in, state 1; Finalize marks its stream 8, destroys the lwmutex and clears the 0x200 bytes. SetParameter (before boot
only; 36 parameters, unknown ones accepted) and GetParameter as libsail's three jump tables: player-wide values
(control thread priority and stack, SPURS SPUs, priorities and exit flag, the file source thread's priority and stack
(read back as 0x4B0 and 0x1000 when 0), the queue's length less 50, two buffer settings), per-stream values by index
(audio 12, 14, 15, 26, 32; video 0, 16, 18-20, 23-25, 27, 30, 31, 35, with their range checks; video 0 takes a
structure of two bounded fields or clears the stream's settings), and parameter 33, the built-in source's file calls
(the game's structure of 0x28 bytes with every call present, or NULL for libsail's own). Compared: every parameter
set with six values and read back at three indices: 2596 checks over the five scripts, 0 differences (parameter
33's copy of libsail's own calls masked: each side's code).

Part 6, Boot and the control thread (runtime/hle/src/cellSailControl.cpp): Boot (state 0, every stream with its
renderer, adapter or AU receiver, else INVALID_STATE) keeps the game's argument, sets state 1 and starts
"_libsail-control" with the player's priority and stack. The thread records its frame (+0x3C8), marks Boot running
(+0x250), takes the player's lock, makes SPURS of its own when the game gave none (4 KB from the game's allocator,
revision 2, SDK 0x330000, the player's SPU count, priorities and exit flag, "_libsail" its prefix), sets up the dmux
pipeline (+0x300), sets state 2 and sends the events libsail sends (state changed to 2 when subscribed; Boot
completed with its argument when subscribed), signals +0x24C and releases the lock, then runs the message loop:
+0x19C 200 while it waits, the queue taken under its mutex with 3 s waits on its condition, the message dispatched by
its code's low 16 bits (a completion, code 0, by its handle's). Stop (0xD1, Finalize's) ends the loop; the thread takes
the lock again, puts the player's descriptors back to open, closes the dmux pipeline (state 0xC), releases the lock,
finalizes and frees its own SPURS, sets state 10 and exits. A failure in set-up sends state 9 and Boot completed with
the error. The event handler gets a stack depth record (+0x3D0) as libsail keeps it. Players with streams, descriptors
and every other message stop the process with what was asked (later parts). Compared with libsail: a stream without
its renderer refused, a player without streams booted on its own SPURS with events subscribed, booted again (refused),
finalized; one on the game's SPURS without events: the answers, both control threads' lv2 calls (each thread's in
order, keyed by lv2 thread ID: the host reuses threads), the handler's records and the players, 0 differences over 2629
checks in the six scripts (+0x3C8/+0x3D0 masked: stack addresses; the handler's r7: past its four arguments).

Part 7, descriptors made and held by the control thread: the game's commands (Create, Add, Remove) go through libsail's
command protocol: under the player's lock a reply record {the answer's address, the calling thread's ID} is posted at the
queue's head with the command, the caller waits once on the player's condition (+0x24C), and the control thread, under
the lock, stores the answer and wakes that thread with sys_cond_signal_to (a failed signal is an error event and a fatal
one, the lock kept, as libsail does). Create makes 0x100 bytes plus 0xC0 per stream (the audio, video and user tables:
0x90, 0x78 and 0x4C bytes per entry, each holding its index and the descriptor) from the player's allocator, takes
types 0 to 2 only (an unknown type's memory is kept: libsail checks after allocating), heads it {1|0x81|0x82, 0, 0},
puts it first on the player's list (+0x3BC, linked through +0x34) and gives it to the game. Add makes it the current
(+0x22C) or the next (+0x228) descriptor (not the current one twice; FULLED past two), created ones becoming 2 and open
ones 3, and answers the count; Remove takes the last added back (USING while it plays, state 5), 2 back to created and
others to open, and answers the count left; Destroy is posted without waiting (INVALID_STATE before Boot) and frees a
descriptor of the player's list (an open one would be closed first: a later part). Errors reach the game as event 1
after libsail's "error 0x%X" print. At the player's end the descriptors it holds go back to created or open and every
descriptor on its list is freed (state 6). Compared with libsail on a booted player without streams: every refusal,
add, remove and destroy above, and the allocator's memory (the player's block with its queue, the descriptors) now
