## D-591 · 2026-10-10 · The codec cores' operation tables and PTS functions, pspocket's own cores behind them

On a PS3 each of cellAdec's codec core modules exports the table Sony's libadec calls it through (CellAdecCoreOps,
twelve function descriptors) and, where its module corrects a missing PTS itself, a _SceAdecCorrectPtsValue_* function;
RPCS3 exports both for the cores it has (cellAdec.cpp's LPCM, cellAtracXdec.cpp's four ATRAC3plus tables). pspocket's
own cores (D-197, D-198, D-577 to D-579) were reachable only from its own front end. Each is now also offered as its
module's exports (runtime/hle/src/adec_tables.cpp), for Sony's modules and any other caller:

- **The tables**, each a variable of its library (Registry::add_variables, as D-567), 48 bytes laid out when first
  linked, under RPCS3's names and NIDs: g_cell_adec_core_ops_lpcm (cellAdec, 0x369D9D3A), the four
  g_cell_adec_core_ops_atracx* (cellAtracXdec), and in a build with FFmpeg (as their cores) _Mp3 (cellMP3dec), _mpmcl1
  (cellMPL1dec), _mpmc (cellM2BCdec), _M4Aac, _M4Aac2ch and _M4Aac2chmod (cellM4AacDec, cellM4AacDec2ch,
  cellM4AacDec2chmod), _ac3 (cell_libac3dec) and _atrac3 (cellAtrac3dec). Each entry is the descriptor of an internal
  function of cellAdec, _CellAdecCoreOp<operation>_<core> (RPCS3's names; its NID nid_of of the name), which calls the
  core's own code, the AdecCore pspocket's front end calls: nothing is decoded twice. Being internal, they are no
  functions of the cores' libraries: cellAtracXdec still has none on the host (host_has), so the comparison of
  ATRAC3plus with Sony's libadec and libatxdec (D-198, D-193's harness) still runs Sony's core.
- **The ABI** (RPCS3 cellAdec.h). getMemSize writes CellAdecAttr's workMemSize; open and openExt take the core's handle,
  the four notifications as (function, argument) pairs and the resource (openExt also the SPURS resource); getVersion
  writes the version and returns nothing; getPcmHandleNum and getBsiInfoSize return their numbers; the others as the
  front end calls the core. A pointer RPCS3 ensure()s that is not guest memory (the core's handle, for its context's
  size; the resource, parameters, access unit information, attributes, version) and a notification without a function
  are logged and refused with CELL_ADEC_ERROR_ARG (D-042).
- **The notifications.** A core opened through its table notifies the functions its open was given, as guest calls with
  RPCS3's arguments: AUDONE (PCM handle, argument), PCMOUT (PCM handle, PCM address, size, argument, a pointer to the
  information block's address, the PTS type, the error), ERROR (error, argument), SEQDONE (argument). pspocket's front
  end opens its cores with its own four functions marked direct (CoreNotify), and the core calls them as C++, as
  before. A core keeps the pairs where its context has them and, in a word its layout leaves unused, whether they are
  guest functions: LPCM at +0x114, ATRAC3plus at +0x12C, the cores on FFmpeg at +0x1A0 (CoreNotifier, store_notify). A
  core's thread function is linked at its first open, as a process driving a core through its table need not import
  cellAdec.
- **The PTS functions**, with FFmpeg: _SceAdecCorrectPtsValue_mpmcl1 (cellMPL1dec), _mpmc (cellM2BCdec), _M4Aac,
  _M4Aac2ch and _M4Aac2chmod (cellM4AacDec, cellM4AacDec2ch, cellM4AacDec2chmod), RPCS3's NIDs: (core handle,
  CellCodecTimeStamp*) corrected by the core's own rule (AdecCore::correct_pts, D-577: its last PTS plus that frame's
  length), CELL_OK. Half a timestamp answers FATAL, as the front end's rule does; a core of another codec or a pointer
  that is not guest memory is logged and FATAL. MP3, AC-3 and ATRAC3 have none (libadec corrects theirs with its fixed
  steps).
- **Which serves (D-563, D-175).** The cores on FFmpeg are not compared with Sony's yet: their eight libraries are
  firmware-first, so a game or firmware module importing one gets Sony's module where the system software has it, and
  pspocket's table and PTS function where it does not. The compared cores are not marked: LPCM (cellAdec, D-197) and
  ATRAC3plus (cellAtracXdec, D-198). What the loader does with an importer of theirs: a game's import of one of their
  tables is the host's (the host exports it and the library is not forced, D-503), and so is a firmware module's
  (D-593); libadec.sprx and libatxdec.sprx are not loaded for them. With --lle, Sony's serve, as for any library. In a
  build without FFmpeg there is no ATRAC3plus table of pspocket's and libatxdec serves as before.
- **pspocket's own front end** still calls its cores directly. core_for asks first for the table cellAdec's imports
  linked, and the loader links only firmware modules' exports there (LleModules::link_host_imports): with the system
  software a firmware-first codec decodes on Sony's core, without it on pspocket's, called directly; pspocket's own
  tables never come back to it the long way through its imports. LPCM and ATRAC3plus have no imported table (cellAdec
  imports none, D-198) and stay on pspocket's cores. A test links pspocket's own table as an import to drive a core
  through it as libadec would; open keeps the table in the context (core_ops), so the decoder stays on it.

Tests: tests/hle/test_adec.cpp (LPCM's table driven as libadec drives a core, its twelve entries called as guest code
and the notifications coming back as guest calls: every answer, item, information block, callback and PCM output the
same as through the direct path; the four ATRAC3plus tables likewise, the error frame's notification and cellAdecOpenEx
reaching openExt), tests/hle/test_adec_cores.cpp (each core on FFmpeg through its table the same as directly: MP3,
MPEG layer I with its PTS function, ATRAC3, and with the tests' encoders layer II, the three AAC tables and AC-3; the
PTS functions on a core's context: none before stays none, a given PTS kept, a missing one corrected by 720 and then
1152 ticks, the 33-bit carry, and the three refusals), tests/hle/test_lle.cpp (the markers; a synthetic firmware module
importing LPCM's table gets pspocket's with and without the core's module installed, one importing MP3's gets
pspocket's without and Sony's with, a game likewise; cellAdec's own imports get Sony's MP3 table or nothing, never
pspocket's, and no LPCM or ATRAC3plus table), tests/hle/test_hle.cpp (the HLE NID check now covers the variables too:
each NID is nid_of of its name or the NID database's). scripts/progress.py's own library functions: 5,654 before, 5,673
after (of 6,625): the 13 tables, the 5 PTS functions and D-592's table.

## D-592 · 2026-10-10 · cellDmuxPamf's table on pspocket's PAMF core; the raw elementary stream core stays Sony's

On a PS3 libdmux calls the PAMF core only through the table libdmuxpamf exports, g_cell_dmux_core_ops_pamf
(CellDmuxCoreOps, fourteen descriptors), as RPCS3 does (cellDmuxPamf.cpp); pspocket's cellDmux calls its core directly
(D-194). The core is now offered the same way (runtime/hle/src/cellDmuxPamf.cpp, dmux.hpp):

- **The table**: a variable of cellDmuxPamf (0x28B2B7B2, RPCS3's REG_VNID), 56 bytes laid out when first linked, whose
  entries are descriptors of internal functions of cellDmux under RPCS3's names (_CellDmuxCoreOpQueryAttr to
  _CellDmuxCoreOpResetStreamAndWaitDone, each NID nid_of of its name): RPCS3's checks of the caller's pointers, then the
  core_* function pspocket's cellDmux calls itself. QueryAttr writes CellDmuxPamfAttr; QueryEsAttr writes
  CellDmuxPamfEsAttr whatever its answer, as RPCS3. Being internal, they are no functions of cellDmuxPamf, so the
  comparison of cellDmux with Sony's libdmux (D-194) still runs Sony's libdmuxpamf.
- **Open and EnableEs** keep the caller's notifications where libdmuxpamf keeps them: the CellDmuxPamfHandle (0x1C) at
  the start of the demuxer's memory (its DmuxPamfContext, then demux done, program end code and fatal error; the program
  end code's function only when the PAMF specific information asks for that callback) and the CellDmuxPamfEsHandle
  (0x14) at the start of the stream's (its DmuxPamfElementaryStream, then access unit found and flush done). The handle
  is given back whatever the answer, as RPCS3. A notification RPCS3 requires without a function or an argument, a
  pointer that is not guest memory, or memory not aligned to 16 bytes or too small for its handle: PAMF's ARG (D-042).
- **A demuxer opened through the table** notifies those functions, as guest calls on its PPU thread with RPCS3's
  arguments: demux done and fatal error (the handle, CELL_OK, the argument), program end code (the handle, the
  argument), flush done (the stream's handle, the argument), and access unit found (the stream's handle, a DmuxAuInfo,
  the argument). The DmuxAuInfo (0x30 bytes, on the thread's stack) is the CellDmuxAuInfo (address, size, auMaxSize 0,
  random access, user data, PTS, DTS) and the address and size of the unit's specific information, which is copied
  into the stream's DmuxPamfElementaryStream (+0x34) as libdmuxpamf does. An answer other than 0 means a full queue: the
  unit is reported again after a release. pspocket's cellDmux is still notified directly.
- **createThread and joinThread.** libdmuxpamf's open starts the demuxer's thread, and so do RPCS3's and pspocket's;
  RPCS3's createThread starts another on the same context, which could only race the first for its events (libdmux
  never calls it). pspocket keeps the one thread: createThread answers CELL_OK, logged once. joinThread (RPCS3: every
  stream let go, the SPU side closed, the PPU thread joined) stops it; after it only close is taken (anything else is
  logged and FATAL: the SPU side is gone and would never answer), a second joinThread is CELL_OK, logged, and close does
  not join again. The thread's function is linked when the first demuxer opens, as a process driving the core through
  its table need not import cellDmux.
- **No firmware-first marker**: the core is compared with libdmuxpamf (D-194). A game or firmware module importing the
  table gets pspocket's (D-593); libdmuxpamf.sprx is not loaded for it.
- **The raw elementary stream core** (g_cell_dmux_core_ops_raw_es, 0x9728A0E9, with which libraries other than libdmux
  demux a bare elementary stream) is left to Sony's module, for two reasons. Its table is cellDmuxPamf's too, and which
  implementation serves is decided per library: marked firmware-first, as an uncompared core must be (D-563), Sony's
  module would take the compared PAMF table with it wherever the system software is installed; unmarked, an uncompared
  raw core of pspocket's would displace Sony's. And pspocket's demultiplexer has RPCS3's raw path only on its SPU side
  (dmux_pamf.cpp): the PPU side's raw variants (RPCS3's _CellDmuxCoreOpSetStream, QueryEsAttr and EnableEs with raw_es:
  the filter read as a raw stream's, no specific information, other memory sizes) are not written, and none of it has
  run or been compared. So a module importing the raw table gets Sony's libdmuxpamf where it is installed, which then
  serves that module's PAMF table too (one implementation of a library, D-175); without the system software the raw
  table stays unlinked and is listed. To do, on the Mac: the raw variants, compared with libdmuxpamf's raw core, then
  the table exported, unmarked.

Tests: tests/hle/test_dmux.cpp (the table driven from guest code as libdmux drives it, in a process that does not import
cellDmux, with guest notifications that log their arguments: the same access units as cellDmux's own run hands the game,
to their addresses, sizes, timestamps, random access flags, user data and specific information, each notification with
RPCS3's arguments; the table's entries, the attributes, both handles and the notifications kept in them; the refusals
(ARG, UNKNOWN_STREAM); flush, reset, disable and close; createThread and joinThread).

## D-593 · 2026-10-10 · The loader: a module's imported variable the host exports is the host's, as a function is

LleModules::choose took a firmware module's imported variable from a candidate module or from one that could join; its
comment still said "the host exports none", from before D-503. A function import already went to the host when the
host has it and its library is not forced, and so did the game's own imported variables (D-503) and load_file's
linking of a module's (the host's variable when the library's module is not chosen). With the codec cores' tables on
the host (D-591, D-592), a firmware module importing one would have brought in the core's module although the host
serves the table, or, where no module exports it or that module could not join, had a gap listed that load_file then
linked to the host's variable.

- A firmware module's imported variable now comes, as a function does, from a candidate module, else from the host when
  it exports it and its library is not forced (a forced library's module joins and serves it, D-563), else from a
  module that can join; one that nothing exports stays unlinked and is listed, as before (D-177).
- The libraries whose variables the modules chosen link to the host are the host's for the rest of the process, as the
  libraries of their functions are (host_linked_): a module of one of them can no longer join later, so one
  implementation serves each library.

Tests: tests/hle/test_lle.cpp (D-591's test: a synthetic module importing LPCM's table is chosen with no gap and gets
pspocket's table, with and without the core's module installed; one importing MP3's firmware-first table brings in
Sony's module where it is installed). The other loader tests pass unchanged.

## D-597 · 2026-10-10 · The comparisons with Sony's modules, ready for the Mac: the firmware-first libraries, the codec cores, cellVdec's new codecs

The firmware-first libraries (D-563: libmixer, cellVpost, cellKey2char, cellPngEnc, cellFiber), the video codec cores'
version queries (D-575) and cellVdec's DivX 3.11, VC-1 and MVC (D-588 to D-590) were made without Sony's modules; each
is to be compared with its module on the Mac before its marker goes. The comparisons are now written, so a session on
the Mac only has to run them, read the differences and fix them.

**The suite** (tests/hle/compare_util.hpp, over firmware_compare.hpp). Each comparison sends the same calls with the
same synthetic inputs to pspocket's library and to Sony's module, each half in a fresh process (fixture), reaching the
exports as a game does: a guest call through the export's descriptor, Sony's module's own in its half, pspocket's linked
stub in the other. The inputs are the libraries' own tests': the mixer's notify callback and players
(test_libmixer.cpp), the colours and windows of test_vpost.cpp, test_imgenc.cpp's pictures and chunks, test_fiber.cpp's
scripts (their routine now in fiber_script.hpp, shared by both tests) and test_vdec_codecs.cpp's streams
(vdec_streams.hpp: the same encoders and pictures; test_vdec_codecs.cpp keeps its own copies while other work changes
cellVdec's tests, and can include it later).
What a game can see is written as observations:
- lines, compared one for one by their key, realigned when one half has a line the other lacks: answers and error codes,
  output words, structures' bytes (as "hex:" values, whose differing bytes the report names);
- numbers, within a stated tolerance (relative past 1, absolute below);
- data (pictures, samples, decoded PNG pixels) under a rule: exact; within N steps a byte, with an alpha channel exact;
  or big-endian floats within a tolerance;
- notes, listed where the halves differ but not counted, for what may legitimately differ (timing, compressed sizes,
  opaque objects' bytes, the exports of Sony's module that pspocket lacks).
The report at the end of each comparison: "N of M observations differ", the first 80 differences, each as "the step:
pspocket's value | Sony's", the differences counted by group for the large tables, the notes, and the values within the
tolerance but not equal (as test_vdec.cpp counts RGB one step off). A half that makes no progress for a minute prints
its last step on stderr, every minute, so a module stuck on something pspocket's lv2 lacks names where.

**Running it on the Mac**, with the system software installed:
`PSPOCKET_TEST_DEV_FLASH=$PWD/inventory/firmware/installed/dev_flash build/host/tests/hle/test_hle "[compare]"`, or one
library with "[compare][libmixer]", "[compare][vpost]", "[compare][key2char]", "[compare][pngenc]", "[compare][fiber]",
"[compare][codec-cores]" or "[compare][vdec]" (for the last, scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh first, D-588: without the VC-1
decoder or the tests' encoders those parts skip). PSPOCKET_COMPARE_PRINT=1 also prints both halves' observations in full
(to read Sony's answers); PSPOCKET_COMPARE_TRACE=1 prints each call before it is made and each observation as it comes,
so the last line before a crash (a module faulting) names the call. The comparisons are hidden ([.]): ctest and the
gate, which sets PSPOCKET_TEST_DEV_FLASH, leave them out while they are expected to differ, so they hold up no build.
When a library matches, its test loses the [.] together with the library's firmware-first marker (a decision of its
own), and joins the gate as D-193's comparisons have. Without the firmware each skips. PSPOCKET_COMPARE_SELF=1 runs
pspocket's half twice instead, the second in Sony's place, so the whole comparison runs anywhere: the halves must agree
(a half that does not repeat itself would show differences on the Mac that are not Sony's), and each test checks
pspocket's own values against its unit tests' (a few dozen checks each). What needs no firmware is checked in every
ctest run: each function a comparison calls is in the NID database under its library with that name, is pspocket's
own, and the library is still firmware-first.

**What each compares, and what a difference means.**
- **libmixer** (test_libmixer_compare.cpp; both halves over pspocket's cellAudio): every answer before cellAudioInit and
  after; the audio port the mixer opens (its number, state, channels, blocks and size); the AAN handle and port numbers;
  the notify callback's rules and each call's argument, tag and sample count in order; strips with levels, an expression
  in dB and a mute, a bus and a looped player, heard at the speakers after each change (the total level, the total mute
  and back, the player stopped) and found in the port's ring with the mixer paused (each distinct block's eight
  channels); pause and play again; the timestamps after the first (within 0.1%); Finalize and a second mixer. Then the
  players: a stereo wave once at double speed, looped from frame 90, at half speed, held at its end (ONESHOT_CONT),
  SetParam while playing, a start past the wave's end, each first block at the speakers frame by frame; and the three
  utilities over a range of arguments (GetLevelFromDBIndex from -200 to 200, the first thing D-563 named to check).
  Samples within 1e-6 count as the same: the inputs are exact in binary, but Sony's may sum them in another order or
  scale them once more. The latency after Start and the callback count are notes (thread timing). A difference is in
  pspocket's mixing, port or callback (libmixer.cpp): RPCS3's speed change and loop handling are its guess, and so are
  the parameters RPCS3 ignores.
- **cellVpost** (test_vpost_compare.cpp): QueryAttr over 17 configurations (its attribute: Sony's memory size, delay and
  versions, where pspocket has RPCS3's); Open with eight bad resources (pspocket only checks that one is there),
  OpenEx's refusals, Close; Exec of test_vpost.cpp's 17 flat colours, ramps in each matrix, range and chroma siting,
  ramps, edges and impulses enlarged and reduced with each scaler type, the tiny cases, windows (inside, outside, past
  the edge), the eight exec types with the three interpolation types, three alphas, and Exec's checks, with the picture
  information each time; a YUV handle: copies, a flat picture enlarged, ramps and impulses scaled. Same-size RGBA
  within one step a sample (the arithmetic is the SPU program's), scaled pictures within two (its filter's taps and
  rounding are not known), the alpha, YUV copies, untouched pixels outside a window and the bytes past the output
  exactly. A difference in the scaled pictures means another filter: the impulse pictures show Sony's taps to copy.
- **cellKey2char** (test_key2char_compare.cpp): Open before and after cellKbInit, on a zeroed handle and on garbage;
  the mode and arrangement checks; GetChar's checks; every one of 95 key codes in all 25 arrangements and the three
  modes, with ten modifier and LED combinations (four in the native modes), each opened afresh: GetChar's answer,
  charNum, processed and characters, where *charCode points (written when it changes), and the 128-byte handle after
  each call that may change it; a handle marked broken (byte 0 = 255, RPCS3's reading); Close. A difference in the
  characters is a layout table or the native modes' composition (pspocket types them as the English one, D-565); one in
  the handle, where Sony's keeps its state; one in *charCode's place, where its buffer is.
- **cellPngEnc** (test_pngenc_compare.cpp): QueryAttr over twelve configurations; Open's and OpenEx's refusals and the
  handle; test_imgenc.cpp's pictures in every colour space and depth, palettes with and without PLTE, with hIST and
  bKGD, the texts (tEXt, zTXt, iTXt), time, gamma, physical size and an sPLT, the colour chunks (cHRM, sRGB, sBIT, bKGD,
  oFFs, sCAL, tRNS), iCCP, a 64x64 picture under each filter set and level; the queue (four waiting, WaitForInput and a
  fifth once all four are encoded, oldest first, Reset, EMPTY); a buffer too small; a file and one that cannot be made;
  EncodePicture's checks; an encoder on the SPUs. Each stream: its information (every field but streamSize exactly, and
  streamSize its own PNG's length), whether it is a whole PNG with good CRCs, its chunks in order, every chunk but IDAT
  byte for byte (zTXt's, iTXt's and iCCP's compressed parts as libpng reads them back), the pixels as libpng decodes
  them, and the bytes past it untouched. The compressed bytes may legitimately differ (zlib's version and settings and
  libpng's filter choice are the encoder's own; Sony's is libpng 1.2.8 on zlib 1.2.3, D-199) and give the same pixels:
  the IDAT size, the zlib header and each row's filter are notes, to read Sony's choices off. A difference in the
  chunks, the pixels or the queue's answers is pspocket's to fix.
- **cellFiber** (test_fiber_compare.cpp): test_fiber.cpp's eight scenarios, each in its own process, the scripts
  calling the half's own exports: the log (the order fibers and contexts ran in, with each call's answer made inside
  them), every answer and output word (statuses, causes, the context that switched, numWorker), and the attribute
  structures as the four initializers leave them, with the SDK version and without (a game sets fields over them). The
  schedulers', fibers', contexts', worker controls' and the trace buffer's bytes are notes: the SDK keeps them opaque,
  and pspocket keeps libfiber's state on the host (D-568). Workers take fibers in their own order: only the joins'
  statuses are compared there. ConnectEventQueueToSpurs and DisconnectEventQueue are not sent (their arguments are not
  known: to read in libfiber by hand). A difference in the log is a scheduling rule (D-568 lists each choice made).
- **The codec cores** (test_codec_cores_compare.cpp): each of the six modules in a process of its own; the version and
  characteristics queries with a good, a misaligned and a null pointer, and the 24 bytes around the output (filled
  first). A pointer outside guest memory is not sent to Sony's (it would write there). The exports Sony's module has
  that pspocket lacks are a note: what is left of these libraries.
- **cellVdec's new codecs** (test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp), four families: DivX 3.11 (QueryAttrEx with and without its
  information and RPCS3's checks, six pictures with and without SetFrameRate, a frame size given smaller and larger than
  the stream's, 720x576 without the information); MPEG-4 part 2 as DivX and as MPEG-4 with two pixel aspect ratios;
  VC-1 (QueryAttrEx for levels 0 to 10 and with its information, OpenEx of the simple and main profiles,
  test_vdec_codecs.cpp's streams: I and skipped pictures, range mapping with pulldown, an access unit before the
  headers, a new sequence header, the decode modes); MVC and MVC2 (two views in each access unit, the views apart, and
  the base view alone as H.264, to read MVC's differences against). For each decoder: every answer, the callbacks in
  order, the pictures announced before EndSeq (the lag), and for each picture its item, the places of the item and its
  frame buffer, its information block at the codec's size by RPCS3's attributes (DivX 0x20, DivX 3.11 0x18, MPEG-4 0x38,
  VC-1 0x170, MVC 0x214), its frame buffer (Sony's layout as known from H.264) and its samples. VC-1 and MVC must be
  exact (VC-1's inverse transform is exact by the standard, the MVC pictures are I_PCM); DivX and MPEG-4 part 2 within
  one step a sample (the standard lets each decoder round its IDCT, IEEE 1180). The differences answer the questions
  D-588 to D-590 left: the information blocks' layouts, range mapping, access units before a sequence header, what
  libmvcdec gives of the second view, the frame buffers and the lag for these codecs.

Found while writing it: a picture with more than one text chunk aborted cellPngEnc's stream (D-598).

Tests, here (no firmware): the seven name checks pass in ctest; `test_hle "[compare]"` skips all of them;
PSPOCKET_COMPARE_SELF=1 runs every comparison, both halves agree (key2char 43,641 observations, vpost 536, pngenc 614,
libmixer 119 and 460, fiber 216 over its eight scenarios, the codec cores 42, vdec 1,127 over its four families) and the
sanity checks pass. Under ThreadSanitizer (D-571's build), in that mode, only cellVdec's comparison reports races, the
ones test_vdec_codecs.cpp has too: vdec_test_util.hpp's waits read the callback log while the decoder thread's guest
callback writes it with the interpreter's plain stores. They do no harm here (the counts only pace the waits, and the
log's entries are read after SEQDONE); the cellVdec tests are not in D-571's set.

## D-598 · 2026-10-10 · cellPngEnc: a picture's text chunks kept where libpng's pointers find them

cellPngEnc (D-566) kept the strings of a picture's text chunks in a vector and handed libpng pointers into them until
png_set_text took them all. Each text chunk reserved room for four more strings, which moved the strings already there;
a short string (a keyword: its characters inside the string object) moved its characters with it, so with a second text
chunk libpng read the first's keyword from freed memory and refused it ("tEXt: invalid keyword"): the stream of any
picture with more than one text chunk aborted (STREAM_ABORT). The unit test had one text chunk; the comparison suite's
pspocket half, with tEXt, zTXt and iTXt in one picture, found it (D-597). The strings are in a deque now, which never
moves a string it holds. Test: tests/hle/test_imgenc.cpp, three text chunks with short keywords and texts in one
picture, read back with libpng (before the fix the stream aborted).

## D-607 · 2026-10-10 · cellRudp's life and sys_crashdump's log areas, firmware-first; RPCS3 has nothing more to port

A scan of the grey cells (scripts/progress.py's missing functions, 751 on 2026-10-10 with D-591 to D-596 in) against
RPCS3's bodies (runtime/hle/scripts/gen_rpcs3_stubs.py's test of a stub, over every module of
rpcs3/Emu/Cell/Modules) found five functions RPCS3 implements that pspocket did not. They are now pspocket's, and their
two libraries firmware-first (D-563), no Sony module having been at hand:
- **cellRudp** (runtime/hle/src/cellRudp.cpp): Init (a second one ALREADY_INITIALIZED; CellRudpAllocator's two
  descriptors kept, or the library's own allocator without one), End and SetEventHandler (NOT_INITIALIZED before Init;
  End forgets the allocator and the handler), RPCS3's checks and error codes; per process. An allocator that is not
  guest memory is INVALID_ARGUMENT, where RPCS3 reads it unchecked. Nothing calls the allocator or the handler yet: the
  library's other 28 functions (contexts, bind, listen, read and write, polling) are bare stubs in RPCS3 and need
  Sony's librudp read or compared on the Mac; until then they log and fail, and where the system software is
  installed a game gets Sony's librudp whole.
- **sys_crashdump** (runtime/hle/src/sys_crashdump.cpp): sys_crash_dump_set_user_log_area and
  sys_crash_dump_get_user_log_area, the memory areas a game names for a crash dump (a 16-byte label, an address, a size:
  24 bytes), indices 0 to 127, EINVAL past 127 or with no entry, as RPCS3 has them. RPCS3 keeps nothing and its get
  writes nothing; here set keeps the 24 bytes as given and get writes them back, an index never set reading as zeros.
  pspocket makes no crash dumps. An entry that is not guest memory is EINVAL. To compare on the Mac: what Sony's get
  answers for an index never set, and whether set checks the area.
What the scan found of the other 746: 446 are stubs in RPCS3 (a log, then a constant); 283 are names RPCS3 has no
body for (sys_libc's and sys_libm's internals and the module entry points, which only PPUFunction.cpp names; the
codec cores' operation tables and the other variables); 13 are the audio cores' PTS functions for codecs pspocket has
no core for (one-line stubs in cellAdec.cpp); two are fatal in RPCS3 (cellMicStopEx, sys_lv2coredump's one); and two
have bodies D-596 already left out on purpose (cellSailSoundAdapterGetFrame gives no frame; cellSysmodule_0x59521326
needs the OpenPSID's key, D-184). So nothing else can be made from RPCS3: the remaining functions need Sony's modules
(on the Mac, with the firmware) or, for sys_libc's and sys_libm's internals, a game's own copy of the C library to
read their arguments in.
The count: 5,686 of 6,625 library functions pspocket's own before, 5,691 after.
Tests: tests/hle/test_rudp.cpp (Init with either allocator, End, the handler, every error, a process each, the rest
left to Sony's) and tests/hle/test_crashdump.cpp (set and get at both ends of the range, an entry replaced, an index
never set, each EINVAL with nothing written).

FFmpeg is optional (D-181, D-576): without build/ffmpeg/<host> the media libraries build without decoding, under
PSPOCKET_HAVE_FFMPEG. A fresh checkout before scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh has run (the Mac's first build, a cloud
session's) must still build with -DPSPOCKET_WERROR=ON and pass its tests, the decoding cases skipping. It did not:
- tests/hle/test_adec_cores.cpp did not compile under -Werror: some twenty helpers of the FFmpeg-only tests (bit
  writers, tone and energy measures, each codec's frame builders and parameter writers) sat outside the FFmpeg guards
  and went unused. Each codec's section now has its helpers and its tests under one guard; only the rule's test (the
  firmware's core first, pspocket's where none is linked) runs without FFmpeg.
- Four tests that need a decoder FFmpeg gives were not guarded and failed without it. They now SKIP with the reason:
  test_adec.cpp's ATRAC3plus flow and its comparison with Sony's core, and test_atrac.cpp's AT3+ files and its
  comparison with libatrac3plus (pspocket's ATRAC3plus core is on FFmpeg), and test_vdec.cpp's comparison with Sony's
  libvdec (pspocket's cellVdec decodes no picture without it). With FFmpeg each runs as before.

floating point, test_libm's fmax/fmin signed zeros on glibc); test_hle 620 cases, 91 of them skipped. The build with

## D-600 · 2026-10-10 · ThreadSanitizer over the day's new code: the decoders, the video codecs, PSN, the comparisons

D-584 to D-587 left the runtime with no race reports (scripts/tsan.sh). The code added since (pspocket's own audio
cores and their operation tables, D-576 to D-579 and D-591; DivX 3.11, VC-1 and MVC in cellVdec, D-588 to D-590; PSN
content, D-580 to D-583; the unverified Ext functions, D-594 to D-596) was swept the same way: every group of
scripts/tsan.sh (core, ppu, spu, lv2, rsx, hle once per test file, boot) built with -DPSPOCKET_TSAN=ON and run with
scripts/tsan.supp. Three races were real and are fixed (D-601, D-602), each with a test that shows it under
ThreadSanitizer. What is left is one report in test_audio.cpp, the test's own: the test thread writes a port's guest
word with a plain store while cellAudio's thread reads it atomically, where a game's code would make that store (and
its own accesses are suppressed as the guest's, D-585). It does no harm and changes nothing in the runtime; the test
can write the word atomically when it is next changed.

## D-601 · 2026-10-10 · cellSync2's queue links and entries shared atomically; cellVdec's frame rate under its mutex

- **cellSync2's queue** (runtime/hle/src/cellSync2.cpp): a popper reads its head's link and copies the next entry out
  before its stwcx. of the head. When another popper took that head meanwhile, freed it and a pusher took it again, the
  pusher writes the link and the entry as the first reads them; the stwcx. then fails and the popper reads again, as
  libsync2's lock-free queue does on the hardware. Those were plain host loads and stores racing each other. The links
  (qu::link, qu::set_link) and the entries' words (copy_in, copy_out) are now relaxed atomics, the PPU's aligned loads
  and stores they stand for, as the mutex's owner fields are (D-587, whose helpers they now share: shared_load and
  shared_store). What orders them is libsync2's own lwarx/stwcx. and lwsync. Test: tests/hle/test_sync2.cpp, four
  pushers and four poppers on a queue two entries deep (entries freed and taken again all the time): every element
  popped once and whole, each pusher's in order; under ThreadSanitizer no report.
- **cellVdec's frame rate** (runtime/hle/src/cellVdec.cpp): the decoder's thread stored a SetFrameRate command's rate
  without the decoder's mutex, while cellVdecGetPicItem reads it under the mutex on the game's thread (the information
  block's frame rate code for MPEG-4, DivX and H.264). It is stored under the mutex now, as the rest of what GetPicItem
  reads. Found reading the decoder's thread; no test shows it (the tests take their pictures long after the command).

## D-602 · 2026-10-10 · A host variable is handed out only once it is laid out

HleProcess::link_variable placed a variable under the link mutex, recorded its address, and laid it out (zeroed, then
its initializer) after releasing the lock, since an initializer may link functions and other variables (D-531). A
second thread linking the same variable meanwhile found the address and returned it at once, so it could read the
variable unwritten: a libsync2 queue's first push read the default notifier table as zeros while the first pop laid
it out (a spurious INVAL), found by ThreadSanitizer. Each linked variable now has a once flag: the first thread lays it
out, any other waits for that before it gets the address. The initializers link no variable that links them back, so
no layout waits on itself. Test: tests/hle/test_hle.cpp, eight threads linking libsync2's notifier table at once in a
fresh process, twenty rounds, each reading its four notifiers the moment it has the table.

## D-603 · 2026-10-10 · Mutation fuzzing of pspocket's parsers of game data

A game's files are untrusted input to pspocket's own parsers: a damaged disc, a cut download, a save another version
wrote, a header a game filled wrong. Each must end in an error or a valid result, never a crash, a hang or a write
past a buffer. tests/common/mutation_fuzz.hpp takes valid inputs the tests' own writers build (synthetic, rule 1),
corrupts copies of them deterministically (one to four mutations each: bits flipped, bytes set, a run of random
bytes, the input cut or extended, a part copied over another, bytes put in or taken out, or a length, count or offset
field set to an edge value: 0, 1, all ones, the sign bit, the input's size give or take a little, its own value give
or take one, doubled) and hands each to the parser. The targets:
- test_recomp_common (test_fuzz_formats.cpp): ELF executables, PRX modules and SPU programs with their tables and
  relocations; SELF headers and SELFs decrypted with made-up keys; NPD files (SDATA, EDATA, every block layout) and
  their LZ decoder; packages installed into a temporary dev_hdd0.
- test_disc (test_fuzz_disc.cpp): ISO 9660 and Joliet discs walked and read; PARAM.SFO; a disc image as the game's
  file system with the scan of its modules.
- test_hle (test_fuzz_files.cpp, test_fuzz_images.cpp, test_fuzz_media.cpp): trophy packs, their configuration and
  TROPUSR.DAT; cellL10n's converters; fonts; the PNG, JPEG and GIF decoders; PAMF and the demuxer; the audio cores
  (MP3, MPEG layers I and II, AAC, AC-3, ATRAC3plus); the loader's executables and modules.
The writers the fuzzing shares with the ordinary tests moved to headers of their own (tests/disc/disc_writer.hpp,
tests/hle/atrac_writer.hpp, pamf_writer.hpp); tests/hle/ttf_writer.hpp writes the TrueType fonts the font fuzzing
starts from. In ctest each target runs its default number of inputs
(a few hundred to a few thousand; test_hle takes about five seconds longer) and prints one line: inputs, accepted,
refused. "[fuzz]" runs them alone; PSPOCKET_FUZZ_ITERS=<n> runs n times as many, PSPOCKET_FUZZ_SEED=<n> another
sequence (the same seed gives the same inputs), PSPOCKET_FUZZ_TRACE=1 names each input before it runs and
PSPOCKET_FUZZ_DUMP=FILE writes it, to find the one a crash came from. Run under scripts/asan.sh (D-604) as well, where
a read or write past a buffer is a report even when it does not crash. What they found is fixed in D-605.

## D-604 · 2026-10-10 · scripts/asan.sh: the memory safety sweep

As scripts/tsan.sh does for data races (D-585), scripts/asan.sh [GROUP...] [--no-build] [--no-fuzz] builds build/asan
(-DPSPOCKET_SANITIZE=ON: AddressSanitizer with LeakSanitizer, and UBSan), runs each group's tests (core, common, ppu,
spu, lv2, rsx, hle, disc, game, codesign, codegen, boot; test_hle once per test file, so a file's crash stays its own)
with every check reporting, the fuzzing included, and prints one line per group: its reports, their distinct places
(scripts/asan_report.py) and how its tests ended. Logs in build/asan-logs/<group>/. Suppressions, each with its reason:
scripts/asan.supp (LeakSanitizer: the lifted SPU programs' dispatch tables, kept for the process's life on purpose,
D-231) and scripts/ubsan.supp (FreeType 2.2.1, third party and built as it is: its function pointer casts, shifts of
negative values and empty-array arithmetic). Undefined behaviour in pspocket's own code is fixed, not suppressed.
The first sweep (before D-605's fixes): core, common, ppu, lv2, rsx, disc, codesign and boot no report; spu 9 (its
interpreter's address overflow, and the SPU programs' tables); hle 84 at 62 places (FreeType's, the tables again, a
null pointer to memcpy in sys_io, cellPngEnc's palette rows read past the picture). After D-605 and the suppressions
the sweep is to be run again in full (`scripts/asan.sh`), the second time with PSPOCKET_FUZZ_ITERS raised, and what it
reports fixed the same way: that run was cut short with the session.

## D-605 · 2026-10-10 · What the fuzzing and the sweep found, fixed

Each with a test that shows it (rule 7):
- **SELF** (recomp/common/src/self_decrypt.cpp): an ELF's offsets and sizes come from the file; one that puts a segment
  past 1 GB, or claims to inflate past what deflate can make of its bytes (1032 to 1), is refused before the ELF is
  allocated, where it threw or wrapped. **NPD** (npd.cpp): a compressed file's block stored whole but longer than a
  block is refused (RPCS3 stops there too), where it wrote past the block. **PRX placement** (prx_place.cpp): a
  segment past the 32-bit address space is refused, not cut to its low word. **Hashes** (hash.cpp): an empty update
  passes memcpy no null pointer. Tests in tests/common.
- **The loader** (runtime/loader/src/lle.cpp, loader.cpp): a PRX's module information, its export entries with their
  NID and address tables, and its import entries and tables are read only where guest memory is committed (a load
  refused, or the walk of the imports ended, logged); a REF's target is checked to its last byte. Test: test_lle.
- **The SPU interpreter** (runtime/spu/src/interpreter.cpp): LQD and STQD's address was a signed sum that overflows
  for a base past the largest int; it wraps now, as the SPU's adder and the lifter do. Test: test_interp_branch_mem.
- **The JPEG decoder** (runtime/hle/src/jpeg_decoder.cpp): a scan naming a Huffman table past the four, a progressive
  band past the block or an approximation out of range, and a table whose counts overflow their code lengths are
  refused as libjpeg refuses them (jdhuff.c, jdphuff.c), where they indexed past the decoder's tables. Test:
  test_jpgdec.
- **cellAdec's AC-3 core** (adec_ac3.cpp): the information block's raw header bytes (8 from byte 5) were copied from a
  unit of any size, past the end of a short one; the bytes it lacks are zeros now. Test: test_adec_cores, a unit
  ending where guest memory does.
- **cellPngEnc** (cellPngEnc.cpp): a palette picture's rows fell to RGBA's four components, reading four bytes of the
  picture for each one-byte index, past its end on the last row. Shown by test_imgenc's palette pictures under
  scripts/asan.sh.
- **sys_io** (sys_io.cpp): io_printf with no string passed memcpy a null pointer.
- **cellAdec's ATRAC3plus core** (adec_atracx.cpp): a frame is copied whole from its unit's start, as libatxdec copies
  it, also when the unit is shorter; a unit at the end of guest memory made the copy read past it, a host crash. Such
  a frame is now an error (ATX_FATAL, logged, nothing out), as a decode without a configuration is. Test: the
  cellAtrac fuzzing target (test_fuzz_media.cpp), which crashed on its 98th input with the default seed.

## D-537 · 2026-10-09 · cellSpursJq and cellFiber pspocket's own (part 1: cellSpursJq, libspurs_jq's PPU side)

cellSpursJq had no implementation (RPCS3's cellSpursJq.cpp registers todo stubs; libspurs_jq.sprx ran LLE). All 63
functions are now pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/cellSpursJq.cpp), read from libspurs_jq (fw 4.92) and compared with it
running on pspocket (tests/hle/test_spurs_jq_compare.cpp).
- The SPU half stays Sony's SPU code: a job queue is a SPURS workload whose policy module (libspurs_jq's SPU program:
  it pops the commands, runs the jobs, gives descriptors back, releases semaphores, wakes waiters) runs on pspocket's
  native SPURS as any game's own policy module does (spurs_custom.cpp), unchanged. pspocket reads it at the first queue
  of a process from the user's /dev_flash/sys/external/libspurs_jq.sprx (decrypted like any firmware module) and finds
  it by shape: the module's table of contents (module info + 0x20) holds the image's size and address; the image is at
  a 128-byte boundary of the text and starts with an SPU GUID (four `ila $2`). Nothing of the module is in the
  repository. Without the system software, queue creation undoes its work and answers CELL_SPURS_JOB_ERROR_STAT (the
  call fails, nothing runs half-made).
- The queue (4 KB) is laid out where libspurs_jq lays it out: the command ring header and its waiting ring header, the
  policy module's bytes, the handle bitmap, the two "_sreJQ" event flags (128 waiter bits), the lightweight mutexes and
  condition, the descriptor pool's eight classes (free lists through the descriptors' first word, a 1 KB waiting ring
  each), the exception handler. Every update is the lwarx/ldarx-stwcx./stdcx. pair libspurs_jq makes, through the
  reservation system (the class Reserve of D-531), so the policy module's GETLLAR/PUTLLC and other PPU threads contend
  with it as on the hardware. Both pushers are libspurs_jq's: the default one (pushers in flight count themselves in
  the header, claim the next entry of their lap with a conditional store, the last one moves the write index) and the
  "submit with entry lock" one. A full ring or an empty pool class puts the caller in the waiting ring (a PPU thread on
  an event flag bit, a fiber through cellFiberPpuWaitSignal); the policy module wakes it, and a wake-up that comes first
  leaves the entry marked so nobody sleeps.
- Semaphores (a 29-bit count and one waiter), SendSignal, ports (one and several threads, with descriptor buffers) and
  port2s (copies into the pool), the exception handler setters and GetSuspendedJobSize (the job runtime's "JOBCRT Ver"
  header read from the job's binary) are libspurs_jq's to the instruction. cellSpurs, cellFiber and sysPrxForUser
  calls go to the firmware module when the process has it in place of pspocket's, else to pspocket's own.
- libspurs_jq's slips are kept, each marked in the code: creation does not clean up after a failed
  cellSpursSetExceptionEventHandler; a semaphore acquire that took event flag bit 0 never gives it back; an old-SDK
  (< 0x300000) port sync stores one word of its doubleword with stwcx.; a single-thread port sync writes the caller's r31
  low byte to the port's byte 0x17; a port initialized when Open fails keeps the handle its stack held;
  cellSpursJobQueueSetExceptionEventHandler2 is the same code as the first.
Surprises, decided as libspurs_jq does: the flags tests are rotate pairs that read as `flags & ~4` (allocate, port2 sync
and flush), `& ~7` (PushJob2, PushAndRelease, port2 push), `& ~5` (port2 job list), `& ~3` (port2 copy); SendSignal on a
waiting job also clears bit 23 with the signal count; the policy module reads the waiting ring after the command list in
whole 128-byte lines, so a depth that is not a multiple of 16 loses waiters (a test with depth 4 hung on Sony's code too:
the tests use 16).
Deviations: libspurs_jq's assertions are fatal logs with its text; objects that are not guest memory are refused with
CELL_SPURS_JOB_ERROR_INVAL and the call site logged (libspurs_jq would fault); the list of ten titles that get policy
module workarounds (the queue's +0xA0) is the module's data and is not reproduced (the PARAM.SFO read is made, no title
matches); the workload's exception handler, which libspurs_jq fills from the faulting SPU's local store, logs the queue
and calls the game's handler with the job information zeroed (pspocket's SPURS has no SPU threads and stops on a policy
module fault, so it is not reached).
Tests: a 1219-call one-thread script with SPURS workers off (every function, every argument's errors and alignments,
attributes, both pushers into full rings, pool classes, semaphores, signals, ports and port2s; 23 byte checkpoints of
the whole data area, 4.9 million bytes, and the 25 lv2 calls in order) the same as libspurs_jq's; 43 jobs (single
pushes beyond a full ring of 16, a job list, SYNC/FLUSH, port and port2 pushes and copies, blocking pool allocations
given back by the policy module, semaphores) through libspurs_jq's policy module on one SPU, 122 steps, each answer,
job output and the queue at rest the same with either PPU side, for the default pusher, the entry lock one and busy
waiting; firmware-free tests of attributes, creation without dev_flash, both pushers' ring encodings, semaphores,
signals, a port and GetSuspendedJobSize. A push costs 329 ns against libspurs_jq's 1532 ns interpreted (20000 pushes).

liblv2.sprx (fw 4.92) exports three small libraries besides sysPrxForUser, each one wrapper over an lv2 sys_ss call;
they are now pspocket's own, making the same calls with the same arguments: sysPs2Disc_BB7CD1AE(arg) is

sys_get_bd_media_id(buffer) is sys_ss_media_id(0x10001, buffer) (879) and sys_get_console_id(buffer) is

## D-901 · 2026-10-10 · cellSail's built-in file source (x-cell-fs), as libsail

Every cellSail player registers libsail's own source for the "x-cell-fs" protocol at Initialize. Part 2 of D-562 laid it
out and left its callbacks and file calls failing loudly; they are now pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/
cellSailFileSource.cpp), read from libsail.sprx (fw 4.92, its fn_1bf24..fn_1d0e0 and the reader thread's entry) and
compared with it running on pspocket (tests/hle/test_sail_source.cpp).

- **The source** (0x138 bytes in the player's block): +0 the command for the reader (-1 none), +1 the items ready, +2 the
  next to check out, +3 the next to fill, +4 the reader's state (0 ended, 1 closed, 2 open, 3 started), +8 the open
  file's descriptor, +0x10 the reader's thread ID, +0x18 its path (287 bytes on the reader's stack), +0x1C the path
  changed, +0x20 two items {buffer, size, session, 0}, +0x40 the CellSailSource it registers (its argument the source
  itself), +0xC0 an lwmutex and +0xD8 an lwcond (both "_saifs0"), +0xE0 the read size (1 MB), +0xE8 and +0xF0 a Start's
  length and position, +0xF8 its session (0 once the reader took it), +0xFC Read's arguments (on the reader's stack),
  +0x100 the file calls.
- **The file calls** are fourteen words: -1, open, a call after open (none of libsail's), close, fstat, read, lseek,
  cancel (libsail's answers 0), then none. pspocket's table had read, lseek and fstat in the wrong words; player
  parameter 33 (the game's 0x28 bytes, D-562 part 5) takes them in libsail's order. libsail's are cellFs's, the
  registers passed on as they are. A file is opened {path, 0 (read-only), &fd, 0, 0}, then the call after open, when
  the game gave one, {path, 0, fd, 0, 0}; a descriptor of 0 is CELL_SAIL_ERROR_INVALID_FD.
- **At once**: ReadSync opens the URI from its 13th character on (past "x-cell-fs://", whatever is there), stats the
  file for its size (fstat's failure ignored), seeks when the offset is not 0, reads and closes it; a short read
  answers the read's 0. GetCapabilities answers 0x71 for any stream. InquireCapability refuses start flags 1 (from a
  byte position, the only start Start takes) and takes every other: libsail's test is inverted.
- **Playing**: Makeup loads cellFs (cellSysmodule 0xE, when libsail loads modules), makes the lwmutex and lwcond and
  starts "_libsail-source_fs" (the player's file source priority and stack, 1200 and 4 KB when 0; parameters 7 and 34)
  and waits for it to run; Cleanup cancels the open file's calls, tells the reader to end (10), joins it
  (sys_ppu_thread_join, 44), frees the buffer, destroys the lwmutex and lwcond and unloads cellFs. The callbacks hand
  the reader one command at a time under the lwmutex (each waits for the last to be taken): Open (0; once taken, the
  path copied, marked changed when it is not the reader's, and the 2 MB buffer allocated from the player's allocator
  (boundary 0x80): two items of 1 MB), Start (1; only from a byte position, its position, length and session kept until
  the reader took the last start), Checkin (2), Stop (4), Close (5; the buffer freed at once), Read (7; its arguments
  written once taken), Clear (8). The open file's calls are cancelled before Stop, Close and Cleanup; Checkout takes
  the items in turn under the lock (CELL_SAIL_ERROR_FATAL with none ready); Cancel does nothing.
- **The reader** (libsail's state machine, each answer a cellSailSourceNotify*): closed, Open opens the path (or keeps
  the file a Read left open when the path did not change) and answers, open; open, Start seeks unless the position is
  the one it thinks it is at, answers 0 and starts; started, it fills an item while one is free (one read of up to 1 MB
  or the length left: the item's size and session, StreamOut) and at the length's or the file's end says InputEos and
  is open again. Stop of a started source answers 0 (open again), of an open one 1, of a closed one nothing; Close
  answers the close's result (closed), 1 when closed; Start when closed is taken without an answer; Read reads as
  ReadSync and answers. Waiting, an open source polls each second (fstat's EBADF: media state 2, the file closed, five
  seconds on opened again: media state 0); a started one without its file opens it again five seconds on (seeking to
  where it was; ENOTMOUNTED waits again); a read's EIO with fstat's EBADF is the medium gone (media state 2, the file
  closed, a session error), another read error media state 1 and a session error, read again half a second on. A
  failed lock, wait or signal ends the reader with a terminating session error.
- **Stack variables where libsail has them.** libsail hands the file calls stack variables (the descriptor, the stat
  buffer, the read count, the seek position) and keeps two of its reader's in the source (the path, Read's arguments).
  pspocket takes each from a frame of the size libsail's function makes (Frame), so they are at libsail's addresses:
  a game's file calls see the same pointers, the source the same words, and a reader started again on a reused stack
  finds what libsail's would (the path below).
- **libsail's slips, kept.** Read in the closed state keeps the file open for an Open of the same path and takes the
  position after it as the size read, not the offset and the size, so a Start from that position skips the seek and
  reads from the wrong place. Checkout does not count an item out (Checkin counts one fewer, whichever it is): a third
  checkout of two ready items gives the first again. Close frees the buffer before the reader has taken the close.
  Cleanup leaves the descriptor of a file still open in the source (the reader closed it), so the next reader's first
  Open either reuses it, closed, when the path in its stack frame is still the same, or closes it again first. A
  failing call after open leaves the file open. Without the buffer, Open clears the path and points the second item
  at 1 MB; the reader then ignores the Open (Open itself answers CELL_SAIL_ERROR_MEMORY). Closing an open source
  without a file answers the last lwcond signal's result. Stop goes on when its lock fails.
- **Where libsail would fault** (a NULL or unmapped URI, start command, capabilities or item pointer, or Read's size
  pointer), pspocket logs the call site and refuses the call with CELL_SAIL_ERROR_INVALID_ARG (D-042).
- Calls go where libsail's go: sysPrxForUser's lwmutex, lwcond, thread and string functions through `sail::lv2_lib`,
  lv2's join through `sail::sc`, cellFs, cellSysmodule and the notifications through `sail::module_call`. The file
  calls go through their descriptors (libsail's own too, as libsail calls them through its table): the cost is a
  guest call per file operation, next to a read of up to 1 MB.
- **Compared** in tests/hle/test_sail_source.cpp (`[sail]`): each script in two fresh processes with libsail loaded,
  one calling libsail's exports and one pspocket's, the source's callbacks called through the descriptors the source
  holds; a synthetic /dev_hdd0 (a PAMF header and 2.5 MB of a pattern, a file shorter than its header). Compared: the
  answers, the script's memory (the player and its source, the messages the source posted, drained from the ring of a
  player that has not booted, the items' data, a log of the game's file calls and of the allocator's frees), the
  allocator's memory (the player's block, the read-ahead buffers with what was read into them) and each thread's lv2
  calls in order. Masked: the callbacks' and libsail's file calls' words (each side's code); with a booted player the
  control thread's stack words, the handler's r7 and the commands' records in the ring (D-562's); the registers past a
  file call's arguments in its log (whatever the caller left there); and, where libsail's DescriptorOpen calls ReadSync,
  the stack variables handed to the game's calls (that caller's stack differs; called directly, they are equal).
  Scripts: DescriptorOpen through the source (makeup, ReadSync of a missing file, the header read twice, a short file,
  the capabilities, a shared source, cleanup on the last close, by the game's thread and the control thread at the
  player's end), the same through the game's file calls (one call after open failing), the reader called directly
  (every callback in every state, items across chunks to the file's end, a range, the buffer refused, Cleanup while
  started, Makeup again over the descriptor Cleanup left), the reader through the game's calls, the reader's failures
  and timeouts (the poll finding the medium gone, the file opened again five seconds on, seeks and reads failing, the
  retry half a second on), and OpenStream and CloseStream (D-562 part 13) through the source, opening and closing the
  file, and through the game's calls with the file gone (the stream not opened, CANCEL). Before the merge of D-562
  parts 9-13 the first five scripts compared with 0 differences (576 checks), the same in five runs. A test without the
  firmware runs the direct script on pspocket's side alone and checks its answers, messages and the items' data
  against the file.

## D-903 · 2026-10-10 · The loader links every host module's internal functions, whatever the game imports

Internal functions (`Function::internal`) are what pspocket's own modules hand out by address: a thread's entry (cellDmux's
demuxer, the decoders', cellSail's control and copy threads), a callback a library gives another (cellGcmCallback,
cellDmux's notifications to cellSail). The loader linked them only for the libraries the game imports, before any guest
thread runs; a function linked later, while guest threads run, is only safe for the first kPreparedChunks stub chunks.
But one host module calls into others the game need not import: a game that plays a movie through cellSail imports
cellSail, not cellDmux, cellAdec, cellVdec or cellVpost, and cellDmuxOpenEx then failed (0x80610205) for want of its
demuxer thread's descriptor (D-562 part 13; D-592 meanwhile made cellDmuxPamf link that one on demand). Now the loader
links every internal function of every registered host module (`HleProcess::link_all_internal_functions`, a couple of
hundred stub entries of the 8,192 per chunk) after the imports, so every chain of host modules finds its threads and callbacks
linked, and the on-demand links (cellDmuxPamf's, cellSail's) just find them. Libraries a game gets as Sony's modules
are unaffected (their internal functions are the module's own). Tests: the loader's boot test checks every registered
internal function has its descriptor after loading an executable that imports no cellDmux, cellDmux's among them.

## D-904 · 2026-10-10 · sys_libc's last names against a game's copy of the SDK's C library (part 1: SPU, slots)

The 132 names sys_libc and sys_libm still lacked (128 under sys_libm) were left out by D-514..D-516 because nothing
described their signatures or structures. No firmware module has the C library (one firmware function imports sys_libc:
memcpy) and no game imports it: a game links it into itself. So a game's copy is the reference: Assassin's Creed's
EBOOT (BLES00158) holds the whole library of its SDK (Dinkumware's C99 library with Sony's additions: the locale-file
machinery, the time tables, the SPU threads' local store accessors and their printf). It was read where it lies in the
executable (by its strings, its TOC slots and its calls); nothing of it is in the repository.
- The comparison fixture (tests/hle/game_executable.hpp): the executable loaded into a fresh process and never started,
  its library's functions called by address under the interpreter next to pspocket's functions of the same names in the
  same process. PSPOCKET_TEST_AC_EBOOT names the executable and PSPOCKET_TEST_AC_LIBC_MAP a file of "name 0xADDR"
  lines, both game data kept in inventory/; the tests ("[gamelibc]") skip without them. The first comparison, _Printf,
  already shows the SDK's float conversions rounding half away from zero and printing zeros past the 17th digit where
  sys_libc prints the exact value (D-905 takes printf, scanf and the parsers; D-906 the locale and time internals).
- spu_thread_read_* and spu_thread_write_* (30): lv2's sys_spu_thread_read_ls/write_ls a word at a time, as the SDK's
  library does: a char or short is the byte or halfword of its aligned word, written back by reading, changing and
  writing that word; an int, long, pointer or float is the word at the address as given (lv2 refuses a misaligned one;
  the value is then 0 where the SDK's leaves its stack's bytes); a long long or double is that word and the next, high
  first. A write answers lv2's result (the second word's for 64-bit values); read_mem reads a byte at a time into the
  caller's memory and leaves r3 as the last read's result (the id when the size is 0); write_mem writes whole words while
  more than four bytes remain and then merges the last one to four bytes into the word there, reading and writing it
  back even for none. Compared with the game's on a running SPU thread made in the test: every read at sixteen
  addresses, eighteen writes and write_mem of twelve lengths, the local store and the answers the same (r3 after a
  float or double read is what each left there, as the ABI allows).
- raw_spu_read_* and raw_spu_write_* (30): no executable seen links them, so they follow the SPU threads' ones word for
  word on a raw SPU's local store, guest memory at 0xE0000000 + 0x100000 * id (D-528), read and written directly; an
  address outside committed memory reads 0 and writes nothing, answering CELL_EFAULT.
- _get_fd and _put_fd: Sony's table of 256 descriptor slots, 0..2 holding 0..2 and the rest free (-1), under the
  library's lock 4: _get_fd(value, extra) takes the first free slot and answers its index, -1 when none is free;
  _put_fd(index) frees a slot below 256. The SDK's open and close never use it. Compared with the game's table after its
  start-up fills it.
- _Getmem(size): Dinkumware's (Plauger's) call for raw memory from the system, here the main-area allocator, never
  given back; NULL for 0 bytes or none left. The SDK's copies have none of their own (their malloc is dlmalloc, D-502).
- _Atrealloc, _Once_ctor, _Once_dtor and the _d2rv, _rv2d, _Fd2rv, _Frv2d, _Ld2rv, _Lrv2d conversions: neither game's
  executable links them and nothing describes them; they log the call and answer an error, as D-510's _Eadd and kin.
Tests: tests/hle/test_libc_spu.cpp (both families on an SPU thread and a raw SPU, the slots, _Getmem, the unknown
names), tests/hle/test_libc_spu_game.cpp (the comparisons); the SPU program builder moved to tests/hle/spu_program.hpp.

## D-908 · 2026-10-10 · AES-CTR on Apple platforms carries the counter over all 128 bits

CommonCrypto's CTR mode with kCCModeOptionCTR_BE counts in the counter's low 64 bits only and wraps there without a carry
into the high half; PolarSSL's aes_crypt_ctr (RPCS3's, and what the PS3 formats expect) counts over all 128 bits. So on
the Mac and the iPhone, where crypto.hpp's AES goes through CommonCrypto (D-580), any CTR data whose counter crosses a
64-bit boundary decrypted wrongly from that block on: PS3 packages with such an IV installed garbage names and contents
(the PKG tests failed on macOS from D-583 on, never on Linux, whose portable AES is PolarSSL's), and SP 800-38A-style
counters of all ones rolled over wrongly. aes_ctr now cuts the data where the low half would wrap and goes on from the
counter with its high half incremented and its low half 0; the portable AES was right. Tests: test_crypto's
platform-against-portable rounds add a counter whose low half wraps within the data (the all-ones case there now passes
on Apple platforms too); test_pkg's game package compares canonical paths, as test_psn does (b6ff761), since macOS's
temporary folders are reached through /var -> /private/var.

## D-909 · 2026-10-10 · scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh runs under macOS's bash 3.2

D-576 and D-577 added the EXTRA array to build-ffmpeg.sh, empty for the decoders' builds; under `set -u` bash before 4.4
calls an empty array's "${EXTRA[@]}" an unbound variable, so on the Mac (bash 3.2) the script stopped before configuring
and build/ffmpeg/macos kept the decoders of 2026-10-08, without D-588's VC-1 and DivX 3.11: cellVdec refused those
codecs (CELL_VDEC_ERROR_ARG) and test_fuzz_media's VC-1 case failed on the Mac only. The script expands it as
${EXTRA[@]+"${EXTRA[@]}"}, which every bash takes; the Mac's macos, macos-tests and ios builds were made again with it.

## D-910 · 2026-10-10 · cellSpursJq's comparison reads the pool's free lists as sets

D-537's job comparison ends with the queue at rest, each descriptor class's record among its answers. A class's free
list is a stack of blocks linked through their first words; jobs pushed with PushAndRelease give their descriptors back
from the SPU as they end, in whatever order the policy module finishes them, so which block is on top varied between
runs (class 7: head 0x110380 or 0x110000, two blocks free either way) and the test failed about one run in three with
either PPU side. It now compares each free list as its count, wake-ups and waiters and the set of its blocks; six runs in
a row agree.

## D-911 · 2026-10-11 · The comparisons with Sony's modules on the Mac: what they show (part 1)

D-597's comparisons (test_hle "[compare]"), written in a session without the firmware, ran on the Mac with the installed
system software for the first time, after FFmpeg was rebuilt with every decoder (D-909). Of eleven: the codec cores'
version queries agree; libmixer's two cannot run, firmware 4.92 shipping no module that exports libmixer (D-563 made it
from RPCS3 for that reason), and now SKIP saying so (compare_util.hpp require_firmware_module); the others show
differences or stop: cellVpost (500 of 536 observations: QueryAttr's attribute, the limits Open checks, Exec's
picture information), cellPngEnc, cellVdec's MPEG-4 part 2, MVC and VC-1, while cellFiber, cellVdec's DivX 3.11 and
cellKey2char stop with a fault in Sony's module running on pspocket (cellFiber's at its second
cellFiberPpuInitializeScheduler). These libraries stay firmware-first (D-563): a game gets Sony's modules for them
while the user's system software is installed, so none of this reaches a game; making pspocket's own match is the next
work on them.

## D-906 · 2026-10-10 · sys_libc's locale and time as the SDK's C library has them

The last 28 of sys_libc's (and sys_libm's) locale and time names are pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/sys_libc_locale.cpp,
the time ones in sys_libc_time.cpp, the shared layouts and conversion machine in libc_locale.hpp), and sys_libc's
locale, time, multibyte and wide-class functions now give what the SDK's give. The reference is a game's statically
linked copy of the SDK's library (Assassin's Creed's, BLES00158; addresses only in inventory/libc-ac/ac-libc-map.txt,
nothing of it in the repository), read and called next to pspocket's (D-904's fixture).

**What the SDK's library is.** Dinkumware's C99 library with the newer locale design: a locale is a `_Linfo` of 452
bytes (name, next, collation and wide collation state tables, ctype/tolower/toupper, MB_CUR_MAX, multibyte and wide
state tables, wide translation and class tables, an 80-byte `struct lconv`, a 21-pointer `_Tinfo`); `_Loctab` is its
64 locale-file keywords {name, offset, kind} (kinds 0 grouping string ... 8 wide table); the four state tables are
thread-local (here in the thread's block, which grew to 512 bytes); `_Times` is the current `_Tinfo`, whose name lists
are delimited strings and whose ten format pointers share one four-field string. Sony's choices on top: setlocale knows
"C" alone, `_Findloc` reads no file (so `_Getloc` finds "C" only), the time zone and summer time come from lv2.

**The 28** (AC's address in the map where it has a copy):
- `_Clocale` (variable, sys_libc): its name "C", the rest filled by `_Getcloc` (the current tables, MB_CUR_MAX 3,
  `_Locale`, `_Times`; the translation table left out, as the SDK's). `_Locale`: the "C" lconv, the 14 chars 0x7F
  (the SDK's char is signed), false/true "false"/"true", the rest "" but decimal_point ".". `_Loctab`: the 64 entries.
  `_Times`: the "C" names.
- In AC: `_Defloc` ("C"), `_Findloc` (NULL), `_Freeloc` (frees what a locale holds that "C" does not, by `_Loctab`'s
  kinds; state tables by their "made" halfword), `_Getcloc`, `_Getgloballocale`/`_Setgloballocale` (the thread's
  global locale pointer, now also sys_libstdcxx's: its locale::global and _Init keep the C++ _Locimp there, as the
  SDK's C++ library does), `_Getloc` (the plain component of "name;category:name;...", overridden by the category's
  own; looked up from `_Clocale`), `_Skip`, `_Getnloc` and `_Getlname` (pspocket's names for the two category-mask
  helpers the SDK links beside setlocale and never calls: set pcats[1..6] (and [0] for all) from a name, -1 for a bad
  mask or name, 1 changed / 0 not; build "name;category:name;..." into a malloc'd buffer), `_Getptimes` (&_Times),
  `_CStrftime`, `_Gentime`.
- No copy in AC (Dinkumware's design, Plauger's book for the C89 parts, adapted to the C99 `_Loctab`; their file syntax
  pspocket's reading, nothing to compare with): `_Setloc(cat, p)` (Plauger's per-category copy for categories 1..6, 0
  all: collation tables; ctype tables, MB_CUR_MAX (at most 8), multibyte/wide tables, wide tables; monetary; numeric
  with false/true; time; messages no/yes), `_Readloc` (keyword lines, blank lines skipped, '\' continues, a table
  line's '[' ends the keyword), `_Makeloc` (to the next LOCALE line), `_Makestab` ("ctype[lo:hi] sum",
  "mbtowc[state, lo:hi] sum", copy-on-write tables, $@ the entry and $$ its value), `_Makewct` ("wctype name lo:hi
  value ...", copying the "C" table's names), `_Locsum`/`_Locterm`/`_Locvar` (terms: numbers, 'c', $^ $a..$v $@ $$,
  $0..$9 states, $A..$Z variables, F I O R preset to the state-table bits), `_Nnl` (strip a line's newline: 1 when
  there was one); `_Getdst` and `_Isdst` (Plauger's rules over the locale's dst_rules or time_zone's fourth field; with
  none, the "C" locale, lv2's summer flag); `_Wcsftime`/wcsftime (the AC build has neither, its wchar_t is 16 bits:
  derived from `_CStrftime` with sys_libc's 32-bit wchar_t, conversions' text widened by the multibyte conversion).

**What changed in sys_libc's own functions** (D-511, D-512, D-515 asserted other behaviour; their tests in
test_libc.cpp changed to the SDK's):
- setlocale: NULL or "C" answers "C" (the `_Clocale` name), anything else NULL, the category not looked at:
  setlocale(LC_ALL, "") and "POSIX" are NULL now, setlocale(99, NULL) is "C". localeconv is `_Locale` (0x7F chars).
- strftime is `_CStrftime` over `_Times`: Dinkumware's table-driven conversions with three-deep format expansion and
  the format read as multibyte characters; an unknown conversion gives its letter and a NUL ("%q|" is 3 bytes "q\0|");
  numbers clamped at 0 and cut to their width (year -5 is "0000", 12345 "2345"); %C is year/100+19; %z and %Z come from
  the locale's time_zone only, empty in "C" (D-515 printed lv2's offset); the E modifier uses the era fields
  ("+:offset:start:end:name:format"), O the alt_digits; %V/%G/%g count every year as 365 days (the SDK's leap test for
  them can never pass), so 2020-12-30 and -31 are week 01 of 2021 (D-902's "%V at a year's start"); a buffer too small
  answers 0 and keeps the pieces that fit. A locale whose formats expand into themselves stops with a log (the SDK's
  loops for ever), and a modifier as the format's last character ends it (the SDK's reads past the string).
- asctime is "%c\n" through the "C" _Tinfo into the thread's 26 bytes (wday 7 gives no day name, years cut to four
  digits); gmtime, localtime and `_Ttotm` use Plauger's calendar (2100 a leap year: gmtime(4107542400) is 29 February
  2100), negative fields before 1900, localtime = zone + summer offset with tm_isdst 1, `_Ttotm`'s non-zero isdst adds
  the summer offset and is stored as given; `_Gettime` past the fields answers the NUL with length 0 (Plauger's 1);
  time() answers -1 when lv2 fails. mktime (no copy) keeps D-515's meaning on the same calendar.
- Multibyte: the "C" locale is UTF-8 of up to three bytes, MB_CUR_MAX 3 (`_Mbcurmax` 3), as the SDK's (its wchar_t
  is 16 bits; with sys_libc's 32-bit one a wide character past 0xFFFF has no form, EILSEQ, and a four-byte lead is
  EILSEQ); no overlong or surrogate checks; mbstate_t is {_Wchar, _Byte, _State} with a pending sequence kept;
  `_Mbtowcx`/`_Wctombx` run Dinkumware's state-table machine when a locale has tables. btowc of a byte past 0x7F is
  WEOF, wctob of é EOF; `_Getpmbstate` and its kin answer the thread's 64-byte state tables (D-512 had 8-byte states).
- Wide classes: the SDK's table layout ({ranges, 0}, {name, first}, ..., {NULL, end}; ranges {lo, hi, value}), its
  order (alnum 1, alpha, cntrl, digit, graph, lower, print, punct, space, upper, xdigit, blank 12), cntrl 0..0x1F (DEL
  is not); `_Getpwctytab` answers the table. `_Wctrans` (no copy in AC) the same layout, tolower/toupper deltas.
- The ctype table's \t..\r carry _BB as well as _CN (0x4C0, 0xC0), as the SDK's.
- Collation in "C": strxfrm/wcsxfrm/`_Strxfrmx`/`_Wcsxfrmx` write as much of the string as fits (the SDK's leaves the
  pieces); `_CStrxfrm(sout, size, save, tables)` and `_CWcsxfrm(sout, &src, size, ps, tables)` have the SDK's
  signatures. Collation by a locale's state tables is not done (logged, code order): only a locale file's collate
  lines could make them, which the SDK's setlocale never loads.
- sys_libstdcxx: kCharMax 0x7F (the facets compare the lconv's "not available" with it).

**How it was checked** (tests/hle/test_libc_locale_game.cpp, "[gamelibc]", 0 differences): strftime 99,286 calls (every
conversion and modifier over 650 dates and odd fields, literal and multibyte formats, buffers 0..29); `_Gentime` and
`_CStrftime` 876,688 calls over four _Tinfos (eras, alt digits, zones, self-referring formats); gmtime, localtime,
asctime, ctime, `_Ttotm`, `_Daysto`, `_Gettime`, time 16,689 calls; locale objects, setlocale (11 categories × 16
names), `_Getloc`, `_Getnloc`, `_Skip`, `_Findloc`, the global pointer, `_Getcloc`'s result 1,300; `_Mbtowc`,
`_Wctomb` (all 65,536), `_Mbtowcx`/`_Wctombx` with state tables, `_Iswctype`, the class table 74,209; strcoll,
strxfrm, `_CStrxfrm`, `_CWcsxfrm` 516. Not compared: formats whose first byte is no multibyte character (the SDK's
then reuses whatever its stack held), `_Getlname` (it always frees or mallocs through the game's own allocator, which
an unstarted executable lacks), the file functions (no copy). The game's _Once needs its lwmutex, which the test makes
with the game's own start-up function. Firmware-free: tests/hle/test_libc_locale.cpp (strftime and the calendar, eras,
wcsftime, `_Getdst`/`_Isdst`, the locale objects, a locale file read, made current with `_Setloc` and freed).

Not done here: printf's %lc/%ls, scanf's wide conversions and the wide streams still convert bytes one to one (they are
libc_format.hpp's and stdio's, D-905); sys_libstdcxx's codecvt<wchar_t, char> and ctype<wchar_t>::widen are bytes
too, where the SDK's C++ library converts UTF-8 through the same machine (its do_widen gives WEOF past 0x7F).

## D-905 · 2026-10-11 · sys_libc's printf as the SDK's: the output internals, the SPU printf's, against a game's copy

The SDK's C library (Dinkumware's, Sony's additions; no firmware module has it) as Assassin's Creed (BLES00158) links
it was read and pspocket's printf rewritten to give what it gives, piece by piece (runtime/hle/src/libc_printf.hpp, an
engine over the library's print-formatting structure that works on the host's buffers for sprintf and the rest and on
guest memory for the internals a game calls; runtime/hle/src/sys_libc_format.cpp). 18 names new, under sys_libc and
sys_libm: _Putfld, _Puttxt, _Putstr, _Litob, _Ldtob, _Genld, their _W forms, the six SPU printf internals
(__spu_thread_printf, __spu_thread_putfld, __spu_thread_puttxt and the __raw_spu_ ones), plus _Printf, _WPrintf,
spu_thread_printf/sprintf/snprintf, raw_spu_printf and spu_raw_sprintf/snprintf moved onto them. (The input side,
_Getfld .. _WStoxflt, went to D-907.)
- _Pft: +0 the value (long long or double), +16 a vector argument, +32 pfn, +36 arg, +40 s, +44 n0, nz0, n1, nz1, n2,
  nz2, +68 prec, +72 nchar, +76 width, +80 flags (u16: ' ' 1, '+' 2, '-' 4, '#' 8, '0' 16, Sony's separators ',' 0x80,
  ';' 0x100, ':' 0x200, '_' 0x400), +82 qual; the SPU printf's adds the SPU at +84 (flag 0x20: %s's text is in its
  store). _WPft: +0 value, +8 pfn, +12 arg, +16 s, +20 n0 .. +40 nz2, +44 nchar, +48 prec, +52 width, +56 flags, +60
  qual: the game's build has a 16-bit wchar_t (qual at +58); sys_libc's is 32-bit (D-512), so its wide text is words.
- Floating point (_Ldtob, _Genld): the value scaled by powers of ten in double arithmetic, eight digits at a time, 19
  significant at most, rounded half up on the first dropped digit: "%.0f" of 0.5 is "1", "%.1f" of 0.25 "0.3",
  "%.20f" of 0.1 "0.10000000000000000000", "%.20f" of 1/3 "0.33333333333333330301". %a is exact, as few digits as
  needed. The host's correctly rounded snprintf is gone (and faster: 20,000 vsprintf calls of 11 mixed conversions
  took 21.0 ms before, 12.1 ms after, the same session).
- Integers (_Litob) as C99, but: L is 32 bits (ll and j are 64; q is no qualifier at all: "%qd" prints "qd"); "% Ld"
  has no space; %p is the hex digits alone, '#' or not.
- Any conversion character it has none for prints itself padded to the width, taking no argument ("%5k" is
  "    k"); %% is padded too; %s of NULL is "(null)" whatever the precision; %n of the narrow printf is not padded.
- The "C" locale's multibyte characters are UTF-8 (U+00E9 is C3 A9), by the bits, with no surrogate or overlong
  checks: %ls/%lc (wctomb) and the wide printf's %s (mbtowc) and %c (btowc: none past 0x7F, EOF). The game's 16-bit
  build stops at three bytes; for the 32-bit wchar_t the same rule goes on to six (31 bits), as UTF-8 was first
  defined: derived, no game shows it. This differs from D-512's byte-a-character "C" locale for mbrtowc and kin, which
  stays as it is here (reported to the main session).
- %ls goes through a buffer of 64 bytes, or of width + 3 (malloc) when right-justified and wider; a buffer that fills
  is put out unpadded ("%-100ls" of a long string is not padded); a failed output inside it is ignored.
- Sony's AltiVec vectors: v, vl or lv four 32-bit elements, vh/hv eight, vhh/hhv sixteen, vll/llv two 64-bit, vL/Lv
  two doubles, v with a floating conversion four floats, vc sixteen characters, "%xc" and "%cx" (o, u, x, X) sixteen
  bytes; the vector at the va_list's next 16-byte boundary. Each element is a field of its own after a separator (a
  space unless , ; : or _ is given; for signed integers a ' ' flag and a separator both), which counts in its width;
  floats keep the space as their sign too (" 1.5 -0.3  2.0  0.0").
- The wide printf: no vectors, no %S; %n takes its pointer and stores nothing, and its field is padded ("%5n" puts
  five spaces); padding 31 characters a piece (32 narrow).
- swprintf answers -1 when a piece of the text does not fit, written as far as it fits, with a NUL (C99's negative);
  sprintf writes no NUL after a failure; snprintf always writes one (n > 0).
- The SPU printf (__spu_thread_printf on a thread's store, a word at a time through lv2 as the library's accessors,
  D-904): format characters one a time, literal ones to pfn one a time; flags " +-#0", qualifiers h hh l ll j t z L;
  every conversion takes the next quadword, %% too ("%d %% %d" of 1, 2, 3 is "1 % 3"); %s's text stays in the store,
  read 128 bytes at a time, "(null)" for address 0 (its length measured at 0 meanwhile); %n writes the count into the
