## D-914 · 2026-10-11 · D-652 and D-653 in libsre's Task2 model, merging main (part 9)

Main brought D-652 (a CellSpursTaskset2's task IDs claimed and given back under the host's lock) and D-653 (its event
flag IDs read and cleared atomically), both written for D-626's model that part 8 replaced. What they protected and
where it went:
- **D-652**: the host table of unjoined IDs is gone. A Task2 task's ID is its enabled bit, claimed in one reservation
  operation and kept from its creation through its exit until its join clears it; the count and the destruction flag
  change in one reservation operation on the same line, the exit slot in reservation operations on its own. Nothing
  else is shared, so there is no lock to take: a task created, run and ended by other threads while another is created
  cannot leave its ID free before its join, the race D-652 fixed.
- **D-653**: libsre's DestroyTaskset2 does not clear the event flag IDs (it refuses while a Task2 task is not joined, so
  no join can be waiting on them), so the release store has nothing left to do; the IDs are still read with atomic
  loads (JoinTask2, CreateTask2's check, DestroyTaskset2), as D-587's shared words, since a cellSpursCreateTaskset2 at
  the same address writes them.
- The shutdown completion now clears a TaskInfo's ELF bits with a compare-and-swap on that doubleword (libsre's
  ldarx/stdcx.) rather than an update of the whole line, which could put back a stale copy of a neighbouring TaskInfo
  that a creation on another thread writes with plain stores.
D-650's and D-652's test of creators and joiners on eight threads stays, polling TryJoinTask2 through AGAIN (libsre's
answer while the task runs); D-653's test of a destruction during joins becomes the same race against the shutdown
that ends them: DestroyTaskset2 BUSY while they poll, then the join waiting wakes with SHUTDOWN, exactly one poller
gets SHUTDOWN and the others STAT, and the destruction succeeds, 24 rounds at the same address.

## D-912 · 2026-10-11 · cellVdec's new codecs against Sony's libvdec (part 1): the comparisons as a game decodes

D-597's comparison of cellVdec's DivX 3.11, MPEG-4 part 2, VC-1 and MVC with Sony's libvdec 4.92 (D-911: DivX 3.11
crashed, the others differed) is reworked so that what it compares is what a game sees, and widened.

- **Why DivX 3.11 "crashed".** Two things, neither an engine fault. Its five decodes each waited 60 s for AUDONEs that
  never came: Sony's DivX 3.11 core has two frame buffers and holds the third access unit back while the game holds a
  picture, and the old test took its pictures only after EndSeq. Then OpenEx without CellVdecDivxSpecificInfo2: libvdec
  reads the frame size from address 4 there (its pointer to the information is a register that is only set when the
  information is given, and is 0 otherwise), which faults on a PS3 as it does here. That case is no longer sent; a game
  always gives the information.
- **A decoder's life as a game lives it** (test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp decode()): each access unit's AUDONE awaited, then
  the pictures announced by then taken at once (GetPicItem, GetPicture); hold() decodes without taking pictures until an
  access unit is held back, then takes one picture at a time (how many pictures each core holds); items_ahead() takes
  items ahead of their pictures and sets the frame rate inside the sequence. A callback due that does not come within
  10 s is "none" (no 60 s waits).
- **The decoder's memory**: 64 MB, so every decoder gets what QueryAttrEx asks for (Sony's libvdec refuses less than its
  codec's part, part 2), filled with 0xA5 before each OpenEx so the bytes a decoder leaves unwritten show (the
  information blocks and items have many).
- **Widened**: QueryAttrEx over every level of each codec with and without codec specific information (picture sizes,
  buffer counts, deblocking, the refusals); OpenEx with the codec's part and one byte less; DivX and MPEG-4 told their
  size, an 80x48 stream (not a multiple of 32 lines), DivX with three buffers held; VC-1 told its size and held; MVC's
  sizes for every level. Each picture's frame buffer is read with its core's own layout (part 2).
- **A damaged stream**: DivX 3.11 written at 96x64 and told 128x96 decodes into garbage in both decoders; its pictures and
  which of them a decoder reports damaged (the item's status, the information's error word, the PICOUT's data) are
  notes, the rest compared.
- **MVC through DecodeAuEx2 is not sent**: Sony's libvdec hands libmvcdec the picture information's address from 0x10
  bytes past where it keeps it (the caller's r26 saved in its frame), and writes the information there when the picture
  comes: on a PS3 wherever the game's r26 points; here a fault at 0x15c. Nothing to compare. The H.264 base view decode
  D-597 added to read MVC against goes too (MVC never decodes through DecodeAu, part 2); H.264 is compared in
  test_vdec.cpp (D-196).
- **compare_util.hpp**: PSPOCKET_COMPARE_DUMP=<dir> writes each half's observations (lines, and each data block as a
  file) for reading off line, Sony's into a scratch directory only; PSPOCKET_COMPARE_ONLY=<text> runs only the steps of
  a comparison whose names contain it (one case at a time).

Tests: the four comparisons (hidden, [compare][vdec]); with PSPOCKET_COMPARE_SELF=1 both halves agree and the sanity
checks hold the values Sony's module gave.

## D-912 (part 2) · 2026-10-11 · cellVdec's DivX 3.11, DivX, MPEG-4, VC-1 and MVC as Sony's libvdec 4.92 decodes them

Read in libvdec and its cores (libdivx311dec, libdivxdec, libsmvd4, libsvc1d, libmvcdec; only what is understood is
written, runtime/hle/src/vdec_layout.hpp and cellVdec.cpp) and checked by part 1's comparisons: DivX 3.11 0 of 542
observations differ, MPEG-4 part 2 as DivX and as MPEG-4 0 of 890, VC-1 0 of 437, MVC 0 of 191 (before: a crash, 89,
84 and 167 differences).

- **Sizes.** Each core's memory query with the codec specific information, reproduced: libdivxdec's (n frame buffers
  of (lines to 16 + chroma lines to 8 + 48) x (width to 16 + 32), plus 0.5% truncated, plus 0x9E86B, to 16 bytes;
  level 0 with the size, so the level only bounds it), libdivx311dec's (two frames plus 0x4D800), libsmvd4's (three
  frames of (lines to 32 + 32) x (width to 16 + 32) x 1.5 + 0x80, 0x80 a macroblock, 0x15380), libsvc1d's (six frames,
  nine for the main profile, of ((lines to 32 + 128) x (width to 16 + 32) x 1.5 + 256) to 256, two tables per
  macroblock, fixed parts) and libmvcdec's (libavcdec's algorithm for two views: twice the decoded picture buffer, four
  more frames, its own blocks, + 0x33700 + 0x4FC100). libvdec adds 0x41580 + 5 x 0x50 + 0xA8 and each codec's part
  (DivX 0x34F8, DivX 3.11 0x3500, MPEG-4 and VC-1 0x3493, MVC 0x41580 + 0x12FD); QueryAttrEx adds 0x858 and the ring
  ((information + 0x90) x elements + (elements x 0x14 + 0x14) x 2 + 0x40; 0x20 elements, 0x30 for H.264 and MVC). Every
  refusal is ARG. RPCS3's max-size tables are the cores' level limits.
- **Open** refuses memory less than the codec's part (ARG); one byte less than all QueryAttrEx asked opens (D-196).
  VC-1's simple and main profiles open, as Sony's (pspocket refused them FATAL); their access units are still not
  decoded (AU error, logged).
- **The ring.** Each access unit takes the lowest free element at DecodeAu (none free: FATAL). Its picture's item is in
  the element (+0x40), its information block in the blocks after the elements; libvdec writes them when it announces the
  picture, and only these bytes: item: codec, start address, size, the number of access units (a byte), the first
  access unit's PTS, DTS and user data, status, attributes (the rest as a free element has them: start and size 0, PTS
  and DTS ones, user data 0; the information's address set at open). GetPicture frees the element; an access unit that
  makes no picture frees it at AUDONE. GetPicItem gives the items in turn.
- **Frame buffers**, the cores' own: DivX 3.11 two at the core's +0x3D700, DivX three in turn (memory for n; one
  holds back past two) at +0x76680, MPEG-4 three at the decoder +0x16980, VC-1 six after its per-picture tables, at
  +0x118A00 + the macroblock table + the block table to 128. Laid out in 16-byte strips (8 Cb, 8 Cr a chroma line), one
  strip of repeated edge each side and lines of edge above and below: DivX's and MPEG-4's 16 luma and 8 chroma lines,
  VC-1's 64 and 32 with its lines to 32. The item's start address is the frame's (DivX) or its first luma sample's
  (MPEG-4, VC-1). A VC-1 skipped picture shows the frame before it again.
- **A core holds at most so many pictures** (decoded, not yet released by GetPicture: DivX 3.11 2, DivX 3, MPEG-4 3,
  VC-1 4) and holds the next access unit back (no AUDONE) until the game takes one. pspocket counts the pictures it
  holds, announced and still inside FFmpeg. Pictures are announced one access unit late, but MPEG-4's at once.
- **Information blocks**: DivX 3.11's (type, size, frame rate code, frame address, size, 0, 0x30, an error word),
  DivX's (RPCS3's fields from the VOL as libdivxdec reports them: colour codes 0 without a description; then the frame
  address, size, 0, 0x30, an error word), MPEG-4's (the VOL's aspect ratio code, pixel sizes, time increment resolution,
  fixed rate and increment, size; the VOP type; luma, Cb and Cr addresses; the frame's luma lines; 3), VC-1's (the
  sequence header as read when the picture is announced, the picture's entry point and header fields, the headers its
  access unit carried, the addresses, the frame's lines, the range mapping), each with the bytes Sony leaves unwritten
  left. An MPEG-4 VOL and visual object parser (cellVdec.cpp) gives the fields.
- **The frame rate code**: StartSeq forgets a SetFrameRate made before it (libdivxdec's and libdivx311dec's reset), so
  it is 0 unless set inside the sequence; for the streams compared the stream's own timing gives 0 too.
- **VC-1**: libsvc1d leaves range mapping to the game (the flags and values in the information; D-589 applied it: no
  longer); the picture's size given is the sequence header's as read when it is announced (a 64x48 picture announced
  after a 32x32 header is given cut to 32x32, its item's size 0x600); an access unit before the headers is done with
  CELL_VDEC_ERROR_AU in AUDONE's data; decode mode 3 is taken and then refused by the core: ERROR with
  CELL_VDEC_ERROR_FATAL, then nothing more (no AUDONE, no SEQDONE). FFmpeg's skipped pictures, references to the picture
  before with its access unit, are given the access unit still owed.
- **MVC never decodes through cellVdecDecodeAu** on Sony's libvdec 4.92: it converts the information to DecodeAuEx2's
  layout and its MVC decoder reads that as libmvcdec's chunks (address, size, ...): the size word is 0 and
  mvcDecAccessUnit answers "bad parameter", FATAL. pspocket refuses it the same way; through DecodeAuEx2 (part 1: no
  behaviour of Sony's to match) it decodes the base view (D-590), logged. MVC's information past 0x214 bytes is not
  written (it was H.264's, into the next block).
- **A picture decoded with errors concealed** (FFmpeg's decode error flags) is reported as Sony's cores report a damaged
  picture: CELL_VDEC_ERROR_PIC in the PICOUT's data and the item's status, the DivX error word 0x11.
- **Pictures**: DivX 3.11's samples are within one step of Sony's (2.05% one step off), DivX's and MPEG-4's too (1.15%),
  none more: the IDCT's rounding, which the standard leaves to the decoder (IEEE 1180), accepted as D-597 set. VC-1's are
  exact. Frame buffers likewise.
- **H.264 (unchanged here, test_vdec.cpp)**: its frame buffers no longer have their gaps written (Sony's libavcdec leaves
  them); their place stays pspocket's, and its information block is still written whole: Sony's leaves bytes of it
  unwritten (seen through the 0xA5 fill) and places its frames in libavcdec's memory, which test_vdec.cpp does not
  compare. To do with H.264's own comparison.

Tests: tests/hle/test_vdec_codecs.cpp rewritten to these behaviours (Sony's sizes, the information blocks, MPEG-4 without
lag, VC-1 without range mapping and cut to the sequence header, mode 3's ERROR, the simple and main profiles opening, MVC
refused through DecodeAu and decoded through DecodeAuEx2); vdec_test_util.hpp's decode_stream takes the pictures as a
game does. The four comparisons with the firmware: 0 differences each; test_vdec.cpp's H.264 comparison and the codec
cores' version queries pass.

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellPngEnc as Sony's libpngenc answers and writes it (part 1)

D-597's comparison of cellPngEnc with libpngenc.sprx (firmware 4.92) showed 134 of 616 observations differing (D-911):
pspocket's library (D-566) was RPCS3's checks on libpng 1.6. Sony's module was read (its exports, its encoder thread,
its chunk setters; nothing of it in the repository) and pspocket's rewritten to do what it does; the comparison, widened
and made independent of libpngenc's thread timing, now shows 0 of 1,834 observations differing.
What libpngenc is, and pspocket's now:
- **The handle** is the work memory's first 128-byte boundary (RPCS3: the memory itself). Open over memory already open
  makes a new encoder there (pspocket refused it). QueryAttr's memory and Open's checks were right; a priority of -1
  is refused too.
- **Two queues.** EncodePicture queues a command (four at most: BUSY); libpngenc's thread encodes them while fewer than
  four streams wait. WaitForInput is BUSY with four commands waiting, not four streams (pspocket refused a fifth picture).
  Reset, with fewer than five streams waiting (else BUSY), turns the commands waiting into streams of state STREAM_SKIP
  and leaves libpngenc's abort flag up: the next picture is skipped too (STREAM_SKIP, no bytes). Reset keeps the streams
  (pspocket dropped them). pspocket encodes a command as soon as there is room, on the calling thread.
- **EncodePicture's checks** (ARG): no colour conversion but RGBA or ARGB to RGB and gray and alpha to gray (pspocket
  also added an opaque alpha); a filter set needs one of libpng's filter bits (0 is refused); a buffer needs more than
  0x30 bytes; the pitch is measured in the encoded colour space's samples (an RGBA picture encoded as RGB needs 3 bytes
  a pixel, and the stream then fails FATAL when the row cannot hold the picture's own); a palette picture needs its
  PLTE; the SPU encoder takes 2560 columns at 8 bits, 1280 at 16. Every ancillary chunk is checked: its fields
  (palette sizes against the bit depth, tRNS and bKGD against the palette given before them and the bit depth, sBIT 1 to
  the depth, cHRM's white point at most 0.8 and each point's x + y at most 1, gAMA up to 21474.83, sRGB 0 to 3, units
  0 to 1 or 0 to 2, tIME's fields, iTXt's language, sPLT's depths and 8-bit entries, pCAL's parameters, unknown chunks'
  locations), and the memory the chunks take (libpngenc's own measure of each string and buffer) against addMemSize:
  with addMemSize 0, any text, iCCP, sPLT, pCAL or unknown chunk is refused.
- **The PNG is libpng 1.2.8's**: chunks in 1.2.8's order (gAMA, sRGB, iCCP, sBIT, cHRM before PLTE; PLTE, tRNS, bKGD,
  hIST, oFFs, pCAL, sCAL, pHYs, tIME, sPLT, the texts after it), unknown chunks before PLTE, after it or after IDAT by
  their location, unsafe ones too; IDAT in 2048-byte chunks; gAMA and cHRM from the floats png_set_* keeps, times 100000
  by the PPU's fused multiply-add, truncated (gAMA 0.45455 is 45455; 21474.83 is 2147483008); sCAL's numbers by
  libpngenc's own "%d.%06de%+03d" ("1.000000e-03"; pspocket printed ".001"); a text's length is its strlen, an empty
  zTXt is a tEXt. libpngenc installs no warning handler, so each of libpng's warnings ends the stream with FATAL: a
  keyword with spaces to tidy, a PLTE on a gray picture, a tRNS out of range or on an alpha picture, a cHRM point past
  0.8 as a float (0.8 itself), a palette background past the palette or the bit depth, an hIST whose count is not the
  palette's, an unknown chunk's location 0 or 3. A 1-bit sample a byte is any byte but 0 (libpng's packing).
- **A stream too long for its buffer**: what fits is written a chunk piece at a time (the signature, IHDR, the first
  IDAT's header), then STREAM_OVERFLOW with streamSize 0 and processedLine the rows written before the write that
  failed (pspocket wrote what fitted and gave its size).
The PNG is written here rather than by the build's libpng 1.6, which orders and checks chunks otherwise; IDAT, zTXt and
iCCP are zlib's of the build with libpng 1.2.8's settings (the window bits tidied as 1.2 does), so their bytes may
differ from zlib 1.2.3's for the same pixels and texts (notes in the comparison, D-597).
Tests: tests/hle/test_pngenc_compare.cpp (0 of 1,834 against Sony's; PSPOCKET_COMPARE_SELF=1 agrees with itself);
tests/hle/test_imgenc.cpp updated to Sony's answers (the queues and Reset's skips, the refusals, FATAL for a keyword to
tidy, the memory of a text, 1.2.8's chunk order, sCAL's and gAMA's bytes, a buffer too small).

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellJpgEnc as Sony's libjpgenc answers and writes it (part 3)

cellJpgEnc (D-616) was made without a Sony module, its structures inferred from libpngenc's; D-618's comparison had
never run. Run against libjpgenc.sprx (firmware 4.92), 788 of 816 observations differed: most structures were wrong.
Sony's module was read (its exports, its encoder thread, its libjpeg; nothing of it in the repository) and pspocket's
library and encoder rewritten to do what it does. The comparison, rewritten on Sony's structures and widened (21
configurations, every sampling and colour space, sizes 1x1 to 50x61 at both DCTs, qualities 0 to 100, restart
intervals, a pitch past the row, extended parameters, the queues and Reset, buffers too small, files, every check, an
SPU encoder), shows 14 of 3,751 observations differing, all in two features below.
- **The structures** (Sony's): CellJpgEncConfig {maxWidth, maxHeight, encodeColorSpace (gray 1, RGB 2, YCbCr 3),
  samplingFormat (4:4:4 0, 4:2:2 1, 4:2:0 2, 4:1:1 3, none 4), enableSpu (b8, +16), exParamList, exParamNum}: the JPEG's
  colour space and sampling are the encoder's, not each picture's. CellJpgEncPicture {width, height, colorSpace,
  pictureAddr, userData (u64, +16)} (rows of the picture's width); CellJpgEncPicture2 {width, height, pitchWidth,
  colorSpace, pictureAddr, userData (u64, +24)} (EncodePicture2 is the pitch, not planes); CellJpgEncEncodeParam
  {enableSpu (b8), restartInterval, dctMethod, compressionMode, compressionModeParam, exParamList, exParamNum}, each
  extended parameter {marker, data, size}: a marker segment after SOI, its code the marker's low byte; the stream
  information has the quality used at +28 before userData.
- **QueryAttr**: sizes 1 to 65535, a colour space 1 to 3, sampling 4 exactly when not YCbCr, no extended parameters;
  memSize 0x1B630 (0x388A0 with SPUs) + the width to 16 times 12 (gray), 30 (RGB, 4:4:4), 22 (4:2:2), 18 (4:1:1) or
  33 (4:2:0), + 0x1780; cmdQueueDepth 4, versionUpper 0x270000, versionLower 4.
- **Open** (and OpenEx): the handle is the work memory's first 128-byte boundary; too little memory, a PPU priority
  past 0xBFF or an SPU priority past 0xFF is ARG; opening over memory already open makes a new encoder there.
- **The queues** are libpngenc's (part 1): four commands (BUSY), the thread encoding while fewer than four streams wait,
  eight streams; Reset (BUSY with five or more streams) turns the commands into STREAM_SKIP streams, skips the next
  picture too and keeps the streams.
- **EncodePicture's checks**: a picture within the encoder's size, a colour space the encoder takes (gray only into a
  gray encoder; YCbCr not into an RGB one; RGB, RGBA and ARGB into any), a pitch of a row at least; enableSpu only on
  an encoder opened for SPUs and only with the fast DCT; dctMethod 0 or 5; compressionMode 0 or 1; quality at most 100;
  restartInterval at most 0xFFFF; each extended parameter's data given and its size 1 to 0xFFFD; location 0 or 1; the
  size limit mode only into a buffer; a file needs its name; a buffer its address and limitSize of at least 0x1000 plus
  the extended parameters' segments.
- **The stream is libjpeg 6b's, byte for byte** (jpeg_encoder.cpp rewritten on its algorithms): no JFIF APP0 (pspocket
  wrote one), jpeg_set_quality's tables (quality 0 is 1) forced to baseline, jccolor's fixed-point conversion (a YCbCr
  picture taken as it is), jcsample's downsampling with its alternating bias, the last column and row repeated to the
  iMCU, dummy blocks at the DC of the block before, jfdctflt in double with the two fused multiply-adds and the fused
  quantisation libjpgenc's compiler made (QUALITY) or jfdctfst with its scaled divisors (FAST), jchuff's bit buffer,
  restart markers and fill, and jcmarker's order (DQT, SOF0, DHT as the scan first uses each table, DRI, SOS). RGBA and
  ARGB give the RGB picture's stream. A scratch harness compared 186 of Sony's streams: none differ.
- **A buffer too small**: the stream is written until the buffer is full (to its end), then STREAM_OVERFLOW, streamSize
  0, processedLine the rows written before the one whose data did not fit. A file that cannot be made is
  STREAM_FILE_OPEN; the quality is reported in every stream's information.
Still different, each logged once when a game uses it:
- **The stream size limit mode** (6 observations): libjpgenc predicts the quality from a trial encoding of a corner of
  the picture and tables of stream sizes by quality in its data (4 sampling groups, 3 activity rows, 101 qualities),
  retrying lower up to three times; the tables are Sony's measurements, which pspocket does not carry. pspocket takes the
  highest quality up to the one given whose stream fits (searched by halves): its streams fit as Sony's do, at a higher
  quality (64x48 in 0x1000 bytes: Sony quality 69, pspocket 95).
- **The SPU encoder** (8 observations): libjpgenc's SPU program converts, samples and transforms in its own arithmetic
  (its first coefficients differ from libjpeg's) and pads the stream with two zero bytes after EOI (streamSize counts
  them). pspocket encodes those pictures with libjpeg's FAST path: the same headers and tables, a picture within a
  rounding of Sony's.
cellJpgEnc stays firmware-first (D-563) while these differ.
Tests: tests/hle/test_jpgenc_compare.cpp (PSPOCKET_COMPARE_SELF=1: 0 of 3,751; against Sony's: 14, the two features
above); tests/hle/test_jpgenc.cpp rewritten for Sony's structures and answers (libjpeg 6b's tables and colours, the
markers of every sampling at both DCTs read back by pspocket's decoder, the queues and Reset's skips, the overflow's
rows, the size limit mode, files, every check). compare_util.hpp: PSPOCKET_COMPARE_DUMP=<dir> writes each half's data
observations (the streams) to files for reading a difference.

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellVpost as Sony's libvpost answers and converts (part 4)

cellVpost (D-564) was RPCS3's: its attributes, idm handles and a float conversion and scaler of pspocket's own. The
comparison with libvpost.sprx (firmware 4.92) showed 374 of 536 observations differing, and most of its pictures were
ones libvpost refuses (sizes under 32, unaligned buffers, empty windows). Sony's module was read (its PPU wrapper over
four SPURS task stages: input, interlace conversion, scaler, colour conversion) and run on chosen pictures (thousands of
probes: flat colours over the whole YUV cube, impulses, noise, every window placement); nothing of it in the repository.
pspocket's library is rewritten to do what it does. The comparison, rewritten on what libvpost takes and widened (25
configurations, every resource field at its limits, OpenEx's checks, flat colours, noise and ramps in both matrices,
ranges and chroma sitings, 13 scalings by each scaler type, windows, every exec and interpolation type, every check, YUV
output) now shows 88 of 791 observations differing, in the features listed last.
- **QueryAttr**: inMaxWidth and outMaxWidth even, 32 to 1920, the heights even, 32 to 1088, depths 8 bits, the input YUV
  4:2:0 planar, the output RGBA or YUV 4:2:0 planar, both reserved words 0 (else Q_ARG_CFG_INVALID). memSize is twice
  the larger frame (the width to 16 times the height plus two chroma planes of half the width to 16 times half the height
  plus one) plus 0x9FE5 (RPCS3: 4 MB); delay 0; versions 0x40000 and 0x05060606.
- **Open** makes the handle in the work memory, at its first 128-byte boundary, its first word its own address (Exec and
  Close check it: a pointer that is no handle is HDL_INVALID). O_ARG_RSRC_INVALID for no memory, less than QueryAttr's, a
  PPU priority past 0xBFF, an SPU priority outside 16 to 255 or SPUs other than one (the stack is not checked). OpenEx
  takes {memAddr, memSize, spurs, priority[8], maxContention}: a SPURS instance, priorities 0 to 15 not all 0, a
  maximum contention of 1. Close clears the handle.
- **Exec's checks**, in libvpost's order: the handle, the input (given, 128-byte aligned: INPICBUF_INVALID), the
  control parameters (CTRL_INVALID: exec type to 7, scaler type to 3, interpolation type to 2, the sizes as QueryAttr's
  and within the handle's, chroma siting, range and matrix 0 or 1, both windows inside their pictures, even and at least
  32 square, both reserved words 0), the output (128-byte aligned: OUTPICBUF_INVALID), the picture information.
- **The output** is the whole picture: the input window scaled into the output window, black around it (Y 0, or 16 in
  broadcast range; chroma 128). The picture information takes libvpost's tables for the exec type's scans and
  structures; an RGBA output's range is 0.
- **The colour conversion** is libvpost's fixed point, found exactly from all 2^24 colours' slices: R, G, B = (A * Y +
  Cu (U - 128) + Cv (V - 128) + B) >> 20, clamped; full range A = 2^20 and B = 2^19; broadcast A = 64 * 19076 on Y - 16
  and B = 523264; the chroma weights 128 times BT.601's 11485, -2818, -5850, 14516 (broadcast 13078, -3204, -6658,
  16520) or BT.709's 12900, -1534, -3834, 15201 (broadcast 14690, -1746, -4378, 17322). Each pixel's chroma: its 2x2
  block's (siting type A), or for odd columns the byte average, rounded up, of its sample and the next (type B).
- **The scaler type 0** is libvpost's bilinear: vertically first, then horizontally; weights in 1/256, each sum rounded
  down; vertical positions in 1/65536 per row; horizontal ones in 1/256, sixteen output columns at a time from a
  multiple of 16 in the output picture (each sixteen 16 steps of 1/65536 on, rounded down to 1/256, its columns a 1/256
  step apart); a row past the window's bottom is the picture's, a column past its right edge its last; chroma planes
  sited (step - 1) / 4 on (horizontally for type A only); past a halving horizontally, every second column first.
Still different, each logged once when a game uses it: scaler types 1 to 3 (libvpost's sharpening and 4-tap and 8x4-tap
filters, the last from tables of coefficients in its data), exec types 1 to 6 (part 6), a horizontal reduction past a
half, a chroma window not at a multiple of 16 enlarged, and the bytes libvpost writes past a YUV output whose chroma
planes have an odd size. cellVpost stays firmware-first (D-563) while
these differ.
Tests: tests/hle/test_vpost_compare.cpp (PSPOCKET_COMPARE_SELF=1 agrees with itself); tests/hle/test_vpost.cpp rewritten
for libvpost's answers (its memory, handle, checks, conversion, sitings, scaler positions, windows, information).

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellPngEnc's and cellJpgEnc's queues across threads after D-651 (part 5)

Main's D-651 (a picture takes its place before it is encoded; a Reset meanwhile drops it) was written for the
libraries before parts 1 and 3. Merged, the libraries keep libpngenc's and libjpgenc's queues as compared (four commands
waiting, the one being encoded among them; the thread encoding while fewer than four streams wait; Reset turning the
waiting commands into STREAM_SKIP streams and skipping the next picture), and D-651's race is closed the way Sony's
thread closes it: the command being encoded keeps its place, a Reset meanwhile leaves it to finish and queue its stream
first, and only then are the commands still waiting skipped (before, the Reset turned it into a skipped stream too and
its encoder then popped the next picture's command). D-651's tests are rewritten for those queues: eight threads at once
give four to eight pictures taken (the rest BUSY), each taken picture exactly one stream (its own bytes, or STREAM_SKIP
after a Reset), nothing left after; D-650's two encoders on two threads stand as they were, on the new structures.

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellVpost's exec types: libvpost's fields and interlace conversion (part 6)

The exec types are libvpost's, found by running its module on noise pictures at every type, interpolation type, size and
output format (all 144 such probes match but the edge-adaptive type's few pixels):
- A field picture out (PTOP_ITOP, PBTM_IBTM, ITOP_ITOP, IBTM_IBTM, IFRM_IFRM) is only the output's rows of its parity,
  luma and chroma alike; the other rows are left as they were (IFRM_IFRM writes the top field's, then the bottom's).
- A field picture in becomes a frame by the interlace conversion when the output is a frame (ITOP_PFRM, IBTM_PFRM) or
  when it is scaled (the field types): the field's rows kept, the others' made from them: type 0 repeats the field's row
  (above for the top field, below for the bottom), type 1 averages the rows above and below as bytes (rounded up), type
  2 averages along the one of three directions whose three pixels about it differ least (a diagonal only two or more
  less than straight down; the chroma averaged straight); then the frame is scaled as any frame, and a field out takes
  its parity's rows of the scaled frame.
- Kept as a field (the field types at the same size), a row's chroma for RGBA is its field's (rows 2 (y / 4) + parity).
  A progressive picture out as a field (PTOP_ITOP, PBTM_IBTM) is the frame's conversion, its parity's rows.
Type 2's direction choice is close to libvpost's (its SPU code compares absolute differences of bytes, some of whose
rounding is not known): about 1% of the interpolated pixels of noise differ.

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellVpost: the bilinear scaler's first sixteen columns (part 7)

A chroma plane enlarged into windows at multiples of 16 in both pictures: libvpost's first sixteen columns' positions
are its lanes' offsets, and every negative one is 0 (not only the first: an enlargement past four times has two), which
each later sixteen keeps; for other windows the lanes keep their negative offsets (part 4's rule took only the first
lane, and for any input window). With part 6 the comparison shows 49 of 791 observations differing: scaler types 1 to 3
(36), the edge-adaptive interlace conversion's few pixels (7), a horizontal reduction past a half (2), and the bytes
libvpost writes past a YUV output whose chroma has an odd size (4). cellVpost stays firmware-first (D-563).
What is known of the rest, for whoever takes it up: scaler types 2 and 3 scale vertically with libvpost's 4-tap filters,
tables in its PPU module's data (five of 64 phases, each tap in 1/256 written twice; chosen by the ratio, out over in
times 4 plus 0.6), and type 3 horizontally with its 8-tap ones (seventeen tables of 256 phases in 1/4096, chosen by the
ratio times 16 plus 0.6; past enlarging, the bilinear one); type 2's horizontal filter and type 1's sharpening are
computed by the SPU program. The tables are Sony's data and stay out of the repository: matching them means reading
them from the installed libvpost.sprx at run time, as cellFont reads libfont's (D-526).

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellJpgEnc's stream size limit mode from libjpgenc's tables, read from the firmware (part 8)

libjpgenc chooses a size-limited picture's quality from tables of stream sizes in its data. They are now read from the
user's installed system software at the first size-limited picture, as cellFont reads libfont's (D-526): a new helper,
runtime/hle/src/firmware_data.cpp, decrypts /dev_flash/sys/external/<module> with the build's SELF keys, accepts it only
when it is firmware 4.92's (its prx_identity) and gives back the bytes at a virtual address of its image; nothing of the
data is in the repository. Without the module the mode falls back to part 3's search, logged once.
The algorithm is libjpgenc's encoder thread's, read from its code:
- A trial encoding at quality 75 with the fast DCT (the encoder's colour space, sampling and restart interval; no
  extended parameters) of at most 128x128 of the picture (its top-left corner, or with both sizes past 128 four blocks
  of half that about the quarter points) into a 0x4000-byte buffer gives the activity: its bytes (less 394 past 1182
  when width plus height pass 256) per 10,000 samples (three a pixel, one for gray). A trial that fills its buffer
  counts 0x4000 bytes over the rows it reached less a margin (1, 2, 4 or 8 by how many).
- A curve of sizes by quality is made from the tables (four sampling groups, three activity rows): above the smallest
  row's value at quality 75, between the two rows about the activity (weights in hundredths, the first whose sum is at
  most it), else from the nearest row scaled by the activity over its value (plus a 10% margin, 5% in later tries); for
  pictures of at most 9,999 pixels always the smallest row scaled.
- The target is a share of the limit less the extended parameters' bytes: 80 (75 for activity under 400), 75/70 for up
  to 89,999 pixels, 55 up to 39,999, 60 up to 9,999; less 4 for RGB, 6 for gray, 2 for subsampled YCbCr, 8 or 4 for
  4:4:4; as activity per 10,000 samples, quartered under 400, halved under 800. The quality is the curve's binary search
  for it, less 8 (4 for YCbCr) under quality 40 for plain pictures, at most the one given, less 4, 10 or 12 for small
  plain pictures under 75; a step (4, 3, 2 or 1 by size, doubled for targets under 8 KB, plus 8, 4 or 2 past quality
  60) lowers the later tries.
- If the stream does not fit, the activity is estimated again from the target over the rows reached, the curve made
  again about the quality tried, and the next quality is its search, at most the one tried less 6 or 10, less the step
  doubled per try; three tries at most, then STREAM_OVERFLOW.
Probes on Sony's module and pspocket's (1,116 size-limited pictures: six encoder kinds, gray to ARGB, 33x17 to 640x480,
smooth, noisy and mixed, limits 4 KB to 32 KB, both DCTs, restart intervals): every quality, size, row count and stream
byte the same. The comparison: 14 of 3,751 to 6 (the SPU encoder's, part 9). The comparisons of cellJpgEnc and cellVpost
mount the installed /dev_flash in pspocket's half too, as a game has it.

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellVpost's 2x4-tap and 8x4-tap scalers from libvpost's tables; the bytes past a YUV picture (part 9)

libvpost's filter tables are read from the installed system software at the first picture that needs them
(firmware_data.cpp, part 8: libvpost.sprx of firmware 4.92, its identity checked; nothing committed); without them the
types fall back to the bilinear scaler, logged once. Found by probes (impulse responses at 16 offsets, both signs, 26
ratios; random pictures with windows, fields and both formats; every case byte for byte):
- Scaler type 2 (2X4TAP) is the bilinear scaler horizontally and libvpost's 4-tap filter vertically; type 3 (8X4TAP)
  the 4-tap vertically and the 8-tap horizontally.
- The 4-tap vertical filter: one of five tables of 64 phases in 1/256, chosen by out over in times 4 plus 0.6 (as a
  float; 0 and 1 the first, past 4 the last), the phase the position's 6 bits below the row (positions as the bilinear
  scaler's, the chroma's sited the same way), over the row above to two below; the sum rounded down, clamped. Rows above
  the window are its first; below the picture, mirrored about its last. An output row whose position reaches the last
  row is filtered there at phase 0 with the rows below it the last. It is applied at any height, the same one included.
- The 8-tap horizontal filter: one of seventeen tables of 256 phases in 1/4096, chosen by out over in times 16 plus 0.6
  (2 to 16 the table one below, 0 and 1 the first, past 16 the last), the positions in 1/256 each its own (not sixteen
  at a time): ((x + f) step) / 256 less f whole steps, f the window's column in its 16-column block of the output;
  taps over three columns before to four after, mirrored after the window's last column and before the 16-byte block
  holding its first (the columns between are the picture's); the products summed in pairs, each pair's sum in 1/16
  rounded down, then the four rounded to the nearest and clamped. Where the width is kept the pass is a copy.
- A YUV output whose size is no multiple of 16: libvpost writes its chroma sixteen rows at a time through a buffer of
  sixteen in 16-byte transfers, so past the picture go the first bytes of the V row sixteen above the row after the
  last (still in its buffer).
The comparison: 49 of 791 to 24. Left: the linear-sharp scaler (type 1, 16), reductions past a half with the bilinear
scaler (4), the edge-adaptive interlace conversion (7, part 6), and the tail bytes after such a reduction.

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellVpost's linear-sharp scaler (part 10)

Scaler type 1 (LINEAR_SHARP), read from libvpost's scaler program (its code paths found by comparing the SPU
instructions executed for type 0 and type 1 on the same picture, then the type-1 kernel read) and checked byte for byte
on random pictures, windows and both formats:
- Only luma, and only where the width changes (else type 0's). For each output row the two source rows about its
  position are sharpened, then type 0's vertical step between them, then type 0's horizontal pass.
- The sharpening of a sample: its corners' mean (the byte mean, rounded up, of the means of the up-left/up-right and
  the down-left/down-right neighbours), the sample plus half its difference from it (rounded down), clamped; then moved
  toward the median of it and its left and right neighbours by w/256 of their difference (rounded down), w half the
  byte mean of |up-left - down-right| and |up-right - down-left|, rounded up (no move on flat diagonals, the median on
  steep ones): edges are sharpened, their ringing held back.
- Neighbours: the rows above are the picture's (the first output row's its own row); below the picture mirrored, the
  last row for an output row whose position reaches it; before a window not starting a 16-byte block the picture's
  column, otherwise and past the window's end the edge sample.
The comparison: 24 of 791 to 12 (the edge-adaptive interlace conversion, 7; reductions past a half, 5).

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellVpost's bilinear reductions past a half and its chroma siting at windows (part 11)

Read from libvpost's scaler program and checked byte for byte on random pictures over input windows at columns 0 to
66, output windows at 0 to 72, widths kept, enlarged up to eight times and reduced up to 2.4 times, both chroma types
and both formats:
- A bilinear width reduction past a half (types 0 and 1) first halves the rows: sample m of the halved row at
  start + (m / 16) block + (m % 16) lane in 1/256 of the window's columns, where full = in/out width in 16.16, lane =
  512 (full rounded down to even) / full, block = 8192 (full rounded down to even) / full, and start the output
  window's column in its 16-column block times -(full / 256) plus, for a type-A chroma plane, its siting at the full
  step ((full - 1.0) / 1024); before the window its first column, past its end its last. The halved row (half the
  width) then goes through the ordinary horizontal pass at its own step, its sixteen lanes from the block's start, with
  no siting.
- The sixteen lanes of the ordinary horizontal pass at a type-A chroma plane: a lane whose sited position would fall
  before the input's 16-column block while its unsited one does not starts at the block, for every lane when the output
  window starts a block (as before) and otherwise for lane 0 only (seen where the output window's column is the input
  window's scaled: lane 0 of every block after the first then starts one siting earlier than the formula).
The comparison: 12 of 791 to 7, all the edge-adaptive interlace conversion (interpolation type 2).

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellVpost's edge-adaptive interlace conversion, from libvpost's program (part 12)

Interpolation type 2's kernel was read from libvpost's interlace program by evaluating it with symbolic pixels (in
scratch, nothing of it in the repository): each made pixel between the field's rows above (U) and below (D) is the
byte mean, rounded up, of U[x + d] and D[x - d], d one of 0 (straight down), -1 (up-left to down-right) and +1:
- A direction's cost is mean(mean(|U[x+d-1] - D[x-d-1]|, |U[x+d+1] - D[x-d+1]|), mean(|U[x+d] - D[x-d]|, 0)), every
  mean of two bytes rounded up (avgb): the side pairs weigh a quarter each, the centre pair a quarter, with libvpost's
  roundings, not a sum of three.
- The cheaper diagonal (up-left on a tie) is taken when straight down costs more than it (no margin; part 6 had two).
- Columns past the row's ends are mirrored with the edge column repeated (-1 is 0, -2 is 1; past the last likewise).
- The chroma is averaged straight, the field's edge rows as before.
cellVpostExec no longer logs that type 2 may differ. Test: test_vpost.cpp's edge-adaptive case (a tie between the
diagonals, which the sum took the other way, and a mirrored edge). The comparison: 7 of 791 to 0.

## D-913 · 2026-10-11 · cellJpgEnc's SPU encoder, from libjpgenc's SPU program (part 14)

A picture on the SPUs (enableSpu, the fast DCT) is no longer libjpeg's FAST on the PPU: libjpgenc's SPU program was
read (its colour conversion, DCT and quantisation evaluated with symbolic inputs in scratch; nothing of it in the
repository) and its behaviour checked byte for byte against libjpgenc.sprx on 360 pictures (sizes, qualities, restart
intervals, every sampling, RGB, RGBA, ARGB and YCbCr input, gray and RGB encoders, buffers too small, the size limit):
- jpeg::Dct::Spu (jpeg_encoder.cpp). RGB to YCbCr in single precision: each channel fa(fma(R, kR, fm(G, kG)), fma(B,
  kB, offset)) truncated to a byte, the weights the decimal ones (0.299, 0.587, 0.114; -0.16874, -0.33126, 0.5; 0.5,
  -0.41869, -0.08131) truncated to floats, the offsets a half plus 150 units of 2^-24 and 128.5 less 7 of 2^-16 (12,157
  of the 16.7 million colours get a Y one above libjpeg's). Downsampling, edges below, dummy blocks and the Huffman
  coding are libjpeg's. The DCT: an 8-point transform factored by tangents (tan pi/8, tan pi/16, tan 3pi/16 and
  cos pi/4 as six-decimal floats), columns then rows; quantisation: each coefficient fma'd with its multiplier and
  16384.5, truncated, less 16384; the multipliers the AA&N scale products over 8 (to six decimals) over the table
  entry, from the SPU's reciprocal estimate (frest, fi) and one Newton step. All in the SPU's single precision as
  pspocket models it (pspocket/spu/fp.h: results truncated toward zero, denormals zero), done exactly in doubles
  (TwoSum), with RPCS3's frest table and fi model through pspocket/spu/fp.h.
- Past the picture's right edge the SPU program's row buffers hold whatever its local store held (it converts them
  whole): undefined, here black (a zero pixel converted), what Sony's gives with a fresh local store away from its
  scratch bytes. Pictures a whole number of MCUs wide (16 columns at 4:2:0, 32 at 4:1:1) are exact.
- Its output (cellJpgEnc.cpp, SpuRing): the stream goes through a 4096-byte buffer in local store, its first 4094
  bytes, then 4096 at a time from the buffer's start; each piece is sent only while the game's buffer has more than
  4096 bytes from the piece's start, else the stream overflows there (the rows done before; at the last piece every
  row). A stream that fits the first piece with two bytes more is followed by two bytes past EOI, counted in
  streamSize: what the buffer held there (zeros at first, then earlier streams', the size limit's trial and tries
  included).
The comparison's SPU pictures are now 32x17 (and 64x48 past 4094 bytes, a buffer of 0x1000, a shorter stream after
a longer one): its 33-wide picture showed only the undefined columns. The comparison: 6 of 3,751 to 0 of 3,792.
Test: test_jpgenc.cpp's SPU case (Y 29 against libjpeg's 28 for RGB 0,0,250; the bytes past EOI, zeros, then a longer
stream's; no bytes past a long stream; a buffer of 0x1000 overflowing with every row).

## D-916 · 2026-10-12 · A firmware module starts through its module_prologue, as liblv2 starts it (part 1)

cellRudp's comparison (D-633) found Sony's librudp spinning in its scheduler on sys_lwcond_wait answering CELL_EFAULT:
the lwcond's lwmutex word was 0, because sys_lwcond_create had failed (CELL_ESRCH) on the library's global lwmutex,
which had never been created. librudp makes that lwmutex in a C++ static constructor, and a module's static
constructors run in its module_prologue (NID 0x0D10FD3F), which pspocket never called: the loader, the run-time
module loader and the tests' firmware fixture all called module_start directly (RPCS3 ppu_load_exec's shortcut for the
modules it preloads). liblv2 starts a module as RPCS3's sys_prx_.cpp entryx shows: _sys_prx_start_module gives
module_start in `entry` and module_prologue in `entry2`; when entry2 is set it is called as prologue(entry, args,
argp) (entry all ones without a module_start), and the prologue sets up the module's lock, runs the constructors and
then calls module_start with the two arguments, returning its result. Stopping is the same with module_stop and
module_epilogue (NID 0x330F7005: module_stop, then the destructors and atexit functions).

Now: the LLE loader records each module's prologue and epilogue (PrxModule); a module's start is an hle::ModuleEntry
{entry, wrapper} wherever starts travel (LleModules::take_starts and starts, BootState::module_starts, the module
loader's start, stop and dependency starts); run_module_entry (guest.hpp) makes the call as entryx does; the boot
(loader.cpp) sets r3 to module_start's descriptor (all ones without one) and the arguments to 0 when it calls a
prologue; _sys_prx_start_module and _sys_prx_stop_module write entry2 (no longer always all ones); pspocket's
sys_prx_start_module and sys_prx_stop_module run the wrapper. Every firmware module whose constructors do work was
affected (static locks, tables, std objects): with this librudp's lock exists and its scheduler waits as it should, and
the comparison's first run went from a spinning module to 5 of 649 observations differing.
Test: test_lle.cpp "a firmware module with a module_prologue is started through it" (a synthetic PRX whose second
management export is a prologue that records the descriptor it is given and calls it: started at boot and by
sys_prx_start_module, module_start runs from the prologue, which was given module_start's descriptor).

## D-916 · 2026-10-12 · cellRudp as Sony's librudp does it, call for call (part 2)

D-630 to D-633 wrote cellRudp without Sony's module; its comparison (D-633) found 201 of 342 observations differing,
and much of the design was wrong where it matters to a game or to a peer: the mux modes, the event handler's role, the
signatures (Accept takes seven arguments), the IDs, the options and their checks, the structures, the wire format. The
library is rewritten from librudp's behaviour, read from the module (firmware 4.92's librudp.sprx) in a scratch area
outside the repository; nothing of the module is committed, the code is pspocket's own (cellRudp.cpp's header gives the
architecture, rudp.hpp the wire format). What a game and a peer see, each matched against the module:
- The answers and their order: every call's checks in librudp's order (Bind's mux mode 1 or 2 only, the socket not
  looked at; Listen and Initiate refuse without the event handler; EnableInternalIOThread before any context, priority
  below 0xC00; NetReceived and ProcessEvents THREAD_IN_USE with the thread; Terminate of a terminated context
  INVALID_CONTEXT_ID); context and poll IDs from 0.
- Options: 4-byte values only; the defaults (MAX_PAYLOAD 0x542 under a 0x582 segment, 64 KB buffers, delivery and
  order critical, non-blocking, 60 s connection timeout, 30 ms aggregation, SACK on, 10 s cookies, 20 s keep-alive
  timeout); a connection's parameters refused once it is not idle; LAST_ERROR cleared by its reading; booleans read
  back as 0 or 1; librudp's hidden option 0xFF.
- Structures: CellRudpContextStatus is 48 bytes (state, parent, children accepted, lost, sent and received packets and
  bytes, retransmissions, the smoothed round trip in microseconds), CellRudpStatus 0x128 bytes of counters (per packet
  type, per quality level, connections made and failed by reason), its context count and memory words written whatever
  size is asked. The memory words count librudp's allocations as it sizes them (each with its 16-byte header), the
  peak included.
- The wire format: packets of a 2-byte prefix (vport code, length), their vports, an 8-bit type and flags, the window
  in a byte, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, the acknowledgement delay, SYN parameters (stream, delivery, order,
  level, versions 0x100, token, segment size), RST reasons, options (cookie, segment size, SACK blocks, retransmission
  count and delay, time stamp, padding for the 32 and 64-byte alignment flags); a write larger than one payload in a
  message context goes as several segments, all but the last flagged; aggregation per destination.
- The handshake: a listener's cookie (a RST, reason 2, carrying 32 bytes: its time, a random word and a SHA-256 of
  them with a secret), the SYN again with it, SYN-ACK, ACK; P2P contexts opening at once with Activate; Terminate's
  RST and the peer's CLOSE_WAIT with CONN_RESET; a terminated context lingering, gone for the game, until its timer
  lets it go (then SOCKET_RELEASED for its socket's last context).
- Events: the context handler's (CLOSED with the reason's error, ESTABLISHED, WRITABLE, READABLE, FLUSHED, a child
  ready) with the next round of events, blocking contexts woken instead; the event handler's SEND without the thread,
  100 and 101 around the thread's sendings and receivings.
- Timers and recovery: the context timer, round-trip estimation, retransmission timeouts from 1 to 16 s, delayed
  acknowledgements, SACK, fast retransmission, window probes, keep-alive.
- Reading: the read information's size byte stays the game's (librudp writes it back); a read that took a latency
  critical message counts in the status (+0x40).
- A packet for nobody (another vport, another mux mode) is passed over in silence; a datagram is malformed only where
  a packet runs past its end.
- Sockets go through libnet as librudp's imports do: without the game's sys_net_initialize_network_ex GetLocalInfo's
  address stays zero and the internal I/O thread gets no wake-up socket, as on a console; its thread ends with
  sys_net_free_thread_context. librudp's clock is sys_time_get_current_time.
The comparison (test_rudp_compare.cpp) is rewritten for the real API: the game is the network (SEND's datagrams are
described field by field, random values and times masked, and delivered with NetReceived, each direction compared in
order), a listener with cookies, a stream connection without aggregation, P2P with a loss and its retransmission,
malformed datagrams, the internal I/O thread over lv2's loopback with blocking contexts; each part waits for its
contexts to go. Before: 201 of 342 observations differ; now 0 of 1,808, and the same twice running. Tests: test_rudp.cpp
(the checks and defaults, the handshake with its cookie, data both ways with its read information, a loss, the reset
and its end, packets for nobody, the I/O thread with blocking contexts and libnet).

## D-916 · 2026-10-12 · cellRudp's comparison widened: failures, reordering, windows, keep-alive, the game's allocator, small segments (part 3)

Part 2's comparison left whole areas unseen: its P2P connection never came about in either half (both sides
Activated: Activate waits for the peer's SYN, so a P2P connection is one side Activated and the other Initiating; both
Activated, nothing is sent, and that case stays as a step of its own), and nothing failed, reordered, filled a window
or ran through the game's allocator. Added, each matched against the module:
- Connections that do not come about: a peer that never answers (a 3 s connection timeout: the SYN sent again, a RST
  with reason 3 at the end, CLOSED with CONN_TIMEOUT; the context stays, closed); a SYN to a context that does not
  listen (no answer: the client keeps trying); clients whose stream, delivery or order modes differ from the
  listener's (a RST with the mismatch's reason, CLOSED with CONN_RESET), and whose SACK or payload differ (accepted;
  the accepted context's options).
- A datagram held back behind the next (selective acknowledgements), a burst with one lost.
- A receiver that does not read, with a 4 KB receive buffer: the window closes, the sender holds its segments, the
  window opens as it reads.
- Keep-alive (300 ms probes, a 1.2 s timeout): probes answered, then the peer silent: CLOSED with
  KEEP_ALIVE_FAILURE on the prober, CONN_RESET on the other.
- The game's allocator (cellRudpInit with one): every allocation's size and every release, in order up to the
  contexts' end (from there sorted: which context lingers longer follows the clock).
- A 600-byte segment size set before any context: the payload stays 0x542, a payload of 0x219 is too large; a
  1000-byte message does not fit a datagram.
That last one found a difference: librudp writes a packet into the destination's datagram piece by piece (the prefix's
place, the vports, the header, the payload), each only when it fits, and stops at the first that does not with what it
wrote kept and the prefix left 0; those bytes go out with the datagram (an 8-byte datagram a peer reads as malformed)
and the message is never sent. pspocket rolled the packet back; it now writes as librudp does (a header that does not
fit is dropped whole, where librudp keeps the fields that fitted: not reached with a segment size of 0x40 or more).
Times the halves need not share are kept out of the comparison: the read information's retransmission delay is a
note, how many SYNs and probes fit in a time is compared for the first ones only, and each part ends by waiting until
nothing more is freed for 1.5 s (the timers of contexts that went are freed when they come due, up to a retransmission
timeout later). The comparison: 0 of 2,631 observations differ, three runs in a row (about 110 s a run).
Test: test_rudp.cpp "a packet larger than the datagram leaves its start in it".

## D-918 · 2026-10-12 · cellSysconfPs1emu as Sony's libsysutil_sysconf_ps1emu requests it (part 1)

The PS1 emulator's settings library (four exports known only by their NIDs, in libsysutil_sysconf_ps1emu.sprx, a
libsysutil module pspocket always serves itself, so the four failed when called) is pspocket's own
(runtime/hle/src/cellSysconfPs1emu.cpp), read from the module (fw 4.92) in a scratch area. The module is a client of
libsysutil's: each export builds a request as libsysutil's own requests are built (D-534: the packet begun on channel 0
with ID 0x110, FixedMemory 0, a document with the magic "SYSC"), sends it to the system software and reads the reply
into the same document, its root's "result" first (a negative one is the answer):
- 0x83E79A23 (port, u8 out[2]): "getBattery" {portNo}; "status" to out[0], "level" to out[1]; a level out of the
  status's range (status 0: 1-2, 1: 1-5, 2 and 3 any; a status above 3) is CELL_SYSUTIL_ERROR_VALUE, the bytes written
  all the same.
- 0x6A12D11F (port1, port2): "swapGamePad" {port1, port2}; only the same port twice is refused (the low words
  compared), no range.
- 0x639ABBDE (port): "disconGamePad" {portNo}.
- 0xEFDDAF6C (port, u16 out[2]): "getPower" {portNo}; "status" and "reserved" to the two halfwords.
Ports above 6 (the low word, unsigned) and a null output answer 0x8002BB01 before anything is sent; a reply larger than
the module's 0x6000-byte buffer is libsysutil's TRUNCATED; a missing attribute is cxml's NO_ATTRIBUTE (with what was
read before it written). On pspocket's console the channels are closed (D-534), so each request answers 0x8002b007,
as Sony's module does on pspocket.
Compared (tests/hle/test_sysconf_ps1emu_compare.cpp): every export's checks on closed channels, then channel 0 opened
with a ring and the test answering as the system software in another process would (the request taken out of the
ring, the reply put in, under the channel's mutex): results above and below zero, every battery status with levels in
and out of range, power words, missing attributes, replies of 0x5000, 0x6000, 0x6001 and more bytes; the answers, the
outputs, each request's bytes as the system reads them and the lv2 calls of each call: 0 of 293 observations differ.

## D-918 · 2026-10-12 · The module-management entries of the modules pspocket serves itself (part 2)

The chart's "(module management)" (nids.txt's nameless library "[]": RPCS3's names for the NIDs every PRX exports in
it, module_start, module_stop, module_prologue, module_epilogue, module_exit and the variable module_info) had nothing
of pspocket's: no game imports them, and a firmware module pspocket replaces never runs. Decided: they are the entries
of the modules pspocket serves itself. A game that loads a firmware module by its path whose libraries are the host's
gets a module with no code from the loader (RuntimeModules, D-159), which until now had no entries at all
(sys_prx_get_module_info reported none, starting and stopping ran nothing). It now has the host's, registered under
the nameless library (runtime/hle/src/module_management.cpp) and reached as a firmware module's are (D-916 part 1):
- module_prologue(entry, args, argp) and module_epilogue: as the SDK's start-up code (read from librudp.sprx and other
  fw 4.92 modules) they call the entry with the arguments' low words unless it is all ones and answer its result (0
  without one). The SDK's also make the module's lock and run its C++ constructors (the epilogue its destructors and
  atexit functions): the host's libraries have none, their state being the host's. The SDK's refuse a second start
  with 0x8001000A by a counter in the module's data; the loader refuses one first (ALREADY_STARTED), so none is kept.
- module_start: SYS_PRX_RESIDENT (0), as Sony's modules answer; module_stop and module_exit: 0.
- module_info: the module's description as a PRX carries it (ppu_prx_module_info, 0x34 bytes): attributes 0,
  version 1.1, the name "pspocket", no TOC or tables.
sys_prx_start_module on such a module now runs the prologue with module_start (the result word 0, as before), and
sys_prx_get_module_info reports module_start and module_stop. pspocket-boot --hle-list prints the library's lines with
its empty name first; scripts/progress.py counts them as "(module management)" (and test_hle's NID check takes the
names the NID database gives these fixed NIDs).
Compared (tests/hle/test_module_management.cpp) with librudp's prologue and epilogue on a fresh module: the entry
called with the low words of 64-bit arguments, its answer passed through, nothing called for an entry of all ones:
0 of 7 observations differ. A firmware-free test loads a host-served module by path and checks the reported entries,
the start's and stop's results and the second start's refusal.

## D-918 · 2026-10-12 · cellSailRec pspocket's own, from libsail_rec (part 3: the recorder before Boot and the game's objects)

cellSailRec is the recorder side of libsail (libsail_rec.sprx, fw 4.92: 58 exports, all with RPCS3's names, none of
them pspocket's until now). It is read from the module in a scratch area (nothing of it committed) and made pspocket's
own part by part (runtime/hle/src/cellSailRec.cpp, cellSailRecObjects.cpp, cellSailRecControl.cpp, cellSailRec.hpp;
compared in tests/hle/test_sail_rec_compare.cpp: the same script in two fresh processes, libsail_rec loaded in Sony's).
What it is: the game's feeders (CellSailFeederAudio/Video, its callbacks, which libsail_rec drives) give frames; the
recorder converts and encodes them on the game's SPURS (its own SPU programs, among them an AAC encoder, and the
firmware's AVC, MPEG-4 and M4HD encoders) and gives the streams to a composer: the game's (CellSailComposer, type 3) or
its MP4 writer (type 1, through the firmware's MP4 library). A control thread runs it from a message queue laid out
as libsail's (D-562), with a second thread bringing the SPU tasks' messages from a SPURS queue. It has no camera or
microphone of its own: a console without them records what the game's feeders give it, like any other.

This part, everything up to Boot and the objects the game owns:
- **Initialize** (recorder, allocator, handler, argument, attribute {0x1C, mode 0/1, audio, video and user streams,
  messages, timescale}, resource {0xC, SPURS, 0}): the recorder (0x2000 bytes) cleared once both sizes are right,
  then the allocator, SPURS and the resource's last word checked (so a NULL allocator leaves it cleared); SPURS's SPU
  count asked; one block from the allocator (boundary 8: the slots, 0x2B8 bytes an audio stream, 0x460 a video one,
  0x28 a user one, and the ring, 16 bytes a message, 50 per stream and 50 when the game gives 0); the queue's lv2
  pair ("_saiqu0") and the recorder's lwmutex and lwcond ("_saicx0"); the defaults (control thread 900 with 0x3000
  bytes of stack, task handler 0x370 with 0x8000, the common taskset's eight SPU priorities, the MP4 composer's 600
  and 0x2000, each audio slot's and video slot's parameters, a video stream's SPU count one less than SPURS's but at
  least 1), the timescale 1000000 when 0, the MP4 composer's file calls (libsail_rec's own: internal functions here).
  The allocator failing is MEMORY with the state 9.
- **Finalize**: INVALID_STATE once finalized; a booted recorder is told to end and its thread joined; then the lwcond,
  the lwmutex, the queue's pair (skipped when the queue's count reads -1, as libsail_rec checks) and the block.
- **Set/GetParameter** (before Boot): the recorder's own (2, 29, 64 to 67, 82, 83: set from param0 only with a nonzero
  param1, read back with param1 NULL, some sign-extended) and the per-stream ones by index (audio 68 to 72, video 73
  to 77 and 79 to 81; 78 refused; an unknown recorder parameter accepted and kept nowhere).
- **SetFeederAudio/Video, Register/UnregisterComposer** (type 3 only, once; Unregister also once booted),
  **Subscribe/UnsubscribeEvent** (events below 12, a subscription's parameter 0), **ReplaceEventHandler** (EDEADLK
  taken as the lock held), **Boot**'s refusal when a stream has no feeder (INVALID_STATE).
- **The commands' sending side**: CreateProfile (1), DestroyProfile (2), CreateVideoConverter (3: the two formats'
  fields checked as libsail_rec does, the conversions 4 and 9 to 1, 11 and 12 to 1, 4 and 9), DestroyVideoConverter
  (4), OpenStream (5), CloseStream (7), Start (9), Stop (0xB) and Cancel (0xE at the queue's head): each argument
  check, then INVALID_STATE before Boot (the recorder not running); once running, libsail's command protocol (a
  reply record posted at the queue's head, one lwcond wait).
- **DumpImage**: the version (0x492000), the "modules are the process's" flag, the recorder's first 0x880 bytes, the
  profile in use with its parameters, the MP4 composer and its streams, each slot with its feeder (and a video slot's
  converter), each block at the next 64-byte boundary, the padding counted only when it fits.
- **Feeders**: Initialize (four of the game's eleven callbacks required, the attribute NULL; libsail_rec's own eleven
  callbacks put in front, their argument the feeder), Finalize, the notifications as messages to the recorder (audio
  0x0F to 0x12, video 0x19 to 0x1C; an error's terminated flag in bit 31 cleared) or to a diagnostic handler the
  feeder may hold (its value sign-extended); r3 afterwards is what libsail_rec leaves (the queue's unlock).
- **The composer**: Initialize (the game's 17 callbacks, the last three words 0; its two lwmutex and lwcond pairs
  "_saimx0", "_saimx1"), Finalize (state 1 only), GetStreamParameter (0 or INVALID_STATE: libsail_rec writes nothing),
  GetEsUserParameter (0), GetEsVideo/AudioParameter (an open stream's 0x50 and 0x48 bytes; the index checked only
  against 3, a negative one read before the table), NotifyCallCompleted (the pending call's completion once, or the
  diagnostic handler), NotifySessionError, Get/TryGet/Release of access units on a stream's ring: times in 90 kHz
  (the product wrapping in 64 bits, a signed quotient), the number taken n whenever any are there, *remaining the
  units less that, a Get's failed wait answered 0 (user and video) or its error (audio), Release giving back at most
  those there (the user stream's message carrying n). libsail_rec's user stream copies the game's first entry over
  the rest (its units are never read): kept.
- **Profiles' setters**: SetStreamParameter (the buffer size, all ones for 1 MB, less refused; the stream parameters
  by the composer type), SetEsAudioParameter (AAC: channels, layout, the five sample rates, equal bit rates within
  half and six times the rate; the extension copied in before its checks, so a refused one stays; its float 0.0 or
  -0.0), SetEsVideoParameter (MPEG-4, AVC and M4HD; the frame rate codes; up to 32 encoder options, each ID one the
  encoder knows: the four and seventeen IDs libsail_rec accepts, interface constants of the encoders).
- **Video converters' queue**: CanProcess, CanGetResult, Process (FULLED, or one wait for room with the count read
  once before it), GetResult (EMPTY at once, or after a wait even when woken).
Registered: all 58 (and the internal functions the objects carry: the feeders' and composer's tables, the file
calls, the two threads). The control thread, profiles' and converters' making, the streams and the recording are later
parts: they stop the process with the call site (rule 5). So cellSailRec is marked firmware-first (D-563): where the
system software is installed a game gets libsail_rec until the rest is compared too.
Compared: Initialize and Finalize (82 observations), every parameter (1,456), the recorder's API before Boot with
DumpImage at 26 sizes into aligned and unaligned buffers (390), feeders (119), the composer (388), profiles (612),
video converters (44): 0 of 3,091 observations differ (each half's code addresses, the lv2 objects' IDs and stack
words masked; the profiles, converters and composer streams laid out by the script as the control thread lays them
out).

### D-918, part 4: cellSailRec's control thread, task handler, profiles, Cancel and Finalize once booted

libsail_rec's own threads, natively (runtime/hle/src/cellSailRecControl.cpp), as fw 4.92's module runs them:
- **The control thread** ("_libsail-control-ex", from Boot): the command it answers is 0x20 (Boot's); its stack's top
  less 2000 kept for the event handler; under the recorder's lwmutex a SPURS queue of 16 messages of 16 bytes (SPU to
  PPU) at +0x580 with an lv2 event queue attached, the task handler started ("_libsail-task-handler", its priority and
  stack from +0x858), the clock in mode 0 (0x58 bytes, its lwmutex "_saisr0", priority protocol, recursive), the
  composers' table (none in use, the recorder), each audio and video stream's pipeline (cleared, state 1, the
  recorder and the clock) and its feeder's makeup (the recorder, the index, the state 1, the game's makeup through
  libsail_rec's table). Then running (+0x700), the state 2, the state event, Boot's completion event, the lwcond
  signalled, the lwmutex released, the messages taken. At the end, in the reverse order: the video and then audio
  feeders' cleanups and pipelines, the clock (also when its making failed, as libsail_rec does), the profiles freed
  (each one's first 4 KB cleared), the task handler stopped (+0x514) and joined, the event queue detached, the state
  10; a failure ends with the state event 9 and Boot's completion with the error (sign-extended). Which steps are
  undone follows libsail_rec's flags exactly (no detach when the attach failed, no join when the thread was not made).
- **The message loop**: 200 at +0x510 while waiting (the queue's condition, 3 s at a time), then the message's first
  word; codes above 0x35 passed over, as are 6, 8, 0xA, 0xD, 0x12, 0x13, 0x1C, 0x1D, 0x24 to 0x2A, 0x2D, 0x2F.
  Completions drive the continuation engine (a failed step marks its record and is an error event, "error 0x%X"
  printed first, unless it is a cancellation; the record's last step runs its continuation with 0 or CANCEL; an
  answer above 0 is the steps sent out again, else the record's own completion goes to the step it belongs to).
  CreateProfile (INVALID_STATE in state 0; one block of (2 video + audio + user) * 512 + 4096 bytes, boundary 8, or
  MEMORY; the profile's 0x118 bytes from +0x438 all ones, the type, state 1, the recorder; each stream's parameter
  entry {1, index, profile} and the rest all ones; first on the recorder's list), DestroyProfile (taken off the list
  and freed; 0 also for one not there), Cancel (each audio and video feeder's callback 6), Finalize's message 0x30
  (the stop record in use, the recorder no longer running, every event unsubscribed; a booted recorder told to end
  with 0x31), the converters' notifications 0x32 to 0x35 (their callback).
- **The task handler** pops the SPURS queue as libsail_rec does inline (not through libsre): its pop index marked while

### D-918, part 6: cellSailRec's streams over the composers: OpenStream, CloseStream, Start, Stop, Finalize's stops

libsail_rec's stream control and composers, natively (runtime/hle/src/cellSailRecStream.cpp, cellSailRecCompose.cpp),
as fw 4.92's module runs them on its control thread:
- **The steps**: each command is a tree of asynchronous steps over the composer in use, each stream's feeder and its
  pipeline; a step's record {flags, steps out, its parent's handle} at the recorder's +0x400 (the command), +0x410 (its
  streams' step, +0x420 the next), +0x450 (Finalize, +0x460), +0x470 (a session error, +0x480), each slot's start (its
  own record) and +0x30 (its stop), the handles' continuations libsail_rec's internal functions (pspocket's own here).
- **OpenStream** (message 5): booted, no command pending, the profile free; the path kept in the profile with a '/'
  after it (0x421 bytes at most; none added past 0x41F), the command 0x21 pending, the state 3, answered at once; then
  the profile in use, its composer attached (the game's: its makeup callback with the recorder and the composers table,
  registered under its type) and its stream parameters' defaults (90000 and half of it, the buffer at least 1 MB), the
  composer opened (its instance of the size its table asks; the game's open callback with the path); its continuation
  opens every closed slot, video first, each its own record, the feeder asked to open with the profile's format (the
  defaults for the game's and the MP4 composer: video coding 3 with MPEG-4, audio coding 1, 1024 samples a frame, 48
  kHz, AAC); the first stream marked as the one the composer follows. A composer that cannot be had is an error event
  and everything closed (the completion carries CANCEL).
- **CloseStream** (7): open, no command; closing, answered; each slot out of the composer and its pipeline and feeder
  closed, the composer closed (its close callback gets the step's handle in r5), its instance freed, the game's composer
  detached (unregistered, its cleanup callback), the profile free again, event 5.
- **Start** (9): open, no command; the start parameter {0x18, 0, start, duration} (its second word set to 0x100 in the
  game's copy; another size or a word set: INVALID_ARG), the end time (all ones without a duration), the file name
  after the profile's path (a leading '/' dropped when there is a path); starting, answered; a new session, the clock
  reset, the composer started (its start callback with the path and the session) and each open slot's pipeline, then
  each slot's feeder with the session and the times. **Stop** (0xB): recording, no command; the stop parameter {0x10,
  0, the end time} or none (0); each slot's feeder stopped at the end time, then its pipeline, then its composer stream
  ended; the composer's stop completes when its last stream ends and has given back its units, which completes Stop.
  The flushing stop (0xC, posted by libmp4) and a composer's session error (0x2E: an error event; a terminating one
  while recording stops everything) stop every slot and the composer at once.
- **Finalize** by the state: recording stopped and closed, an open stream closed, then the loop's end.
- **The game's composer** (the table libsail_rec gives it): the states (1 closed, 2 open, 3 recording, 4 opening, 5
  closing, 6 starting, 7 stopping) moved on by the recorder's continuations; its streams (10 added, 12 recording, 11
  ended, 13 done, 9 removed) with their parameters copied for the game, their ring sized from the stream parameters
  (the units for the parameters' time, and 4), the game told by its callbacks (add, end, an access unit arrived with
  1); an access unit kept in the ring while the stream records and the game has its callback, else given straight back
  (a release message); the game's callbacks find in their registers what libsail_rec leaves there (the makeup the
  recorder and the composers table, the cleanup zeros, close and end the step's handle, the stop its caller's word).
User streams: libsail_rec never gives them to a composer (its user-stream functions are unreachable); only their
parameters' "first stream" flag is set. Not reproduced, by nature: libsail_rec's faults, where pspocket stops the
process with the call site (rule 5): a composer whose instance cannot be allocated or whose makeup refuses leaves the
type in use at -1, and libsail_rec then reads its composer table at the session counter. A recorder without audio and
video streams can start but never stop (no stream ends to end the composer's stop), as libsail_rec.
Compared (tests/hle/test_sail_rec_compare.cpp, a recorder without audio and video streams and the game's composer,
its callbacks recording r2 to r5): OpenStream and CloseStream with the callbacks answered by the script, with an open
that fails, without callbacks, with paths of 0, 0x41F, 0x420 and 0x430 bytes and one ending in '/'; the commands
refused around them (Start's parameter checks, Stop, a second OpenStream, CloseStream when closed); DumpImage of an
open stream; Finalize with the stream open; the same with every event unsubscribed: 0 of 229 and 0 of 52 observations
differ (each half's continuations' descriptors masked in the records and the callbacks' handles). The feeders'
stream side, the pipelines and the MP4 composer stop the process with the call site until their parts.

## D-919 · 2026-10-12 · cellSail's playback engine from libsail (part 1: the file source merged)

cellSail's last 17 functions (Start, Stop, Next, Cancel, OpenEs/ReopenEs/CloseEs of each kind, the adapters' GetFrame
and GetFrame2, cellSailAuReceiverGet) need libsail's playback engine behind them: the elementary streams opened and
closed, the data flow through the source, cellDmux, the decoders' pipelines and their copy threads to the renderers
and AU receivers, the clock. It is made pspocket's own part by part, read from libsail.sprx (fw 4.92) and compared with
it running on pspocket in tests/hle/test_sail.cpp (parts 14 on).

Part 1: the built-in x-cell-fs file source (D-901; its first commit message says D-564) merged. Its OpenStream scripts
had not run since the merge of D-562 parts 9-13 and differed only in the test: cellDmux keeps the pipeline's callback
(each side's own code) in its memory, which the source's 2 MB buffer now comes before, so the fixed place the script
masked missed it (masked now by value wherever it is in the allocator's memory); and the player's message ring held
the reader thread's answer and the control thread's own completions in whatever order the threads ran (compared in no
order now). The eight file source comparisons and the D-562 parts pass, three runs.
