## D-919 · 2026-10-12 · cellSail's playback: Start, Stop, Cancel, the data path and the AU receiver (part 3)

libsail's playback engine (runtime/hle/src/cellSailPlay.cpp; the clock's sync engine in cellSailClock.cpp; the dmux
pipeline's data path in cellSailDmux.cpp; the decoders' play side and both copy threads in cellSailPipelines.cpp; the
renderers' and AU receivers' play calls in cellSailRenderers.cpp; the adapters' and the AU receiver's play callbacks
and frame calls in cellSailAdapters.cpp), read from libsail.sprx (fw 4.92). cellSailPlayerStart, Stop, Cancel,
cellSailAuReceiverGet, cellSailSoundAdapterGetFrame and cellSailGraphicsAdapterGetFrame/GetFrame2 are registered.
- **Start** (command 0x6C, call 10): refused (INVALID_STATE) unless the stream is open or started (player state 4 or 6)
  with no call running and nothing deferred but an input's end; a frame-step command (its +4 64) while not playing is
  refused, any other command is the descriptor's InquireCapability's to refuse; a command with flag 0x10 is kept as the
  repeat information (once). The start information (+0x1D0) comes from the command or its defaults. Every open
  elementary stream is started (its dmux part added and enabled or enabled; the renderer started, told whether the
  stream was only open; the decoder's sequence started; or the AU receiver started; steps 0x70-0x7B on the record at
  +0xE0), then the source with its start command (the byte past the header, the length to the end) and the session
  word at the player's +4 (the low 10 bits count sessions, by 128 then by one; flags for the start type, the
  complete-stream flag, a frame step, the end pause, the streams open, the rate in bits 22-31); Start completes when
  the source answers (state 6, event 3 and the call's completion event). Start while started stops the stream first.
- **Stop** (0x7D, call 11; INVALID_STATE unless started): the source stopped, the dmux pipeline reset, every started
  stream stopped (its decoder flushed, its renderer or receiver stopped), state 4 when all answered. **The input's
  end** (0x17; event 8 without an EP walk): the source drains, the pipeline drains, each decoder ends its sequence and
  each renderer or receiver plays out what it holds; then state 4. A call made while another runs is deferred (the
  record's bits: 2 start, 4 next, 8 stop, 0x10 the input's end). **Cancel** is posted at the queue's head (0xD0): the
  source's cancel, every open stream's renderer's or receiver's cancel; it answers 0.
- **The data**: StreamOut items are checked out and fed to cellDmux while it wants them; each AU found goes to the
  decoder while it takes AUs, or to the AU receiver; the copy threads ("_libsail-adec_copy", "_libsail-vdec_copy")
  copy PCM and pictures (through cellVpost where asked) into the renderers' frames.
- **The AU receiver** (cellSailAuReceiverGet and its callbacks): a queue of four AU records (+0x100, the dmux's user AU)
  filled one at a time while AUs are found and records free; Get hands them out double buffered (two slots, the AU
  handed out held until the next Get gives it back: message 0x16), by the game's session (16-bit compare), time and
  flags (bit 0 the AU before, bit 1 the latest due, bit 2 only AUs marked as bit 3 says); its answers 28, 1, 12, 257,
  260, 268, 276, 516, 528, 532, 784, 788 and 0x200 + those given back << 8 | 4 or 8. A receiver's stop (flushed: the
  queued AUs given back; draining) is answered only through the game's next Get once nothing is queued, libsail's:
  a game that stops calling Get holds the player's Stop, Start-while-started and the stream's end.
- libsail's quirks kept: a failed start of a stream never completes Start's step; the video copy thread unlocks a
  mutex it does not hold for a picture's further fields; the feeding does not check the source's checkout answer; the
  decoders' 0xD2 errors are not acted on; the AU receiver's checkin counts a free record also for an AU given straight
  back while not started, so its free count can pass four. The video copy thread's small tables (fields shown and
  cellVpost's picture structure per H.264 pic_struct, the field order swapped, the frame time per frame rate code in
  90 kHz ticks) are the standards' values as libsail uses them.
- Later parts, failing loudly until then: cellSailPlayerNext (not registered yet), a deferred Next, a repeat into the
  next descriptor, EP skipping (start type 16), the elementary streams of a started stream opened, reopened or closed,
  OpenStream of a descriptor not yet opened, MP4 and AVI streams, libsail's sample rate converter (libapostsrc_mini).
  The adapters' frame calls are compared in part 4.
- **Compared** (tests/hle/test_sail.cpp part 16, `[sail]`): a player with one AU receiver over a PAMF stream of user
  data AUs (synthetic packs) through a game's source in guest code (its start and stop answering at once, its checkout
  handing out items, the rest recorded): Start's and Stop's refusals, a start, a start while started (its stop
  answered through Get), five items fed and the AUs queued, Get in each way with the input's end coming meanwhile and
  the stream drained through Get, a second start stopped with AUs queued, Cancel, CloseStream, Finalize: 0 differences
  in three runs; every earlier `[sail]` test passes. Without the firmware, the same script runs on pspocket's side
  alone and its answers are checked against libsail's (`cellSail: the playback through an AU receiver on pspocket
  alone`).

## D-919 · 2026-10-12 · cellSail's Next, the switch to the next descriptor, as libsail (part 5)

cellSailPlayerNext (command 0xA7, call 12), the last of cellSail's 124 functions to be pspocket's (all registered now),
with libsail's switch to the next descriptor (runtime/hle/src/cellSailPlay.cpp):
- **Next** is refused (INVALID_STATE) unless the stream is open or started with no call running and a next descriptor
  (+0x228), or with a deferred call other than an input's end; a command is the next descriptor's InquireCapability's
  to refuse and is kept as the repeat information (with flag 0x10 it stays for later starts). Accepted: state 5, the
  pause off; an open stream moves on at once, a started or ending one is stopped first (with start flag 1 ended,
  flushed; 0xA9). A Next deferred behind a running step (the record's bit 4) runs when it is done.
- **The switch** (records +0xD0, +0xE0): the next descriptor made ready as OpenStream does (0xAA), its start information
  from the repeat command, the renderers' formats for it; a different source closed and the next one's opened, the
  same one told of the descriptor (0xAB, 0xB2); the dmux pipeline reopened for a different kind (0xAC, 0xB3), else
  kept with the new source. Each stream slot: kept when its next entry is chosen and compatible (the ES filter, for
  PAMF the coding's fields; the decoder: coding, channels, rate, frame / coding, profile, specific bytes, picture and
  format out; the renderer's format), its dmux part removed when it differs; otherwise the decoder or renderer (or both)
  closed (0xAD-0xB1) and, the entry chosen, opened again with the new format (0xB7-0xBB), an AU receiver only closed
  when its stream is not chosen; a slot not open completes its steps at once. Once all are in: the old descriptor's
  open streams chosen again (event 10 each), it is closed for the player (state 1, event 5), the next one current
  (the descriptor count one less), each stream kept or reopened open (its dmux part added again with the later SDKs,
  event 9), event 4, and its streams start; Next completes (0xA8: state 6, the run type from the start type; a
  failure: state 4). A failed switch takes the new stream down (closed, or stopped when streams had started) and
  answers CANCEL (0xBC, 0xBD).
- libsail's ways kept: an AU receiver's stop is answered only through the game's Get, and a graphics adapter's stop
  waits for the frames the game holds to come back through GetFrame2, so a game must keep calling them for Next (and
  Stop) to go on.
- Still failing loudly: a repeat into the next descriptor (repeat mode 2, its seamless path and messages 0xCB-0xCF),
  EP skipping, the elementary streams of a started stream, OpenStream or Next of a descriptor not opened (its header
  read through the source), MP4 and AVI streams, libsail's sample rate converter.
- **Compared** (tests/hle/test_sail.cpp, `[sail]`): part 19, an AU receiver: Next refused before a stream, without a next
  descriptor and with a refused command; Next from the open stream (switched to and started), AUs; Next while playing
  with a start command (stopped first, answered through Get) and refused while it runs; AUs; Stop. Part 20, a sound
  and a graphics adapter: Next while playing from AVC 96x64 to AVC 128x64 on another channel (the audio stream kept,
  the video decoder and the graphics adapter closed and opened again: the game's pictures given back and asked for
  again), the new stream played to its end. 0 differences in three runs each; all 31 `[sail]` tests pass. A firmware-free
  test checks part 19's answers on pspocket alone. The scripts' source now keeps its item table apart from the items
  (from 14 items on, the table had overwritten the first items in parts 17 and 18; their firmware-free answers redone).

## D-919 · 2026-10-12 · cellSail's descriptors the game never opened, as libsail (part 6)

A descriptor added without cellSailDescriptorOpen (state 2) is opened by the player when OpenStream or Next makes it
ready (runtime/hle/src/cellSailControl.cpp): opening (4), its stream opened on the control thread as Open's command
does (the protocol's source found by the URI, made up by its first user, libpamf loaded), then its header read through
the source's asynchronous Read: 2 KB into a buffer from the player's allocator, the read's handle kept at the
source's +0x60 so the game's NotifyCallCompleted completes it (message 0x4A). The read done: a header longer than what
was read is read again whole; else it is parsed (stream offset and size, cellPamfReader, a stream without entry points
flagged (+0x18 bit 0), the mux rate, the duration), the streams chosen and the descriptor in use (5). A refused Read
closes the descriptor's stream again and the preparation fails (the descriptor left opening, libsail's); a read that
fails closes the descriptor (back to added) and the call fails; a failure after the read frees the buffer (when a second
read was refused, the first buffer a second time, as libsail does). Its total size goes to a word on libsail's stack.
- **Compared** (tests/hle/test_sail.cpp part 21, `[sail]`): a descriptor with a header of two units added unopened and
  OpenStream (read in 2 KB, then whole), a start and AUs, Next to another unopened descriptor (made ready the same way,
  switched to while playing), AUs, Stop, CloseStream, and a descriptor whose source's Read fails (OpenStream completes
  with CANCEL after an error event): 0 differences in three runs; all 33 `[sail]` tests pass. A firmware-free test checks
  its answers on pspocket alone. The test's source answers its Read at once (ReadSync's copy, then
  NotifyCallCompleted from the control thread).

## D-919 · 2026-10-12 · cellSail's elementary streams of a started stream, as libsail (part 7)

OpenEs, ReopenEs and CloseEs while the stream plays (runtime/hle/src/cellSailEs.cpp): a stream not chosen is opened,
then started (0x8D/0x93/0x99); a chosen one reopened is stopped first, a video renderer keeping its last frame,
whether its format changed or not (0x90/0x96/0x9C: event 10), then started again with its entry as it now is (event 9)
while the stream plays; CloseEs of a started stream stops it (keeping nothing) before closing it (0x9F/0xA2/0xA5). As
libsail: a failed start of a reopened or newly opened stream closes it with a completion on record 0 (which libsail then
reads at address 4), and a stopped stream's dmux part stays enabled, so with the later SDKs its start fails (the
enable is refused), the stream is stopped and closed again and the ReopenEs call never completes, leaving the player's
Stop and CloseStream refused until Finalize.
- **Compared** (tests/hle/test_sail.cpp part 22, `[sail]`): an AU receiver's stream while playing: CloseEsUser (stopped
  through Get, closed), OpenEsUser (opened, started), AUs, ReopenEsUser (stopped through Get, its start refused, closed;
  the call left running), Stop and CloseStream refused, Finalize: 0 differences in three runs; all 35 `[sail]` tests
  pass; a firmware-free test checks its answers on pspocket alone.

## D-919 · 2026-10-12 · cellSail's repeat into the next descriptor, as libsail (part 8)

Repeat mode 2 (SetRepeatMode 2) with a next descriptor (runtime/hle/src/cellSailPlay.cpp): at the source's end of
input the next descriptor is made ready (as OpenStream does; the record at +0x120 running, kind 4; message 0xCB). A
refused preparation marks the record, is an error event, takes the next descriptor back to added and closes it, and
the stream ends as without a repeat. Ready: its start information (no command) and the renderers' formats; when it has
the same source and either another dmux kind or every stream compatible (an open stream chosen again and its dmux
part, decoder and renderer format the same; a stream not chosen staying unchosen; user streams only chosen), it is
swapped to without stopping: the dmux pipeline given its source, each open or chosen stream's old entry chosen again
(event 10, the old entry looked at again after the game's handler) and its new entry open (event 9; user entries take
the old ones' values), the old descriptor closed for the player and the next one current (one descriptor fewer), then
event 5, the source told of the descriptor (0xCC: event 4) and a new session started on it (0xCD: event 6). Otherwise
the stream ends (0xCE) and the player switches to the next descriptor as Next does (0xCF; a failure leaves the player
open: state 4, then 2). A call deferred meanwhile runs instead (the next descriptor left opened).

## D-920 · 2026-10-12 · libvdec's last functions, its PTS correction and frame rates, as Sony's libvdec (part 1)

libvdec's six functions RPCS3 names that pspocket lacked, and Sony's two unnamed exports, are pspocket's own, read in
Sony's libvdec 4.92 and compared with it (tests/hle/test_vdec_ext_compare.cpp: DivX 3.11, DivX, MPEG-4 part 2, VC-1 and
H.264, each a process of its own per half; 0 of 954, 961, 958, 1,036 and 1,004 observations differ).

- **cellVdecGetPicItemExt** (and **GetPicItemEx**, the same code in Sony's module; GetPicItem is it with no third
  argument): the next item, then the codec part's extra: H.264 and MVC write the address of the picture information's
  part past 0x138 bytes to the third argument when it is given; the other codecs write nothing.
- **cellVdecSetFrameRateExt(handle, rate, scale)**: scale 0: `rate` is the codec's code (H.264 and MVC 0 to 7, the
  others 1 to 8; else ARG), kept with its frame duration in 27 MHz ticks (24000/1001 1126125 ... 60 450000); else the
  duration is scale x (27000000 / rate) in the PPU's 32-bit arithmetic (a division by 0 gives 0), and the code the one
  of its whole frames a second (23, 24, 25, 29, 30, 50, 59, 60), none for another. Set at once on the game's thread (it
  was queued in order with the access units); a closed decoder SEQ. **cellVdecSetFrameRate** is it with the code less
  0x80, plus one but for H.264, MVC and JVT: JVT's codes start at 1, so its 0x80 is ARG, as Sony's.
- **StartSeq** forgets the frame rate for every codec (it did for DivX only), the PTS base and the VOP time.
  **cellVdecStartSeqExt(handle, arg)**: StartSeq with the codec part's argument (H.264's low byte 1 and top four bits,
  MVC's top bits, the SMVD codecs' low byte), kept; pspocket's decoders do nothing different with it (logged when not 0).
- **cellVdecGetInputStatus(handle, status)**: libvdec's input queue (access units and EndSeq's flush not yet done by its
  decoder thread) as two bytes and a half word: full (four or more: DecodeAu would be BUSY) 1 0, empty 0 1, else 0 0;
  no state checked. MVC: Sony's reads a word its MVC part never writes: FATAL here. A closed H.264 decoder: libavcdec
  refuses the query and libvdec reads its stack word, 0 in the runs: full.
- **cellVdecSetPts** sets the ring's PTS base (33 bits) and loses its unverified mark (D-594).
- **cellVdecDecodeAuEx2** is the form Sony's libvdec decodes in (its DecodeAu converts its CellVdecAuInfo to it, with
  the two words RPCS3 calls unknown 0); **libvdec_652B7BC0** is it again (Sony's export runs the same code). Compared
  with the two words 0: as DecodeAu. Given (a probe with them set), Sony's libvdec hands them to its codec part: the
  DivX, DivX 3.11 and MPEG-4 parts leave them, the H.264 and VC-1 parts take them as a second piece of the access unit
  (its address and size: libavcdec's access unit call takes two pieces, and refuses one past its limits, FATAL).
  pspocket decodes the first piece alone, so the two stay unverified for now, as OpenExt (it takes the game's SPURS,
  which pspocket's decoder does not use) and **libvdec_20DA0CFA**, MVC's decode of an access unit in its two views
  ({base view address, size, 2 words, dependent view address, size, 2 words, PTS, DTS, user data, codec specific data}):
  its checks (MVC only, ARG; mode past 2 ARG) and a ring element per view; pspocket decodes the base view (D-590) and
  frees the dependent view's element when the access unit is done.
- **_cell_vdec_prx_ver**: 0x00492000.

What they act on, missing in pspocket's libvdec until now:
- **A picture whose access unit had no PTS gets one** (Sony's ring, when it announces the picture): the last PTS's time
  plus the frame duration, kept in 27 MHz ticks (33-bit PTSs, wrapping at 2^33 x 300), once a PTS is known (an access
  unit's or SetPts'). The duration is the rate set, else the stream's: DivX 3.11 none (Sony's word is its stack's: 0
  here); DivX 0 (libdivxdec reports the same VOP time for every picture); MPEG-4 part 2 a fixed VOP rate's increment,
  else the VOP time since the previous picture (modulo time base and increment; then added before the picture's time);
  VC-1 the sequence header's FRAMERATENR/DR (libvdec's table, 48000/1001 rounded up) or FRAMERATEEXP; H.264 the VUI
  timing (two ticks a frame: the eight rates by their whole frames a second, else 27 x 10^9 / (fps x 1000)).
- **Frame rate codes**: DivX's information block takes the code set, else the one of the duration's whole frames a
  second (0 for none); VC-1's the code set (the stream's when none is set; a rate set that names none leaves the byte);
  H.264's the code set, else the VUI timing's (0xFF for an unnamed rate), else the byte as it was.
- **VC-1's frame buffers** (D-912 had them in turn): libsvc1d takes, when it decodes the access unit, the first frame
  buffer neither holding a picture not yet released (decoded, announced or not, or of an access unit still in the
  decoder) nor a reference (the last anchor; for a B picture the one before); a skipped picture shows the frame before.
  The choice is made when the access unit is given to FFmpeg (which hands the picture over later).

The comparisons with Sony's libvdec now force Sony's codec cores too (tests/hle/firmware_compare.hpp FirmwareLibrary's
`also`, compare_util.hpp Setup::forced, vdec_test_util.hpp kVideoCores): as pspocket gets cores of its own (part 2 on),
Sony's libvdec loaded in a test would otherwise be linked to them, and the comparisons would no longer be with Sony's
cores. Setup::ours_on_firmware runs Sony's module in pspocket's half too, over pspocket's libraries: the codec cores
driven by Sony's libvdec (part 2).

Tests: test_vdec_ext_compare.cpp (hidden, [compare][vdec-ext]; each life: PTSs missing, SetPts first, SetFrameRate's
codes, SetFrameRateExt's codes and rate/scale forms, a rate before the sequence, StartSeqExt, DecodeAuEx2 and its twin,
the refusals, the input queue held until DecodeAu is BUSY; the input status right after EndSeq is a note, the threads'
timing); test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp's VC-1 comparison (its held pictures now in Sony's frame buffers); test_vdec.cpp
(the unverified marks).

## D-920 · 2026-10-12 · libdivx311dec, the DivX 3.11 core, pspocket's own (part 2)

The codec cores Sony's libvdec drives had only their version queries (D-575); their decoding APIs were Sony's modules'
alone. libdivx311dec's nine functions are now pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/vdec_cores.cpp, over vdec_ffmpeg.hpp: an
FFmpeg decoder for the cores), compared with Sony's module two ways, samples within one step (D-912's IDCT rounding):
- called directly, as libvdec calls it and past what libvdec ever sends (tests/hle/test_vdec_cores_compare.cpp: each
  half makes a SPURS instance and a taskset with pspocket's cellSpurs and gives it to the core): 0 of 419 observations
  differ;
- driven by Sony's libvdec, as a game importing one of libvdec's unverified functions gets it (D-594): D-912's DivX 3.11
  lives with Sony's libvdec in both halves, over pspocket's core and over Sony's (test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp, part 1's
  Setup::ours_on_firmware): 0 of 542 differ.
libdivx311dec is not firmware-first: Sony's libvdec loaded for a game links to pspocket's core.

The core's PPU side is reproduced as Sony's module runs it; its SPU program's part (decoding an access unit into the
frame buffer the PPU side picked and reporting what it did) is done on FFmpeg:
- **QueryAttr(param {type, width, height, frame buffers}, *size, *version)**: two frame buffers only; type 15 sizes for
  1920x1088 (0x68EC00), else 16 to 1920 by 16 to 1088 (two frames plus 0x4D800); version 0x103; else ARG (0x80615502).
- **Open(param, memory, size, taskset)**: the frame buffers past the decoder's 0x3D77F bytes (128-byte aligned at
  +0x3D700); no memory, memory holding an open decoder (its mark 0xBABEFACE at +0x3D64C), no taskset or other than two
  frame buffers ARG; the taskset's cellSpurs errors as they are. **Close** leaves the mark 0x88888888 (a second Close ARG).
- **DecodeAu(handle, au {address, size, width, height, four words}, mode 0x20/0x21/0x22, *status)**: the first frame
  buffer neither held by the game nor the reference to come; none, or no picture entry free (two), BUSY (0x80615510).
  A picture is shown one access unit late (the next DecodeAu or FlushPicture makes it ready, with the frame decoded
  before); mode 0x21 skips all but I pictures, shown at once with no frame (GetPicture's frame 0, its skip byte 1); a P
  picture with no reference: AU (0x80615520), status 0x40020000; the status word from the SPU side's error bits (a
  picture FFmpeg concealed errors in: 0x11, as D-912).
- **GetNumOfPictures, GetPicture** (its frame, the frame's size, the access unit's four words, width and height, type,
  0x30, status, skip byte; PIC 0x80615540 when the status has errors), **ReleasePicture** (the frame held longest),
  **FlushPicture** (the waiting picture ready; Sony's counts its entry once more, kept), **Reset** (every frame and entry
  free, the references gone): their states and answers as Sony's, including GetPicture's taking the head entry off when
  none is ready.

Different, and a note in the comparison: a core opened for one size and given access units of another (libvdec always
gives both the same) — Sony's SPU program decodes the first picture otherwise (up to three steps off); pspocket decodes
at the access units' size.

Tests: test_vdec_cores_compare.cpp: the comparison (hidden, [compare][vdec-cores]) and a firmware-free test of
pspocket's core against the values Sony's gave; test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp "The DivX 3.11 core under Sony's libvdec"
(hidden, [compare][vdec-cores]).

## D-920 · 2026-10-12 · DecodeAuEx2's access unit in two pieces, as Sony's libvdec's codec parts take it (part 3)

Part 1 left cellVdecDecodeAuEx2 and its twin unverified: compared with the two words of CellVdecAuInfoEx2 that RPCS3
calls unknown set to 0 only. Those words are the second piece of an access unit (a ring buffer's wrap): the structure
is the two pieces' addresses, then their sizes, then the PTS, DTS, user data and codec specific data (Sony's DecodeAu
converts its CellVdecAuInfo to it with no second piece). Read in libvdec's codec parts and compared:
- **H.264**: libvdec hands both pieces to libavcdec's access unit call, on the game's thread. libavcdec refuses a second
  piece of no address, and, for a game of SDK 2.4 or later (or of none: libvdec gives libavcdec all ones for a version
  of 0), pieces past 0x1FFFFF80 bytes together: DecodeAuEx2 answers FATAL and the ring element stays free.
- **VC-1**: libsvc1d's DecodePicture2 takes the pieces when libvdec's decoder thread decodes the access unit; a second
  piece needs a first of whole 128-byte blocks and a 16-byte boundary, else it refuses the access unit: ERROR with
  FATAL and the decoder does nothing more (as D-912's decode mode 3).
- **MPEG-2** takes both too (libsmvd2's DecodePicture2: not compared, as the rest of MPEG-2); **DivX, DivX 3.11,
  MPEG-4 part 2 and JVT** give their core the first piece alone.
pspocket decodes the two pieces as one access unit where Sony's codec part takes them (H.264, VC-1, MPEG-2), with
libavcdec's and libsvc1d's refusals, and the first piece alone for the others.

Found with it: a decoder stopped by a fatal error (VC-1's) keeps every access unit and flush given to it in its input
queue, so GetInputStatus shows them (full after four); pspocket dropped them.

Compared (test_vdec_ext_compare.cpp, DecodeAuEx2 now giving odd access units in two pieces, and lives with a second
piece of no address, a first piece not of whole 128-byte blocks and a second piece off a 16-byte boundary): 0 of 1,115
(H.264), 1,117 (VC-1), 1,004 (DivX), 1,001 (MPEG-4) and 997 (DivX 3.11) observations differ. DecodeAuEx2 and
libvdec_652B7BC0 lose their unverified marks (D-594); OpenExt and libvdec_20DA0CFA keep theirs.
Tests: test_vdec.cpp (the unverified marks; DecodeAuEx2 in two pieces decodes as DecodeAu, and libavcdec's refusals).

## D-920 · 2026-10-12 · libdivxdec, the DivX core, pspocket's own (part 4)

libdivxdec's nine functions (divxDecQueryAttr, Open, Close, DecodeAu, GetNumOfPictures, GetPicture, ReleasePicture,
FlushPicture, Reset) are pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/vdec_cores.cpp), its PPU side as Sony's module runs it, its
SPU program's part on FFmpeg. Compared with Sony's module called directly (test_vdec_cores_compare.cpp: 0 of 2,040
observations differ, samples within one step) and driven by Sony's libvdec (D-912's MPEG-4 family lives over pspocket's
core and over Sony's: 0 of 1,088 differ).

What libdivxdec does, read in the module and checked against it:
- **QueryAttr {type, width, height, frame buffers}**: 2 to 4 buffers; types 10 to 14 size for their level's largest
  frame (176x144 to 1920x1088), else the size given (16 to 1920 by 16 to 1088, or 1408x1152); the frames plus 0.5% plus
  0x9E86B, to 16 bytes; version 0x30806. **Open** needs its own 0x31B7C bytes, its two SPU tasks' context save areas
  and overlay table (0x23C00, 0x9C00 and 0x174D0 as Sony's SPU programs give them to cellSpurs and cellOvis) and the
  frames; the frame buffers start at the 128-byte boundary past those, 0x20000 on (+0x76680 from 128-byte aligned
  memory); as many picture entries as buffers.
- **Picture entries** (free, a packed P picture still without its words, waiting, ready) in a ring with a free head, an
  output head and the current picture; frame buffers with their reference state and the game's holds. A frame buffer
  is taken when neither held nor a reference (with two buffers the backward reference may be); DecodeAu is BUSY while
  the game holds all it may (three or more buffers: one kept back) or all entries but one are in use. An I or P picture
  waits until the next is decoded (or the flush) and is then ready with the frame shown: the previous anchor picture;
  a B picture, and one skipped by the decode mode (0x21 all but I, 0x22 B), is ready at once (a skipped one with frame
  0). GetPicture takes the output head off even when it is not ready (SEQ): with B pictures the head is often a waiting
  P picture, so a game asking for a B picture right after its access unit loses that P picture, as on a PS3.
- **DivX's packed bitstream**: an access unit with a P VOP then a B VOP is decoded VOP by VOP; the P picture waits
  without its access unit's words, the B picture is ready with them, and the next access unit, an N-VOP (vop_coded 0),
  gives the P picture its words (mark 0x31). An N-VOP otherwise is a picture of the previous one's frame (mark 0x32); a
  second VOP after anything but a P picture is left (status 0x400). B pictures with two frame buffers: ERROR,
  0x80000200.
- **What the SPU program reports**, as pspocket's does: the layer's size (the frames' layout follows it, whatever the
  size opened for), aspect ratio code and pixel sizes, time increment resolution, fixed VOP increment, interlacing and
  each VOP's top field first, type, time and modulo seconds; a word libvdec reads as "fixed rate" set for every stream;
  no colour description (the visual object's is not read: cellVdec's DivX information now writes 0s there too, the D-912
  life with one checks it); a P, B or N-VOP with nothing to predict from: AU, status 0x20.
- **Frame buffers**: each picture's samples as decoded; a reference picture's edges padded when its next command comes
  (a VOP's decoding, the flush or Reset; FFmpeg's delayed anchor pictures written when it gives them); a B picture's
  edges never (they keep what the buffer held). FFmpeg decodes with its floating point AAN IDCT (FF_IDCT_FAAN), the
  nearest to Sony's: the pictures driven by libvdec are exact, the core's own lives within one step.

Notes in the comparison, not differences: the chroma edges of the picture a flush makes ready (Sony's SPU program pads
them as it answers, so what the game sees of them is the threads' timing), and the pictures after a refused anchor
access unit (Sony's decodes the B pictures that then predict from the wrong pictures, FFmpeg leaves them; a game that
drops an anchor gets garbage either way). Libvdec's answers are 32-bit (Sony's core zero-extends r3; pspocket's
sign-extends, as every HLE error code).

Not yet in cellVdec (found with these lives): its own DivX and MPEG-4 decoding of streams with B pictures is not Sony's
libvdec's with libdivxdec and libsmvd4 (frame buffers, the lost pictures above), and libsmvd4 reports MPEG-4's interlaced
pictures in error, undecoded (to be read with libsmvd4).

Tests: test_vdec_cores_compare.cpp (the comparison, hidden, and a firmware-free test against Sony's values: I and P
pictures, B pictures, the decode modes, packed bitstreams, N-VOPs, layers of other kinds, two and four buffers, a
smaller stream); test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp ("The DivX core under Sony's libvdec", hidden, and DivX lives with an

## D-920 · 2026-10-12 · libsmvd4, the MPEG-4 core, pspocket's own; the s-cores' shared PPU framework (part 5)

libsmvd4's seventeen decoding functions (smvd4GetMemorySize, GetMemorySize2, CreateInstance2, ReleaseInstance,
Initialize, DecodePicture, FlushPicture, Discontinue, CancelDecode, GetPicture, GetNumPicture, ReleasePicture,
GetSideInfoPic, GetAuxData, GetSideInfoSeq, GetExistenceFlag, SetAuxData) are pspocket's own
(runtime/hle/src/vdec_smvd4.cpp), with its version query (D-575) the whole library: no longer firmware-first.
Compared with Sony's module called directly (test_vdec_cores_compare.cpp: 0 of 5,903 observations differ, samples
within one step but where noted) and driven by Sony's libvdec (D-912's MPEG-4 family over pspocket's cores and Sony's,
now with B pictures, interlaced and quarter sample streams: 0 of 1,418 differ).

**The s-cores' framework** (runtime/hle/src/vdec_score.hpp, for libsmvd2, libsvc1d and libsjvtd too): Sony's s-cores
are one design, a PPU library over an SPU task on the caller's taskset that talks to it through two SPURS queues of
one 0x80-byte entry (SPU to PPU, PPU to SPU) in the instance's memory, each attached to an lv2 event queue. Their
answers come from the status word the program leaves, mapped alike in every s-core but for its prefix (answer(),
strict_answer() for Initialize and CreateInstance2, picture_answer() for GetPicture's 0xF00 warnings); their pictures
wait in a queue of frame buffer slots in decoding order (a sequence number each, the get and release counters, the
current picture, the two last anchors as references, FlushPicture's mark: PictureQueue). pspocket makes and attaches
the queues as Sony's core does (their errors are CreateInstance2's answer: a taskset that is none gives cellSpurs's
0x80410902) and detaches them at ReleaseInstance, but runs no task: the program's part is each core's own file.

What libsmvd4 does, read in the module and checked against it:
- **Memory**: levels 0 to 6 (720x576, 176x144, 352x288, 352x288, 720x480, 640x480, 720x576); a block of 0x80 bytes per
  macroblock, three frame buffers ((height to 32 + 32) x (width to 16 + 32) x 1.5 + 0x80 each) and 0x15380 bytes.
  GetMemorySize2 takes type 5's size (words 8 and 9, signed, within the level's). CreateInstance2 takes types 4 and 5
  only (others SEQ), 128-byte aligned memory, the taskset in word 7 (none: SEQ); a refused size is FATAL, too little
  memory NO_MEMORY. The frames start at +0x14A80.
- **What the caller reads back is in the instance's memory**, written field by field as Sony's program writes it, so
  its gaps show the caller's memory: the sequence information at +0x80 (whether a layer is in force, its start code,
  then its fields in syntax order; a field a layer leaves out keeps the last value, but verid and priority become 1
  without an identifier and the fixed VOP increment 0 without a fixed rate), the used bytes at +0x13C (to the end of
  the first VOP; all of an access unit without one; where the parse stopped in a refused layer; 2 when the decoder
  dies), the existence flag at +0x144 (1 once a layer was accepted, 0x10000 once a VOP was, never cleared; written by
  every DecodePicture, so 0xA5A5A5A5 before the first), the auxiliary data at +0x148 and each slot's information block
  at +0x280 (addresses, size, lines, one access unit, the last GOV's fields and the VOP's, the auxiliary data, the
  status with 0x300 added).
- **Access units**: headers then the first VOP. A layer whose frame is larger than the instance's kills the decoder
  (0x..81, then 0x..80 for every command, Initialize included); MPEG quantisation is refused (no picture until the next
  layer). I and P VOPs are decoded; B and S VOPs are not (0x..02; their slot keeps its frame and information, an anchor
  all the same, so a P VOP after one predicts from the slot's old frame); an interlaced layer's VOPs are not decoded
  either (0x..02, P VOPs 0x400 in the picture's status); not coded VOPs give the last anchor's slot again; quarter
  sample motion is taken as half sample. A P VOP with no anchor is predicted from the third slot's frame and flagged
  0x800 unless decoded into that slot; Discontinue flags P VOPs until the next I VOP; nothing is concealed.

FFmpeg made to do that: each P VOP's reference rewritten from its anchor slot's frame before it is decoded
(vdec_ffmpeg.hpp: the decoder keeps its last picture's buffer, which is its reference; writing it is outside FFmpeg's
API contract and only done for this low-delay use), each picture's buffer filled with its slot's old frame
(get_buffer2) and error concealment off, so what FFmpeg does not decode keeps what the slot held as Sony's does, the
quarter sample flag cleared from the layer FFmpeg is given, FF_IDCT_FAAN (155 samples of the comparison's frames one
step off, in 9 frames).

Not reproduced (logged; notes or wider tolerance in the comparison): bit 2 of an interlaced P VOP's warning (set by
Sony's program for some P VOPs from their macroblocks; GetPicture's answer is the same), a P VOP with no anchor decoded
into the third slot itself (Sony's program overwrites its reference as it decodes: a few samples up to 2 steps off),
a P VOP before FFmpeg has had any picture of the layer's size (grey), and the layer features besides MPEG quantisation
the program refuses (shapes, sprites, depths, complexity estimation, NEWPRED, reduced resolution, scalability: refused
alike, not compared). A handle that is no instance (Sony's reads whatever memory it points to) is logged, ARG.

cellVdec's own MPEG-4 decoding still decodes B pictures and interlaced layers (Sony's libvdec over libsmvd4 gives those
pictures undecoded): not changed.

Tests: test_vdec_cores_compare.cpp ("The MPEG-4 core (libsmvd4) against Sony's", hidden, and a firmware-free test
against Sony's values); test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp ("The DivX and MPEG-4 cores under Sony's libvdec", hidden);
test_codec_cores.cpp and test_codec_cores_compare.cpp (libsmvd4 no longer firmware-first).

## D-920 · 2026-10-13 · libsmvd2, the MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 core, pspocket's own, with a decoder of its own (part 6)

libsmvd2's twenty decoding functions (smvd2GetMemorySize, GetMemorySize2, CreateInstance2, ReleaseInstance, Initialize,
DecodePicture, DecodePicture2, FlushPicture, Discontinue, CancelDecode, SetDecodeMode, GetPicture, GetNumPicture,
ReleasePicture, GetSideInfoPic, GetAuxData, GetBnrData, GetSideInfoSeq, GetExistenceFlag, SetAuxData) are pspocket's
own (runtime/hle/src/vdec_smvd2.cpp, on part 5's vdec_score.hpp), with its version query (D-575) the whole library:
no longer firmware-first. Compared with Sony's module called directly (tests/hle/test_vdec_score_compare.cpp: 0 of
7,970 observations differ, every sample of every frame buffer exact) and driven by Sony's libvdec
(test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp's MPEG-2 family, Sony's libvdec over pspocket's core and over Sony's: 0 of 1,560 differ).

**The decoder is pspocket's own** (runtime/hle/src/vdec_mpeg2.cpp, .hpp), not FFmpeg's: FFmpeg's samples are within a
step of Sony's (D-912), and its error handling and buffers are its own. Written from ISO/IEC 13818-2 and 11172-2 (the
standards' code tables, cross-checked with FFmpeg's) and from what Sony's SPU slice program was seen to compute:
- its inverse DCT: the AP-922 row transform (row constants 2^14 x sqrt2 cos(r pi/16) x sqrt2 cos(u pi/16), r 4, 1, 2, 3
  for the row pairs 0/4, 1/7, 2/6, 3/5, rounded at 2^11 and shifted by 12 to 16 bits), then a column transform in
  16-bit arithmetic on the tangent constants' high product halves, shifted by 5;
- MPEG-1 blocks reconstructed as MPEG-2's (saturation and mismatch control, not MPEG-1's odd values);
- the frame buffers in Sony's layout (macroblock after macroblock, 16 lines of luma then 8 of Cb and Cr: 0x180 bytes),
  field pictures in their lines, prediction (frame, field, 16x8, dual prime) from the references the program takes;
- the BNR data (smvd2GetBnrData): two histograms over bands of slice rows (a slice's band its vertical position over
  rows / 4 + 1): words 4 to 7 a P or B picture's residual (each slice: 10240 an intra macroblock, else 128 plus its
  luma coefficients' magnitudes as dequantised before saturation, the sum >> 8), words 0 to 3 the motion (each
  non-intra macroblock's vector differences' sizes, weighted 4 for one vector a direction, 2 for two, halved for both
  directions, 4 for dual prime forward);
- damage: a code no table has, a coefficient past the block's end, a macroblock past its row or the picture, data
  ending inside a macroblock, a slice outside the picture, missing or out of order (below).

**What the program does, read in the module and checked against it** (the details are vdec_smvd2.cpp's head):
- Memory: levels 0 to 4 and 16 (1920x1152, 352x288, 720x576, 1440x1152, 1920x1152, 1280x720); a line store and four
  frames (width to 16, at least 48; height to 32, at least 64), 0x500 bytes per SPU task plus 0x2B500 of tasks and
  queues (two SPURS queues of two entries: part 5's QueuePlaces now has a depth), 0x4600 of its own; GetMemorySize2's
  size within the level's; CreateInstance2 clears 0x3C00 bytes; no taskset SEQ, too little memory NO_MEMORY.
- The side information (0xBC bytes a picture) is the program's record of the headers, kept in its SPU's local store:
  a field a picture's headers leave out keeps its value, from picture to picture and from instance to instance on the
  same SPURS instance (a new SPURS instance's SPUs start with none: libvdec makes one per decoder; a taskset that
  clears local stores, none either). A picture header resets its flags and writes MPEG-1's coding extension values,
  which an MPEG-2 coding extension overwrites; Initialize, Discontinue, CancelDecode and a broken link in an open GOP
  clear the GOP's flag and parity and the picture flags, and the references; FlushPicture clears the picture type.
- Closed captions into the record: ATSC's (GA94, type 3: flags, em_data, the triples, marker and the rest to the next
  start code) and DVD's (CC: the user data as it came, 9 + 3 x (attributes & 63) bytes, none past 128 or when a start
  code comes first), with where the user data was (sequence, GOP, picture).
- A header whose flags call for more fields than it has (a picture display extension with one frame centre offset
  where repeat_first_field calls for two or three) reads them from what follows, start codes too: the parse goes on
  after what it read, so a user data start code read that way is never seen, and a first slice's makes the picture
  damaged, with nothing of it decoded.
- Pictures: a frame, or a field that is not the other of the last one's, takes the first free slot; I and P frames wait
  for the next anchor or FlushPicture, B frames go out when both fields are decoded (or not decoded at all in the mode
  that skips them: 0x80, GetPicture 0x..28). References from the picture queue: a P picture the newest anchor, a B
  picture the two; one gone (Initialize, CancelDecode, FlushPicture) is the queue's 0xFF, which the program takes for
  the last slot, whose frame it reads as it is (0x800); a reference with a warning 0x400. A field of the parity already
  decoded is no picture; an MPEG-2 picture without its coding extension is damaged and not decoded (its slot keeps
  its frame, the BNR data the last picture's). A marker bit that is not 1 is a warning (0x10: 0x80615001). A sequence
  end code after a picture is used with it, then flushes. A picture too large for the instance kills it.
- DecodePicture2's two pieces are joined as the program's DMA joins them: the second lands at the first address after
  the first piece whose low four bits are the second's, so (a2 - a1 - s1) & 15 bytes of whatever follows the first
  piece in memory come between; the used count is mapped back.
- **Slices**: the picture starts at its first slice of vertical position 1 (slices before it are passed over; with none
  the picture is damaged and nothing of it decoded, its BNR data 0). A slice that starts where the one before it ended
  (or in that one's row: another slice of the row) is written in its place; one that does not damages the picture and
  is written from where the one before ended, predicted from its own place, until a macroblock is written at the
  picture's end or past it (into the memory after the frame, as on a PS3: the next frame buffer's first macroblock);
  the next slice is then expected after its own last macroblock. A slice outside the picture is not decoded. After a
  slice in error the next start code is looked for from where the reading stopped (a macroblock in error reads on
  through start codes: those slices are lost), and the macroblock in error counts as passed, not written.

Not reproduced (notes in the comparison): what a macroblock in error leaves for the next. The program keeps what it had
parsed in its coefficient buffers, so the next macroblock coding those blocks has it too, and counts it in the BNR
data; how far it parses (into the bytes after the slice) is its own. Here each block starts from no coefficients, so
the first macroblock after one in error can be off, and with it what is predicted from it: such pictures' samples
(GetPicture's 0x..11 to 0x..13, or 0x400) are notes, but the streams whose damage is their slices' order, whose frame
buffers are cleared first and compared to the sample. Probes with slices cut short got their slices placed as Sony's
and differed in that one macroblock (and the BNR data of the slice in error).

cellVdec's own MPEG-2 decoding (FFmpeg, its information block as RPCS3 fills it) is not Sony's libvdec with libsmvd2:
not changed; the comparison under Sony's libvdec shows what Sony's gives (its information block is 0x1C8 bytes).

Tests: test_vdec_score_compare.cpp ("The MPEG-2 core (libsmvd2) against Sony's", hidden; its firmware-free twin against
Sony's values; "The MPEG-2 core's inverse DCT is Sony's slice program's"), mpeg2_writer.hpp (MPEG-1 and MPEG-2
streams written bit by bit: every kind of macroblock, field pictures, extensions, user data),
test_vdec_cores_compare.cpp ("The tests' MPEG-2 streams decode with FFmpeg": the writer checked against another
decoder), test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp ("The MPEG-2 core under Sony's libvdec", hidden: DecodeAu and DecodeAuEx2 in two
pieces, the decode modes, held pictures, items ahead), test_codec_cores.cpp and test_codec_cores_compare.cpp (libsmvd2
no longer firmware-first).

## D-920 · 2026-10-13 · libsvc1d, the VC-1 core, pspocket's own: simple, main and advanced profiles (part 7)

libsvc1d's twenty-one decoding functions (svc1dGetMemorySize, GetMemorySize2, CreateInstance2, ReleaseInstance,
Initialize, DecodePicture, DecodePicture2, DecodeSeqHeader, SetPictureSize, FlushPicture, Discontinue, CancelDecode,
SetDecodeMode, GetPicture, GetNumPicture, ReleasePicture, GetSideInfoPic, GetAuxData, GetSideInfoSeq,
GetExistenceFlag, SetAuxData) are pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/vdec_svc1d.cpp, on part 5's vdec_score.hpp), with
its version query (D-575) the whole library: no longer firmware-first. Compared with Sony's module called directly
(tests/hle/test_vdec_score_compare.cpp: 0 of 26,805 observations differ, every sample of every frame buffer exact but
where noted below) and driven by Sony's libvdec (test_vdec_codecs_compare.cpp's VC-1 family, Sony's libvdec over
pspocket's core and over Sony's: 0 of 1,276 differ).

**The samples are FFmpeg's VC-1 decoder's** (VC-1's reconstruction is exact by the standard; Sony's four SPU programs,
headers and pictures, blocks, prediction, deblocking, gave the same samples in every stream compared), written into
Sony's frame buffers (16-sample strips, 64 lines of edge above and below the luma, 16 samples each side, Cb and Cr in
each strip's halves; field pictures' edges each field's, vdec_layout.hpp) and given out through Sony's picture queue.
What FFmpeg reads otherwise than the standard is changed in the bits it is given (pan-scan windows it does not read
left out, DQUANT 2 given as DQUANT 1 with each picture's VOPDQUANT to match, a progressive P picture's DMVRANGE in an
interlaced sequence of extended differential vectors); the simple and main profiles go through FFmpeg's VC-1 decoder
(pspocket's build has no WMV3 one) as STRUCT_C behind a sequence header's start code, an entry point made from its
coding tools, and the frames as BDUs. Where the program predicts from other frames than FFmpeg would (after
FlushPicture, a skipped picture, a P picture with no anchor before it), FFmpeg's references are rewritten with the
program's (vdec_ffmpeg.hpp keeps the decoded pictures for it), or the anchor's access unit decoded again first. FFmpeg
is opened again at Initialize (its intensity compensation tables are its own state).

**What the program does, read in the module and checked against it** (the details are vdec_svc1d.cpp's):
- Levels 0 to 10 (0 the largest, 2048x2048; 1 and 2 the simple profile's, 3 to 5 the main profile's, 6 to 10 the
  advanced profile's): nine frame buffers at level 0 and the main profile's levels, six at the others. GetMemorySize2
  takes types 3 to 5 (type 5: a size within the level's, to 16); CreateInstance2 takes 0x480 bytes less than asked for
  (the PPU side's own state), types 4 and 5 a taskset, type 3 the core's own SPU threads or taskset (below).
- The PPU side's state word: a picture size past the instance's (SetPictureSize, a sequence header) stops the program
  for good (0x80615381, then 0x80615380 from every call that looks at the word; GetNumPicture, GetPicture,
  ReleasePicture, GetAuxData and GetSideInfoPic do not). DecodePicture2 checks a second piece (at a 128-byte boundary,
  after a first one of 16-byte blocks) before the state.
- After Initialize the first access unit must begin with a sequence header (else no picture, its bytes passed over to
  the next start code); after the advanced profile's CancelDecode (the pictures dropped) or Discontinue (kept) the
  stream goes on at its next entry point; the simple and main profiles' Discontinue leaves the next P picture no anchor.
- The bytes used: to the frame's stop bit's byte; an end of sequence after the frame taken (the anchor then given out,
  the flush's flag); user data after the frame used only when it is the access unit's last; a frame's user data before
  it ends the access unit with no picture, a sequence's or entry point's flags it (0x10, 0x1000) and the BDU after it is
  passed over with it; the simple and main profiles' frames to their header's end when no macroblock is coded, else to
  the frame's last byte.
- The records (GetSideInfoSeq's 0x38 bytes, GetSideInfoPic's 0x100 a field): a field a header leaves out keeps the value
  an earlier one gave it, across Initialize (which clears the first-entry flag alone). A new instance's are its
  program's own, zeroed: a simple profile's (so SetPictureSize before the first sequence header lays the frames out to
  16 lines, and a simple or main profile sequence's size is 2x2 until it comes). The advanced profile's entry point's
  fields and whether it was the first since Initialize; the picture header's: types, quantizer, motion vector modes and
  tables (codes as the program writes them), VOPDQUANT, transform types, interlaced frames' and field pictures' fields
  (a field picture two records), pan-scan windows, range mapping. A simple or main profile picture writes the coding
  tools and size into the entry point's part and keeps the rest (flags, broken link, closed entry, pan-scan, reference
  distance, coded size flag, extended differential vectors, range mapping).
- Statuses: a P picture with no anchor (0x800), predicted since an anchor with a warning (0x400), a picture the decode
  mode skips (0x80: its frame buffer left as it was); GetPicture's 0x11, 0x12, 0x14, 0x18 for them and the warnings.
- The simple and main profiles: DecodeSeqHeader takes STRUCT_C behind a sequence header's start code (none: a default
  sequence of no tool but sync markers, the warnings 0xC); a frame of at most one byte is a skipped P picture; range
  reduction is a warning (0x2, the record's picture not valid) but at level 0 and the main profile's levels, its P and
  B pictures given out expanded; sync markers a warning at every level; the frames are laid out to 32 lines when
  SetPictureSize comes after an advanced profile sequence, else to 16.
- Sony's libvdec (read in the module, its calls traced): Initialize when it opens a decoder, CancelDecode and
  SetDecodeMode {0, 0} at StartSeq, SetAuxData before each command, GetPicture, GetAuxData, GetSideInfoSeq,
  GetSideInfoPic and ReleasePicture for each picture; a picture whose GetPicture answers a warning is given out in
  error (0x80610106). DecodeAu's mode 3 is the simple and main profiles' sequence command: libvdec reads four words at
  the access unit's address, the height and the width (SetPictureSize(width, height), its answer not looked at) and the
  sequence header's address and size (DecodeSeqHeader; its warnings ignored, its errors fatal). An advanced profile
  access unit in mode 3 so gives a size past the instance's: the fatal error part 1 saw.

**Not reproduced** (logged where it can come; the comparisons leave each out where Sony's program does it):
- Field pictures' corner padding: Sony's program pads the edge strips' lines outside the picture racing with itself
  (they keep a frame buffer's earlier samples now and then).
- A simple or main profile picture in frames laid out to 32 lines whose height is not a multiple of 32: Sony's program
  decodes the macroblock rows to 32 lines, the last from the bytes after the frame's.
- Sync markers' frames and bytes used (Sony's program reads such frames otherwise than FFmpeg), and the bytes used of a
  simple or main profile frame whose macroblocks end on a byte's boundary (Sony's count one more: pspocket does not read
  the macroblock layer).
- RESPIC pictures (multiresolution) and intra macroblocks in range reduced P pictures (expanded twice); logged.
- CreateInstance2 type 3 (the core's own SPU threads, or its taskset in a SPURS instance given): refused (SEQ) and
  logged; libvdec gives a taskset (type 5).

halves, 32 lines of edge above and below the luma (16 the chroma) that the program never writes, and one strip each side
that repeats the first and last columns of a reference picture's lines. The parameters' first flag (libvdec's
!disableDeblockingFilter) 0: neither the edge strips nor the loop filter (FFmpeg's skip_loop_filter); the strips are
compared, the filter is not (the tests' I_PCM and skipped macroblocks are never filtered).

**What the program does, read in the module and checked against it** (the details are vdec_sjvtd.cpp's):
- The memory: frame buffers (frames + 2, each with its motion data), a table a macroblock column and one a macroblock,
  0x31D00 more, and the areas before them (0x95A50, 0x100 a macroblock row, 0x24A80 for the first flag set and for the
  second's default); without the caller's taskset (GetMemorySize, GetMemorySize2's parameters with none) room for one
  of its own too, a CellSpursTaskset2 (0x2900). Levels 0 to 16 (0 and 11 to 15: 1920x1088; 1 and 16: 176x144; 2 to 5:
  352x288; 6: 352x576; 7, 8: 720x576; 9: 1280x720; 10: 1280x1024); types 4 (the level's largest picture and the
  defaults: libvdec's without the codec specific information) to 6; frames 1 to 16 (16 by default), frame buffers one
  more, the lowest free taken.
- The decoded picture buffer: its size set at a sequence's first picture after Initialize (the VUI's
  max_dec_frame_buffering when given and not 0, else the level's MaxDpbMbs over the frame's macroblocks; at most 16 and
  the frame count); a new sequence parameter set at an IDR picture without Initialize keeps it. The instance's first
  sequence's size is what its frame buffers hold: a later sequence that needs more stops the decoder (0x80615881, then
  0x80615880 from DecodePicture, Initialize, FlushPicture, Discontinue, CancelDecode, SetDecodeMode, SetAuxData,
  GetSideInfoSeq; ReleaseInstance releases and answers 0x80615880; the queries answer as before). Output by C.4.5.3's
  bumping, or by the HRD's times (C.4.5.2) once a picture timing message with its delays came since Initialize: removal
  times from the last buffering period's (C.1.2), a picture without a timing message output when decoded. Reference
  marking by the sliding window or the memory management operations (operation 5 outputs every picture before it and
  starts the order counts and frame numbers again).
- Access units: no NAL unit, a warning (0x8); parameter sets alone, no picture and no error; a delimiter alone, or
  slices whose parameter sets the decoder does not have (Initialize forgets them), no picture (0x20; the sequence
  structure then has none); a picture larger than the instance's, refused as busy (0x80615821, nothing used) after the
  pictures before its IDR picture are output. The existence flag (the instance's second word, not set at creation): 0x1
  a sequence parameter set, 0x2 a picture parameter set, 0x10 an access unit delimiter, 0x100 a buffering period
  message, 0x200 a picture timing message. FlushPicture's mark (GetNumPicture's 0x80615822) stays until a picture.
- GetPicture's nine words: the luma's first sample, Cb's, Cr's (Cb + 8), the structure word, width, height, the strips'
  lines and chroma lines, the frame buffer. The structure word 0x40000004 with 0x10 two fields shown, 0x1000 the bottom
  first, 0x4000 a field repeated, 0x800 a field pair, 0x400 a field alone (a bottom field's addresses a line down):
  from pic_struct (a frame's 1 and 2 taken as 0 and 7), else a frame's fields' order counts.
- GetSideInfoPic's blocks (0x188 bytes, two for a field pair): the cropping in samples, a status (0x1 a reference
  missing, 0x80 passed over), whether the picture is a random access point (an IDR picture, or the one a recovery
  point message names), the slice type code (1, 2, 4: B over P over I), the slices' NAL units' bits, IDR flags (the
  first picture after CancelDecode's too), the picture type, the order count, pic_struct and the bottom field flag; the
  decode mode at +0x168. GetAuxData: SetAuxData's 16 bytes of each field's access unit.
- GetSideInfoSeq's structure (0x7E0 bytes): the sequence parameter set as the program reads it, its VUI's HRD (each
  CPB's bit rate, cbr_flag and size). The VUI's fields are the record's (kept when a set has no VUI, written from then
  on); delta_pic_order_always_zero_flag is kept across sets of other types; the cropping when on, the timing when fixed.
- SetDecodeMode takes 0 and 0xFF (else SEQ): 0xFF passes the non-reference pictures over (0x80615828, given out
  undecoded, their frame buffers as they were). CancelDecode drops every picture; the P and B pictures after it warn
  (GetPicture 0x8061581b) until an IDR picture. Discontinue keeps everything. ReleasePicture with none: 0;
  GetSideInfoPic and GetAuxData with none write a count of 2 and answer EMPTY.
- Sony's libvdec (read in the module, traced): type 6 with the codec specific information's size, its deblocking flag
  as the first flag (inverted), the second -1, the frame count from numberOfDecodedFrameBuffer; type 4 without it.

**Not reproduced** (each left out of the comparisons where Sony's program does it, with the reason in the tests):
- What a sequence parameter set leaves out (the VUI's fields past a flag of 0) in a new instance: Sony's SPU task keeps
  what its local store held, an earlier instance's task's or anything; pspocket's are 0 there, then the instance's own.
  Likewise GetSideInfoSeq before an instance's first picture (Sony's: an earlier instance's).
- Field pictures given out alone (picture timing messages on fields): Sony's answers warnings that change with what
  its memory held before; the second side information block of a lone field is a stale copy. pspocket gives each field
  alone with its structure word; not compared.
- The parameters' second flag 1 (libvdec gives -1): Sony's refuses every access unit (0x80615842) and gives its frame
  buffers out with warnings anyway; pspocket refuses them and gives none.
- libvdec's information block of a sequence without a VUI: its video signal, colour and timing bytes come from the
  structure's words the core leaves unwritten, on libvdec's stack, so from what Sony's core's own calls left there:
  notes in the libvdec comparison.
- Streams of CABAC (the tests' are CAVLC): the side information's bits are the NAL units' there too, unverified.
- Found on the way: in pspocket's SPURS, Sony's ReleaseInstance leaves five of the core's six tasks waiting when the
  instance was initialized again after a stream, and a new instance in the same memory overwrites their saved contexts
  (the comparison gives each instance its memory). pspocket's core has no SPU tasks.

Tests: h264_streams.hpp's streams (I_PCM, P_Skip and B_Skip pictures; field pairs; VUIs of every field and HRD
parameters of more CPBs; buffering period, picture timing, recovery point and closed caption messages; slices of
different types; memory management operations 1 to 6); "The JVT core (libsjvtd) against Sony's" (the call-for-call comparison, `[.]`), "The JVT core
(libsjvtd): pspocket's own, answering as Sony's did (D-920)" (its own half with Sony's values, firmware-free) and "The
JVT core under Sony's libvdec: pspocket's against Sony's" (`[.]`, with the codec specific information's flags and
counts and DecodeAu's modes). libmvcdec stays firmware-first (D-933).

## D-921 · 2026-10-12 · sceNp's last 24: the product category getters as libsysutil_np, its requests to the NP service

sceNp's 24 functions answered as RPCS3's stubs (D-182) are pspocket's own (runtime/hle/src/sceNp.cpp), so the whole
library (239 functions) is; libsysutil_np.sprx is always served natively (D-175).

**The product category functions** were RPCS3's TODOs (infos pointing at the category, counts never written, dval 0).
They are now Sony's libsysutil_np 4.92, read from it and compared with it (tests/hle/test_np_commerce_compare.cpp:
11,971 calls on each side over random store data, every answer as an offset and every byte of the data and the
category, info and price objects the same): the twelve getters that were stubs (GetCurrencyCode, GetCategoryId,
Name, Description, ImageURL, GetSkuId, GetProductId, ProductName, SkuName, SkuDescription, SkuImageURL, SkuUserData:
the record's address plus the field's offset) and the ten around them. The data (version 1): be32 version, be32
status, the currency at +8 (its three letters, be32 decimals at +12), the category record at +16 (760 bytes), the
child category count at +776, the children from +780 (760 each), then the SKU count and the SKUs (1,004 each). An
info is {category, record} and writing one NUL-terminates its record's strings in the data (a currency at +3; a
category at +55, +247, +631, +759; a SKU at +55, +103, +295, +359, +743, +871, +999). InitProductCategory keeps the
data and size first, then checks the version (else INVALID_GPC_PROTOCOL_VERSION, 0x8002942A), the status (a browse
server error 0x80029600 | status, 0x80029600 past 255) and the currency, and sets dval to 10 to the decimals' power
in 32 bits (0 for none; Sony's multiplies that many times, squared here). GetChildProductSkuInfo checks only that a
SKU's first four bytes lie in the data, as Sony's does. GetSkuPrice splits the price at +1000 by dval. Sony's checks
no pointer; one that is not guest memory is refused here with a log.

**The requests to the system software's NP service** (_sceNpSysutilClientMalloc/Free, _sce_np_sysutil_send_packet,
_send_packet_sub, _send_empty_packet, _recv_packet, _recv_packet_fixedmem, _recv_packet_fixedmem_sub,
_cxml_prepare_doc, _cxml_set_npid, sce_np_matching_set_matching2_running, sceNpDrmExecuteGamePurchase): Sony's sibling
modules build their requests with them; pspocket serves those itself, so a game reaches them only by importing them.
Each does what libsysutil_np does, over pspocket's cxml and packet functions (D-534), called as Sony's module calls its
imports: a document's tables from a FixedMemory instance, its magic and root element; Document::Write through a
PacketWriter on channel 0 (1 for _sub) under the request number; a reply read into the receive buffer (or the
FixedMemory instance, 0x6000 bytes) until done (a reply larger than the buffer is read away and answered 0x8002B006),
made a document and its "result" returned when negative; an NP ID as an element with a "handle" child (its "data" the
online ID) and "opt" and "reserved" files. The client heap is Sony's: _sys_heap_create_heap("SceNpSysutilClientHeap",
pool size, 0x80000000, {8, pool}) over the game's NP pool, with the 0x18000-byte receive buffer from it, made at first
use while NP is up (Sony's sceNpInit makes them) and deleted by sceNpTerm; before sceNpInit the heap is 0 and liblv2
says "invalid heap area 0x0", as with Sony's. matching2_running keeps a byte the older matching library checks (with
matching 2's own state) before refusing with UTILITY_UNAVAILABLE. sceNpDrmExecuteGamePurchase is SCE_NP_DRM_ERROR_INTERNAL
before sceNpInit, then Sony's "drmrequest" (magic NPDR, reqtype 2, an empty reqarg) as request 268 between
cellSysutilPacketBegin and End; pspocket's console has no system software, so its channels are closed and the call
answers the channel's 0x8002B007 as Sony's code does on it: no store opens (its purchase mutex, which serialises
nothing here, is left out). These eleven are unverified (D-594): comparing them needs Sony's sceNpInit's whole set-up.

Tests: test_np_commerce_compare.cpp (with the firmware); test_np.cpp: the product category test now checks Sony's
behaviour, and a new case covers the client heap before, during and after NP, the closed channel's answer and the
matching 2 flag (its low byte).

## D-922 · 2026-10-12 · sceNpTrophy's later queries from pspocket's trophy service

sceNpTrophy's five functions answered as RPCS3's stubs (RPCS3: UNIMPLEMENTED) are pspocket's own
(runtime/hle/src/sceNpTrophy.cpp), so the library (24 functions) is. Sony's libsysutil_np_trophy (4.92) asks the system
software's trophy service for every query (request 295 on channel 1; these build documents "2", "3", "k", "j" and
"a"); pspocket's trophy service is its own module, so they answer from the installed sets as GetGameInfo and
GetTrophyInfo do, after Sony's own checks in its order. Read from Sony's module; unverified (D-594), the system's side
being in no module.
- **GetGameDetails(context, handle, details, u64 options)**: GetGameInfo's details alone (Sony's calls the same
  request without game data). No details: INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything; options: NOT_SUPPORTED after the context
  and handle.
- **GetTrophyDetails(context, handle, flags, details, u32* count, u64 options)**: no flags, details or count:
  INVALID_ARGUMENT; *count (the room) read and set to 0 first, nothing asked for none. Sony's asks in requests of up to
  12 trophies: from bit position p, the next set bits (at most room - p of them), their details written from
  details[p], p being where that request's scan began, and *count adds each request's; so a request that is not one run
  of trophies from 0 spreads over the array as Sony's spreads it (kept). Each trophy's details are GetTrophyInfo's (a
  hidden one still locked: HIDDEN). Sony's goes on asking without end when the room is past 128 (empty requests); the
  loop stops there, logged.
- **GetLatestTrophies(handle, npId, max, entries, u32* count, u64 options)**: the user's unlocked trophies over every
  installed set (each TROPUSR.DAT under /dev_hdd0/home/00000001/trophy), newest first, max of them, as 32-byte entries
  as Sony's parser lays out the reply: be64 tick, be32 trophy ID, be32 1 (the reply's "unlocked" stored as a word),
  then the set's communication ID (nine characters, NUL, its number). pspocket's console has one user: any npId is
  that user's.
- **GetUserInfo(handle, npId, user_info, u64 options)**: the reply's 48-byte "user_info" string: the user's name as
  cellUserInfoGetStat reads it (localusername), "User" without one.
- **NetworkSync(handle, callback, arg, u64 options)**: Sony's calls callback(12, 0, 0, arg) when the system's
  "reqsync" says 0 and (10, 0, 0, arg) otherwise, before it returns; offline the synchronisation fails: 10.
Test: tests/hle/test_trophy.cpp "sceNpTrophy's later queries": the checks before init, details and options, the
batches' layout over 15 trophies, a hidden trophy, the latest trophies before and after two unlocks, the user's name,
the sync.

## D-923 · 2026-10-12 · NP's last eight stubs: matching's cancels and room messages, Plus, TSS, Commerce2, OAuth

The last functions of the NP libraries answered as RPCS3's stubs are pspocket's own, so sceNpMatchingInt (11),
sceNpPlus (1), sceNpTus (62), sceNpCommerce2 (52) and sceNp2 (80) are whole. Each was read in Sony's module
(libsysutil_np, _np_tus, _np_commerce2, _np2); its own checks come first in its order, then the offline answer that
matches the rest of pspocket's NP (no PSN, D-059). Unverified (D-594) but the Commerce2 one, which is Sony's exactly.
- **sceNpMatchingCancelRequest(ctx, req)**: matching 2 running (UTILITY_UNAVAILABLE), NP (NOT_INITIALIZED), the
  context (CTX_NOT_FOUND), then the request ID's kind in bits 23..28 (6, 15 or 23, else INVALID_REQ_ID); pspocket never
  issues a request offline: REQUEST_NOT_FOUND (0x8002A727).
- **sceNpMatchingCancelRequestGUI(ctx)**: matching 2 only (Sony's checks neither NP nor the context), then the system
  asked to close a GUI: pspocket's matching GUIs are answered at once, none is open: CELL_OK.

  size at +12 from 1 to 256: past it TOO_BIG_VALUE) and the room (INVALID_ARG), then the context; no room offline:
  ROOM_NOT_FOUND, as the other room requests.
- **sceNpManagerIsSP()** (sceNpPlus): Sony's asks the system once NP is up (request 262) and answers 0 when it cannot
  tell; pspocket's user is offline, never a PlayStation Plus subscriber: 0.
- **sceNpTssGetDataNoLimit / Async**: libsysutil_np_tus runs GetData's code with the size limit off: GetData's answers.
- **sceNpCommerce2DestroyGetProductInfoListResult**: Sony's answers 0 and does nothing; so here.
- **sceNpAuthGetAuthorizationCode2**: GetAuthorizationCode's code with a request of its own (326): its answers.
Test: tests/hle/test_np.cpp "NP's last stubs".

## D-924 · 2026-10-12 · Each test process its own temporary directory

Several tests make files under fixed names in the temporary directory (pspocket-test-pngenc, pspocket-pngenc-compare-
ours, pspocket-rawspu, ...). Two test runs at the same time, the gate beside a library agent's run in its clone, then
removed each other's files: cellPngEnc's comparison aborted in the gate (alone it agrees with Sony's module, 0 of 1,834
observations). Every test executable now gets tests/own_temp_dir.cpp (pspocket_add_test adds it): at start it makes
TMPDIR/pspocket-test-<pid> and points TMPDIR at it, so std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() answers it, and removes it
at exit. A test's own fixed names stay as they are; processes no longer meet. (D-923's sceNpMatchingCancelRequest and
SendRoomMessage were registered under each other's NIDs; the NID test caught it and they are swapped back.)

The gate under load also showed cellRudp's comparison (D-916) depending on time: its refused client went on sending
its SYN on librudp's real-time timer through the next clients' connections, and whether one of those SYNs shared a
datagram with a client's own depended on the machine's load (19 of 2,652 observations then, the status counters after it
one datagram apart). The refused client now ends once its refusal is seen; three runs under the same load agree with
Sony's module (0 of 2,648).

## D-925 · 2026-10-12 · cellPrintUtility's ten from libsysutil_print, with a system side to test them

Clone a's part of the sysutil sub-modules (its D-541, read from Sony's libsysutil_*.sprx, 4.92) brought to main for
printing; its other modules there (BGDL, RtcAlarm, GameExec, RemotePlay) stay main's own (D-669..D-673). The ten
functions RPCS3 left stubs now do what libsysutil_print does, through pspocket's libsysutil (D-534):
runtime/hle/src/cellPrintUtility.cpp, over runtime/hle/src/sysutil_sub.hpp (a request's packet, FixedMemory, cxml
document, send and reply read as the module's code does them, each step in its order; a fault where Sony's would read a
bad pointer logs the call site, answers CELL_EFAULT and gives back what the request took).

  system's event 0x121 calls once through the dispatcher cellSysutilPrintInit registers (pspocket's: an internal
  function, cellPrintUtility_PrintEvent); cellSysutilPrintShutdown unregisters it, clearing the callback when that
  succeeds. Each request checks cellSysutilPacketBegin's answer, prints its failures through liblv2's printf ("doc.Write

  module's exports, one pspocket's; after every call the answer, the script's memory, libsysutil's globals and
  FixedMemory, the channels' shared memory, the lv2 calls of the script's thread and the requests the system side read.
  The system side lays out a channel's ring as the system software does; a thread of the test's answers each request
  with a queued reply (cxml documents built on the host) when the script's thread waits for it, and reads a packet out of
  the ring for a writer waiting for room (SendBand's band behind its document); any other wait closes the channel.
  56 calls, 891 lv2 calls, 33 requests answered (the dispatcher registered and unregistered, liblv2's printf output

## D-926 · 2026-10-12 · cellPesmUtility from libsysutil_pesm; the system software's shared memory in lv2

The front end of the system software's PSP movie recorder (copy to a PSP or Memory Stick: device, entry, recording,
sample encryption, the MP4 protection box), read from libsysutil_pesm.sprx (4.92): runtime/hle/src/cellPesmUtility.cpp,
its fifteen functions RPCS3 leaves stubs and two exports nothing names (0x6312A6CC writes the version 0x30001 and 1;
0x8AB3156B answers -1, as LoadAsync and UnloadAsync do).

- **The module's way, mirrored.** One object made at the first call (operator new, as the module's: the request in
  flight, a state 0 to 5, a list of the shared memories it opened). A request object begins packet 0x13D on channel 0
  (its answer not looked at), takes FixedMemory 0, builds an element named after the command ("PesmCmdInitialize" ...)
  with the function's fields from the module's table (ints and strings, magic "PESM") and writes it (its answer not
  looked at). The reply is read into FixedMemory; when its root is the command's, the reply's fields are read over the
  values the function put there (a missing one keeps its value: often an argument, e.g. Initialize's second container,
  OpenDevice's name address), the request deleted and "PesmResult" answered. A root of another name answers 0x80861001
  and keeps the request (with its packet and FixedMemory): the next call reads its reply instead of sending. The state
  checks are the module's (0x80862001; InitEntry and InitEntry2 answer 1), as are the calls left in state 3 by an early
  answer (no shared memory 0x80862002, PrepareRec's missing info -19, a sample past 1 MB 0x80861002); GetSinf answers 0
  whatever the reply; EncryptSample's address is the reply's offset into the shared memory.
- **On pspocket's console** (closed channels, D-534) a failed read leaves the request's own document, so each request
  reads itself back: its command's root, none of the reply's fields. Sony's module run on pspocket answers the same.
- **libsysutil's exports, as they answer.** The module calls the cxml functions through libsysutil's exports, which
  catch guest memory that is not there (a reply that is no document: GetDocumentElement and CheckElementName read
  address 0), log it and answer; the module goes on to 0x80861001. pspocket's makes the same calls through
  sysutil_sub.hpp's as_export, which answers as the export does, instead of ending the call.
- **The recorder's shared memory.** Initialize opens 2 MB of 64 KB pages under the key 0x8086000000000200 through
  cellSysutilSharedMemoryAlloc, which the system software makes: libsysutil tries again every 100 ms while lv2 has none,
  so Sony's module would wait for ever on pspocket's console. pspocket's opens it only when lv2 has it, and otherwise
  goes on as the module goes on when the opening fails (logged once): the calls that need it answer 0x80862002. The
  module's stack word that EncryptSample2's reply values start from is not reproducible; pspocket's start from 0.
- **lv2: the system software's shared memory** (RPCS3 init_system_shared_memory, lv2_memory::system_handle):
  Kernel::create_system_shared_memory(key, size, flags) makes one as the system software does, charged to none of the
  process's containers and kept by the kernel; the process's sys_mmapper_allocate_shared_memory of its key, other than
  newly created, opens it, one handle at a time (a second answers EEXIST, as RPCS3's handle count does), and freeing the
  handle leaves the object and its key. Kernel::shared_memory_key_exists(key) tells an HLE module whether one is there.
  pspocket's console makes none; a test's system side does. Test: tests/lv2/test_memory.cpp "the system software's
  shared memory".
- **Compared** with Sony's module (tests/hle/test_sysutil_more.cpp, `[sysutil]`): the version and loads, every call
  before initialization, the closed channel without and with the system's shared memory (Initialize opening it,
  Finalize giving it back, the calls left in a call), then a system side answering: results, missing fields, strings,
  replies of another root (the request kept and answered later), a reply that is no document, a truncated one, the
  system going away; the shared memory's contents after the copies. 80 calls, 948 lv2 calls, 31 requests answered: 0
  differences. Without the firmware: "cellPesmUtility on pspocket's console".

## D-927 · 2026-10-12 · cellFiber's two-worker comparison waits for both workers

The gate under the agents' load failed cellFiber's comparison (D-914) once: "a worker control's fibers on two workers"
saw pspocket's worker 1 answer 0x8076000F (CELL_FIBER_ERROR_STAT) from RunFibers where Sony's run answered 0. Each
worker is a host thread calling RunFibers; one that started after the six fibers had run and the control was shut down
met the shutdown, so the observation depended on when the machine let the thread start. The script now waits (at most
a minute) until libfiber counts both workers in its word's top byte before it finalizes and shuts the control down;
both runs then see the same. Alone the comparison agreed every time (0 of 31 observations).

## D-928 · 2026-10-12 · sys_fs's attribute comparison leaves the ctimes out

The gate under load failed sys_fs's comparison with libfs once ("attributes": output differs at +0x123, the low byte
of the first CellFsStat's ctime). Both runs share one tree of host files: the first run's cellFsSetAttribute sets the
file's ctime to the host's clock, which the second run's first cellFsStat then reads, so the two first stats agree
only when no second boundary falls between the tree's making and the first run's change. The two stats' ctimes (the
host's clock, not libfs's doing) are no longer compared; their other fields still are. Alone it agreed every time.
Two more sections read times their runs set from the host's clock, and a later gate failed one ("symbolic links": the
link's times at +0x113): the link's stat and the "sizes" section's stats after the files' changes leave their three
times out; the times the "attributes" section sets itself (SetAttribute's atime and mtime) are still compared.

  default, a bit rate from the pixels a second). The option IDs are libsail_rec's tables, read from the installed
  module. Anything else UNSUPPORTED_STREAM (FATAL for another codec): an error event, the slot closed again.
- **The pipeline** (0x3C0 bytes in the slot): by the feeder's coding and the codec a conversion on an SPU task of
  libsail_rec's in the common taskset (five kinds: ARGB or RGBA, YUV 4:2:2 or YUV 4:2:0 to the encoder's layout, ARGB

  scaler cellVpost2 (module 0xF043, message 0x20) when the slot scales, or the feeder's picture straight to the encoder;

  imports: 44 more) with its work area and the units' records for the composer's delay at the frame rate, its
  notifications (0x21) on the recorder's SPURS queue; the ring of units (the largest unit; doubled and at least the
  delay's bytes at the bit rate unless the stream is the composer's first). Started: the pump asked (0x1E); each frame
  scheduled against the stream's time (the frames so far at the frame's duration, or the shared clock's time for it,
