## D-939 · 2026-10-13 · Games that start from /dev_hdd0/game: installed PSN games and disc games' updates, on the iPhone

The engine checklist's PSN item was partial: the Mac tools install a PSN game's package and the player's licence and
decrypt its executable (D-580 to D-583), but nothing started a game the way a PS3 starts one from the hard disk, and
the app could neither install a package nor list the game. Now, as RPCS3 starts them (rpcs3/Emu/System.cpp,
Emulator::Load):

- **An installed game** (a folder of /dev_hdd0/game whose PARAM.SFO has category HG, from its package) starts with its
  executable's guest path as argv[0] (/dev_hdd0/game/<folder>/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN), its USRDIR as /app_home (writable,
  RPCS3 mounts the executable's folder), no disc, and cellGame sees an HDD game: cellGameBootCheck answers
  CELL_GAME_GAMETYPE_HDD with the folder's name, cellGameContentPermit the folder.
- **A disc game whose update is installed** (/dev_hdd0/game/<TITLE_ID> with a PARAM.SFO of the disc's title ID,
  category GD, and an executable of its own) starts the update's executable with the disc in the drive, as a PS3 does:
  cellGameBootCheck answers the disc's type with CELL_GAME_ATTRIBUTE_PATCH and the update's PARAM.SFO (its APP_VER),
  the content stays the disc's (/dev_bdvd/PS3_GAME), cellGamePatchCheck opens the update, and the calls about the disc
  (cellGameDataCheck of the disc, cellDiscGameGetBootDiscInfo) read the disc's PARAM.SFO through /dev_bdvd as RPCS3
  does. Trophies come from the update's folder, else the disc's (sceNpTrophy already did that for category GD).
- hle::GameInfo keeps the folder's name (`dir`): a PSN game installed under a name apart from its title ID is reported
  by its folder, as RPCS3 takes the name from the path.

Where (runtime/loader/hdd_game.hpp): read_hdd_game (a folder of hdd0/game, its PARAM.SFO), find_update (RPCS3's test:
the title ID's folder, category GD, USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN), hdd_game_of (the folder an executable is in), mount_app_home.
pspocket-boot: an executable in --hdd0's game folder starts that way (an update needs --bdvd, its disc); booting a
disc's own executable while --hdd0 holds its update says so (a PS3 would start the update; pspocket-boot runs the
executable it is given). Found on the way: start_main_thread took the boot options apart from the state that
prepare_kernel_config had read, and both callers passed none, so argv[0] was always the disc's path; they pass the
state's now.

The game's own modules: save_installed_modules (runtime/disc/modules.hpp; C: ps_psn_save_modules) walks an installed
game's or an update's USRDIR as save_disc_modules walks a disc's (D-239), a PSN module decrypted with its licence (free
content, or the player's .rap), saved under its /dev_hdd0 guest path for the preparation.

The app (app/ios, through ps_game_options.game_dir, ps_game_probe_installed, ps_game_find_update and the PSN C API):
- a .pkg or .rap put in Games (or picked with +) is installed into Documents/hdd0 once per file (its size and date),
  once it has not changed for 3 s (Files copies a big file in for a while), one package at a time in the background
  with the screen kept on; the library shows how it goes, which licence a game still needs, and that the package may
  be deleted. A package refused before (an update put in before its game) is tried again after the next install; a
  split package installs from NAME_00.pkg. The file itself stays: the app never deletes the user's files.
- installed PSN games (category HG with an executable) are games of the library, their covers from their ICON0.PNG;
  their executable decrypts with the licence (a missing .rap is the game's problem line until one is installed, then
  it is tried again).
- a disc game with an update installed starts the update: its executable decrypted into
  pspocket-games/<TITLE_ID>/update-<APP_VER>/, prepared like any (the library is made again for the new executable),
  its modules scanned once per version, the disc mounted as ever.

Tests: tests/disc/test_psn.cpp (an installed game from its package, an update found or not, its modules saved, its
USRDIR as /app_home), tests/hle/test_sysPrxForUser.cpp (the boot check of each kind), ctest pspocket_boot_hdd_game (a
synthetic installed game that exits 0 only when its argv[0] and /app_home are the HDD game's).

### D-932, part 4: cellCelp8Enc, the 8 kHz encoder, pspocket's own

libcelp8enc (cellCelp8Enc: QueryAttr, Open, OpenEx, Close, Start, End, EncodeFrame, WaitForOutput and GetAu; the
module exports nothing else but its two module functions) is libcelpenc's design (part 1) for MPEG-4 CELP's
narrowband coder (8 kHz, multi-pulse excitation). pspocket's (runtime/hle/src/cellCelp8Enc.cpp) answers as the library
does and does the SPU program's work on the host, bit for bit (celp_mpe_enc.cpp, with the LSP decoding, adaptive
codebook and pulse positions of part 3's decoder, celp_mpe.cpp). With it every function of the four CELP libraries is
pspocket's own (23).

What differs from libcelpenc:
- QueryAttr: workMemSize 0xBB00 (0x4000 and the handle's 0x7B00), versions 0x04000000 and 0x200. Codes from
  0x806140A1: SEQ 0x806140A2, ARG 0x806140A3; the SPU program's answers 0x4000 and 0x5000 become 0x806140B2 and
  0x806140B3, any other but 0x1000 0x806140B1 (none can happen on the host).
- The handle's memory is 0x7A80 bytes (the frame's copy at +0x1c80, the header or access unit at +0x2180, the SPU
  program's state at +0x2200) and 0x4000 more are wanted after it. One OpenEx (no OpenExt).
- Start: excitationMode 0 (multi-pulse), sampleRate 1 (8 kHz), a configuration of at most 26 that the library's table
  marks (0, 2, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24 and 26), wordSize 0 (floats: there is no 16-bit input), else ARG; a frame is
  320 samples (configurations 0 and 2), 160 (6 to 21) or 80 (24 and 26), its bytes four times that.
- The header, 29 bytes: ".mp4", 0, 0x4003, 1, 8000, the bit rate (3850, 4650, 5700, 6600, 7300, 8700, 9900, 10700,
  11800, 12200), a frame's bits twice (154, 186, 114, 132, 146, 174, 198, 214, 118, 122: the SPU program's fixed point,
  as libcelpenc's), 32 bits of 0, 2, 11 (the CelpHeader's bits), then 14496-3's CelpHeader (multi-pulse, 8 kHz, no fine
  rate control, the configuration, no enhancement layers, no bandwidth scalability), padded to a byte (232 bits; the
  SPU program answers with the bits / 8).
- Only the first access unit is empty (an access unit codes the frame before; the LPC analysis looks 40 samples
  further); the others are a frame's bits in bytes (20, 24, 15, 17, 19, 22, 25, 27, 15 and 16). The SPU program
  scales the frame by 32767 in its single precision.

The SPU program is the reference encoder (ISO/IEC 14496-5: NEC's nec_mode_decision.c, nec_qrms_enc.c,
nec_abs_exc_analysis.c, nec_exc_acb_enc.c, nec_exc_mp_enc.c and nec_exc_gain_enc.c, Matsushita's pan_lspqtz2_dd.c,
Philips's phi_lpc.c, with the decoder's tables; external/usac-refsoft, never in the repository) compiled for the SPU
and vectorised. pspocket's encoder does its arithmetic as part 3's decoder does (the SPU's single precision, the
program's order and grouping of every sum, the SDK's division, reciprocal, square root, logarithms and 2^x). Where the
SPU program differs from the reference software:
- The input is not high-pass filtered (the reference's preprocessing is in the program, switched off).
- The LPC analysis (every 80 samples, a 200-sample window: a 240-point Hamming window's first half, then a quarter
  cosine over 80; the 10th-order lag window) is in single precision; Levinson-Durbin also stops when the residual
  energy falls to a millionth of the first, and a window's energy of at most 1 gives all zeros. LSP roots not found
  keep the previous frame's LSPs divided by pi once more.
- The open-loop pitch search updates each lag's energy recursively; the voiced/unvoiced test of a quiet or unpitched
  frame compares the pitch gain times the mean square (not the RMS) with 93750 (250 x 375): the reference's
  gain x RMS > 375 only at an RMS of 250.
- The adaptive codebook search tries the open-loop lag's index and one index either side (the reference 8 either side,
  NEC_LAG_IDX_RNG 16).
- The multi-pulse tree search keeps as many candidates as the next pulse has positions (the reference 32), each best
  found as a tournament over vectors of four whose pairings the later side wins only when strictly greater (on ties
  not always the reference's first largest); each pulse's sign is its position's correlation's (the reference searches
  the sign combinations of its four best position sets below 8 pulses), and only the best candidate goes to the gain
  search (the reference's four).
- The comb filter's gains are 0.6 and 0.8 (as in the decoder).

Not reproduced: no SPURS instance, task set or queue is made (their errors cannot happen); the SPU program's state
(+0x2200) is kept on the host; float samples of exponent 255 are outside pspocket's SPU model.

Compared: in the scratch harness (Sony's SPU program under pspocket's SPU interpreter, inventory/, never in the
repository), every frame's LPC coefficients and LSPs, quantiser indices and quantised LSPs, each subframe's LPC
coefficients, weighting filters and their memories, weighted speech, signal mode and open-loop lags, RMS index and
values, each subframe's lag, pulse, sign and gain indices, the excitation's memories and the access unit, for 11
kinds of synthetic audio with 10 seeds in each of the 10 configurations (56,100 frames: 30 a run with seeds 1 to 3, 60
with seeds 4 to 10; every signal mode, 0 to 3, reached): 0 differences; the 10 headers: 0 differences. Under the library
(tests/hle/test_celp8_compare.cpp, firmware 4.92): QueryAttr; Open's and OpenEx's checks, the handles and the
resource OpenEx changes; every call in every state; Start's eleven parameter checks and ten headers; 446 frames
(speech-like, sines, a chirp, noise, a square wave, impulses, noise in a sample's last bits, a constant, gated speech,
speech past full scale, silence) and every access unit byte for byte: 0 of 2514 observations differ. Without the
firmware, the test encodes speech through the library and decodes it with part 3's decoder: 6.9 to 8.8 dB SNR.

## D-940 · 2026-10-13 · The shader interpreter: a draw whose programs are still compiling is drawn, not left out

The engine checklist's "Draws while a shader compiles". Since D-158 a draw whose vertex or fragment program, or
pipeline, is still compiling in the background is left out once the frame's 4 ms wait is spent: a game's first
session on the phone shows objects popping in as their shaders land. RPCS3's answer is its "async with shader
interpreter" mode; pspocket's is the same in spirit:

- **Two functions run any program** (runtime/rsx/shader/interp.hpp, interp.cpp): the vertex function rsx_vs_interp and
  the fragment function rsx_fs_interp. The programs are decoded on the CPU as for the translation (ir.hpp) and encoded
  into fixed-width words (8 a vertex instruction, 12 a fragment one, the fragment program's flow-control ends and elses
  as instruction indices), once per program, in a buffer of their own. The MSL runs each operation as msl.cpp
  translates it (same helpers, same order of modifiers, the same RPCS3 citations), and reads at run time what the
  translator fixes at compile time from VpOptions and FpOptions (texture kinds, 2D coordinates, flat and two-sided
  colours, point sprites, stipple, depth bounds, the texel conversions and alpha kill, sRGB, the alpha test and alpha
  to coverage, output swizzles). Vertex flow control: a pc and a call stack of 8, the translation's 65536-jump guard;
  fragment flow control: a stack of open IFE/LOOP/REP blocks, BRK, RET and the loop index of indexed inputs as the
  translation's lexical blocks have them. What the translation refuses (its unsupported opcodes, an indexed input past
  SSA outside a loop) the interpreter refuses too: the two draw the same.
- **What cannot be read at run time is a variant**: the fragment function's colour outputs (0 to 4) and depth export are
  preprocessor variants of one source (RSX_MRT, RSX_DEPTH), as the translation writes them. The vertex function puts
  out every varying (flat copies of the colours beside the smooth ones, all six clip distances, the point size).
- **Textures by kind**: a unit's texture goes to its kind's slot (fragment: 2D, 1D and shadow at 0-15, cube at 16-31, 3D
  at 32-47, depth at 48-63, the depth bounds copy at 64; vertex: 0-3, 4-7, 8-11), every other slot a 1x1 stand-in of
  its type, every sampler bound (the interpreter indexes them). 65 fragment textures need Apple GPU family 6 (A13) or
  later, and the Macs; where a pipeline cannot be made the draw is left out as before.
- **In the backend** (metal_backend.mm): at the three places a draw was left out for a compile (its fragment program,
  vertex program, pipeline), it goes to the interpreter instead, when the interpreter's functions and its pipeline for
  the draw's targets and blending are made; else it is left out as before. The interpreter's functions are programs like
  any other (made in the background, the vertex function and the commonest fragment variant as soon as the backend
  starts, the others when first needed), its pipelines are pipeline_for's like any pair: the shader cache records both
  and makes them ahead at the next launch (D-114). The report line counts "drawn by the interpreter".
  MetalBackendConfig::shader_interpreter (on) and force_interpreter, PSPOCKET_RSX_INTERPRETER=1: every draw through it.

Cost: an interpreted draw is slower on the GPU (a loop over the instructions, registers in thread memory) and binds 77
textures; it lasts only the frames until the draw's own compile lands. Tests (tests/rsx/test_metal.mm): the interpreter
compiles in every variant into pipelines; every end-to-end draw of the suite again through it
(test_rsx_metal_interpreted: the same pixels as the translation's); random programs drawn both ways into a 32-bit float
target (64 fragment programs with every arithmetic, pack and unpack operation, modifiers, condition codes and IFE and
LOOP blocks, and 64 vertex programs with dual issue and conditional writes a round; PSPOCKET_FUZZ_SEED,
PSPOCKET_FUZZ_ITERS; PSPOCKET_TEST_ONLY=<n> draws that program alone and then each of its instructions as a NOP in
turn): every float the same within 4e-6, a denormal counting as zero (the translation's constant folding flushes a packed
value's denormal bits); the two disagreements it found were the translation's (D-941, D-942); and a game's view of it: a
draw whose pipeline compiles, and one whose program was never seen, drawn at once by the interpreter. The phone's numbers (how many draws a first session
interprets, and what they cost) come with the next phone session.

## D-941 · 2026-10-13 · Under the depth clamp, a fragment program that can discard exports its depth

Found while checking D-940 against the D-258 test: on Apple GPUs (the M4 here) a fragment function that can discard its
fragment gets no depth clamp from MTLDepthClipModeClamp, the RSX's NV4097_SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL clamp (D-258): with an
alpha test on, the depth stored was the unclamped 0.75 where the clip range ends at 0.7. Metal does clamp an exported
depth to the viewport's range (D-266). So FpOptions::clamp_depth, set where the backend sets the clamp mode: a program
that can discard (KIL, a texture's alpha kill, the alpha test, alpha to coverage, depth bounds, polygon stipple) exports
the depth it was rasterized at (in.position.z; r1.z when it exports its own). The backend clears the option for
programs that cannot discard, so their keys and compiles, and the shader cache recorded on the Mac, stay as they were;
the translation's version and fingerprint are unchanged (no existing key's MSL changed). The interpreter (which can
always discard) takes its depth variant under the clamp. Regression: the D-258 test's alpha-tested draws, clamped to
0.7 and clipped as before, translated and interpreted.

## D-942 · 2026-10-13 · Metal's pack intrinsics miscompile next to another write to their register: pspocket packs by hand

Found by D-940's random programs, where the translated program and the interpreter disagreed and the translated one
contradicted its own MSL: `PK16R R0.zw, H3` then `DP2AR R0.xw, ...` drew R0.w as the pack's value (or 1.0), not the
DP2A's, and the pack's own lanes came out wrong too. Reduced to plain MSL on the Mac's compiler (M4, safe and fast
math alike): any of Metal's pack_float_to_unorm4x8, _snorm4x8, _unorm2x16 or _snorm2x16, bitcast to a float and written
to some components of a vector that another write overlaps, is compiled wrongly. A plain bitcast, the half2 bitcast
(PK2), the unpack functions and a pack written to a register of its own are not affected. So the translation (and the
interpreter) pack by hand (msl.cpp kPackHelpers, emitted into the programs that pack): round(x * n) of the exact
product, a float product that lands on k + 0.5 decided by its rounding error from an fma, which matches Metal's
intrinsics bit for bit on every code's value and half-step and 100,000 random values (tests/rsx: "pspocket's packs are
Metal's ... bit for bit"); the plain float product rounds a quarter of the half-steps the other way. A program that
packs (PK4, PKB, PK16, PKG) gets a key of its own (":pk"), so a shader cache recorded before holds none of its old
translation, and every other program keeps its cache. Regression: the reduced program, translated and interpreted.

## D-933 · 2026-10-13 · The H.264 and MVC codec cores pspocket's own (part 1: libavcdec)

libavcdec is the H.264 core Sony's libvdec loads (eight decoding calls; GetVersion and QueryCharacteristics were already
pspocket's, D-575): a PPU library whose helper thread hands an SPU program on SPURS each access unit and gives the
caller's callback what the program answers. pspocket's (runtime/hle/src/vdec_avc.cpp, with the H.264 syntax readers in
vdec_h264.hpp) answers as the module does and does the SPU program's work on the host: it reads the stream itself
(parameter sets, slice headers, SEI, picture order counts), keeps the decoded picture buffer as Sony's does (a model
measured from Sony's outputs, below) and has FFmpeg decode the samples, written into Sony's frame buffer layout (D-196).
libavcdec is no longer firmware-first (codec_cores.cpp).

What Sony's core does, and pspocket's with it:
- QueryMemory: the level's (10 to 42) or the caller's frame size (4 to 120 by 4 to 68 macroblocks, within the level's
  largest frame), deblocking up to 2, buffers up to the level's; the memory is fourteen blocks (the frame buffers the
  fifth, as many as the buffer and two) and 0x299500 bytes, to 128. Open: the arguments' checks (the SDK version picks
  the access unit size limit), the memory zeroed up to +0x294300, the context in its last 0x1380 bytes (magic
  0xBE264DEC), a SPURS instance of its own when given none ("_libvdec_avc"), a task set "_libvdec_avc_<handle>".
- The states: open, flushing (Flush; AccessUnit is SEQ until the flush is done), resetting (Reset; Reset's flags 0
  to 3, keep the parameter sets or not), closed. After Close, the calls that take the context's lock answer 0x80010005
  (the lock is gone); Close again is SEQ.
- AccessUnit: up to five access units queued (BUSY when fewer than two places are left), side data up to 0x40 bytes
  copied into a table of 46 entries, freed when the access unit's pictures are released.
- Messages: AU done (the access unit, its side data, discarded, in error, whether a sequence it decodes is active, the
  error code), a picture (0x178 bytes of information), flush done, reset done, a severe error.
- The decoded picture buffer: max_dec_frame_buffering when the stream gives it (num_reorder_frames is not used), else
  the level's MaxDpbMbs, at most what the frame buffers the decoder was opened with hold (a 64 x 80 stream in a decoder
  opened for 5 x 4 macroblocks gets 16 frame buffers and a buffer of 14). At each access unit: the caller's releases are
  taken; the picture decoded last joins the buffer; an IDR picture outputs everything (or nothing, with
  no_output_of_prior_pics_flag); a reference picture's marking (the sliding window or its memory management
  operations) comes before pictures are output while the buffer holds more than its size; then the pictures whose PTS
  this access unit's DTS reached are output (a picture whose PTS is before its DTS, or that has no DTS or PTS, leaves
  only when the buffer outputs it). The outputs follow the access unit's AU done.
- Frame buffers in turn from the second; a buffer is free once its picture left the buffer and the caller released it,
  counting only those free before the access unit's buffer step. Frame IDs are the lowest free; skipped pictures (decode
  modes 1 to 3 leave non-reference pictures out) are given 256 and up and need no release.
- The GOP flag (+0xC of the information) is set on the first I picture after an SPS, in its access unit or an earlier
  one; an IDR picture without one has none.
- Errors: a sequence it refuses (0x10 a profile or level it does not know; 0x12 Extended, High 10, High 4:2:2, chroma
  other than 4:2:0, more than 8 bits, a frame under 64 x 64, or any sequence after Reset with flags 0; 0x13 a frame
  larger than the decoder was opened for) gives each access unit an AU done in error and a picture skipped and in error
  at once, the code with the first only. An access unit with no slice to decode gives 0x11 (0x10 with a slice) before a
  sequence, 0x51 (0x50) within one, with the last picture's type and order count. Before any frame buffers are laid out
  the error picture is in the first, made blank (luma 0, chroma 0x80, its gaps too).

Not reproduced (documented tolerance):
- Within a sequence, an access unit with no slice makes Sony's core vary with its SPU side's timing (two runs differ):
  the frame buffer of its error picture (blank, a copy of a picture a line down, or left as it was) and the NAL unit
  flags of the pictures after it (their own, or another access unit's). pspocket leaves the buffer as it was and gives
  each picture its own flags.
- Before any sequence, access units with no slice and no SPS are taken by Sony's core as field pairs (an error picture
  for every second one, one access unit late), as are High 4:4:4 and CAVLC 4:4:4 sequences, whose SPS its parser reads
  as another profile's; pspocket gives each its error picture at once.
- A damaged slice (cut short) is 0x50 in Sony's core, the next picture 0x66 (the frame number gap); pspocket decodes
  what FFmpeg decodes.
- The information's padding (+0xD to +0xF, +0xCA, +0xCB) is the helper thread's stack in Sony's module (0 in a new
  thread, what its Reset left after one); pspocket writes 0. The SPU side's working memory, queues and task contexts
  are not written.

Compared (tests/hle/test_vdec_avc_compare.cpp, the user's firmware 4.92): QueryMemory over levels and sizes, Open's
refusals, IDR, I/P, B, buffers of 1, 2 and the level's, non-reference pictures, IDR pictures between, decode modes 1 to
3, the clock (PTS against DTS, missing stamps, 33 bits), held pictures and the queue, side data, every call in every
state, Reset's flags, refused sequences, access units with no slice, GOP flags, a decoder opened smaller than its
stream, its own SPURS, other sizes and levels; every answer, message, information byte and frame buffer: 0 of 2215
observations differ. Sony's libvdec over pspocket's core against Sony's libvdec over Sony's (test_vdec_ext_compare.cpp,
libvdec's H.264 lives: as a game that imports libvdec's unverified functions gets it): 0 of 1145 differ. Without the
firmware, some of the lives run through pspocket's core against Sony's recorded answers. Shared files changed:
codec_cores.cpp (libavcdec no longer firmware-first), modules.cpp, test_codec_cores.cpp and
test_codec_cores_compare.cpp (that mark), test_vdec_ext_compare.cpp (Sony's libvdec over pspocket's core).

## D-933 · 2026-10-14 · The H.264 and MVC codec cores pspocket's own (part 2: libmvcdec, the MVC core)

libmvcdec (seven decoding calls) is libavcdec's PPU program with other numbers, over an SPU program of its own for one
view or two (Blu-ray 3D's stereo pairs). pspocket's shares vdec_avc.cpp with libavcdec (a Core of each module's
numbers: errors 0x806159xx, open mark 0xBE264DDC, a context of 0x1F80 bytes, 82 side data entries of 0x48 bytes that
count their pictures' releases, 36 other commands, the memory cleared to +0x4F6400, its own SPURS and task set at
+0x4F6400 and +0x4F7400, "_libvdec_mvc"); its memory is sixteen blocks, the frame buffers two views' (the buffer count
even, at most 32). libmvcdec is no longer firmware-first.

What Sony's core does, and pspocket's with it:
- Open has no SDK version. AccessUnit takes its pieces in a structure (the base view's, its continuation, the second
  view's, its continuation, each with its size); the first access unit fixes whether there is a second view (one with
  the other is ARG). No GetStatus.
- The AU done message has every piece and its size, the flags spread out, and the pictures the access unit gives. A
  picture's information is 0x158 bytes after a 0x44-byte message: libavcdec's fields with the view (0, 1), whether it
  is its access unit's first picture and how many pictures that gives where libavcdec has its GOP flag (which
  follows), the rest moved, no frame packing, the flags as one doubleword (the SPU side's, libavcdec's one bit down,
  spread over bits 33 to 63).
- Its decoded picture buffer is not libavcdec's: a picture is stored as soon as it is decoded, as H.264's reference
  decoder (JM) does (its marking, then pictures output while the buffer is full, a non-reference picture that would
  come first output at once instead of stored); the clock as libavcdec's. With one view a picture output at once comes
  with the next access unit's messages (after its AU done); with two views the base view picture comes at once and its
  second view picture with the next access unit's (before its AU done). An IDR picture's outputs come after the AU done
  with one view, before it with two. The frame buffers are split for two views with one view too (half the buffer);
  each picture of a pair takes the next one in turn.
- Frame IDs as libavcdec's (free once released and out of the buffer); a picture output at once before takes its ID
  after the access unit's marking; a flush counts IDs freed since.
- What the VUI leaves out of the video signal is inferred (5, 2, 2, 2) where libavcdec gives 0.
- Skipped pictures (the decode modes) and error pictures have no frame buffer (frame 0); an error picture passes over
  one in turn (the second of two in a row none); an unknown profile's or level's has no IDR flag.
- After Close the calls that lock answer 2: the module maps the lock's failure through its own codes, which have none
  for it, and answers what its stack held there.

The second view: FFmpeg has no MVC decoder, so pspocket decodes the second view with a second FFmpeg H.264 decoder
given a one-view stream made from it (vdec_mvc_view.cpp): each access unit's base view picture as decoded, as an I
picture of I_PCM macroblocks, then the second view's slices as one view's, their reference lists spelt out
(ref_pic_list_modification) as MVC builds them with that I picture as the inter-view reference, their marking spelt out
(memory management operations), a copy of their PPS whose id's length and delta_pic_order_cnt_bottom keep a CAVLC
slice's data on its byte alignment. Not so (the base view's samples stand for the second view, logged once): field
pictures, other than 4:2:0 8-bit samples, long-term references, more than two second-view PPSs. Not exact: direct
prediction from a B picture's first list 1 reference when that is the base view's (the I picture has no motion).

Not reproduced: the information's padding (+0x71 to +0x77 and the flags' low 33 bits, stack leftovers in Sony's
module); errors with two views (not measured).

Compared (tests/hle/test_vdec_avc_compare.cpp, "The MVC core (libmvcdec) against Sony's"): QueryMemory (in a scratch
sweep 720 parameter sets agree), every life of libavcdec's comparison with one view, and two views' lives (I_PCM
second views, anchors predicted from the base view, P pictures from the second view's last, buffers of 1 and 2,
non-reference and B pictures, IDR pictures between, decode modes 1 to 3, the views changing, side data released a view
at a time): 0 of 2782 observations differ, frame buffers included; libavcdec's comparison after the change: 0 of 2215.
Without the firmware, a test runs some of the lives through pspocket's core against Sony's recorded answers. Shared
files changed: codec_cores.cpp (libmvcdec no longer firmware-first; with libsjvtd's, D-920 part 8, no codec core
is), modules.cpp, test_codec_cores.cpp and test_codec_cores_compare.cpp (that mark).

## D-944 · 2026-10-13 · The audio cores against Sony's (part 1: their sizes, and MP3 call for call as libmp3dec)

cellAdec's cores on FFmpeg (D-577: MP3, MPEG audio layers I and II, MPEG-4 AAC, AC-3, ATRAC3) were RPCS3's structures
read by their names and served only where the firmware has no module (firmware first). They are now compared with
Sony's: tests/hle/test_adec_cores.cpp's "the cores on FFmpeg against Sony's cores (D-944)" runs each feed through
cellAdec twice, over pspocket's core and over Sony's core module from the user's firmware (FirmwareCores: libadec's
front end is pspocket's in both, so only the cores differ), and compares every call's answer, the callbacks, the PCM
items (handle, status, size, PTS, user data), the information blocks byte for byte and the PCM. It stays hidden
([.compare-adec]) until every core agrees.

Sony's answers taken for every core (Spec in adec_*.cpp): getMemSize (MP3 0x27300, layer I 0x64000, layer II 0x3E400,
MPEG-4 AAC 0x299A9A, its 2-channel 0x1A2CF0 and 2-channel modified 0xBAC70, AC-3 0x5EB2F, ATRAC3 0x3CB80; a core
fails loudly if FFmpeg's state does not fit, which it does), the versions (MP3 0x01030000, layer I 0x01080000, layer
II 0x02040000, AAC 0x03070000, AC-3 0x20070323, ATRAC3 0x01020000; layers I and II and AAC also write theirs into the
attribute at +8, as their getMemSize does), and the PCM handle counts (MP3 and ATRAC3 3, the MPEG layers and AAC 4,
AC-3 8).

MP3, as libmp3dec does it (adec_mp3.cpp):
- The bit reservoir is the core's own: FFmpeg's ADU decoder (mp3adufloat, added to scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh) gets each
  frame with its main data (main_data_begin bytes back from what the frames before left, then its own) right after its
  side information. A frame whose main data begin before what the reservoir holds (a stream entered mid-way) gives a
  PCM item of size 0 and no error, and its whole main data area stays for the frames after. After a frame whose main
  data the decoder refuses, the reservoir is empty and the decoder silent (FFmpeg flushed: libmp3dec's next frame
  starts from silence).
- CellAdecMP3Info: ui_header the header's low 20 bits; ui_main_data_remain_size the reservoir held before the frame
  (what the frame before left after its main data, uncapped: 820 seen); ui_main_data_now_size 0. The block lives from
  frame to frame: a unit refused leaves the last frame's (zeros before any) and writes i_error_code as libmp3dec's own
  number for the error. Its table (libmp3dec.sprx, 0x4998) pairs -1 to -7 with CELL_ADEC_ERROR_MP3_ERROR to
  BAD_BLKTYPE, -10 to -12 with BAD_VERSION to BAD_MODE_EXT, -15 to -23 with HUFFMAN_NUM to PCMOUT.
- Versions: a clear MPEG-2.5 bit is MPEG-2.5 whatever the version bit beside it, so the reserved version decodes as
  MPEG-2.5 (FFmpeg gets the header as MPEG-2.5's); nothing is BAD_VERSION. The PTS correction is by the rate's index
  (48, 44.1, 32 kHz and their halves and quarters: every frame steps 2160, 2351 or 3240 ticks).
- A unit shorter than its frame is decoded, zeros past its end (libmp3dec reads its own buffer there; the same while
  the main data are inside the unit). A wrong CRC is flagged and the frame decoded.
- The PCM: floats as decoded (past 1 where the stream goes: 4.98 seen), 16-bit rounded half away from zero and held in
  range (55,296 samples of Sony's float and 16-bit outputs: every one not at full scale rounds so). write_pcm has
  Rounding::Nearest for it; the other cores keep libatxdec's (floats held below 1, integers floored).

Not reproduced (documented tolerance): the padding byte before i_error_code, where libmp3dec leaves a byte of its own
after an error (0x16 or 0x08 seen); libmp3dec's checks of the main data (HUFFMAN_NUM and the others), as FFmpeg decodes
what it refuses; a unit shorter than a header (libmp3dec reads the rest from what its buffer held); the floats differ
from libmp3dec's in their last bits (3.6e-7 at most, 121 dB), so a 16-bit sample at a rounding boundary can differ by
one step.

Compared (the user's firmware 4.92): MP3 float and 16-bit, the bit reservoir (in use, full past 511, entered
mid-way with a refused unit), each header error and block type 0 between good frames, an error first, MPEG-2, MPEG-2.5
and the reserved version, MPEG-2.5 without PTS, units of 0 bytes, of part of their frame and of two frames, CRC: 11 of
11 agree. Still differing (part 2): layers I and II (the information's channel count and frame size), ATRAC3 (its
first output and the information), MPEG-4 AAC (the PCM at 63.5 dB, a frame counter in the information), AC-3 (its
first frame).

## D-943 · 2026-10-13 · sys_lv2coredump_D725F320 pspocket's own: a retail console's core file

liblv2coredump.sprx is the module that writes a game's crash dumps. libsysmodule loads it as a process starts when
the executable declares SYS_PROCESS_CRASH_DUMP_ENABLED (sys_process_param's crash_dump_param_addr). It exports
sys_lv2coredump_D725F320(fd), the library chart's last function, and sys_crashdump's two log area functions
(pspocket's own since D-607). pspocket's sys_lv2coredump (runtime/hle/src/sys_lv2coredump.cpp) does what Sony's module
does on a retail console, step for step: the same lv2 calls, the same calls into the libraries it imports (liblv2's
heap, lightweight mutex, thread and printf functions; cellGame; cellSysutil), the same heap blocks and the same bytes.

**lv2.** _sys_process_get_paramsfo now reports the declaration as the retail kernel does: flag 0x10 at +0x10 and the
declaration's address at +0x38 (the loader passes crash_dump_param_addr from the executable). +0x20 holds a debugging
console's crash dump settings; it is 0, because pspocket's console is a retail one.

**Start.** lv2coredump_start is the module_start that libsysmodule runs with no arguments. It reads the paramsfo and
checks the declaration, which must be readable and hold {0x20, "dump", 1, 0, 0, 0}. A bad declaration prints the
module's error and leaves the module idle. Otherwise start makes, in Sony's order:
- the lightweight mutex "_l2cMTX";
- the 64 KB heap "_LIBLV2COREDUMP_";
- the event queue "_l2cDBG", registered as the PPU exception handler (944);
- a sys_fsw_connect_event call;
- the title information read through libsysutil_game: title ID, title, version, SDK version;
- the thread "__COREDUMP_HANDLER__" (priority 1001, 16 KB stack), which waits on the queue.
The configuration is the declaration's: crash reports to /dev_hdd0, no extra parts.

**D725F320(fd)** writes an ELF64 core file (OS ABI 0x66, PPC64) into the open file: the program headers, then one
PT_NOTE note per part.
- SYSTEM_INFO: the console's OpenPSID and the system software version the module was built with.
- DUMP_CAUSE_INFO: the handler's exception records (none here).
- PROCESS_INFO: sys_dbg_get_process_info, the PPU thread and SPU thread group counts (from sys_dbg_get_thread_list),
  and the PPU GUID.
- GAME_APP_INFO: the title information start read.
- The memory part, which is empty on a retail console.
The ELF header's program header count grows as each note ends. The TTY gets the progress report: "Generating Core Dump
File", one dot per 4 %, then " Done." or the error. The call answers CELL_ENOSPC when /dev_hdd0 has 10 KB or less
free, or when start never configured the module.

**Never written.** A debugging console's settings add parts: the PPU and SPU threads and registers, the SPU local
stores, the synchronisation objects, memory, modules, the RSX state and SPURS. pspocket's lv2 reports no such
settings, so pspocket never writes those parts and does not implement them, as Sony's module on a retail console never
writes them.

**Left as follow-ups:**
- The user's log areas (USER_LOG_INFO, filled by sys_crash_dump_set_user_log_area). Sony's module keeps the areas
  itself; pspocket's sys_crashdump, firmware-first, keeps them apart.
- The handler thread's crash report after an exception. pspocket's lv2 sends the queue no exception yet. The handler
  logs any event it gets (a game's 959 or 972, the queue's last from 945 or 988) and goes on waiting.
- The libsysmodule hook, left out because it does not follow from what is known. RPCS3's cellSysmodule start
  (rpcs3/Emu/Cell/Modules/cellSysmodule.cpp) loads liblv2coredump when bit 4 of paramsfo +0x10 is set. pspocket's
  cellSysmodule has no start of its own to hang that on. Sony's module also serves the firmware-first sys_crashdump,
  so which module a process gets (pspocket's or the firmware's) is a loader decision still to make. Until then the
  start runs only where a test calls it, and a game's D725F320 answers CELL_ENOSPC, as the unstarted module does.

**Compared** in tests/hle/test_lv2coredump_compare.cpp (firmware 4.92). The same process runs both halves: the
declaration in memory, /dev_hdd0 on a directory of the test's. Sony's module is started by the LLE loader and
pspocket's by lv2coredump_start; then D725F320 writes into a file.
- With the declaration: the answer and the core file match byte for byte, note by note. 0 of 13 observations differ.
- Without it: CELL_ENOSPC and an empty file in both. 0 of 4 observations differ.
Without the firmware, the same file checks pspocket's start (the handler's queue hears a game's 959 only with the
declaration) and the four notes. tests/lv2/test_process.cpp checks the paramsfo.

## D-944 · 2026-10-13 · The audio cores against Sony's (part 2: MPEG audio layers I and II, ATRAC3, MPEG-4 AAC)

Part 1's comparison (tests/hle/test_adec_cores.cpp, [.compare-adec]) over the other cores. What each does as Sony's
does now:

- MPEG audio layers I and II (adec_mpeg.cpp, libmpl1dec and libm2bcdec): the output is the stream's own channels
  whatever channelNumber says up to 2; past 2 every frame is refused (libmpl1dec 0x80613112, libm2bcdec's
  OPENBS_EX 0x80612B21), as a multichannel extension is asked for. libmpl1dec has its own error range, libm2bcdec's
  numbers from 0x80613100 (RPCS3 lists none). Refusals: no 12-bit sync (MPEG-2.5 and the reserved version too) SYNCF,
  free format and bit rate 15 BITRATE, the reserved rate SAMPLEFREQ, the other layer's header, a unit shorter than its
  frame and a frame the decoder refuses SYNCF_EX (0x22); emphasis 2 decodes. A refused unit gives an item of 1152
  samples of silence in the information block's channels (libmpl1dec copies only a layer I frame's 384 of them out:
  Decoded::copied) and leaves the block as the last frame decoded left it; before any frame the block reads stereo,
  48 kHz, bit rate index 14, 1152 stereo samples, L_R. channelNumber in the block is the output's channel count, and
  outputFrameSize 1152 samples of the channels in bytes (layer I's too). Floats are not held below 1. StartSeq refuses
  a downmix flag past 1 only.
- ATRAC3 (adec_atrac3.cpp, libat3dec): the sound is FFmpeg's with its sign turned over (FFmpeg's ATRAC3 decoder has the
  opposite polarity: -6.0 dB against Sony's until turned, 116 dB after); a sequence's first frame, and the first after
  a refused unit, comes out empty (decoded all the same: the frames after overlap it); the information's nbytes is a
  channel's (nbytes / nch). Floats held below 1 and integers floored, as before (round to nearest made 16-bit worse).
- MPEG-4 AAC (adec_aac.cpp, libm4aacdec and its 2-channel forms): the block lives from frame to frame (a refused unit
  leaves the last frame's) and its word at +0x74, past RPCS3's structure, counts the frames decoded since the start or
  the last refusal. A refused unit gives a frame of silence in the last frame's channels and starts the decoder
  afresh (FFmpeg's opened again: its overlap and window shapes as at a sequence's start, which a flush alone does not
  reset); a frame FFmpeg refuses is INVALID_SECTION_DATA (0x8061241C, libm4aacdec's for raw data that are not AAC's).
  An ADTS frame its unit cuts short waits for the next unit, whose bytes complete it (libm4aacdec reads the two as one
  frame, whatever the second holds).

Not reproduced (documented tolerance): perceptual noise substitution's noise in AAC (each decoder's own random
numbers: the comparison's AAC streams are encoded without it); an AAC unit without its sync whose bytes hold a false
one (libm4aacdec reads on from it into the next unit); ATRAC3's frame after next when a sequence's first frame is
refused (up to 12 16-bit steps: libat3dec's state after its partial decode of the bad frame).

Compared: 45 cases of MP3, layers I and II, ATRAC3 and AAC agree, each in every answer, callback, item, information
byte and PCM sample (floats within their last bits, 16-bit within one step). Still differing (part 3): AC-3.

## D-944 · 2026-10-13 · The audio cores against Sony's (part 3: AC-3; the compared cores no longer firmware-first)

libac3dec's behaviour, from the comparison and probes of its output by parameter (adec_ac3.cpp):

- StartSeq refuses only word size, LFE, compression, stereo, dual mono and karaoke modes past their enums, more than
  six slots, and a channel pointer outside 0 to 5, with libadec's ARG (0x80610003). It does not check the output mode,
  the scale factors or two pointers alike; -1 is no pointer (it is refused): a channel is left out by pointing past
  numberOfChannels.
- Routing: each channel of the output mode (L, C, R, Ls, Rs, then the LFE when outLfeOn), whether or not the stream
  has it, goes to its pointer's slot in that order, a later one taking a slot an earlier one has; channels outside the
  output mode write nothing; slots past numberOfChannels are not out (0 slots: no PCM).
- Downmixes, nothing normalised: Lt/Rt L + 0.7071 C - 0.7071 (Ls + Rs), R + 0.7071 C + 0.7071 (Ls + Rs); Lo/Ro L + clev C
  + slev Ls; 3/0 the surrounds into the fronts at slev; 2/1 and 3/1 the centre into the fronts at clev (2/1) and the
  surround as half of each; 1/0 half of L, R, the centre at clev and the surrounds at slev; a mono stream into 2/0 both
  sides at 0.7071; stereoMode auto is Lt/Rt (Lo/Ro only where annex D's dmixmod prefers it); the 1+1 output mode is
  the 2/0 one.
- pcmScaleFactor from -2 up to 2, anything else silence; floats held below 1, 16-bit rounded to nearest
  (Rounding::HeldNearest: 85 dB against Sony's either way the precision allows, 82 dB floored).
- CellAdecBsiAc3 is 0x50 bytes (so getMemSize's total grows by 12 bytes a PCM handle): codecType word 0x1001,
  versionInfo 0x04990000, totalCallNum every call, the bit rate in bit/s, esSizeBit and validity 0, the rate as
  MPEG-4's sampling frequency index (48 kHz 3, 44.1 kHz 4, 32 kHz 5), outputQuantization 0xFF float and 3 16-bit,
  karaokeMode 2 for a stream that is no karaoke one, bsi() from bsid as 24-bit words cut at its end (A/52's bsi()
  parsed to addbsi), execDmixType 1 Lt/Rt or 2 Lo/Ro for a 2/0 output whatever the stream, reported for the frame after
  the one that set it up (0 on a sequence's first frame), and the flag at +0x20 when the frame's size or that kind is
  not the frame before's (44.1 kHz's padded frames set it). A refused unit's block is left blank.

Not reproduced (documented tolerance): libac3dec refuses (AC3_FRAME) the frame of FFmpeg's encoder where a sound starts
after digital silence (its priming frame and any such onset; a sound that starts quiet is decoded), its CRCs good: some
check of its own FFmpeg's decoder does not make, not found; the next frame's first block shows its partial decode. A
professional encoder's frames are not expected to trip it, so pspocket decodes them, and the comparison's streams start
past it. Output modes past 7 (not in CellAdecAc3OutputMode): libac3dec gives eight slots for mode 8; pspocket takes it
as 3/2. AC-3's PCM differs from libac3dec's by up to two 16-bit steps (its decoder's precision, 85 to 105 dB).

With this, the 67 cases of the comparison agree, and test_hle "[compare][adec-cores]" (hidden: three minutes) holds
them. MP3, the MPEG audio layers, MPEG-4 AAC and its two 2-channel cores, AC-3 and ATRAC3 are no longer firmware-first
(adec_tables.cpp): every game gets pspocket's cores for them, with or without the firmware. Still Sony's first, not
compared: E-AC-3 (libddpdec), MPEG-2 AAC, MP3 Surround, ATRAC3 multichannel (libat3multidec), TrueHD, DTS (libdtslbrdec)
and WMA (libwmadec); the firmware has modules for E-AC-3, ATRAC3 multichannel, DTS Express and WMA to compare with.

## D-945 · 2026-10-14 · Fewer render passes for a tile GPU (part 1: clears that wait, stores the next pass makes dead)

On a tile GPU every render pass loads its attachments from memory at its start (unless cleared) and stores them at
its end. GTA V's prologue walk ran 55 to 96 passes a frame, ended mostly by target changes (D-273: 188 MB loaded and
209 MB stored a frame). What ended them besides (runs 291 and 305, the traced frame): clears. A clear of targets other
than the open pass's ended it and opened a pass of its own; a pass that only cleared (one target cleared alone, then
the depth buffer alone, then all four G-buffer targets with depth drawn) stored what the next pass loaded again.

- **Clears that wait** (metal_backend.mm ClearOp): a clear of targets the open pass does not draw to, made while it
  draws, no longer ends it; nor does a clear of whole surfaces, nor a pass that only cleared when the targets change.
  The clear waits, its surfaces' state (written, newer on the GPU, generations, D-122's parent and children) set at
  once as if it had run. The next pass that has its surfaces does it: a clear of whole surfaces it draws whole as its
  load action, a clear of part of them inside its area as its first draws (a quad, as before). The others run in
  passes of their own right before that pass starts, or before any other GPU work is recorded (a copy, a conversion,
  a readback, a flip, a submit: end_pass), and before anything reads their surfaces (a draw sampling one, bind_texture
  and depth_sampled_directly end the pass drawing first) or reloads them from guest memory (open_pass). In the order
  they were made: a pass takes a clear only when no clear after it that stays waiting touches its surfaces, and a
  clear of whole surfaces makes the waiting clears of them before it moot (nothing read them in between), so a pass
  does a surface's clear of all of it first, by its load action, then the clears of parts of it.
- **Stores the next pass makes dead:** a pass the targets change away from leaves its encoder open with its store
  actions unknown (MTLStoreActionUnknown); when the next pass starts, an attachment it clears whole, or a waiting clear
  clears whole before it, is not stored (DontCare: depth and stencil apart). Any other GPU work recorded first ends
  the encoder and stores everything (render_buffer()), so nothing can read an attachment between the two passes.
- Found on the way: a clear made with fewer colour targets than the open pass has (a clear of the first of them) wrote
  every target of the pass, by its quad or its load action (RPCS3 VKGSRender.cpp clear_surface clears the targets the
  surface registers name), and a clear naming no depth buffer cleared the pass's. The clear quad's pipeline now takes
  a mask of the attachments it writes (clear_pipeline_for).
- Not done: memoryless depth needs to know, before a pass starts, that no later pass loads the buffer and nothing
  samples or copies it. In GTA V's traced frame every depth buffer is read again (the main one by the next frame's
  first passes, the shadow tiles sampled, the reflection views' by the next view's first draw); the DontCare store
  above takes the bandwidth part where it is safe. Copies still end the pass: GTA V's feedback, corner and conversion
  copies need what the open pass drew or come with a target change anyway (D-248), and NV0039's GPU copy commits its
  buffer at once so that its readback reaches guest memory before the labels after it (D-107).
- Measuring aids: the status line and pspocket-boot's --summary windows give MB loaded, stored and not stored a frame,
  the clears done by a later pass and the clears that let a pass go on; PSPOCKET_GPU_AB's line gives each half's render
  passes and MB loaded and stored too (one walk measures all of it), and the flip's command buffer now counts in the
  half of the frame it holds (it went to the next frame's half: one frame in N on the wrong side). Off:
  MetalBackendConfig::merge_passes = false or PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_PASS_MERGING=1.
- Tests (tests/rsx/test_metal.mm, "D-945"): clears folded into the next pass's load actions (one pass instead of three,
  nothing loaded); a clear of another target, whole or in part, letting the pass go on; a draw sampling a target whose
  clear waits sees it; a depth buffer the next pass clears whole not stored, and stored when a draw reads it in
  between; a clear of the first targets of a pass with more (fails before the fix); clears waiting before an NV0039
  copy, an NV308A write and a flip; clears of parts of a target and its depth and stencil done as the next pass's first
  draws, in three orders. Each against the same commands with merging off, pixel for pixel.
- Measured (run 324, "metal bench" in test_metal.mm: a synthetic frame shaped like GTA V's, its passes, sizes and
  clears, every draw one triangle; M4 Mac): render passes a frame 57 to 53, attachments loaded 137.3 to 119.8 MB
  (-13%) and stored 144.7 to 127.1 MB (-12%). In-run A/B (PSPOCKET_GPU_AB=10, six windows of 100 frames a half, the Mac
  busy with other builds): GPU time a frame 4.49/4.21, 4.15/4.22, 4.96/4.01, 3.53/3.27, 3.22/3.28, 3.16/3.04 ms
  (off/on; mean 3.92 to 3.67), the RSX thread's CPU 1.10 to 1.67 ms a frame, 2-4% lower with it in all six. Worked
  through by hand on GTA V's traced frame (run 291's trace, not run again), the same rules make its 85 passes 81: the
  clear-only passes of its first G-buffer target and of its depth buffer become the G-buffer pass's load actions, the
  lighting pass goes on past a clear of part of another target, and a stencil clear between two passes over the frame
  becomes the second one's first draw (about 17 MB loaded and 17 MB stored less a frame).
- **GTA V's walk not measured:** its disc image is no longer on this Mac (inventory/gta5/disc.iso is gone, and no other
  .iso is here), and neither iPhone is connected to copy it back (scripts/ios.sh pull-iso). With it back:
  `PSPOCKET_GPU_AB=30 scripts/gate.sh game` gives both halves' passes, MB and GPU time from one walk, and the gate's
  frame checks the rendering.

## D-944 · 2026-10-14 · The audio cores against Sony's (part 4: ATRAC3 multichannel; what the other four need)

ATRAC3 multichannel (adec_atrac3.cpp) against libat3multidec: Sony's answers (getMemSize 0x42400, version 0x00010000,
three PCM handles, a 0xC-byte block: nch, isJoint and a channel's bytes of a frame), and libat3dec's ways (part 2):
the sound with FFmpeg's sign turned over, a sequence's first frame and the first after a refused unit out empty. It
agrees (68 cases in all now) and is no longer firmware-first. The comparison's harness forces Sony's core modules
(FirmwareCores) and checks the one linked is Sony's, since games get pspocket's.

The other four with modules in the firmware stay firmware-first, each needing more than a comparison:
- E-AC-3 (libddpdec: getMemSize 0x93400, version 0x02080000 written into the attributes too, four handles, a 0x330-byte
  block): its StartSeq refuses (0x80612603) whatever the parameters; its open checks more of its arguments than the
  other cores' (an extended open's resources, by the look of it): what it needs from the front end is to find first.
- WMA (libwmadec: 0x2FF80, 0x01010000, three handles, a 0x14-byte block that is the parameters' first 20 bytes as
  given): it refuses every frame of FFmpeg's WMA 2 (0x80612C80) whatever the parameters say (block size and encoder
  options at each of words 4 to 8, or a big-endian WAVEFORMATEX): the units it expects are not FFmpeg's raw blocks
  (ASF data packets, perhaps). Games do not decode WMA through cellAdec (the XMB's music player does).
- DTS Express (libdtslbrdec: 0x6C720, 0x02080000, four handles, a 0x960-byte block): FFmpeg has no encoder for its
  streams to compare with.
- MPEG-2 AAC, MP3 Surround, TrueHD and DTS have no module in the firmware.

## D-947 · 2026-10-14 · A target a draw samples while drawing to it: read through the texture cache, not copied each time

The first long play of GTA V on the iPhone 18 Pro Max (run 327) went from 30 fps to 4 to 12 in some scenes for minutes
at a time, with the sound late in up to half of its periods. The per-frame lines show why: up to 335 feedback copies a
frame (D-148: a copy of a target a draw samples while drawing to it), each ending the render pass, so up to 411 passes
and 3.3 GB of attachments loaded and stored a frame, 80 to 155 ms of GPU time (about 0.4 ms a copy; 7 to 11 copies a
frame elsewhere). The copies, each a new texture held until the GPU ran the frame, took the GPU's allocations to 8.9 GB
and brought two memory warnings. D-148 shared a copy only between draws that write nothing to the target they sample;
these draws write it.

- **The RSX's texture cache:** the RSX reads such a target through its texture cache, which sees what draws wrote only
  after the game invalidates it (cellGcmSetInvalidateTextureCache, NV4097_INVALIDATE_L2); until then a draw may read
  what the cache took in before. The copy now plays that cache: kept, though the target was written since, while the
  draws go on to the same targets (the pass's targets; a change of them ends it, as the RSX's small cache would have let
  go by then) and no invalidation came. A write and an invalidation, or a write and a change of targets, make it again.
  RPCS3 samples the target in place unless its strict rendering mode is on (texture_cache_helpers.h
  force_strict_fbo_sampling: "MSAA disabled. All access is fast"), which a tile GPU cannot do inside a pass.
- **The RSX front end** counts NV4097_INVALIDATE_L2 commands (RsxState::texture_cache_epoch); the command still marks
  the fragment program dirty, as RPCS3's set_shader_program_dirty.
- **Not changed:** the depth bounds test's copy of the depth buffer (D-261) and D-105's depth conversions.
- **Report:** a line after the per-frame one when a window had such draws: copies a frame (the first, after a write and
  an invalidation, after the targets changed, with the rule off), draws that read a kept copy, invalidations a frame,
  and the three draws behind most of it (fragment program offset, texture unit, target address, size and format).
  WindowStats gains feedback_reused and texture_cache_invalidations.
- **Measuring and switching on the phone:** PSPOCKET_RSX_STRICT_FEEDBACK=1 is D-148's rule (a copy after every
  write); PSPOCKET_GPU_AB=N alternates the two every N frames. The app now reads Documents/pspocket-env.txt at boot
  (PSPOCKET_ names only, one NAME=VALUE a line, each logged), so a switch reaches a phone run over USB without a build.
- Tests: tests/rsx/test_metal.mm, "D-947": without an invalidation 20 draws that read their target after a write read
  the first draw's copy, one copy and two passes; after NV4097_INVALIDATE_L2 the draw sees the write (D-148's test, the
  invalidation added); after the draws went to another target and back, a new copy. tests/rsx/test_methods.cpp: the
  command counts and marks the fragment program dirty.

## D-948 · 2026-10-14 · The signed blend equations done in the shader (programmable blending)

The user's screenshots of run 327 (GTA V on the iPhone): a bright patch around the car where the road is in shadow,
a dark ragged one where it is in the sun, flat light in a parking garage. GTA V blends those with
NV4097_SET_BLEND_EQUATION ADD_SIGNED (0xf006 for colour and alpha, logged once a run: "blend equation 0xf006/0xf006
(signed) is not implemented"), which Metal's blending has not: drawn as add, a source byte meant to darken (0xf0 is -16)
lit the target nearly to white.

- **The equations** (RPCS3 RSXProgrammableBlendPrologue.glsl): ADD_SIGNED adds the source to the target,
  REVERSE_SUBTRACT_SIGNED takes it away, REVERSE_ADD_SIGNED adds the target to the source; on a target of bytes the
  signed side's byte is two's complement over 255, and no factors apply. RPCS3 switches to blending in the shader for
  them (RSXThread.cpp evaluate_programmable_blending_state).
- **pspocket:** a draw with a signed equation has its fragment program translated with FpOptions::blend_in_shader set
  for the outputs it blends on four-channel targets (RGBA8 and BGRA8, which read bytes as signed; RGBA16F and RGBA32F):
  the function takes each one's pixel from the target ([[color(n)]], programmable blending on Apple GPUs, read from
  tile memory, no copy) and blends it with MslFsParams' equations, factors and blend colour after the output is moved to
  the target's channels, as Metal's blending would; the pipeline does not blend those attachments. The other equations
  in the same function work as RPCS3's (min, max, add, subtract, reverse subtract with the factors, the source term
  saturated on byte targets). A draw the shader interpreter draws while its compile runs (D-940) blends as Metal can,
  as before; B8 and G8B8 targets too (logged).
- Tests: tests/rsx/test_metal.mm, "D-948": over a 0x808080 target a source of r 0xf0, g 0x10 gives 0x70 and 0x90 with
  ADD_SIGNED (0xff with Metal's add, the bug: it fails without the shader's blending), the reverse with
  REVERSE_SUBTRACT_SIGNED, and REVERSE_ADD_SIGNED takes the target's bytes as signed.

## D-949 · 2026-10-14 · Shadow-map lookups compare the texel against the reference (the shadows were inverted)

The user's screenshot of run 327's second session (D-948 in): Franklin's shadow and a mailbox post's drawn white on a
sunny pavement; the car's and the parking garage's earlier. A frame trace on the phone (D-947's switch) found the sun's

sampled directly (D-106) into the G-buffer's third target's alpha, multiplied in. No signed blending in that frame: the
comparison itself was backwards.

- D-100 compared the reference against the texel (`reference op texel`), reading RPCS3's TEX2D_SHADOW alone. RPCS3 sets
  its comparison samplers to the texture's function reversed (GL glutils/sampler.cpp: "The stored texture function is
  reversed wrt the textureProj compare function"; VKDraw.cpp get_compare_func(tex.zfunc(), true)): with the reference on
  the left in GL and Vulkan, the RSX's is `texel op reference`. With the reference first a lit surface (its own depth a
  little in front of the stored one, with GTA V's bias) failed and a shadowed one passed: the sunlit ground came out
  shadowed and the shadows lit.
- rsx_shadow and rsx_shadow_depth (the translation's and the shader interpreter's) now compare the texel against the
  reference. The prologue's change changes translation_fingerprint(): shader caches recorded before are not used.
- Tests: D-100's (a DEPTH16 texture, LEQUAL against 0.5: the 0.25 half passes, the 0.75 half fails; linear filtering
  blends three quarters and a quarter at the edge) and D-106's (the depth buffer itself: LEQUAL fails against a
  reference of 0, GREATER passes) now expect the RSX's direction; both fail with the old one.

GTA V's walk on the Mac logged "blend equation 0xf006/0xf006 (signed) drawn as add (the target's format, MTLPixelFormat
