## D-950 · 2026-10-14 · The SPU workers' QoS class, switchable, and their time by host CPU (no gain from interactive)

Run 327 (GTA V on the iPhone 18 Pro Max): 15 to 28 fps held by the CPU, five of the six cores busy, the heat "serious".
The phone has two performance cores and four efficiency cores, and iOS places threads by their QoS class: the SPU
workers ran at user-initiated, the RSX thread at interactive.

- PSPOCKET_SPU_QOS (interactive, initiated, default or utility) sets every SPU worker's QoS class when it starts, and
  PSPOCKET_SPU_QOS_SOLO an instance of one SPU's (GTA V's sound mixer, SPURS "Secondary"); unset, user-initiated as
  before. PSPOCKET_SPU_AB=S with PSPOCKET_SPU_QOS_B switches the workers between the two every S seconds
  (pthread_set_qos_class_self_np), so one session measures both in the same scenes; each SPURS time line says its half.
- The SPURS time line gives the workloads' time by host CPU (pthread_cpu_number_np after each workload's run), as shares.
- Measured on the phone (run 327's busy windows: EDGE/GFX 7 s or more of SPU time in 5 s, 4.5 cores or more): every
  worker interactive 18.1 fps (104 windows), user-initiated 18.2 (57): no gain, the two performance cores are full
  either way. The sound mixer's time fell by about a third at interactive, but with every worker interactive the sound
  came out worse. The main instance's SPU time ran 61% on CPUs 0 to 3, Secondary's 44% (by inference the efficiency
  cores: the idle Secondary sits on 4 and 5).
- Not done: fewer host threads than SPUs. A workload runs only on the SPUs its priorities name (GTA V's EDGE/GFX on SPUs
  1 to 3, its GraphicsMain on 4 alone), so a worker left out would leave its workloads never run (found by review of
  the first version, which had PSPOCKET_SPURS_THREADS, before it ran).

## D-951 · 2026-10-14 · A clear is done in the open pass only when that pass covers it (the black fight scene)

The user's screenshot of run 327 (the fight tutorial, 20 fps): the screen black but a lit rectangle in its top-left
corner, the characters shiny black. GTA V's prologue walk on the Mac (its disc image back) showed the same for whole
camera shots, half to four fifths of each frame black. The gate's frame jumps compare each frame with the one before:
a fault over a whole shot passes them.

- Off switches, a walk each: with PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_PASS_MERGING the frames were right; D-947's copies (strict), D-948's
  shader blending and D-949's comparison were not the cause. Within D-945: the clears that wait (not the stores left
  out), and of those only a clear of whole targets made while another pass draws.
- A frame trace (frame 2950): GTA V draws a 320x128 target (pitch 0x2800, part of its 2560-wide character targets) with
  its 1280x720 Z24S8 depth buffer, clears its G-buffer's first target whole, then clears the depth buffer alone (depth
  and stencil) under a 1280x720 surface clip. The colour clear used to end the 320x128 pass; under D-945 it waits, and
  the pass goes on. The depth clear found that pass open with its depth buffer, and do_clear did it there, its region
  taken inside the pass's area: 320x128 of the depth buffer cleared. The G-buffer was drawn against old depth everywhere
  else, and only that corner lit (640x256 in other shots, the targets' size there).
- Fix (do_clear): the clear's region is taken in its own area (its surface clip within its surfaces, as open_pass makes
  a pass's), and the open pass keeps the clear only when its area holds that region; else the clear goes as any other
  (it waits, D-945, or has a pass of its own). Before D-945 the same could happen to a clear of a depth buffer alone
  right after a pass over a smaller target with it, and a scissor wider than the clip cleared past the clip in a larger
  pass.
- Test (tests/rsx/test_metal.mm, "D-951"): a 16x16 target drawn, depth-tested, with a 64x64 depth buffer at 0.25;
  another target cleared whole; the depth buffer cleared alone to 1.0; a triangle at 0.75 drawn against it is drawn
  outside the corner too. With merging it fails before the fix (the depth there still 0.25).
- The gate: --frame-jumps also counts dark frames, a third of the 64x36 thumbnail black (every channel 4 or less), the
  summary's "dark"; games/gta5/gate.json's dark_frames_max.
- Measured: the walk from frame 2880, every 4th frame saved: no frame with 30% of its pixels black outside the top-left
  corner (234 frames), where each walk with the fault had whole shots of them (frames 2700 to 2976, 3082 to 3176, 3222
  to 3238 in one).

## D-952 · 2026-10-14 · The iOS runtime built for the A12 and later (LSE atomics); the app a game (Game Mode)

Two findings of the research on a steady 30 fps (docs/improve.md), both from build settings:

- **LSE atomics.** libPSPocketRuntime.a held no LSE atomic instruction and 5,444 load- and store-exclusive ones: for an
  arm64 iOS target clang builds for ARMv8.0 (apple-a7) unless told, where the Mac's builds get ARMv8.5 (apple-m1).
  Every atomic on the hot paths (the reservations, ps_res_acquire and ps_res_notify_write; the SPURS lines; the FIFO's
  get and put) was a retry loop. The runtime target now has -mcpu=apple-a12: iOS 17's oldest devices have an A12
  (ARMv8.3, LSE). The Mac's numbers cannot show it; the phone's SPU and RSX threads' CPU in the same scenes will.
- **Game Mode.** The app declared public.app-category.developer-tools, so iOS never gave it Game Mode (CPU and GPU
  priority, background work held back, and Adaptive Power leaves such games alone). It is now public.app-category.games
  with LSSupportsGameMode (iOS 18.6 and later) and GCSupportsGameMode (iOS 18.0 to 18.5) in Info.plist; iOS shows a
  "Game Mode" banner when it applies, and the user can turn it off from Control Center.

## D-970 · 2026-10-14 · The phone's power and heat in the log; in-session translation at "serious" heat; the Metal HUD

From the research on a steady 30 fps (docs/improve.md): what iOS gives the game cannot be judged from fps and the heat
level alone.

- **Power** (game.mm, every 5 s): "power: CPU N s, P% of it on the performance cores, W watts, M moves between the kinds
  of cores", from TASK_POWER_INFO_V2 (total_user + total_system and task_ptime are in mach time units: on the Mac 10.85
  million of them were rusage's 0.452 s at 125/3 ns each; task_energy in nJ), and "Low Power Mode on" when it is.
- **Heat:** each change of the thermal state and of Low Power Mode is logged when it happens (NSProcessInfo's
  notifications), and the session's first line names the cores (hw.perflevel0/1.logicalcpu), the heat and Low Power
  Mode.
- **In-session SPU translation (D-236) now runs at "serious" heat**, stopping only at "critical": run 327 was serious from
  start to end, the programs met in play stayed in the interpreter all session (844 million SPU instructions), and the
  interpreter's load kept the phone hot. It already runs on one core at utility QoS.
- **Metal's performance HUD:** MetalHUDEnabled in Info.plist, hidden on the game's layer unless PSPOCKET_HUD is set
  (Documents/pspocket-env.txt): then it shows and logs a "metal-HUD" line a second (present intervals, frame misses)
  through developerHUDProperties (mode and logging "default", Apple tech talk 110339).

## D-971 · 2026-10-14 · The game's vblanks on the screen's refreshes; frames held 1/30 s at 30 fps

The GCM interrupt thread counted vblanks on a free-running 1/59.94 s timer (RPCS3's period). Against a 60 Hz screen
(16.667 ms) it drifts 16 us a vblank, so a game flipping at every second vblank had a frame held a refresh longer about
every 8 to 17 s (60 or 120 Hz refreshes): a hitch even at full speed. And the RSX thread presented each frame as it
came, so one the GPU finished a little late showed a refresh late while the next was on time.

- hle::display_vsync(at, period) takes the screen's refreshes from the platform; the interrupt thread's next vblank is
  the refresh nearest its nominal time (hle::next_vblank), never within half a period of the previous one, and the
  59.94 Hz timer while no refresh was reported in 100 ms (pspocket-boot on the Mac, a stopped display link).
- iOS: a CADisplayLink at 60 Hz on the main run loop reports each refresh (its CACurrentMediaTime times placed in
  steady_clock time by how long ago they were). PSPOCKET_NO_DISPLAY_CLOCK: the timer as before.
- Present: a moving average of the time between flips; above 30 ms (below 24 ms to leave) each frame is presented with
  presentDrawable:afterMinimumDuration: 1/30 s, a 60 fps game never. PSPOCKET_NO_PACING: off. The 5-s "present" line
  gives the flips' pace, the frames held and the time the RSX thread waited for drawables (to decide whether the
  drawable needs to come off the RSX thread).
- Test (tests/hle/test_gcm_sys.cpp, "D-971"): no reports, the nominal time; a 60 Hz screen, 600 vblanks one refresh
  apart each and on the grid; a 120 Hz screen, every second refresh; a late vblank's next is the refresh after; reports
  over 100 ms old unused.

## D-972 · 2026-10-14 · The SPU runtime's overheads around the translated code (channels, SPURS selection, the tracker)

The research on a steady 30 fps (docs/improve.md; Mac profiles 204 and 206 of GTA V's walk) put about a quarter of the
SPU threads' busy time outside the translated code. The parts done here, each safe without a re-lift:

- **Channels.** ps_spu_wrch and ps_spu_rdch saved 10 and 12 registers before their switch, also for the channels that
  take no lock (a DMA's parameters: lifted code makes six wrch calls a DMA). The locked channels are now out of line
  (wrch_locked, rdch_locked) and the errors cold: wrch's fast path saves only fp and lr, rdch's six registers (its
  decrementer read). The tag mask and tag update writes, the tag and atomic status reads and their counts take no lock
  any more: mfc_command already updates that state without it, on the SPU's own thread, and no other thread reads it.
- **SPURS selection** (select1, select2): "changed" was set whenever a workload was picked, so a worker picking its own
  workload again (GTA V's job chains, over and over) stored the line anyway: a new version, every parked worker woken
  (a bucket mutex and notify_all) and others' read-modify-writes failed. Now only bytes that change count (the
  workload's signal bit when set, the workload flag when not already 0xFFFFFFFF, the contention). The kernel context
  takes the line the selection ended with instead of reading it again (a DMB and two 128-byte reads a dispatch).
- **The module tracker:** lifted_outside tests 32 code words at a time (any_bit; 200,000 random cases against the word
  by word test, no difference); save_module_runs finds each stretch with run_end's NEON scan. A copy over lines of a
  module that hold none of its program's code (its data, D-085) leaves the module identified for the lines it still
  holds, instead of hashing, comparing and scanning it again at its next run (run 142: about 700,000 identifications a
  walk); a copy over any of its code still drops it.
- Small: ps_res_store_line copies the caller's 256 bytes before taking the line's lock; GETLLAR tests whether the old
  reservation was lost before taking the context lock (the event alone needs it); the job chain's clock and its pauses
  use ps_host_now_ns and ps_host_sleep_ns.
- PUT notifications (part 2): watch() also sets a bit for the line's 64 KB granule of guest memory, and
  ps_res_notify_write, after its fence, skips a PUT whose granules hold no watched line (GTA V's RSX commands and
  vertex data, most PUTs) instead of hashing each of its 128-byte lines (a 4.5 KB PUT: 36). The same Dekker pairing as
  D-243 (the reader sets both bits before its fence). Test: a write from an unwatched granule into a watched one bumps
  the watched line.
- Not done (too small or too risky for what they give): DMA lists in one pass (a PUT list needs its per-element
  release fences for the MFC's order), inline small copies (memmove is mostly the bytes).
- Tests: tests/spu, test_reservation, test_lv2 and test_hle's SPURS and SPU program cases pass; "a module with data
  copied over its tail" now also checks that data over its tail does not identify it again (fails before the change).
- Measured on the Mac (GTA V's prologue walk, 128 s; the Mac loaded by three agents' builds, load 30 to 50, so the
  builds alternated: before, after, before, after, then after, before): frames drawn in the 128 s 3,278 / 3,149 / 2,506
  before, 3,681 / 3,653 / 3,451 after (+12 to +38%). Before, the busy half of the walk fell to 7 to 24 fps (10 to 16 in
  the last pair); after, it held 22 to 30. CPU of the main SPURS instance's threads per frame hardly moved (42 to 47 ms
  either way): the time went to waiting (the wake-ups and failed read-modify-writes of the stores that changed nothing),
  which a loaded machine, like the phone's six busy cores, pays most.

## D-973 · 2026-10-14 · PSPOCKET_SPU_QOS_SERIAL: a workload of one SPU at a time on a QoS class of its own

GTA V's GraphicsMain runs on one SPU at a time (maximum contention 1): about 30 ms of each 33 ms frame on one thread
(run 327's budget), the frame's critical path, wherever iOS puts that thread. D-950 found every worker at interactive no
better (the two performance cores full either way); the research's suggestion is to give the performance cores to the
serial stages only.

- The selection notes whether the workload it picked has a maximum contention of 1 (Selection::serial). With
  PSPOCKET_SPU_QOS_SERIAL=interactive (or initiated, default, utility), a worker running such a workload switches its
  thread to that class, and back to its own when it runs another (one pthread_set_qos_class_self_np a change, none
  while it stays). It applies to the sound mixer's instance too, whose workloads are of one SPU. Unset: as before.
- With PSPOCKET_SPU_AB=S it applies in the A half only, so one session measures it on and off every S seconds in the
  same scenes and heat (each SPURS time line names its half).
## D-965 · 2026-10-14 · Native replacements of known SPU middleware builds: derived programs, the contract, capture and check

The plan for a steady 30 fps on the phone (docs/improve.md) puts Sony's EDGE geometry, as GTA V's geometry job runs it,
at 85 ms of CPU a frame in busy scenes, six of its functions 84% of the job. Plan section 6's middleware replacement,
first part: the machinery, and the first function native (runtime/spu/replace/, pspocket/spu/replace.hpp).

- A known build is data: a program key (ps_spu_hash64 of the image as lifted), its code range, and the functions listed
  for replacement — entry, native implementation (or none yet), the registers their callers still read. No title
  check: EDGE is linked by many games, each its own build and key.
- When such a program is registered, ps_spu_register_program registers before it a derived program: a copy whose
  listed entries go to a dispatcher, which runs the native implementation, or the lifted function when the native one
  declines the inputs (it returns 0 having changed nothing) or is switched off. ps_spu_find_program returns the first
  program of a key, so jobs take the derived one; unregistering the original takes it out too. Every path that adds
  programs (built in, a game library, the session translator) goes through the registration.
- The contract (agreed with the main session, after a first plan of every register exact): a native implementation
  leaves every byte of local store, the pc, the stop and channel state, $0, $1 and the callee-saved $80-$127 exactly as
  the lifted function does, and of $2-$79 the ones its callers still read after it (D-967 finds them; the return value
  $3 where there is one). The other volatile registers are unspecified. Reproducing them would mean transcribing the
  compiled loops instruction by instruction — the job's software-pipelined loops leave temporaries of loads past the end
  of their arrays — which is derived code (CLAUDE.md rule 1) and gives up the native layout. A native implementation is
  an implementation of what the function computes, each float operation the SPU's in the SPU's order (the lifted
  code's own helpers, pspocket/spu/lifted.h, or NEON blocks checked against them), vectors laid out as the data is.
- Switches: PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE=0 (no derived programs), =ab (native in half A of PSPOCKET_SPU_AB's period, D-950's
  halves, so one walk's SPURS time lines compare both), PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE_ONLY=ADDR,... (some functions only),
  PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE_SCRAMBLE=1 (after each call the registers outside the contract hold garbage: the check of D-967's
  finding on the walk).
- Capture: PSPOCKET_SPU_CAPTURE=KEY:ADDR,... records the state at entry and at exit (registers, channels, all of local
  store, the lines that changed) of the lifted function, every PSPOCKET_SPU_CAPTURE_EVERY-th call, into inventory/
  (game data). spu-native-check replays each capture through the lifted function (it must give the captured exit: the
  replay is faithful) and through the native one (bit for bit on the contract; a decline must change nothing), and
  --time N gives each the fastest of N runs a capture (the Mac is shared: the fastest run is the one not preempted).
- PSPOCKET_SPU_TRACE_ENTRIES=KEY records every (entry, link register) pair the program's entries were entered with:
  the targets of its calls through registers, for D-967.
- First native function, 0x0ECF8 of GTA V's EDGE build (spu_dad457863220b1cc): the vertex-output callback of the
  culling stage. Every batch of the walk takes its screen-space path (format byte not 3): positions times the
  combined matrix, 1/w by the SPU's estimate and one Newton step, the viewport, integer coordinates packed with a w > 0
  flag, outcodes against the scissor rectangle and depth range, 16 bytes a vertex. Natively: one vertex a lane
  (vld4/vst4 over the big-endian buffers), two groups of four at a time, a zero matrix element's fma left out (an fma
  with a zero factor is its addend), fcgt as integer keys. 400 captured calls of a walk (every 1000th, the whole
  walk): 400 exact, none declined; the fastest run a call 3.0 µs lifted, 2.0 native (x1.48) on the shared Mac. The
  lifted loop was already tight (about 290 host instructions for the job's 82); the SPU float model's zero and
  saturation rules cost the same in either. A walk with it in half A (517,094 native calls): RSX failures 0, SPU code
  interpreted 0.
- Tests (tests/spu/test_spu_replace.cpp): the NEON blocks against the lifted helpers (frest and frsqest over every
  index and exponent, fm, fma, fcgt keys over every float class); a synthetic program and build: derived, native,
  declined, the original untouched, unregistered together.
- Fixed (2026-10-15): the scramble check took a lifted function as returned when its pc was the $0 it was entered
  with. With loop regions listed, a function's lifted code leaves for another listed address, and $0, garbage after an
  earlier native call (outside the regions' contracts: spu-live, nothing reads it there), matched that address by
  chance about once a walk: all of $2-$79 went to garbage in the middle of 0x07A38 and the walk stopped. Leaving for a
  listed address of the program is never a return now. PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE_SCRAMBLE=ADDR,... scrambles after those
  functions only, which found it.

## D-966 · 2026-10-14 · The lifter calls a function listed for a native replacement through the program's table

Three of the six EDGE functions GTA V's geometry job spends its time in (0x07A38, 0x0F008, 0x0A098) are entered only by
the get-pc idiom (brsl $x, next) from functions the job calls directly: the lifted code calls them as C functions,
past any table, so a derived program (D-965) could not take them over. lift() now leaves out of the call targets the
functions pspocket::spu::replace::listed() names for the program (its key and code start): a call into one leaves for
the run loop, which calls it through the program's table and comes back at the return address, as for any target the
lifter has no symbol for. One predicate at the one place the call targets are chosen; nothing else in the lifter moves.
GTA V's EDGE program lifted again: its code differs from before at those three calls only. It takes effect when the
game's SPU programs are lifted again (scripts/lift-spu.sh, or the phone's translation). Test: a synthetic program's
direct call becomes a way out to the listed function once its build is known.

Extended the same day (agreed with the main session): most of the remaining time is in single loops inside large
functions (0x07A38: one loop 78% of its instructions, three 95%), so a loop's head and exit can be listed too. The
listed addresses are the lift's boundaries (LiftOptions::boundaries, filled from the table): a call into one, a forward
jump or a fall-through into one leaves for the run loop; a back edge to one stays a local jump, so a loop whose native
code declines or is switched off runs as before once entered. The predicate is one call at each place a call target,
a local jump or a fall-through is emitted. All 150 of GTA V's SPU programs lifted again with it: the generated code of
the 149 not in the table is byte for byte what it was. Test: a synthetic loop with its head and exit as boundaries
leaves where it falls into either and keeps its back edge local.

Fixed the same day: a boundary reached only by falling into it (0x0B778's decode loop: its head follows the code that
sets it up, its exit follows the loop's last branch) starts no block, so it was no label and no entry of the program:
the lifted code left there for the run loop, which had nothing to go on with. lift() now makes each boundary inside a
function a label of it (an entry in the program's table, a case of the function's switch). A program without listed
addresses is lifted from the analysis as before: all 150 of GTA V's SPU programs lifted again, the 149 not in the
table byte for byte as they were. Test: the synthetic loop's exit, no label of its own, is a label and an entry once
it is a boundary.

## D-967 · 2026-10-14 · spu-live: what a program may still read after a function returns, and the proof for EDGE

D-965's contract leaves the volatile registers a replaced function's callers never read again unspecified; which those
are must be shown, not assumed (EDGE's internal functions need not follow the SPU ABI). The lifter's per-function
analysis cannot say: it counts every register a way out stores as live. recomp/spu/liveness.cpp and the spu-live tool:
interprocedural liveness over the whole program, from an address on, to the end of the program's run.

- Each frame (an entry called with $lr: a brsl $lr target, an indirect call's target, the program's entry) is summarised
  by what it may read before writing and what it writes on every path to its returns; a call uses the summary, a return
  goes on at every return site of its frames (the program's entry returns out: for a job, nothing is read after, the
  SPURS kernel resets the registers). The get-pc idiom is not a call. Code the analyzer did not lift (behind an indirect
  jump) is followed too.
- Where it cannot know it says so: an indirect jump with no known target, a stop, an absolute branch make every
  register live there. Options feed what it cannot see: --jump (a jump table's targets: GTA V's EDGE tables are
  table-relative words after an ila of their base, read from the image by a script in inventory/), --call (an indirect
  call's targets: from PSPOCKET_SPU_TRACE_ENTRIES, D-965), --tail (a jump into another function through a pointer),
  --abi-unknown-calls (an indirect call no run made goes to an ABI callback: it reads the link, the stack pointer, the
  callee-saved registers and the arguments its caller wrote, rather than to any fragment of the program), --variadic (a
  printf to the PPU that saves $4-$19 reads only the arguments written). --why prints a path to each read.
- GTA V's EDGE job (spu_dad457863220b1cc), with its 8 jump tables, the walk's one indirect call target (0x0F0A4 to
  0x0ECF8), its assertion printf (0x12200) as variadic and 8 indirect calls no walk made as ABI callbacks: after
  0x07A38 (returns to 0x11658), 0x0A098 (0x0A8F8) and 0x0ECF8 (0x0F0A8) no register of $2-$79 is read again; after
  0x0F008 (0x11A18) $3, its result; after the decompression fragments 0x0AC10, 0x0AC20 and 0x0B778 (they go on to the
  next fragment of the table at 0x0C1B8, or to 0x0AC10) the 26 registers of the state the fragments share. These sets are
  the functions' live registers in the table of known builds. Without the variadic printf, its saves made $12-$19 live
  after 0x07A38 and 0x0A098 (only on an assertion's path).
- Tests: a call and return (what the callee reads, kills, and what is live after it), a variadic callee.

## D-968 · 2026-10-14 · EDGE's culling stage (0x0F008) native, and the native functions of GTA V's EDGE build

D-965's machinery took 0x0ECF8 first. The functions of GTA V's EDGE build (spu_dad457863220b1cc) native so far, each
checked by spu-native-check on 400 calls captured over a whole walk (every 1000th call) and timed there (the fastest of
7 runs a capture, callees native as in the game; the Mac shared with other work):

| Function | What | Exact | Lifted | Native | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0ECF8 | vertex output: screen-space transform, outcodes | 400 of 400 | 2.85 µs | 1.93 µs | x1.47 |
| 0x0F008 | culling stage (with the callback above) | 400 of 400 | 5.55 µs | 3.62 µs | x1.53 (its own part x2.1) |
| loop 0x080F8 of 0x07A38 | four-bone skinning, two vertices an iteration | 398 of 400 (2 declined) | 2.54 µs | 0.95 µs | x2.68 |
| loop 0x0B850 of 0x0B778 | fixed-point attributes to floats, four streams | 3000 of 3000 | 1.40 µs | 0.40 µs | x3.50 |
| 0x0A720 of 0x0A098 (to 0x0A894) | index decompression, four triangles a control halfword | 3000 of 3000 | 0.80 µs | 0.29 µs | x2.76 |
| 0x0A56C of 0x0A098 (to 0x0A720) | the control halfwords made from a bit stream | 3000 of 3000 | 0.55 µs | 0.22 µs | x2.50 |
| 0x07EF4 of 0x07A38 (to 0x082E8) | one-bone skinning, two vertices an iteration | 3000 of 3000 | 0.62 µs | 0.42 µs | x1.47 |
| 0x084AC of 0x07A38 (to 0x088F8) | normals and tangents through the skinning rows | 2607 of 2607 | 0.40 µs | 0.22 µs | x1.79 |

A larger capture of the walk for each (every 300th to 1000th call, up to 3000, so the whole walk's scenes): 0x0ECF8
2764 of 2764 exact, 0x0F008 2764 of 2764, loop 0x080F8 2988 of 3000 (12 declined to the lifted code: exact),
loop 0x0B850 3000 of 3000 (its row above is that capture, the fastest of 5 runs). In the game (the walk with
PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE=ab, 10 s halves, the dispatcher's host time a call, contention and all): 0x0ECF8 5.57 -> 3.66 µs,
0x0F008 12.4 -> 7.0 µs (with its callback), loop 0x080F8 4.30 -> 1.95 µs.

- 0x0F008, the culling stage: it calls the vertex-output callback through the table (native or lifted; a callback that
  stops before returning leaves the rest to the lifted code, which resumes at its return address), then culls four
  triangles at a time: facing by the sign of the screen-space cross product (the winding flag of ctx byte 6, the mode),
  behind the near plane or w <= 0, an outcode bit all three vertices share (combined by the mode's fnms, as the job
  does), and, when the context enables it, no pixel covered (equal integer x or y, or equal x + y or x - y). The kept
  triangles' indices are packed back over the index buffer through the job's own tables of shuffles and byte shifts,
  read from its image as it reads them, with the same three quadword stores a group (the job's pipeline writes garbage
  past the end of what it keeps, and the last two stores go to a stack scratch pair near the buffer's end: all of it is
  in local store, so all of it is reproduced). The job's loop overlaps three groups; here each group's index loads,
  stores and vertex loads keep the job's order relative to the others (the output is written over the input), and a
  group's tests are four triangles a vector. The "no pixel" test is off in 77% of the captured calls: its six cflts are
  then left out (exact: its result is masked off).
- Loop 0x080F8 of 0x07A38 (78% of that function's instructions; head and exit listed, D-966): four-bone matrix-palette
  skinning of positions, the blended rows kept on the stack for the normals. Natively: the rows of the bones a call
  names are read once into host order with their "not a zero" lanes, the 255 weights fm(cuflt(b), 1/255) made once per
  thread, a zero weight's fma left out (its addend), the rest as the job does it (fm, then fma by bone, the position
  through the rows). Its contract is the live set at the exit (spu-live: of what it writes, only the output pointer
  $86 is read again). It declines when an output it writes overlaps what it reads (the job reads a pair ahead; 2 of
  400 captured calls).
- Loop 0x0B850 of the decompression fragment 0x0B778 (97% of the fragment's instructions; head and exit listed, both
  reached by falling into them, D-966): four streams of fixed-point attributes (at most 23 bits a component; wider
  ones take another path the fragment's own code chooses) to floats, a block of vertices at a time: each stream's 32
  bytes around its pointer through a byte pattern the code before the loop makes (plus the pointer's offset in its
  quadword), shifted, an exponent put in, a bias subtracted (fs). Natively the pattern is one table lookup on the two
  quadwords as local store has them, made for the 16 offsets once (kept while the pattern registers are the same),
  then ushl, bsl and the fsub fs is. The job's loop stores a vertex's values one iteration late (after zeros to a
  scratch quadword); the native loop stores them right after their reads, which keeps local store's order of reads
  and writes, so it is exact even where outputs overlap inputs. It declines when a block's loop would not end within
  2^20 iterations (its step not positive, or the position wrapping). Nothing it writes is read after the exit
  (spu-live), so its contract is local store and the pc.
- The rest of 0x07A38's time, two regions from a head reached by falling into it to the code after them (D-966):
  0x07EF4, the one-bone path beside the four-bone loop (a vertex's three rows by its bone byte, kept on the stack with
  the w lanes masked, the position through them plus their last words: fma by row, as the job does it), and 0x084AC,
  the normals (mode 1) or normals and tangents (mode 2) through the rows either path left on the stack, four vertices
  an iteration (mode 3, another path, declined; never in the walk). Both keep the job's order of reads and writes
  (it reads the next pair or four before it stores), and leave what the job reads after them: the pointers advanced
  and, after 0x07EF4, $72.
- 0x0A720 of 0x0A098, the index decompression's main format (53% of 0x0A098's instructions in one loop; its head is
  where the loop's setup starts, reached by falling into it): each control halfword's four nibbles pick shuffle
  controls from two 16-entry tables in the job's data (A: which of the last triangle's and the stream's indices make a
  triangle, B: how the stream's new indices move up), ten shuffles a halfword over the stream's next 48 bytes and the
  last triangle carried, three quadwords out; the stream moves on by 16 bytes plus 4 for each pair of set bits. The
  job's loop is a stage deep (each iteration stores the halfword before's triangles, its first one a triple the second
  overwrites): kept as it is, with the job's order of reads and writes. Natively the vectors stay in local store's byte
  order, where a shufb is one table lookup (psn_shufb_b, psn_shufb_key_b: tested against psl_shufb), and the tables
  are made lookups once a call; it declines when an output could reach them.
- 0x0A56C of 0x0A098, the stage before (34% of its instructions): 16 indices per halfword of a bit stream, a set bit
  taking the next literal index of the stream and a clear one the next of a running sequence; the shuffle controls
  from prefix counts of set and clear bits by byte (cntb of masked copies) chosen by fsmb, then the literals left moved
  after the halfwords. Both pipelines (a stage deep) and their order of reads and writes kept; the job's word and
  halfword adds on byte-order vectors through byte-swapped lanes. With 0x0A720 it leaves only 0x0A098's setup and two
  short loops lifted.
- Tried and dropped: 0x0AC10, a decompression fragment, from its entry to where its blocks are done (0x0BF60): unit
  normals from two stored components, the third as sqrt(1 - a^2 - b^2) by fm, fa, fs, frsqest, fi and fm, put in
  place by a shuffle from a table the streams index. Exact on all 2639 captured entries, but x1.04 to x1.19 on them and
  nothing in the game (A/B walk: 4.43 µs native, 4.44 µs lifted a call): half its time is the SPU float model's
  operations on every lane (frsqest, fi, the clamps), as many natively as in the lifted code, and which lanes matter
  depends on the table's shuffles. Not listed as native: the fragment stays lifted.

## D-953 · 2026-10-14 · The RSX thread's CPU a draw measured in one session; its lookups by index and hash

The plan for a steady 30 fps (docs/improve.md): on the iPhone 18 Pro Max the RSX thread (the FIFO reader and the Metal
encoding) costs 12.2 us a draw, some 2,700 draws a frame, a whole core at 30 fps. D-953 to D-957 cut what it does a
draw; this one gives the measure and the lookups.

- Measuring: PSPOCKET_RSX_CPU_AB=N[:MASK] switches the RSX thread's fast paths off in every other run of N frames and
  logs every 20N frames its CPU time a draw in each half ("RSX CPU A/B"), with the program lookups' counts. Unlike
  PSPOCKET_GPU_AB the GPU-side experiments (D-945's merging, D-947's cache) stay on in both halves. MASK picks the
  items: 1 the lookups (this), 4 the encoder setters (D-954), 8 the kept lists and pooled copies (D-956), 16 the index
  scan (D-957), 32 the FIFO's argument runs (D-955); all by default. Off, a path is the code before. The halves see the
  same scenes, which separate runs on this Mac did not (three agents and the main session building: load average 30 to
  70). Kept as a comparison switch, for the phone too.
- Where the time went (xctrace's Time Profiler on the walk, 10 s; `sample` gives no call graph on macOS 27.0.1): FIFO
  reading 13%, do_draw's own code 10%, the vertex and index copies 7%, Metal's encoder creation 7% and its draw state
  14%, texture binds 5.5%, the fragment program lookup 4.5% (scanning programs written over each other 3.2%), and the
  surface lookups, the pipeline map, the keys (std::format) of program variants not in their lists, malloc.
- Surfaces by address: an index (address to the surfaces there, in the order they were made) beside the list. A
  surface's address is set only when it is made, and it leaves only through remove_surface. find_surface (up to four
  for a texture a draw binds), get_color_surface and get_depth_surface read it instead of scanning 100 to 150 surfaces.
- Pipelines in an unordered_map by a hash of the key, the last one found first (a std::map of the 72-byte key before).
  The shader cache's and the background compiles' results are taken once a draw, at its start (each of the three
  lookups took them).
- Program variants: a fragment program's compiles are keyed by options without the texture kinds of the units it does
  not sample (their stale registers made one program's draws look different; past the list's 8, every such draw built
  its key and looked it up by string). Both programs' variant lists keep the most recently drawn first, 16 of them.
- The fragment program scan (a program found where another was, D-240) reads the end bit, the opcode and the sources'
  register types instead of decoding every instruction. Test: tests/rsx/test_shader.cpp "the program scan agrees with
  the full decode (D-953)" (3,000 random programs: length, hash and constants as the decode finds them).
- The deferred actions' envelope (D-107): what they touch together, widened as they queue, made again as they leave.
  An access outside it is compared with none of them (GTA V keeps some 250 queued, labels behind readbacks; a draw
  makes about ten accesses).
- Tried, not kept: 64 vertex programs decoded kept instead of 16. GTA V decodes 55 to 65 a frame with either (of some
  430 looked up): programs it writes anew, not ones it comes back to.
- Measured: 11.60 to 11.15 us a draw (-3.9%; eight windows, -1.2% to -7.1%); an earlier build without the envelope
  -5.1% (five windows).

## D-954 · 2026-10-14 · A draw's state decoded once; encoder state set only when it changes

- The draw encoder's state is kept as the draws set it (pipeline, depth-stencil state, stencil references, viewport,
  depth clip mode, scissor, cull mode, winding, fill mode, depth bias, blend colour, the three vertex buffers, the
  fragment and vertex textures and samplers, the fragment constants' and parameters' bytes): a setter whose value the
  encoder holds is left out. Forgotten at each new encoder, after encode_clear_quad (which sets its own state on the
  pass's encoder), and for the texture bindings after a draw by the shader interpreter (D-940). The record holds the
  encoder, so no new one can take its address meanwhile.
- The draw's 16 fragment texture units are decoded once, with texture_control of the enabled ones; the units it
  samples and their samplers use them (each sampled unit was decoded twice more). Vertex units once, when its program
  samples them. The depth-stencil, blend, colour mask, surface and shader program registers once a draw.
- Tried, not kept: the texture units decoded only after one of their registers took a new value (a table from register
  to unit in the FIFO's dispatch): +0.5% (four windows, -0.3% to +1.2%). And the vertex parameters (864 bytes a range)
  bound by offset from the transient memory instead of set as bytes: the setters with it -4.4% (ten windows), without
  -4.9% (five).
- Measured, the setters: 13.53 to 12.87 us a draw (-4.9%; five windows, -2.3% to -10.6%).

## D-955 · 2026-10-14 · The FIFO reads a packet's arguments a run at a time; the get register published lazily

- Rsx::read_arguments takes a method's arguments as far as put (when ahead), the packet's end, the 1 MB IO page and
  the step's budget allow. Each word is read once, as before (an acquire load, the read history, the desync checks),
  and get_ moves past it, but put and the FIFO's address are looked at once a run and the words counted once. Vertex
  program and constant words (two thirds of GTA V's 214 a draw) go to their handlers straight (inline,
  methods_upload.hpp), unless a constant splits a draw (D-260). A FIFO reset set while a method's handler ran ends the
  run, as it ended the batch after any word (D-123).
- The get register reaches the guest before every method whose effect it can see or that blocks (any handler but the
  uploads, vertex data, draw ranges and dirty bits; the semaphore acquire), where the reader stops (idle, blocked, out
  of budget), at jumps, calls and returns, and at least every 1 KB of commands between, no longer after every word: a
  guest polling get took the cache line from the reader at each one, and the next word's acquire load waited for the
  release store. Labels, semaphores, flips and references see get as before. Test: tests/rsx/test_fifo.cpp "the get
  register reaches the guest before a method it can see, after a long upload (D-955)".
- D-229 and D-277 tried runs of words and measured no change, GTA V's RSX thread in separate runs (1.70 to 1.71 and

## D-956 · 2026-10-14 · No heap allocation a draw; target copies into pooled textures

- A draw's working lists (ranges, index offsets, restart positions, the indices Metal runs, the vertex copies and their
  spans, the fragment constants, a converted range's index list) are kept from draw to draw and cleared; the restart
  positions of all its ranges in one list. convert_primitive and restart_list append to the kept list.
- The feedback report (D-947) keys its sources by numbers (fragment program, unit, the target's address, size and
  format) and names them when it logs; a name was formatted for every copy and every draw that read a kept one.
- Feedback copies (D-148) and corners (D-120) go into a new texture at each change, so the GPU never waits for the draws
  that read the old one; making a texture was some 3% of the RSX thread (six of each a frame in GTA V). The old one now
  waits in a pool until the frame that last used it has run (the frame event), then serves the next copy of its format
  and size; one not taken within 8 frames goes, and the pool goes at a memory trim. The 300-frame report counts the
  copies made into pooled textures.
- Measured: 12.27 to 11.70 us a draw (-4.7%; ten windows, +0.4% to -7.5%); the lists alone -2.4% (six windows).

## D-957 · 2026-10-14 · The index scan in NEON

- An indexed draw's indices are scanned (the vertices they reach, where the restart indices are, whether one is all
  ones) in NEON (pspocket/rsx/index_scan.hpp): blocks of 32 16-bit indices (16 32-bit), one look for the restart index a
  block, which is then scanned one index at a time in order (positions ascending, as before); 16-bit indices whose base
  keeps them below 2^20 are compared in their own lanes. An index of all ones is the largest: the largest seen tells
  it.

## D-974 · 2026-10-15 · Sony's MP3 decoder module (flashMP3.pic) native; regions a native function may leave equivalent

The plan for a steady 30 fps (docs/improve.md) puts MP3 decoding at 20 to 58% of GTA V's sound mixer (SPURS 0x10016000,
"Secondary", one SPU): its decode jobs (bb12970d, d07a95df: "Mp3SpuDecode") load Sony's MP3 decoder module,
dev_flash/sys/external/flashMP3.pic from file offset 0x100 (program 884ae88f68a9e778 at LS 0x17400: every MultiStream
game loads this build, so it is a table entry, not a title check), and tail-call its decodeFrame through a register
(no lift needed for the table to take the call). runtime/spu/replace/flashmp3.c decodes as the module does.

- **What the module is.** Michael Hipp's mpglib layer III (its symbols: layer3.c, decoder.c, III_get_side_info,
  III_dehuffman, III_hybrid, synth_filterbank, DescreteCosineTransform36/12/64), its state kept by the caller:
  decodeFrame($3 frame, $4 &consumed, $5 &pcm_bytes, $6 heap of 22528 bytes, $7/$8 oldBlock (mpglib's hybrid_block,
  576 floats a channel), $9/$10 buffs (synth_buffs, 2 x 272 floats), $11 backup (the last 512 bytes of the frame
  before: the reservoir), $12 &bufferLoc (synth_bo)) returns the PCM's address (heap + 2304: 16-bit samples held to
  +-32767 and truncated, channel 0 then channel 1 at +4096, planar). The heap holds the bitstream buffer, the PCM, the
  granule's spectra, the hybrid filter's output and its last new block. An ID3v2 tag or an ID3v1 "TAG" is skipped
  (0, no PCM), a Xing/Info frame gives -1 PCM bytes, a broken header prints to the PPU and returns -1.
- **Its own deviations from mpglib**, found against the module itself on the interpreter (below) and on the game's
  calls: long band 21 is silent (decoded, its lines zero); the 24 kHz table has band 18 at 330 (mpg123's), not 332;
  MPEG-2's scale factor partitions are indexed in bytes rather than rows of four (so partitions past the first read
  overlapping rows), with three zeros after them whatever the block type; mixed blocks have eight long bands at every
  rate (MPEG-2's run 18 lines past a channel's 576, into the next channel's spectrum); region 1 starts at 36 lines for
  MPEG-1 and MPEG-2's short and mixed blocks, 54 for MPEG-2's others, and at long band 6 (short) or 8 (otherwise) for
  MPEG-2.5; short blocks are antialiased at subbands 0 and 1 when the tenth word of the granule's information is not
  zero, a word nothing writes (decodePacket's stack decides: read from local store as the module would); scale
  factors past those a granule reads come from its stack too; dct36 leaves its input as it was; intensity stereo is
  refused (printed). The native code declines (the lifted module runs) what prints or what it does not model: broken
  headers, intensity stereo, reserved rates, layers I and II headers, malformed side information, reads past the
  bitstream buffer, gains past the table.
- **How it differs from the module: equivalent, not bit-exact.** The bar for audio: the PCM within one step, the float
  state within 1e-4 of each region's largest magnitude (both far inside: below). The float order is the host's, in the
  SPU FP environment (round toward zero) the dispatcher runs it in; the window is summed four lanes at a time in NEON.
  The D-965 contract gains **regions** (pspocket/spu/replace.hpp `Region`, `KnownFunction::regions`): f32 and s16
  regions with a tolerance, compared numerically by spu-native-check, and dead regions with the reason in the table;
  everything else stays bit for bit. For the module: the PCM (s16), the four state buffers and the heap's float
  scratch (f32); dead: the padding of its variables (each has a quadword; the bytes past its size by the module's
  symbol table belong to no variable; the job reloads the image before calls anyway: the captured calls find the
  file's bytes there), its rval (stored 101 times, never loaded, its address never taken) and the stack below the
  caller's stack pointer. Everything the module writes in its own variables (init_layer3's tables of pointers, the
  frame header, the timers, the bit position) and the link register in the caller's frame is written as it writes it.
- **The registers its callers read** (D-967's spu-live): the module reads $3-$12 at its entry and nothing else
  volatile; after it returns into either decode job (bb12970d at 0x074A4 and 0x07944, d07a95df at 0x06DD4 and
  0x07274, with the wrapper's tail call at 0x04F3C declared and indirect calls as ABI callbacks) the jobs read $3 and
  no other volatile register but $16-$19, which only the wrapper's next tail call into the module could pass as
  arguments, and the module does not read them. So $3 is the contract's (PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE_SCRAMBLE walk below).
- **Captures freeze the decrementer** through the captured call (the module times itself with SPU_RdDec): replays of
  such a function are deterministic; the decrementer runs on afterwards as if the call took no time.
- **Checked:** 1,161 calls captured over two prologue walks (every 10th of the first 6,000, and every 131st of 72,916):
  1,161 equivalent, the largest PCM difference one step, the floats 4.8e-6 of their peak, everything else exact.
  tests/spu/test_flashmp3.cpp (test_spu_mp3): synthetic layer III streams (tests/spu/mp3_writer.hpp: random side
  information of every kind, Huffman coded with every table, the bit reservoir, garbage ancillary bytes; MPEG-1, 2 and
  2.5 at every rate; mono, stereo, dual, joint with M/S; CRC) decoded natively against FFmpeg's decoder (the features
  where the module deviates left out: within 2 steps), tags, Xing frames and declines; and, with the user's firmware
  (PSPOCKET_TEST_DEV_FLASH), against the module itself on the interpreter: 12 streams, each call from the module's
  state within one step and every other byte as the module leaves it, each stream decoded natively from its own state
  within two steps of the module's.
- **Speed:** the captures x7.9 (59.8 us lifted, 7.6 native a call, the fastest of three on the shared Mac); in the
  walk (PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE_TIME, D-976) 126.9 us lifted, 21.3 native a call (x6.0): at about 630 calls a second,
  80 ms of the mixer's SPU time a second becomes 13.
- **Walks:** the gate's prologue walk with both replacements on (90,873 MP3 calls native, 40,130 inflate calls native,
  2 declined): 19 of 19 checks; a PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE_SCRAMBLE walk (every register outside the contracts garbage
  after each call; 82,772 and 39,098 native calls) ran to its timeout with no fault, no RSX failure, no new message.

## D-975 · 2026-10-15 · zlib 1.2.3's inflate natively on its stream in local store (GTA V's inflateServer task)

RAGE streams its packed resources through zlib on the SPUs: the "inflateServer" SPURS task (spu_3ffe1d50f8a58e15 at
0x3000, two "zlibInflater" tasksets of SPURS 0x10015000) carries stock zlib 1.2.3 (its version string and messages,
built without gzip support) and calls inflate(strm, Z_NO_FLUSH) from its main loop for each 4 KB input chunk it DMAs
in, into 8 KB output chunks it DMAs out, raw deflate (windowBits -15), the 32 KB window in local store, the stream
kept across calls (inflateReset between streams: the window stays allocated).

- **Why not the host's zlib:** a host zlib (libz, libcompression) gives the same output bytes but keeps its own state;
  here the state must stay in the program's local store in zlib 1.2.3's layout, because the SPURS task may yield
  between calls and resume on another SPU from a saved local store, and because native and lifted calls must be able to
  interleave and be checked bit for bit. runtime/spu/replace/zinflate.c is zlib 1.2.3's inflate.c, inffast.c and
  inftrees.c (the zlib licence) kept statement for statement over local store: the z_stream and the inflate_state
  (32-bit: every field four bytes; codes four bytes, op, bits, big-endian val) where the program keeps them, its fixed
  tables and message strings by their addresses in the program's image (a build of 1.2.3 is a table entry: these
  addresses), the window, the code tables, lens and work in local store, the bit buffer 32 bits wide as the SPU's
  unsigned long. Declined (the program's inflate runs): a stream with a zlib or gzip wrapper (check values), a state
  whose window is not allocated yet (zalloc is the program's code; only the first call of the program's life, since
  inflateReset keeps the window), buffers that would wrap local store.
- **Listed for a direct call:** the main loop calls inflate with brsl, so the program is lifted again (D-966) for the
  call to go through the table: scripts/lift-spu.sh, or the phone's own translation. Its generated code differs from
  the frozen game library's at that one call; -DPSPOCKET_GAME_SPU_EXTRA links the re-lifted program on the Mac.
- **Registers:** after inflate returns (0x0767C) the task reads $3 and no other volatile register (spu-live, zalloc and
  zfree as ABI callbacks).
- **Dead regions** (D-974's regions): the stack below the caller's stack pointer, and the task's copy routine's scratch
  quadword at 0x9720 (zmemcpy's routine at 0x03110 writes it before reading it: 400 captured calls replayed with it
  scrambled at entry leave everything else as they did).
- **Checked:** 810 calls captured over two prologue walks (the first 400, and every 97th of 39,328): 808 bit for bit
  (outside the dead regions), 2 declined without a change (the first call, windowless). tests/spu/test_zinflate.cpp
  (test_spu_zlib): raw deflate streams from the host's zlib of synthetic data (stored, fixed, dynamic, Huffman only,
  runs, fast), in the task's chunks and in random ones down to a byte: the output is the data, the counters match,
  Z_STREAM_END at the end; corrupt streams stop with Z_DATA_ERROR and the program's message addresses; the declines.
- **Speed:** the captures x6.2 (41.2 us lifted, 6.7 native a call); in the walk 49.3 us lifted, 12.6 native (x3.9).

## D-979 · 2026-10-14 · Native code for a game's own SPU jobs in games/<title>/spu; GTA V's synthesizer biquads native

The plan for a steady 30 fps on the phone (docs/improve.md) puts GTA V's sound mixer (SPURS 0x10016000 "Secondary",
one SPU) at a whole phone core at full sound pace. A Time Profiler window of the walk (30 s, leaf samples mapped to SPU
addresses through the lifted C's line table): MP3 (884ae88f) 24% of Secondary, the submix job (28281614) 22%, the
synthesizer jobs (012bf135, 54e79c9f; RAGE's modular synth, the vehicles) 16% and 14%, a decode job (bb12970d) 15%.
These jobs are Rockstar's, not middleware other games link: their replacements belong in games/gta5 (CLAUDE.md rule 6).

- The hook, as data the game's directory provides: games/<title>/spu/ holds a table (builds.cpp: program key, code
  range, listed functions, natives, live registers) that registers its builds with pspocket::spu::replace::add_build()
  when the program loads, and the native code. No title in the runtime: a build is found by its program key, as EDGE's.
  games/CMakeLists.txt builds them as an OBJECT library linked straight into every tool that registers or lifts SPU
  programs (pspocket-boot, spu-lift, spu-live, spu-check, spu-native-check, pspocket-prepare): objects are always linked,
  so the registrations run (an archive member nobody references would be dropped). The app compiles the same sources
  into its runtime library, which it force-loads (app/ios/project.yml). add_build() before main is safe: the table of
  added builds is constant-initialised.
- Finding the time: interpreter coverage needs captures, and the jobs' top functions DMA; instead xctrace's leaf PCs
  through atos to the lifted C's lines (each follows its SPU instruction's comment). Captures of the candidates
  (spu-native-check --time) then give each function's cost a call, and the walk's call counts its total: 012bf135's
  0x05B20 1.4 s a walk (510,000 calls, 2.7 us), 0x062C8 0.8 s (394,000, 2.0 us), the submix job's 0x0A920 1.6 s (95,000
  calls, 16.9 us), 0x06048 0.4 s; many others are under 1 us a call, where the way through the run loop a listed
  function takes (the caller's exit and reload, the dispatcher) would eat what native code saves.
- 0x062C8, the synthesizer's biquad: one section in transposed direct form II over 256 floats in place (y = fma(b0, x,
  s0); s0 = s1 + fms(b1, x, fm(a1, y)); s1 = fms(b2, x, fm(a2, y))), the state in words 0 and 1 of its quadword. Native:
  one sample at a time, each operation the SPU's in the job's order (fm's and fma's zero factor, fms's clamp), so exact;
  the zero tests become branches the host predicts, and a loop without them (checked at the end, redone exactly when a
  zero met) measured no faster. Callers read $6 after it (spu-live: the synthesizer's program interpreter can store it
  as a module's result): the job leaves the cwd control of the last sample's address there, and so does the native code.
- 0x05B20, two such sections in series: here $6 is the first section's last y, which the job computes on whole
  quadwords, so its other three words are computations of their own (each coefficient register's word k, the state's
  words rotated, the sample's quadword rotated to the sample, outputs already written included). The samples' lane runs
  on its own, scalar, and the four lanes beside it in NEON, fast (an fma with a zero factor as fma(-0, 1, s0), valid as
  no s0 is a denormal: the state is checked, a denormal in it declines; fm's zero test of y checked at the end, the four
  lanes redone exactly when one was a zero). Coupling the samples' lane to the four (one vector) put the store-to-input
  path on the recurrence: 1,707 ns a call instead of 1,204.
- Checked: 150 captured calls of each over a walk (every 97th), all exact; the fastest of 7 runs a call: 0x062C8 2,040 to
  832 ns (x2.45), 0x05B20 2,700 to 1,200 ns (x2.46). Tests (tests/games): an oracle from the lifted code's helpers on
  whole quadwords (tests/games/gta5_audio_oracle.c) against the natives over synthetic buffers at every word alignment,
  counts 0 to 256, relocated, four mixes (audio, zeros, specials: denormals and exponent 255, silence): exact, the only
  declines a state with a denormal. A walk with them in half A of 10 s halves: 404,000 native calls, nothing declined, no
  RSX failure; the Mac was at a load of 30 and Secondary's 5 s windows moved more than the expected 4% (A/B 1.08), so
  the saving stands on the per-call times: about 1.2 s of the walk's lifted 2.2 s in these two.
- Not changed, for the main session: the translator hash (runtime/game) covers the lifters' sources, not the tables of
  listed functions, so a prepared game library from before a table change keeps direct calls into newly listed
  functions (correct, but without the native code) until prepared again; and the dispatcher reads its switches through
  config(), which takes a mutex on every call of a listed function (EDGE's 1.4 million native calls a walk, from up to
  five SPU threads).

## D-980 · 2026-10-14 · GTA V's submix reverb (0x0A920 of spu_28281614459ce75e) native, exact, x2.9

The single costliest function of the mixer's jobs: 1.6 s of a walk (95,000 calls, 16.9 us lifted). RAGE's reverb on
the submix: per frame of two quadwords (four lanes each, "lo" and "hi"), four all-pass sections in series over int16
delay lines, three banks of six delay lines tapped, mixed and fed back (each bank fed the input with the other banks'
taps), and two of the banks' taps each through a filter run four times on the lo tap and four on the hi tap; the
output a chain of fma over bank 1's taps and the filters' states (games/gta5/spu/rage_submix.c says it in full).
Interpreter coverage over 40 captured calls: 52,000 instructions a call, 75% in the banks' section, the software
divisions that wrap the positions under 8%.

- Natively, every operation through the lifted code's own helpers (psl_fma, psl_fm, psl_fs, psl_fa, psl_cflts) on
  quadwords in guest order (the helpers are lane-wise), in the job's order; csflt 140 of an int16 as NEON's fixed-point
  convert (exact: an int16 times 2^-15); the job's division (magnitudes, shift and subtract, the dividend's sign on the
  remainder) as an unsigned remainder. The twelve filters of a frame are independent: they run side by side (the job
  runs them one after another, each a chain of 24 dependent fma), and the outputs' fma chains take their results in
  the job's order. The delay lines are read and written in the job's order.
- Declined, before anything is written: any slot a line will use in any of the call's frames (positions simulated
  ahead) inside the context, the input, the output or the job's shuffle controls, a length 0 (the job halts there), the
  input or output inside the context, a context off a quadword boundary. Nothing in registers is read after it
  (spu-live at its four call sites).
- Checked: 200 captured calls of a walk (every 331st), all exact; 17.9 us lifted, 6.1 us native a call (x2.94). Tests:
  an oracle in the job's order on whole quadwords in register layout (the slot's halves through shufb with the job's
  controls, xshw, csflt; the division as the job's shift-and-subtract loop) against the native code: four mixes,
  0-16 frames, relocated, in place or not, negative positions; a slot inside the context declined. A walk with
  PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE_SCRAMBLE=1 (the registers outside the contracts garbage after each call): 94,484 native calls of
  it, 926,000 of D-979's two, nothing declined, no RSX failure.
- Later the same night: the usual position step (0 <= pos + 1 < len) without a division, each frame's slots kept from
  the check before the call (positions and counters written once, at the end: nothing but the job reads them and no
  slot is in the context), and, when no word of the context is beyond the host's range (then every value stays finite:
  rounding toward zero never overflows), the filters' fs without its clamp and fma's zero tests of a and b made once.
  200 captured calls still exact: 5.05 us a call (x3.3). Running the twelve filters six at a time instead measured
  slower (6.3 us).

## D-981 · 2026-10-14 · The submix job's comb reverb (0x06048) and delay (0x08748) native, exact

Two more of the submix job's (spu_28281614459ce75e) effects, each called about 190,000 times a walk (four submixes):

- 0x06048: a reverb of Freeverb's structure on four lanes: the input times a gain (a quadword of the job's image), eight
  comb filters with damping (a one-pole store per comb) over float delay lines, their outputs summed in order, four
  all-passes in series (0.5 and -1), the output times 3. Natively the combs' stores stay in registers over the call and
  the fm and fma zero tests of the constant operands are made once (neon.h's psn_fm_n and psn_fma_n, which take the
  operands' "not a zero" masks); the positions step by one a frame with no wrap (the caller wraps them), so each line's
  slots over a call are one run of quadwords, checked once against the context, the input and the output. 200 captured
  calls exact; 2.06 us lifted, 0.94 us native (x2.2).
- 0x08748: an echo, one delay line of int16 pairs (the record as 0x0A920's bank lines) with feedback: the slot's halves
  times the gain are the output, and with the input times the feedback written back. 200 captured calls exact; 656 ns
  lifted, 245 ns native (x2.7); 167 ns (x3.9) once the position step skips the division in its usual case (D-980's).
- Tests (tests/games): oracles in the job's order (records read and written each frame) against both over the four
  mixes, frame counts, relocation, in place or not; slots inside the context declined.

## D-982 · 2026-10-14 · The voice job's sample-rate converter loop native (a loop region), exact, x2.1

The mixer's third-largest job by time after MP3 is the voice job (spu_bb12970d56fb7b8a: "PCMSource", "SrcDownsampleBuf",
"Mp3InputBuffer"; 12-15% of Secondary). Its costliest function, 0x07F28 (2.4% of Secondary), converts a voice's int16
samples to the mixer's rate by linear interpolation; its loop (0x08000 to 0x080D8) is nearly all of it. The function's
setup converts the pitch to a 16.48 fixed-point step through two soft-float helpers: it stays lifted, and the loop is
listed as a region (head and exit, D-966): the lifted code leaves at the head, the native loop runs to the exit.

- Four outputs an iteration: the positions are kept twice, as floats (four lanes, a step apart) and as 16.48 fixed
  point; the fixed point's integer part addresses 16 bytes of samples (unaligned), each lane's offset from lane 0 is
  the float positions' integer parts' difference (cflts 171: four bytes a sample), and the job's shuffle controls
  (that offset's low byte in every byte plus 0x00010203 or 0x04050607, word adds, then & 31) pick each lane's two
  neighbours among the eight samples; out = fma(fs(s1, s0), frac, s0). Natively the same values: the integer part by
  the job's masking (|P| < 1 to +0, exponent 158 and up kept), the controls as table lookups over the samples' bytes.
  The registers the loop takes as constants ($13-$18, $87, $88, set by the setup) are checked (else declined); an
  iteration's samples that a later output store would overwrite first are declined too (order dependent).
- Its exact registers: $1, $79 (spu-live at the exit: the epilogue reloads $80-$89 and $126) and the ABI's; $80, the
  float positions, as the loop leaves them.
- Checked: 300 captured entries of a walk (every 997th of 581,000), all exact; 865 ns lifted, 405 ns native (x2.1).
  Test: an oracle lane by lane (the masking in scalar, the samples through csflt, the shuffles byte by byte) over four
  mixes (special positions: zeros, denormals, exponent 255, negative), counts 0 to 256, relocated; a changed constant
  register declined.
- Needs the lifter to make a boundary inside a function an entry of the program (the EDGE agent's ad69fe2, "a boundary
  inside a function is a label and an entry of the program", not yet in main when this was written): without it the
  head is no entry, the derived program leaves the region out with a warning, and the lifted code falling into the
  head is run by the interpreter there (correct, slow). Lift the voice job again once both are in.

## D-983 · 2026-10-15 · The mixer's DSP natives together: what they save, how it was measured, what was left and why

D-979 to D-982 made six of the sound mixer's (SPURS "Secondary") hottest DSP functions native, every one exact
against the translated job on captured calls (150 to 300 each) and on synthetic oracles (tests/games). Together:

| Job | Function | What | Lifted | Native | Calls a 128 s walk | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| synthesizer 012bf135 | 0x05B20 | two biquad sections | 2.72 us | 1.20 us | 519,000 | 0.79 s |
| synthesizer 012bf135 | 0x062C8 | biquad | 2.04 us | 0.83 us | 405,000 | 0.49 s |
| submixes 28281614 | 0x0A920 | reverb (all-passes, 18 int16 lines, 12 filters) | 16.9 us | 5.05 us | 95,000 | 1.13 s |
| submixes 28281614 | 0x06048 | comb and all-pass reverb | 2.03 us | 0.92 us | 190,000 | 0.21 s |
| submixes 28281614 | 0x08748 | delay with feedback | 0.65 us | 0.17 us | 186,000 | 0.09 s |
| voices bb12970d | 0x08000 loop | sample-rate converter | 0.87 us | 0.41 us | 706,000 | 0.32 s |

About 3.0 s of the gate walk's 27.3 s of Secondary time: some 10% of the mixer's CPU, on the phone (where Secondary was
32 ms a frame in run 327's busy windows) about 3 ms a frame. Profiles of the walk (xctrace, leaf PCs mapped through
the lifted C's line table, the MP3 job as the yardstick since nothing of it changed): the three jobs with natives
fell from 2.02 to 1.49 times the MP3 job's time (-26%); the synthesizer job without natives (54e79c9f) moved -9%
between the two profiles, the noise of such a comparison.

- Measuring: PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE=ab with 10 s halves gave Secondary's 5 s windows A/B 0.96 in one 300 s walk with sound
  (load 20-30) and 1.02 in another (load 5 rising to 27): the effect (5-10%) is under the windows' spread on this shared
  Mac. cellAudio's sound lines in the first: 769 periods skipped in half A against 863 in half B, the pace 0.96
  against 0.95; in the second 114 against 82 (both halves keeping pace). The per-call times (spu-native-check --time,
  the fastest of 7 runs) times the walk's call counts are the measure that holds; the phone's own A/B is for a
  session there.
- Exact, not Accelerate: the jobs keep their filters' state in local store in their own forms (transposed direct form
  II, a state variable filter run four times a sample, int16 delay lines with clamped conversions) and every operation
  rounds toward zero with the SPU's zero rules. vDSP's biquads keep direct-form-I histories (no exact mapping from the
  jobs' states) and round to nearest; vDSP_vrampmuladd and the like compute their ramps their own way. Bit-exact NEON
  in the jobs' order came out as fast where measured (a biquad without its zero tests, its result checked after, was no
  faster than with them: the tests become branches the host predicts), so nothing here differs from the translated
  job by even a bit, and spu-native-check's exact comparison stays the check.
- Tried and left: 0x05370 of the synthesizer job 54e79c9f (a voice into four buffers with ramping gains, 2.0 million
  calls a walk) was exact on 300 captured calls but only 291 to 181 ns: a listed function's caller leaves for the run
  loop and is entered again, storing and reloading the registers it uses (115 for that caller, 0x1A450), which costs
  about what native code saves; its one-pole loop (0x1A71C in the same function) is latency-bound in either form and
  leaves 17 temporaries live. The synthesizer's smaller modules (0x09138, 0x0B878, 0x069A8, 0x0C088, 0x097C0, under
  0.1 s a walk each) and the submix job's buffer cache (0x054F0, DMA and an LRU search) were not done.
- Left for the main session: the voice job's loop region (D-982) needs the EDGE track's ad69fe2 in the lifter; the
  three re-lifted jobs (012bf135, 28281614, bb12970d) must be lifted again for the game library (scripts/lift-spu.sh)
  for their listed calls to reach the natives; the translator hash does not cover the tables of listed functions
  (D-979); the dispatcher's config() takes a mutex on every call of a listed function.
- Gates (this clone at 8898662 with ad69fe2's lifter change applied, the three jobs re-lifted ahead of the game
  library): quick PASS (23 suites), spu PASS (150 programs, no difference), game PASS (fps 29.8 median, RSX failures 0;
  checked against the main repository's message baseline: this clone has none of its own).

## D-959 · 2026-10-15 · The MFC's parameter channels written inline; channels that never block start no block

Each of a DMA's parameter writes (MFC_LSA, MFC_EAH, MFC_EAL, MFC_Size, MFC_TagID) and SPU_WrSRR0 was a call of
ps_spu_wrch, a way out and a block start (a label, so a case of the function's dispatch switch), though ps_spu_wrch
only stores a field for them. lower() now stores the field itself (Size capped at 0xFFFF, TagID masked, as
channels.cpp does). rchcnt, MFC_WrTagMask and MFC_WrTagUpdate never block: their call stays (they can raise an SPU
exception, which ends the thread) but they start no block (analyzer.hpp: inline_channel_write, restarts_in_place).

- scripts/lift-spu.sh carried every entry of a program's previous lift over as seeds, which would bring the old block
  starts back as labels reached through registers. It now keeps OUT/NAME/NAME.seeds, the seeds it used, as
  runtime/prepare does (improve.md's open item). For an existing lift the seeds were derived once: the entries the
  lifter makes with only the images' own seeds subtracted from the old entries, plus the old functions' entries (the
  old lifter then makes the same labels; only some code-word bitmaps differ, toward D-205).
- With D-958 over all 150 programs (LLVM 22): 8,024,636 to 7,380,180 host instructions (-8.0%), spills 2,145,002 to
  1,674,897 (-21.9%), runtime calls 26,872 to 17,978; program entries 39,069 to 30,681.
- Measured in one session (D-962): the final lift against it without D-959, 3.6% less SPU time (GraphicsMain -8.9%).

## D-960 · 2026-10-15 · A function called at its entry loads only what it reads before writing

60% of the entry loads (52,227 of 86,743 in GTA V) were never read before written: the live analysis counts each
store of dirty registers as a read, so a register written on one path only was loaded at the entry for the paths
that skip the write. Now (RegFlow::lazy_loads) the entry loads the registers read before written (real liveness), and
a register is loaded on the edge where a path whose local does not hold it joins one whose local does, when the join
needs it: a forward must-analysis of the locals that hold ctx's value, started with everything valid so the loads
settle on the edges into loops; every read and every store of dirty registers is then checked against it, and a
failure would load at the entry (none in GTA V's 150 programs; clang's uninitialised-use errors over all of them
agree).

- Entry loads 86,684 to 34,514 (static); loads on edges 227,339 to 329,993. Host instructions: +0.7% with every
  function one C function (the run loop's resume points merge every register at every label), +0.2% with D-961.
- Measured in one session (D-962): the final lift against it without D-960, 1.8% less SPU time.

## D-961 · 2026-10-15 · Each SPU function a fast C function and a cold twin for the run loop's resumes

Every label of a function was a case of its dispatch switch, so the run loop could resume it anywhere: 83% of the
backward branches had a label inside their loop, and the C compiler saw irreducible cycles (no loop optimizations:
GTA V's EDGE job hoisted 2,347 instructions out of its loops).

- **The fast function** is entered at its entry, and at the few labels the run loop resumes it at that add no second
  way into any cycle of its flow (fast_entries: strongly connected components; candidates are returns of calls that
  may leave for the run loop, the labels after stops and indirect calls, labels reached through registers, the
  native replacements' boundaries; a candidate that would add one is replaced by the header of the outermost loop
  around it, if that adds none). A call that always leaves has no way on to its return, which often breaks the loop
  around it. Such entries load only their live registers.
- **The twin** (N_resume_*.c, `__attribute__((cold))`, built at -O1 by CMake and by prepare: half the compile time)
  holds the function as before, entered at every other label (PSL_RELOAD and a switch), and leaves for the run loop
  at a backward branch to a fast entry, so it runs at most the rest of one round of such a loop. The entry table
  sends those labels to it. spu-lift --whole keeps the old shape.
- First tries: every loop header an entry made the outer loops irreducible again (EDGE: 2,507 hoists; 146,465 fast
  instructions); outermost headers only, 2,783 hoists; the entry alone, 3,588 hoists and 128,413 instructions but the
  twin then ran whole loops: GTA V's EDGE job's main function is resumed 9 times per entry (after the job kernel's
  calls), 21% of the run loop's entries went to twins, and GraphicsMain took twice the time. The chosen entries:
  2,843 hoists.
- Static over all 150 programs (LLVM 22; with D-958, D-959, D-960, D-963 and D-964 in both): 5,477,958 host
  instructions with one C function each, 4,770,792 in the fast functions (-12.9%), spills 1,311,508 to 1,109,264
  (-15.4%); the twins 4,482,941 at -O1. Translation: pspocket-prepare compiles GTA V's 150 SPU programs (with a stand-in PPU
  translation, three threads on the Mac, one after the other) in 121 s against 233 s for the lift before this work
  (-48%); the cost model still predicts the old sizes (the preparation's rates: SPU 0.03 against 0.33), so the phone's
  first time left will be long until its rates learn.
- Measured in one session (D-962): the final lift against it without D-961, 6.5% less SPU time (GraphicsMain -19%).

## D-962 · 2026-10-15 · Two translations of the SPU programs in one session; poll exits that store only live registers (not kept)

The steady-30 plan's SPU translation track (improve.md, item 2) needed before/after numbers for changes worth a few
percent each, on a Mac whose load average swung from 8 to 100 with three agents building: two walks of one build
differed by more than that.

- **The harness.** scripts/spu-ab-lift.sh copies a lift with its symbols renamed (spb_); -DPSPOCKET_GAME_SPU_B=DIR builds
  it into pspocket-boot beside the default lift (-DPSPOCKET_GAME_SPU), each program registering as the B twin of the
  default program with its key (ps_spu_register_program_b, registry.hpp). With PSPOCKET_SPU_AB=S the SPURS workers run
  the twins in every other S seconds (spu::set_translation_b, applied when a program is attached, D-950's halves), and
  each SPURS time line gives the workloads' total and the part run in half B (A = total - B). spu-lift
  --no-replace-boundaries lifts the functions listed for native replacement as any other, so both halves run with
  PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE=0 on equal terms. With 10-second halves the scenes decided (the same two builds, three walks:
  1.20, 0.77, 1.25); with 1-second halves both halves see the same frames, and two walks (34 windows) agree to a few
  percent.
- **All of D-958 to D-964 against the lift before them** (the main checkout's, both with PSPOCKET_SPU_NATIVE=0, three
  walks, 51 windows): the main SPURS instance's SPU time 5.4% less (each walk 5.8%, 6.0%, 4.3%): EDGE/GFX -3.9%,
  dependency_spu -9.3%, GraphicsMain -1.4%, Physics -13.3%; the sound mixer (Secondary) -12.1%. Each part's share is in
  its entry, against the final lift without it. Apple clang builds the Mac's translation; D-964 is the phone's only.
- **Poll exits storing only the live registers (S5), not kept.** At a loop's attention poll only the dirty registers
  live at the header need storing (the others are written again before anything reads them, here or in a caller).
  Statically on GTA V's EDGE job (LLVM 22, entry-only fast functions): 128,413 host instructions with it, 126,862
  without (+1.2%), spills +1.1%: each poll got an exit block of its own. Dropped.
- **Tail calls, not needed.** A jump to another function of the same program never leaves through the run loop in
  GTA V's 150 programs (0 sites): the analyzer traces a branch's target as part of the jumping function.

## D-963 · 2026-10-15 · Small lowerings: shufb on one register, insertion masks from a table, conversions in NEON, the code's own address

- shufb with ra == rb (20,595 of GTA V's 59,299 sites): one TBL over the one register (vqtbl1q with the index masked
  to 0-15), the special controls by TBX as before; the two-register table needs its registers consecutive (moves).
- cbd/chd/cwd/cdd and the x forms (22,233 sites): psl_cmask_t, a load from a 64-entry table by size and the address's
  low bits.
- csflt/cuflt in the approximate model with a scale of 2^-n (n = 155 - i8, 0 to 32; 1,671 sites): SCVTF/UCVTF with n
  fraction bits, which round x / 2^n once toward zero as FPCR says: what the double-precision path's one rounding of
  the exact quotient gave; no result is denormal.
- brsl $rt, .+4 (600 sites: position independent code taking its own address) was a call, and the analyzer started a
  function at the next instruction holding the rest of the caller again. Now a plain write of rt (analyzer: get_pc).
  GTA V's EDGE job: 18,082 lifted instructions to 12,206, 88 functions to 65.
- Static (LLVM 22, all 150 programs, one C function each, with D-958 to D-960): the code-address change 7,428,266 to
  5,908,699 host instructions (-20.5%), spills -22.0%; the other three 5,908,699 to 5,601,900 (-5.2%), vector moves
  193,244 to 174,220. Measured in one session (D-962): the code-address change 5.4% less SPU time, the other three 3.0%.
- The fuzz generator draws shufb with ra == rb in 40% of its cases and brsl .+4 in a quarter; the synthetic program
  takes its own address.
- GTA V's EDGE build lists three such folded functions for native replacement (0x07A38, 0x0A098, 0x0F008, D-968): the
  first gate walk interpreted them ("no lifted code") and the derived program found no entry to take over. lift()
  makes each boundary (D-966) inside a function's code a label of it; test_spu_replace checks a listed function after
  brsl .+4 has a table entry. The gate then passes (29.8 fps median, nothing interpreted).

## D-986 · 2026-10-15 · The compile cost model fitted again for the fast functions and cold twins

D-961's lift compiles in half the time, but estimate_cost still predicted the old shapes: pspocket-prepare's SPU rate
(real seconds per predicted second) fell from 0.33 to 0.03, so a phone that learned its rate on the lift before would
have said ten times the time left at its first preparation after translator generation 4.

- Per-file times of GTA V's 150 programs (pspocket-prepare --events, three at a time on the M4, a stand-in PPU
  translation): the fast functions 171 s against 1,268 predicted, the twins 168 s against 9,032 (one function of many
  labels: lines times labels says nothing of a compile at -O1). Least squares: fast functions 1.45 s a MB plus 0.546
  per million lines times labels, twins 1.84 s a MB; mean error per file 39% and 35%. Scaled by 1 / 0.33 so the rates
  phones learned keep their meaning: 4.39 and 1.65, and 5.57 s a MB for a twin (estimate_cost's `cold`, for
  N_resume_*.c, in the preparation's jobs and the in-session program cost; the "half of it" for twins goes).
- The up-front estimate before anything is translated: 4.6 predicted seconds a MB of SPU C (23 before) and 0.78 MB a
  saved image (0.33; GTA V's 265 images now give 208 MB of C).
- Measured again: rate SPU 0.35 (0.33 for the lift before with the old model, measured alike).
