## D-997 · 2026-10-15 · The sound follows the output iOS chooses: AirPlay mirroring, interruptions, resets

The user's report: screen mirroring the iPhone to a Mac (AirPlay) silenced the game, and it stayed silent after the
mirroring ended. AVAudioEngine stops when its output changes and posts AVAudioEngineConfigurationChangeNotification;
AudioOutput never listened, so the engine stayed stopped for the rest of the session. Calls, Siri, headphones and a
reset of iOS's media services had the same gap.

- AudioOutput (runtime/platform/apple, macOS and iOS): on its engine's configuration change it connects the time-pitch
  unit to the main mixer again (the mixer converts to the new output's format) and starts the engine on what is there
  now, logged "sound out again (...; restart N)". `restart(why, rebuild)` for what the engine is not told of: nothing
  while it runs; `rebuild` makes the engine and its nodes anew (the ring, the volume and the stretcher's setting kept).
  set_stretch takes the same lock, so it never meets a time-pitch unit being replaced.
- The iPhone (game.mm): the audio session's setup in one function (set_up_audio_session); observers for the end of an
  interruption (session active again, restart), route changes (logged with the outputs' names and kinds, restart),
  the media services reset (session set up again, rebuild) and the app becoming active (restart if stopped). The
  session's first line names the route.
- Checked on the Mac (a scratch program against the platform library, volume 0): the engine plays, a rebuild with the
  stretcher on keeps it playing (23,040 frames, then 49,501). A real AirPlay switch is for the phone.
## D-998 · 2026-10-15 · Assassin's Creed's "jump to LS 0" on its first install was a partial dev_flash, not the SPU translation

Run 331 on the Mac (fresh hdd0, the 1.3 GB install, then the Animus garden): at about 235 s SPURS 0x102eb500's task
(spu_2fed95d316ff1968, the game's sound task, "DARE MultiStream") stopped at LS 0x00004 after `bisl $lr,$14` with
$14 = 0, with libraries from today's translator, `spu-lift --whole` and the translator of 381e1e1 alike, and not with
every SPU program interpreted. Found (agent f2):

- **The cause.** The task keeps a decoder function pointer at LS 0x3de80, written once when it loads the ATRAC
  decoder module (command 0xffdd: 32 KB at LS 0x33980, its init at 0x33990 stores 0x37c58 there) and called for each
  stream whose codec byte (stream block + 0x2d0, at LS 0x2f650) is 4, 5 or 6. The PPU sends 0xffdd only after reading
  /dev_flash/sys/external/flashATRAC.pic itself (0x1044500: open, seek, read; nothing read: "Multistream: atrac failed
  to load %d" and no command). The runs passed `--flash inventory/firmware/dev_flash`, the three files taken out of
  the firmware for GTA V (flashMP3.pic, libsre, libspurs_jq), not the installed firmware's whole dev_flash
  (inventory/firmware/installed/dev_flash, which runs 099-323 and docs/handoff.md use): the file was missing in every
  run 331 log ("atrac failed to load -2147418106"), the decoder never loaded, and the first ATRAC stream (codec 5,
  the garden's sound) called LS 0. Traced with the task interpreted (a library without it): the same crash, no
  0xffdd ever in its command slot, the codec byte 5 set by the stream block's GET at 0x08188. With every SPU program
  interpreted the game ran slower and had not reached that stream by 330 s; the installed hdd0's runs were 120 s.
- **With the whole dev_flash** the reproduce run passes the point: the decoder loads at boot (its init interpreted,
  184 instructions), and the reproduce run (fresh hdd0, the install, walk-garden) reaches 330 s with no fatal error, the garden at 58-60 fps; fresh runs of 100 s (four) and the installed hdd0 to 330 s alike.
- **Fail loudly** (CLAUDE.md rule 5): a /dev_flash file a game opens or stats that the host's folder lacks is now an
  error in the log, once per path, naming the folder (sys_fs log_result); the PS3 always has every file there, so a
  game takes it as its own failure and plays on. scripts/boot.sh and scripts/translate-game.sh pass the installed
  firmware's dev_flash when there is one (else the taken-out files, as before).
- Test: tests/hle/test_ac_sysutil_fs_pad.cpp (a dev_flash folder with flashMP3.pic only: flashATRAC.pic's open is
  ENOENT three times, one error naming the folder; flashMP3.pic and a missing /dev_hdd0 file no error).
- Also found while reproducing: runs side by side whose hdd0 folders share a parent share their hdd1 (cellSysCache:
  "hdd1" beside hdd0's folder) and remove each other's cache at the start ("was in use ... removed"); the Mac runs
  for this put each hdd0 in a folder of its own.

The iPhone's Assassin's Creed (fresh hdd0) stopped drawing at its "press START to install" screen (frame 178, every
PPU thread waiting, its sound task busy as usual: run 331's Instruments trace showed that task at its usual 30%,
not a spin). The Mac showed the same thread states, the same log and the same missing call in 2 of 36 fresh runs
side by side, and a crash in the game's thread registry (SIGBUS reading 0x0b0000f8 at 0x70620, in the next thread's
registration) in 5 more, and alone in 1 of 2 runs without the change below and in runs beside a compile. Found
(events, thread creations and exits, queue destructions traced; the game's code read at the addresses given):

- **The freeze (the game's race).** Its main thread runs the save data work on a worker thread object
  ("SaveFileThread", Gear's thread wrapper at 0x763c8): reset the "go" event, Start (0x6e1c0: create the thread only
  if the object's state word +144 is idle, <= 1; otherwise nothing, no error), reset "done", set "go", wait "done"
  (0xd21a08, 10 ms polls). The worker runs cellSaveDataAutoLoad2, sets "done" (sys_event_port_send), and only then
  stores its state idle (0x764a4), takes its node out of the game's thread registry (an AVL tree under an lwmutex,
  0x4f5b0) and exits. Woken by "done", the main thread starts the object again for cellSaveDataAutoSave2: if it gets
  to Start before the worker's store, no thread is made and it waits for "done" forever (no AutoSave2 after AutoLoad2
  in every frozen log, the phone's included).
- **The registry crash (the same race, later).** The main thread destroys the install's copy worker ("HDDCopyFile
  Thread") right after its "done" (its event queues destroyed, traced) while the worker is still taking its node out
  of the registry: the freed node is in the tree, and the next thread to register faults in it.
- On the PS3 the sender keeps running (lv2's scheduler: the receiver, of the same priority 1001, runs after it), and
  its few instructions come long before the main thread's syscalls. Here each PPU thread is a host thread: when the
  host does not run the sender for a moment (another thread takes its core: the phone's six cores, runs side by side
  on the Mac) the receiver wins. A 2 ms sleep after each send (PSPOCKET_LV2_SEND_DELAY_US=2000) makes it show: 2 of 5
  runs froze, 1 crashed in the registry.
- **The fix (lv2, event.cpp), in two parts.** (1) A PPU thread woken by a PPU thread's sys_event_port_send, of the
  same or a lower priority (a more urgent one would preempt the sender on the PS3), or taking an event such a thread
  queued under 10 ms before, goes back to guest code once the sender has begun its next call into lv2 or a library
  (PpuThread::lv2_calls, counted where calls begin and return, dbg_stop_point), waits in lv2 for anything but a lock,
  or is gone, or 10 ms have passed since it sent: the worker's state store comes before its next call. (2) Before that
  receiver destroys an event queue or creates a thread, under 100 ms after the wake, the sender goes on until it waits
  in lv2 (not for a lock) or is gone, 20 ms at most (sender_barrier): the registry removal is done by then. The
  waiting thread yields for 50 us, then sleeps 20 us at a time. Event queues only, where the races were found.
- **Tries on the way:** (1) alone fixed the freeze, not the registry crash (1 of 2 runs beside a compile). Holding the
  receiver until the sender's second call held it 0.9 ms on average in GTA V (0.35 ms with a 200 us cap after the
  first, sleeping); 30 us after the first was still too short under load (4 of 4 runs beside three others crashed:
  the main thread destroyed the copy worker's queues 6 lines before the worker's exit). The sender's CPU time is no
  measure: the host updates another thread's every 2 ms only (11 changes in 22 ms of a spinning thread, measured) and
  all at once when it stops.
- **Measured:** with the 2 ms sleep after every send, 4 of 4 runs pass the install screen (no freeze, no crash).
  Two gardens (330 s) beside six busy host threads: no crash; 50,000 to 55,000 waits each, 56 to 81 us on average;
  1 to 3 barrier waits (one ran 20 ms). GTA V's gate walk (128 s): pass, median 29.8 fps, slowest window 29.4,
  8,727 waits, 89% ended by the sender's next call, none by the limit, 206 ms in all (24 us each), no barrier wait.
  Assassin's Creed's garden walk (330 s) and training walk (600 s), fresh hdd0, side by side: both to their end, no
  error; 68,000 and 114,000 waits, 597 and 847 ms in all (9 and 7 us each), 3 barrier waits each (1.1 and 0.5 ms);
  the training at 57 to 60 fps. pspocket-boot prints the waits at the end of a run;
  PSPOCKET_LV2_SENDER_FIRST=0 turns both parts off for A/B (one of its two garden runs crashed in the registry at
  boot; the other ran as with the change: 40.8 to 51.4 fps in the garden's busy part against 44.0 to 54.6).
- Test: tests/lv2/test_event.cpp (a sender the host does not run for 3 ms after its send: a receiver of the same or a
  lower priority comes back after the sender's next call, from a wake and from a queued event; a more urgent one at
  once; a queue destroyed after the wake waits for the sender to wait in lv2 even past its next call; a sender that
  neither calls nor waits holds its receiver 10 ms, not more). It fails with PSPOCKET_LV2_SENDER_FIRST=0.
- Not translated code: the phone needs the app rebuilt, not its translations (kTranslatorGeneration unchanged).

## D-987 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE geometry on the GPU, phase 1: what GTA V's EDGE job reads and writes, the hole, go

The steady-30 plan's last item (docs/improve.md, item 4, "later Metal compute"; the user: "do the edge on gpu too").
Before building: what one job of GTA V's EDGE build (spu_dad457863220b1cc) does to the world outside its local store,
and whether its work can wait for the GPU. Measured on the gate's 128 s prologue walk with two diagnostics (kept):

- `PSPOCKET_JOB_TRACE=HASH` (runtime/hle/src/spurs_jobtrace.cpp): every job of one program counted (jobs, GETs, PUTs,
  atomics, bytes) and every `PSPOCKET_JOB_TRACE_EVERY`-th written out (descriptor, DMA list, each MFC command with its
  pc and data; `PSPOCKET_JOB_TRACE_LS=N`: local store and registers at entry), through a new per-thread MFC observer
  (`ps_spu_set_mfc_observer`, one relaxed load a transfer when none is set). Into inventory/ (game data).
- `spu-job-replay TRACE_DIR --key HASH --size BYTES`: each dumped job run again from its entry state with the guest
  memory it read filled in; its writes against the game's. 728 jobs of the walk (every 2500th): all 728 write what
  they wrote in the game. `--coverage` interprets them and counts instructions. The oracle for what follows.

Findings:

- **Volume.** 1.515 M EDGE jobs in the walk, 600 to 700 a frame in play (20,000 a second at 30 fps), 16.7 µs of SPU
  thread time each on the Mac with D-968's natives. A job: 485 vertices, 1573 indices (524 triangles) and 72% of the
  triangles kept on average (the 728 replayed); input 15.8 KB (at most 40 KB) gathered by the job chain from its 17
  element DMA list into an in/out buffer; about 10 KB out. So some 315,000 vertices and 340,000 triangles a frame.
- **Every MFC command a job makes** (3,039 traced): GETLLAR and PUTLLC on its SPU's ring allocator line (three rings of
  3 MB in RSX local memory, one an SPU); two or three PUTs into the allocation (the kept indices, then the vertex
  streams in 16 KB pieces); a 4-byte GET from the allocation as a fence; the command hole PUT (368 to 480 bytes) into
  the FIFO in main memory; and in 13 of 3,039 jobs a GET of an RSX label (the ring was full). Nothing else: no other
  reads, no other writes. The allocation's size is the kept indices (16-byte aligned) plus the vertex streams, in 128
  bytes: it depends on the culling's count.
- **The hole** (decoded from every traced job): SET_VERTEX_DATA_ARRAY_OFFSET for 1 to 6 attributes (0, 2, 3, 4, 8, 14)
  into the allocation, INVALIDATE_VERTEX_FILE, SET_INDEX_ARRAY_ADDRESS and DMA (16-bit, local), BEGIN triangles,
  DRAW_INDEX_ARRAY (the count as arguments of up to 256 indices each), END, SET_SEMAPHORE_OFFSET and
  TEXTURE_READ_SEMAPHORE_RELEASE with the ring position (how the allocator learns the RSX has passed), then a
  non-incrementing NOP over the rest: 64 to 99 words free. The vertex formats are not in it (the PPU's command buffer
  sets them). 1.5% of jobs keep nothing: the hole is all NOP. The hole is sized (EdgeGeomSpuConfigInfo's
  commandBufferHoleSize) for every index kept.
- **Who reads the outputs:** the RSX only. The allocation is in RSX local memory; the SPU reads in those megabytes are
  the jobs' own fences; the hole is FIFO. The job keeps no state between jobs that its outputs depend on (the replays
  start from each job's own entry state and agree).
- **What the job is:** Sony's EDGE geometry, standard. The EdgeGeomSpuConfigInfo is copied into the job's context
  (binary + 0xE700): in the walk the index flavour is 3 (compressed, counter-clockwise) in every job, skinning 0 (none),
  1 (four bones, no scaling) or 4 (one bone, no scaling), matrix format 0, the primary input a custom stream
  description (0xff), the secondary none or predefined 6, the output predefined 0 or 2 or custom, one to six uniform
  tables; culling flavour 2 in 722 of 728 jobs, 1 in 6; four viewports (1280x720, and 256, 128 and 256x384 squares:
  the shadow maps). Where the instructions go (interpreted, 83,000 a job): the culling stage 25%, skinning 25%, vertex
  decompression 17.8%, the screen transform 12.5%, index decompression 9.4%, 0x0FA60 and 0x0F6C8 (output) 5.3%, all the
  rest (the driver, setup, allocation, the hole) about 5%; 6,023 distinct instructions run.
- **The GPU's budget:** a few hundred operations a vertex and fifty a triangle: about 0.1 GFLOP and 25 MB of traffic a
  frame, well under a millisecond of the phone's GPU by estimate (the Mac walk's GPU is 6 to 8 ms a frame).

**Go**, deferred: the job keeps running on its SPU for what the CPU-visible world needs (its control code: the
configuration, the ring allocation, the order of its PUTs, the hole), with its heavy stages (vertex and index
decompression, skinning, the transform and culling, the output compression) recording instead of computing. The
culling's stand-in keeps every index, so the hole draws the full count and the allocation holds every index (the ring
fills somewhat faster; the hole is sized for it); the job's PUTs into the allocation are dropped. Its input buffer (an
in/out buffer, so taken at its entry) and the stages' parameters go into a work item registered under the
allocation's address. The Metal backend, at a draw whose index array lies in a registered allocation, has the GPU make
what the job would have put there (the same bytes at the same offsets, big-endian, as the vertex shader pulls them)
and the kept indices with their count, in a compute pass in a command buffer enqueued ahead of the render command
buffer (no render pass is broken), and draws indirectly with the GPU's count. A configuration the GPU path does not
handle runs on the CPU as today (logged once). Behind `PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU` (off until shown right; `=ab` alternating).
The design's steps and numbers follow in D-988 on.

## D-988 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE geometry on the GPU: the jobs record, the RSX backend computes (PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU)

D-987's design, built. Off by default; `PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=1` (read once, at the first EDGE job or the backend's start)
turns it on, `=ab` alternates it with the SPU path every `PSPOCKET_EDGE_AB` frames (default 30) and logs each half,
`=verify` keeps the SPU path and runs the GPU's beside it, comparing their outputs, `=cpu` runs the GPU's code on the
SPU's thread (a check of the recording without the GPU).

- **What stays on the SPU.** The job runs as before but for its four heavy stages, EDGE's edgeGeomDecompressVertexes,
  edgeGeomSkinVertexes, edgeGeomCullTriangles and edgeGeomCompressVertexes (0x0DAF0, 0x07A10, 0x0EFF8, 0x0F5B8 of GTA
  V's build), now listed in the build's table (replace.cpp) with stand-ins (runtime/spu/replace/edge_gpu.cpp). A
  stand-in copies what its stage would read (the vertex streams and their fixed offsets and descriptions, the bones'
  matrices and weights, the decompressed indices and the EDGE context's view, the output format) into a work item, does
  to the context what the rest of the job reads (scratch pointers, the table of each attribute, the count, the return
  value; checked against the stage's own on 721 of the walk's jobs) and returns. The culling's stand-in keeps every
  index, so the allocation, the PUTs and the hole are the job's own for the full count. The index decompression stays
  (native, D-968). The decision is taken at the first stage, from the configuration: input streams custom (0xff),
  positions bit-packed fixed point, normals and tangents unit vectors, skinning none, four bones or one, matrix format
  0, output 0, 2 or a custom description of F32 and X11Y11Z10N, the vertex-output callback 0x0ECF8, no blend shapes,
  no custom decompression; anything else runs on the SPU as before (5 of 721 jobs: an attribute of id 9, format 4).
- **The PUTs and the hole.** While a job takes the path its thread has an MFC filter (`ps_spu_set_mfc_filter`, a veto
  before each transfer): from its culling on, its PUTs into RSX local memory (the indices, the vertices) are dropped
  and their range kept; at its first PUT elsewhere, its command buffer hole, the work item is published under the
  allocation's address (pspocket/core/edge_registry.hpp) before the hole goes out.
- **The GPU.** The Metal backend, at an indexed draw whose index array starts at a published allocation, takes the
  item; its blob goes into the draw's transient allocation with room for the allocation's shadow (indices at 0,
  vertices after them, at the offsets of the hole), the screen-space scratch and the indirect draw's arguments. The
  draw's EDGE attributes point into the shadow; the others (static streams) are copied from guest memory as ever. At
  submit the command buffer's jobs run in one compute dispatch per transient buffer (one threadgroup of 256 threads a
  job, the bones' matrices in threadgroup memory) in a command buffer committed before the render buffer: no render
  pass is broken. The draw is `drawIndexedPrimitives` with the indirect buffer, its count the kernels' (big-endian u16
  indices, as the vertex shader pulls them, D-271).
- **The kernels** (pspocket/core/edge_kernels.inc): EDGE's stages per vertex (decode, skin, compress into the output
  vertex, transform to the screen with the outcodes) and per triangle (EDGE's culling rules, the kept indices packed in
  order by prefix sums). One source for Metal and C++: the code is the argument of a macro, which C++ expands and the
  backend stringifies (no generated file: the iOS app compiles the runtime's sources as they are, D-014); the
  kernels compile at the backend's start from that text with IEEE arithmetic (MTLMathModeSafe). **The SPU's arithmetic,
  bit for bit:** every product, sum and fused product rounds toward zero, denormals are zeros and a zero factor gives
  +0 or the addend, as the SPU (and the CPU path's lifted code) does, emulated on rounding to nearest by error-free
  transforms (a product's error by fma, a sum's by TwoSum); the SPU's estimates (frest, frsqest, fi) from RPCS3's
  tables. The culling's mode arithmetic is the CPU path's: its masks are NaNs as floats, and the lifted code's default
  NaN keeps a triangle all of whose vertices are past one frustum edge (real hardware would cull it; the image is the
  same).
- **Tools.** `edge-gpu-check PROBE_DIR [--metal]`: the stand-ins and the kernels (C++, and with --metal the Metal
  kernel on this GPU, timed) against the SPU on states saved by `spu-job-replay --probe` (D-987). Tests (synthetic
  meshes, tests/rsx/edge_synthetic.hpp): the kernels against a double-precision reference, the transform against the
  SPU native 0x0ECF8 bit for bit, the emulated operations against the SPU's on 200,000 random operands, the culling
  rules, the stand-ins over a synthetic EDGE context, and the Metal kernel against the C++ code bit for bit.
- **The translation.** The four functions must be called through the program's table (D-966): the EDGE program is
  lifted again with the new table (here: spu-lift into inventory/edge/relift, linked by PSPOCKET_GAME_SPU_EXTRA; it
  differs from before at those four calls only). A translation made before does not reach the stand-ins: with the
  switch on, its jobs simply run on the SPU (nothing breaks, nothing is gained) until the game's SPU programs are
  translated again (scripts/lift-spu.sh). kTranslatorGeneration goes to 5 for it: the phone prepares the game again.

## D-989 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE on the GPU checked: the same bits as the SPUs over a whole walk; the in-walk A/B

- **The same output.** `PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=verify` over the gate's 128 s walk: 1,432,691 EDGE jobs recorded, run on the
  GPU beside their SPU and compared when the GPU was done: every job the same count of kept indices and the same list
  (564,191,201 triangles kept by both); of 713,726,466 output vertices 713,726,428 the same bytes, the other 38 one
  step apart in a packed normal or tangent (a fused product whose error terms' sum rounded the other way, D-988); F32
  positions 0 ulps apart. Offline (edge-gpu-check over 721 jobs saved from the walk): the stand-ins leave the
  context as the stages do in all, the kernels' C++ and Metal give the SPU's bytes in all 716 they take. Before the
  emulation of the SPU's rounding the GPU differed in the last bits (99.0% of jobs the same kept count): it is worth
  its cost (below).
- **Frames.** Dumps every 150 frames from 1500 of two walks with the path off and one with it on (the walks are not
  frame-exact): where the camera stands still (frames 1950 to 2700) the off-off pairs differ by a mean of 0.6 to 1.2
  (of 255) and the on-off pairs by 0.6 to 1.6, the same noise; where it moves, both pairs differ as much (timing).
  Looked at: characters, rooms and shadows right. The gate's thumbnails: 2 frame jumps, no dark frame, with it on or off.
- **The A/B in one walk** (`PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=ab`, 30 frames a half, the Mac shared with other work): the EDGE jobs'
  SPU time 13.24 to 4.68 ms a frame (-65%) and 9.89 to 3.70 (-63%); a deferred job 6.0 to 6.5 us against 17.8 to 20 us
  whole; the RSX thread 8.03 to 7.39 ms a frame (-8%) and 7.02 to 6.59 (-6%): an EDGE draw copies and scans no vertex
  and index data; the GPU +0.3 ms and -0.1 ms a frame (the windows' noise is larger). The kernels alone, a frame's 716
  jobs on the Mac's GPU (edge-gpu-check --metal, the fastest of 20): 0.57 ms with the SPU's rounding emulated, 0.31 ms
  without it; 1.8 ms before the bones' matrices went to threadgroup memory. What a deferred job still costs on its SPU:
  the job's own control code (about half), the index decompression (a third: natives D-968), the job chain around it.
- **Gates.** scripts/gate.sh quick (off): 25 of 25. scripts/gate.sh game off: pass (29.8 fps median, slowest 29.0, 2
  frame jumps, no dark frame). With PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=1: pass on every check but the slowest 5 s window in two of three
  walks taken while the Mac was loaded by other work (load average 20 to 58: 22.8 and 9.0 fps, every SPU workload's
  time inflated in that window), 29.4 in the one walk on a quieter Mac.

## D-990 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE on the GPU after the phone's city (run 331): the job told one triangle, the driver's own steps, notes once a kind

Run 331 (iPhone 18 Pro Max, the city, PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=1): worse than off (16 to 20 fps, the EDGE SPU threads
blocked, a deferred job 9.5 us growing to 78 us), shadows flickering, 134,527 warning lines. Three causes, none
reachable in the gate's prologue walk:

- **The log.** About 3% of the city's jobs reached the culling with fewer indices than configured; note() said each
  distinct text once, finding it in a list of every text said so far under one lock: the list grew to some 100,000 and
  the three EDGE threads queued on it. note() now says a kind once (its numbers left out), at most 64 kinds.
- **The flicker.** Those jobs' counts were cut by GTA V's job driver itself: between EDGE's index decompression and its
  culling it runs a triangle filter of its own (0x06808, on when job descriptor byte 0x1A6 is set) that drops
  triangles by words of the vertices' position table, a table the GPU path never makes on the SPU: it filtered on
  stale local store. The driver has more steps of its own that read or change the stages' tables, each on a field of
  its descriptor (from + 0xF0 in $85 from before the decompression): a position offset added after the decompression
  ($83), the path of descriptor byte 0x1A4 bit 2, the modes of 0x190 to 0x19F and 0x1A7, per-vertex passes after the
  skinning (0x1B0 on). The decompression's stand-in now leaves a job to the SPU unless every one of them is off, as in
  every job of the gate's walk (and the same 716 of 721 saved jobs take the path as before).
- **The rings.** The culling's stand-in told the job every index kept, so its ring allocation held every index: with
  three times the prologue's draws the city filled the rings and the jobs waited for the RSX's label. It now tells one
  triangle (3 indices; the full count when fewer): the allocation is 16 bytes of indices and the vertices, smaller
  than the SPU path's, and the hole draws 3 indices at the allocation's start. The backend takes the draw by that
  address as before, puts the kept indices in an area of their own in the draw's transient allocation (room for every
  index) and the vertices at the offsets the hole gives, and draws indirectly with the kernels' count. The jobs' GETs
  of RSX labels (the ring-full waits) are counted in the window line: on the Mac walk 10.8 a frame with every index
  told, 1.6 to 1.9 with one triangle (the SPU path's jobs: 0.4% of jobs, about 3 a frame, in D-987's trace).
- Checked on the Mac walk with it on: gate game pass (29.8 fps median, slowest 29.4, 2 frame jumps, no dark frame,
  RSX failures 0, no new message shape); frames against two walks with it off at the noise of off against off (frames
  1950 to 2700: mean 0.5 to 1.2); edge-gpu-check and the tests as before. The phone's city has to show the stall and
  the flicker gone (the walk cannot reach it). The kernels' GPU time in the city (2.8 to 4.3 ms a frame on the phone
  for some 2,200 jobs) is next: the SPU's rounding emulated costs about half the kernels' time on the Mac.
- **PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU_EXACT=0** builds the kernels without the emulation (the GPU's rounding to nearest, no zero class):
  the 716 saved jobs' kernels 0.25 to 0.32 ms on the Mac GPU against 0.58 to 0.66 ms (A/B in one session, alternated),
  711 of 716 kept index lists the same as the SPU's and 378 of 716 jobs' vertices the same bytes (the rest a last bit
  apart). Default exact (1); for the phone to measure whether the kernels' time is what the city's frame waits on.
- The notes' kind: first the digits each as '#', so numbers of different lengths made kinds of their own; now each
  number (decimal or hex) is one '#'. Tests: the driver's steps leave a job to the SPU, leave_cull told one
  triangle (the count, the halfword, the buffer's end), the kinds.

## D-1013 · 2026-10-15 · Code copied from the executable's read-only segments is not checked again at each load

The research after run 332 (docs/improve.md, "The last 10% to a steady 30"): GTA V's walk loads SPU job binaries and
modules about 2.3 million times, and identify() checked each one whole (content_check, up to 66 KB: EDGE's job 59 KB,
GraphicsMain's 66 KB) against the image it remembered, 2.5 to 3.4% of the SPURS threads' time. GTA V's SPU code all
lies in its executable's first segment, read-only for the PPU and the SPUs (flags 0x400005); on a PS3 a store or DMA
there faults, so the bytes are the same at every load.

- pspocket/core/immutable_memory.hpp: up to eight guest ranges nothing writes after the executable loaded. The loader
  marks every segment without a write flag for the PPU, the SPUs or the RSX (cleared first, per executable).
- identify(): an image read from guest memory (not a local store copy, D-206) inside a marked range takes a fixed
  check value instead of content_check, so the per-thread table of known images answers at once. Modules still compare
  their local store copy with the guest copy (the SPU may write into its own copy).
- Measured (the gate's walk, xctrace 20 s on the SPURS threads): content_check 0.00% of the main instance's samples,
  identify 0.87% in all. The gate passes (29.8 fps median, slowest 5 s window 29.2). Test: tests/core
  test_immutable_memory.cpp.
- The ranges go with the guest memory they belong to: cleared when one is reserved or released. tests/hle runs one
  fixture's guest memory after another in one process, and a range an earlier test's executable marked made a later
  test's different SPU image at the same address look known (test_hle ended in a bus error in the quick gate once).

## D-1014 · 2026-10-15 · The RSX thread's waits by kind in the log; waiting on a semaphore's line measured and left

The research after run 332 found the RSX thread blocking about 125 times a frame in timed sleeps (10 us doubling to
200 us), each ending up to 200 us after what it waited for. Tried: a semaphore acquire waiting on the semaphore's line
through the reservation system (ps_res_version, ps_res_wait_change: every SPU PUT and atomic, HLE writes and notify()
end it at once), the backoff kept for PPU stores.

- Measured on the gate's walk (two walks, PSPOCKET_RSX_SEM_WAIT=0 against on): the thread waits on a semaphore 0 to 75
  times in 5 s (under once a frame) and a write to its line ended none of those waits (the PPU releases them with plain
  stores, which say nothing). Its waits are a jump to itself 450 to 3,000 times in 5 s (10 to 20 a frame, 76 to 707 ms;
  the PPU patches the word when it has more commands) and idle between frames (about 300 in 5 s). Nothing to gain on
  the walk: the line wait was left out.
- Kept: a line every 5 s from the RSX thread, "rsx: waits in 5.0 s: idle N (ms), semaphore N (ms), jump to self N
  (ms)", for the phone's city, where the research's numbers came from.
## D-1005 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE on the GPU: the jobs counted by route and reason, no text or lock on the way

Run 332 (iPhone, the busy city, PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=1, 27.1 fps): about 1,270 of 2,140 EDGE jobs a frame went back to the
SPU (30.8 us each, 39 of EDGE's 47 ms a frame), but the log said only the first job of each kind of reason, and each
rejection formatted a text and took D-990's once-a-kind lock on its way out (about 1 ms a frame by the research).

- `pspocket::edge::Route` (spu, from the decompression; D-1006 adds the later stages) and `Reason` (the configuration,
  the vertex streams, the output, the job driver's own steps): every EDGE job is counted under its route and reason
  in a table of relaxed atomics (`count_route`), and the backend's window line ends with the jobs a frame by route,
  each with its reasons ("left to the SPU 12.0 (triangle filter 10.0, colour pass 2.0)").
- A recorder's failure is a Reason and a number (the format, the byte); the first job of each reason is said once
  (a bit per reason, one relaxed load after the first). The warnings for conditions the GPU path goes on through
  (culling from a vertex offset, another index count, the output vertex changed, the PUTs' places) are a bit each
  too: no lock, no text unless said.

## D-1006 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE on the GPU from a later stage: the job driver's steps on the SPU, the GPU from its tables

D-990 left every job to the SPU when any of GTA V's job driver's own steps around EDGE's was on (descriptor bytes
0x190 to 0x19F and 0x1B0 to 0x1DF, 0x1A4 & 0x1C, 0x1A6, 0x1A7, $83): about 1,270 of the city's 2,140 jobs a frame in
run 332. The driver's code (the job binary from 0x110B0 on; its descriptor from + 0xF0 in $85), read field by field:

- **Never read** by its code: words 0x190 and 0x19C; 0x198 is copied into the EDGE context's +0x17C (read by nothing:
  the stages read the halfword at +0x17E) and read by the triangle filter; 0x1A5; 0x1A7 other than 0 and 2; 0x1B0 to
  0x1BB and 0x1C0 on but in the paths below. 0x1A4 bits 5 to 7 are the culling's mode (already the culling's $4).
- **Before the skinning** (after the decompression): $83 added to every position (0x11338); 0x1A4 bit 2, extra data
  fetched (0x074C8) and applied by 0x04C30 or 0x0DBA8 (0x11398); 0x1A4 bits 3 and 4, 0x0E398's mode (0x115DC);
  0x1A7 == 2, the output format made 4 (with word 0x194) or the output description changed (0x11488), and more of the
  driver's after the hole.
- **After the skinning, before the culling**: 0x1A6, the triangle filter 0x06808 (by words of the positions' table and
  0x198, 0x1D0 on: run 331's flicker); word 0x1BC with the skinning on, positions and normals changed from extra data
  (0x11658 to 0x119C4).
- **After the culling**: word 0x194 with 0x1A7 0, a palette (from extra data, U8 colours) looked up per vertex from
  attribute 9's table into attribute 19's (0x08A38, called with $85), which the compression puts out.

So a job's route (`choose_route`, pspocket::edge::Route): **from the decompression** when no step reads or changes the
stages' tables (as before); **from the skinning** when a step runs before the skinning (and for the colour pass): the
SPU decompresses and runs the steps, the skinning's stand-in records the SPU's tables (positions, normals, tangents:
four floats a vertex) and the GPU skins, transforms, culls and compresses from them; **from the culling** when a step
runs after the skinning, or the skinning is one the GPU does not make (flavour, matrix format): the SPU skins too, the
culling's stand-in records the skinned positions. In the later routes an output attribute the GPU does not compute
(PS_EDGE_ATTR_TABLE) is the SPU's table as the compression finds it (the colour pass's attribute 19 among them), looked
up as the compression does (0x09008: the first of the 16 id bytes at +0x150 that matches, whatever the count). A job
whose output needs a table that is not there when its route starts is left to the SPU (reason "tables"): the SPU's
compression then puts out what the index buffer's address holds, the culling's compacted list (seen: 284 jobs of the
walk with a U8N colour input, attribute 9, and attribute 19 in their output but no colour pass). The decompression's
own refusals (input formats, streams, an output attribute it does not decode) move a job to the skinning's route.

- The work item (pspocket/core/edge_job.h): `tables`, `nrm_table`, `tan_table` (positions at pos_data), and an output
  attribute's `table`; the kernels read the tables instead of decoding (the culling's route: skin 0). Up to 8 output
  attributes (some descriptions have 5).
- Counted by route and reason (D-1005); `PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU_ROUTE=skin|cull` starts every job no earlier than that stage
  (the later routes checked on every job); `edge-gpu-check --route skin|cull` the same on saved states.
- **Verify by kind, sampled**: each work item carries its kinds (the route, the reason it was taken for); verify counts
  jobs, the same index lists and the same vertices per kind ("EDGE verify by kind" in the window line, "MISMATCH" where
  any differs). `PSPOCKET_EDGE_VERIFY_EVERY=N` verifies the first 64 jobs of each route and reason, then every Nth; the
  others take the GPU path: verify cheap enough for the phone's city.
- Checked: the walk's 657 saved jobs (spu-job-replay probes of the gate's walk) in all three routes: the same output
  bytes, screen vertices and index lists as the SPU's (657 of 657 with D-1007's formats, which the 10 with the colour
  pass put out), the Metal kernel the same as the CPU's; tests on synthetic meshes (the tables against the streams in
  both later routes, the routes each descriptor field gives).

## D-1007 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE on the GPU: U8N out, the packed formats' own arithmetic, fixed point over 24 bits in

The formats run 332's jobs were left to the SPU for, and the packed formats' arithmetic, as GTA V's EDGE build
computes them (the compression's jump tables: predefined formats at 0x0F6A4 by format, 2 at 0x0FA60; a description's
attributes at 0x0909C by format - 1: 1 at 0x09B90, 2 F32, 4 at 0x0997C, 6 at 0x09DA4):

- **U8N out** (format 4): t = x * 255 + 0.5 in one fused rounding (toward zero), cfltu(t, scale 2^24), its top byte:
  floor(t), 0 below 0, 255 from 256 on.
- **I16N** (predefined format 2's tangent; format 1 in a description, now taken): t = x * 32767.5 - 0.5 (fused),
  cflts(t, scale 2^16), its top half (two's complement). **X11Y11Z10N** (format 2's normal; format 6 in a description):
  t = x * (1 - 2^-n) - 2^-n (fused), cflts(t, scale 2^31), the top 11, 11 and 10 bits (x lowest). Both one fused
  rounding with the constants in the caller (0x0F63C on); D-988's x h + h in two roundings agrees but at rare
  boundaries: they were D-989's 38 vertices one step apart in 713 million (not the emulated fused products). Now the
  same bytes as the SPU's in every walk (below).
- **Fixed point over 24 bits** (13.12 to 15.12 in the city; the decompression's wide path 0x0B9B4, taken when any
  component has 24 bits or more): v = raw + bias in 32 bits; csflt(v >> frac, arithmetic) + cuflt(v << (32 - frac),
  scale 2^-32) by fa. With 8 to 24 fraction bits both conversions are exact and fa is the one rounding (the kernels'
  emulated fa); fewer or more fraction bits go to the skinning's route. For 24 bits or fewer the narrow formula gives
  the same value (|v| < 2^24): the kernels take the wide one for components over 24 bits only (ek_bits32 reads up to
  32 bits across bytes). Jobs taking it are counted (and verified) under "fixed point over 24 bits" of the
  decompression's route.
- Tests against the SPU's own instructions in its environment (lifted.h's fma, cfltu, cflts, csflt, cuflt, fa): U8N,
  I16N and X11Y11Z10N on 100,000 random values and every byte's neighbourhood; the wide decode on 20,000 values for
  each of 25, 26, 27 and 32 bits with 8, 12, 16 and 24 fraction bits: all the same. The walk has no wide fixed point
  (the phone's verify by kind checks it on the game's); its 10 colour-pass jobs put out U8N and I16N: the same bytes as
  the SPU's in edge-gpu-check.
- A U8N colour as input (secondary attribute 9) stays a reason for the skinning's route: the walk's such jobs put out
  attribute 19 without a table (D-1006), and the colour-pass jobs need the SPU's tables anyway.
- Verify over the gate's walk (PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=verify, every job): from the decompression, 1,433,707 jobs (17,959
  of them from the skinning for the colour pass): every index list and all 717,145,826 output vertices the same bytes
  as the SPU's; with PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU_ROUTE=cull, 1,471,560 jobs from the culling: all lists and all 736,110,498
  vertices the same.

## D-1008 · 2026-10-15 · EDGE work items published without a lock; one clock read a job

- **Publishing** (pspocket/core/edge_registry.cpp): each publishing thread (an SPU worker) has a ring of its own, one
  producer and one consumer (8,192 items): the item stored, the tail released. The RSX thread, taking, moves what the
  rings hold into a map only it touches (an item published again for the same allocation replaces the earlier one,
  counted). No lock and no shared map on either side; a full ring (the RSX 8,192 items behind) waits for room; more
  than 32 publishing threads share a locked overflow list. Before: one global mutex and an unordered_map for every
  publish and take (about 2 ms a frame of the city's EDGE time by the research).
- **The pool of used items**: each thread keeps up to 64, the rest shared in batches of 32 (a lock every 32 items).
- **One clock read a job**: job_begin takes the job chain's grab time (its own clock read), and a batch's later jobs
  start at the thread's previous EDGE job's end; job_end reads the clock once.
- Test: three threads publish 20,000 items each while one takes them by allocation as they come; every item taken
  once, an allocation published twice gives the later item and one replacement counted.

## D-1062 · 2026-10-16 · Sony's exports pspocket lacks, each sorted by its code: aliases found automatically

The bulletproof plan's net 4: unnamed NIDs identified from the firmware's own modules instead of by hand (GTA IV's
0xb70b4ad3 took a research agent and ppu-dis to place, D-1061).

- scripts/nid_audit.py: every decrypted firmware module (inventory/firmware/analysis/elf, ps3inspect --json), every
  export pspocket's registry (pspocket-boot --hle-list) lacks, sorted by its first instructions: **alias** (register
  set-up, then a plain branch into a body a named export of the library also branches to: named with what each sets),
  **constant** (li r3,K; blr, or lis+ori), **void** (blr), **thunk** (into another library's import stub), **code**
  (anything else, with its length). --imports LIB:NID ... for a game's; --json for every entry (inventory/, game-derived).
- Over the installed 4.92 system software: 1,289 exports in 83 libraries lack a host function (many are internal
  libraries games reach through others); 74 aliases, 11 constants, 3 void, 2 thunks, 1,199 code. Of the aliases, 8 share
  a named export's body: cellGcmSys 0xb70b4ad3 (the body 0xcc0 shared with _cellGcmInitBody, which sets r7=1: what D-1061's
  research found by hand), cellGame 0x47db7335, 0x5a067101 and 0x9c79f4f1 (cellGameGetParamString,
  cellGameCreateGameData and cellGameSetParamString with r6 or r5 = 1 where those set 0), cellJpgDec 0xdb9affce,
  sceNpCommerce2 0x6a53fdf9 and 0x9684d405, _cellAudio 0xcd7bc431 (cellAudioPortOpen's body).
- These are the work queue for net 4: an alias is its named function with the argument fixed; a constant or void

## D-1064 · 2026-10-16 · Glitch detectors on frame thumbnails, shared by the Mac and the iPhone

The bulletproof plan's net 5: the detectors that turn "the user saw a glitch" into an event, the same code for the
bench and the app's reports. pspocket/loader/frame_watch.hpp (FrameWatch), plain C++, fed each presented frame's 64x36
thumbnail and its time:

- partly black: a fifth to 95% of the thumbnail exactly black (0, 0, 0) two frames in a row (D-1060's measure: the
  black sea 56%, a night street 2.5%; a whole black frame is a fade);
- flicker: A, B, A: a frame over 20 of 255 from the one before and the next under a third of that from the one before
  it (a cut is A, B, B);
- hitch: over 500 ms between frames while the game flipped 10 a second or more;
- frozen: the same picture (under 0.5 apart) for 10 s while frames come;
- flagged: the player's own button.
Events are counted always and reported once per kind every 2 minutes; the last 32 thumbnails are kept for a report.
Test: tests/hle test_frame_watch.cpp (synthetic thumbnails: a night scene, a half black frame twice, a fade, A-B-A
against a cut, a gap of 800 ms, 11 s of one picture). Next: fed by the Metal backend's per-frame thumbnail (asked of
the graphics track), in pspocket-boot's summary and the app's reports.

## D-1066 · 2026-10-16 · Two unnamed exports that are named functions: cellJpgDec 0xDB9AFFCE, sceNpCommerce2 0x9684D405

From scripts/nid_audit.py's aliases (D-1062), checked in the firmware's code:

- cellJpgDec 0xDB9AFFCE sets r8 = r9 = 0 and r10 = 1, then branches into the body cellJpgDecExtDecodeData (r10 = 1)
  and cellJpgDecDecodeData (r10 = 0) share: cellJpgDecExtDecodeData without a display callback (five arguments).
- sceNpCommerce2 0x9684D405 branches into sceNpCommerce2DoProductBrowseFinishAsync's body setting nothing: the same
  function.
- Left out: cellGame 0x47DB7335, 0x5A067101, 0x9C79F4F1 are cellGameGetParamString, cellGameCreateGameData and
  cellGameSetParamString with "elmMode" 1 in the request libsysutil_game sends to the system software (the named ones
  send 0); what mode 1 does happens in the system software, so they stay unanswered until a game shows it.
  sceNpCommerce2 0x6A53FDF9 (DoProductBrowseStartAsync with an internal flag 1) likewise. _cellAudio 0xCD7BC431 is
  cellAudioPortOpen's own NID under the internal library name (already answered as cellAudio). cell_FreeType2's
  unnamed constants are FreeType internals nothing imports; the encoders' constants (cellAvcEnc, cellM4vEnc) are in
  libraries pspocket does not register.

## D-1040 · 2026-10-16 · GTA IV's GCM init: libgcm_sys's unnamed 0xB70B4AD3, the command buffer in local memory

GTA IV (BLUS30127) stopped at boot on the phone (game-153115.log): `hle: UNIMPLEMENTED cellGcmSys::? (0xb70b4ad3)`
with r3..r7 = the context pointer, 0x300000, 0, 0, 0, then a jump to guest 0x400 (SIGBUS). Read in Sony's
libgcm_sys (the firmware's libgcm_sys.sprx): 0xB70B4AD3's entry at 0xe58 is `b 0xcc0`, _cellGcmInitBody's at 0xe5c
`li r7,1; b 0xcc0`: the same body with the caller's r7 where _cellGcmInitBody has 1. The body keeps r7 (r31, r28),
passes it to the context's setup (0x70c: flag bit 0x10 of sys_rsx_context_allocate when 0) and to 0x9a8, and with 0
(0xdac) passes local memory's address (sys_rsx_memory_allocate's) where ioAddress goes. 0x9a8 with 0 (0xa48-0xa64):
cmdSize over 0xffff and a multiple of 4 (else CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE), ioSize and ioAddress not looked at, nothing
mapped; the rest as with 1: the context 4 KB into the buffer, the FIFO at offset 0x1000. So 0 is the command buffer in
local memory, an early SDK's way (GTA IV's: 3 MB of local memory, no IO at init).

- runtime/hle/src/cellGcmSys.cpp: init_body(..., io_buffer), _cellGcmInitBody its io_buffer = true, and
  cellGcmSys_B70B4AD3 (a name of its NID, as the NIDs known only by number are) with the fifth argument. With 0 the
  buffer is local memory's base, nothing is mapped; cellGcmGetConfiguration's ioAddress 0xfff00000 and ioSize 0 as
  Sony's. The RSX reads a FIFO whose first offset no IO mapping holds from local memory already (Rsx::set_fifo_pointers,
  RPCS3's rule). Flag 0x10 is not passed to sys_rsx_context_allocate (pspocket's lv2 keeps the mode flags only).
- Tests: tests/hle/test_gcm_compare.cpp now compares each init too (its answer, its lv2 RSX calls, the context's begin
  and end), and a new section runs 0xB70B4AD3 against Sony's with r7 = 0 (GTA IV's arguments; an IO buffer given) and
  1, and _cellGcmInitBody, through the getters (configuration, AddressToOffset of local memory and the IO buffer,
  IoOffsetToAddress, MapMainMemory after), and Sony's two size checks: all the same. tests/hle/test_gcm.cpp: commands
  written at the local context run on the RSX (its reference register), the configuration's IO.
- Found on the way, not changed (every entry, also _cellGcmInitBody): Sony's init writes 0x3a0 bytes of the RSX's first
  state into the buffer (current = begin + 0x3a0), pspocket's none; Sony's cellGcmGetDefaultCommandWordSize is the
  init's cmdSize / 4 and its segment size 0x2000 words, pspocket's RPCS3's 0x400 and 0x100.
- GTA IV's data is only on the phone: the next phone run shows what comes after the init.

## D-1069 · 2026-10-16 · The worker-control fiber test waits for both workers before Shutdown

The gate failed once on "cellFiber: a worker control's fibers run on two worker threads" (2 in 15 runs alone):
one worker thread ran all six fibers before the other thread entered cellFiberPpuUtilWorkerControlRunFibers, the
test's Shutdown came first, and the late RunFibers returned CELL_FIBER_ERROR_STAT, as Sony's does for a control no
longer initialized. The library is right; the test now waits (up to 10 s) until the control word's worker count is 2
before Finalize and Shutdown. 40 of 40 runs pass.
## D-1021 · 2026-10-16 · ZPASS reports written whole once the GPU has counted, the ready word last

- **The race** (research of 2026-10-16): `m_get_report` wrote a ZPASS_PIXEL_CNT report's timestamp and its pad (0)
  when the method ran, through `defer()`, while the count came frames later from the render buffer's completion
  handler. GTA V's queries (EBOOT 0xB21908 begin: count 0, pad 1 from the CPU; 0xB21A00 end; 0xB21AD0 "ready" iff
  pad == 0) read such a report as counted and took its zero: the water module (0x116BE0C/0x116BEF4, 0x116BF58),
  the coronas (0x110CC08) and the light shafts (0x11738C0) all decide on it.
- **Now** the backend writes the whole 16-byte report in the completion handler: the timestamp (`Rsx::timestamp_ns()`
  then), the count, and the pad last with a release store (`Backend::report_zpass(value_addr, whole)`). The front end
  writes nothing for such a report. Non-ZPASS reports (ZCULL stats) and backends that do not count are as before.
- `PSPOCKET_RSX_EARLY_REPORTS=1` (or `Config::early_reports`) keeps the old order, for A/B runs; the alarm
  `reports_early` (D-1022) counts each report made ready before its count.
- Measured on the skyfall-sea route from the user's save (run early1, the old order): **46,086 reports made ready
  before their count** in 250 s (about 9 a frame); with the fix (runs fix1, fix3): 0.
- **What it did not fix**: the black block over the near sea (the bench's r6 frame 5160) reproduces with F1 on (run
  fix3 frames 5430/5460, and every trace-on-black run, D-1028): the water's depth pre-pass is drawn, the water
  surface draws after it do not land on it (being investigated, see the report of this session). GTA V's GPU timer
  (0xB4C120) now reads completion-time stamps: no fps change seen on the route (fix3: median 29.6 fps).
- Test: metal e2e "a ZPASS report is ready only once the GPU has counted it, written whole" (both orders: the pad stays
  1 until the GPU has run the draws; the old order makes it ready with the old zero and counts the alarm).

## D-1022 · 2026-10-16 · RSX correctness alarms, always on

- `pspocket/rsx/alarms.hpp`: relaxed atomic counters in the `Rsx` (`Rsx::alarms()`), bumped where the thing happens,
  for what can show on screen as a wrong picture: `reports_early` (D-1021), `targets_lost` / `targets_lost_kb` (a
  GPU-newer target removed with no copy of its bytes, or the part of it outside the target that took its memory,
  D-1025), `uninit_sampled` (a target nobody drew or cleared sampled as a texture, D-1023), `conditional_pending` (a
  conditional draw decided while its report was pending, D-115), `occlusion_overflow` (a query with no counter left,
  D-1024), `dead_overlays` (a colour target laid over a compressed texture: memory the GPU cannot have written in that

  `WindowStats::alarms`, in pspocket-boot's `--summary` (`"alarms"` totals and per window) and its end-of-run line
  ("RSX alarms: ..."). `scripts/gate_check.py` checks `checks.alarms_max` limits of games/<title>/gate.json.
- On the skyfall-sea route (fix3, 290 s): reports_early 0, uninit_sampled 0, occlusion_overflow 0, dead_overlays 0,
  conditional_pending 2,125, targets_lost 79,466 (36 GB in all: the part of GTA V's overlapping scratch targets at
  0xcd220000-0xcd5fffff outside the next target there, about 12 a frame; see D-1025).

## D-1024 · 2026-10-16 · Occlusion counters grow when a command buffer runs out

- A render buffer had 4,096 counters (`kVisibilitySlots`); a query past them counted nothing and the draw it guarded
  was skipped. Now a draw that would need a counter when none is left sends the buffer so far to the GPU (at the
  draw's start, before it allocates anything in it) and the next buffers have twice the counters
  (`MetalBackendConfig::occlusion_counters`, 4,096 to start); logged, and counted (`occlusion_overflow`, D-1022).
  GTA V never ran out on the routes (0).
- Test: metal e2e "occlusion queries past a command buffer's counters still count" (one counter to start, three
  queries: all count the triangle).

## D-1025 · 2026-10-16 · A new target over GPU-newer targets of other formats starts with their bytes

- **The sky** (phone trace 2815, research of 2026-10-16): GTA V packs its depth into an A8B8G8R8 640x360 target at
  0xcd260000 (#2787), then uses that memory as a Z24S8 depth buffer (#2806+). `get_depth_surface` evicted the colour
  target and made a depth buffer cleared to 1.0: the clouds and sky were tested against nothing. The same memory holds
  F16 320x180, A8B8G8R8 320x320 and 640x360 targets in one frame, each replacing the one before.
- **Now** `get_color_surface` and `get_depth_surface` make the new target first, then (`carry_into`) lay the GPU-newer
  targets it replaces over a staging copy of its memory with D-137's `rsx_*_to_memory` kernels (oldest first; guest
  memory first unless one of them covers it all) and convert that into its texels on the GPU
  (`rsx_memory_to_surface`, the inverse of `upload_surface_bytes`: depth as float plus stencil, then blits), then
  evict them. The new target is initialised and newer on the GPU. A larger target over a smaller one of its format
  (D-120's grow) goes the same way when the smaller one is newer on the GPU. `PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_CARRY=1`: off.
- What lies outside the new target of a replaced one is still lost (the alarm counts it: about 12 a frame in GTA V,
  0xcd260000's 640x360 replaced by 0xcd300000's 128x128 and the like). Writing those parts back would be a
  readback a frame each; left for the exact mode (D-1030) to tell whether it matters.
- On the route: 13 to 19 targets a frame carried; GPU time and passes within the run-to-run spread (fix3 10.2 ms,
  87 passes; base2 10.5 ms, 88 passes).
- Tests: metal e2e "a depth buffer made over a colour target holds the target's bytes" (0x11223344 cleared as
  A8R8G8B8 reads back as depth 0x112233, stencil 0x44; cleared to 1.0 without the carry) and "a colour target over a
  smaller one of another format carries its bytes, the rest from memory" (F16 halves 0x3C00 above, memory's bytes
  below).

## D-1041 · 2026-10-16 · The waker goes on first for every wake and for thread start, the semaphore's lighter

D-999 held a PPU thread woken by another PPU thread's event until the sender had begun its next call into lv2 or a
library (or waited there, or was gone; 10 ms at most), as lv2's scheduler leaves the sender running on the PS3. Every
other wake went through kernel.cpp's wake() with no such rule: a mutex or lwmutex handed over at unlock, a condition
variable or lwcond signalled, an rwlock released, a semaphore posted, an event flag set, a thread's exit waking its
joiner; and a new thread could run before the thread that started it went on (the "bulletproof engine" plan's A1 and
A3).

- **runtime/lv2/src/waker.cpp** (event.cpp's D-999 code moved and widened): wake() notes the PPU thread that wakes
  (note_waker: Waiter::waker, with what the wake was), only when a waiter is woken, so an uncontended lwmutex (which
  never enters the kernel) and a post nobody waits for cost nothing. Kernel::start_thread notes the creator on the new
  thread (note_starter). The woken thread takes it where it goes back to guest code: return_point (kernel.hpp) at the
  end of Kernel::syscall and of every library function (process.cpp's stub_trampoline), and a new thread before its
  first instruction. defer_to_waker applies D-999's rule: not for a more urgent thread, 10 ms at most from the wake;
  sender_barrier (before an event queue's destruction or a thread's creation) as before, for every strict kind.
- **Light kinds** (PSPOCKET_LV2_WAKER_LIGHT, default "semaphore"): held only until the waker is back from the call
  that woke (its lv2_calls past the wake's return), and no barrier. Measured on GTA V's gate walk, with the full rule
  the semaphore's 28,662 waits (220 a second: GTA V's posts are each followed by long stretches of guest code) took
  11.1 s of the walk's 128 s, its median fps 27.6 and its slowest window 16.8 against 29.8 and 26.4 with the events
  only (the machine at load 18; the same at load 11 measured 19 us a wait, at load 50 760 us: the waker not run by the
  host is the case the rule is for, and the case it costs most).
- PSPOCKET_LV2_SENDER_FIRST=0 turns it off, =events keeps D-999's event queues only (A/B). PSPOCKET_LV2_WAKE_DELAY_US=N
  has every call that woke a PPU thread sleep N us at its end (D-999's send delay for every wake). pspocket-boot prints
  the waits by kind at the end and the summary has them (waker_first).
- **Measured** (GTA V's gate walk, 128 s, A/B in one session): two runs each, interleaved (the machine at load
  8 to 25): D-999's events only, median 29.6 and 29.6 fps, slowest window 27.2 and 28.0, 8,332 and 8,032 waits,
  548 and 339 ms; every wake (the semaphore light), median 29.8 and 29.4, slowest 29.1 and 27.8, 40,696 and 40,477
  waits, 868 ms (the semaphore's 31,730 284 ms, 9 us each; the events' 8,673 578 ms; lwmutex 264, 6 ms; thread start
  24, 0.1 ms; join 1) and about 0.9 s the second (semaphore 691 ms); both gates pass. Assassin's Creed, a fresh hdd0
  through the install into the garden (330 s, walk-garden.txt): to its end, no fault or fatal error, the garden at 55
  to 60 fps; 47,790 waits, 1.85 s (event queue 43,943 1.49 s, lwmutex 3,180 343 ms, sleep 611, thread start 5); two
  5 s windows at 2.2 and 0.8 fps while it loads into the garden (at 215 to 225 s), not compared with an events-only
  run: that run was stopped for the disk (6 to 9 GB free), so the A/B on AC is still to do
- Tests: tests/lv2/test_waker_first.cpp, a contract matrix: every primitive (mutex hand-off, cond signal, rwlock read
  and write release, semaphore post, lwmutex hand-off, lwcond signal modes 2 and 3, event flag set, event send) against
  the woken thread's priority the same, lower and more urgent, the waker a host thread the host does not run (it
  sleeps) between its wake and its next call; a post or unlock that wakes nobody leaves no mark and no wait; a new
  thread of the same or lower priority runs after its creator's next call, a more urgent one at once, and a joiner
  waits for the exiting thread to be gone. PSPOCKET_WAKER_MATRIX_ROUNDS=N runs it N times. It fails with
  PSPOCKET_LV2_SENDER_FIRST=0 (every case) and =events (every case but the event's).

## D-1044 · 2026-10-16 · Flips paced by the flip mode (vsync waits for the vblank), behind PSPOCKET_FLIP_VSYNC

The flip mode was stored and never read (lv2 0x101); every flip happened as soon as the RSX reached it, so
cellGcmSetWaitFlip released at the flip, the flip status and the flip handler came at that moment, and nothing tied
the flips to the vblanks the GCM interrupt thread counts (D-971 holds frames at present time instead).

- The RSX (rsx.hpp) keeps the display sync lv2 sets (0x101, cellGcmSetFlipMode; 0x108 resets it to vsync) and counts
  the vblanks lv2's 0xFED reports. With pacing on and vsync, Rsx::do_flip waits on the RSX thread for the next vblank
  (RPCS3 RSXThread.cpp handle_emu_flip with the PS3 frame limit: a flip asked at vblank count N happens once the count
  is past N), so the flip, the flip label (cellGcmSetWaitFlip) and the status and handler follow at the vblank; only
  while vblanks come (one in the last 100 ms), 50 ms at most. HSYNC flips at once.
- lv2's display sync now starts as vsync, as the PS3 and RPCS3 (requested_vsync); GTA V never sets it.
- **Off by default** (PSPOCKET_FLIP_VSYNC=1 turns it on): GTA V's gate walk, A/B in one session: two runs with pacing (and every wake), median 28.8 and 29.8
  fps, slowest window 25.2 and 27.6 (one of them failed the gate's frame jumps, 3 of 2), against 29.8 and 29.4,
  29.1 and 27.8 without: within the noise of a loaded machine, but no better, and a frame finished a little after a
  vblank waits for the next one (the PS3's own rule, at the PS3's speed). Kept off until measured on the phone
- pspocket-boot prints the flips held, their time and the 50 ms limits when pacing is on.
- Not changed: libgcm_sys's full flip ring. Sony's cellGcmSetPrepareFlip with eight flips queued in a context the RSX
  never runs went into the context's callback (0 in the compare test: a SIGBUS), so its answer could not be compared
  yet; pspocket keeps dropping the oldest slot with a warning.
- Tests: tests/hle/test_gcm.cpp (with pacing and vsync five flips each held for a vblank, with HSYNC none),
  tests/hle/test_ac_gcm_spurs_prx.cpp (the default vsync, the RSX's mode following cellGcmSetFlipMode).

## D-1042 · 2026-10-16 · Scripted presses on game time: a frame, a library call, play

D-069's presses count seconds from the boot, so a walk holds for one build's speed only: a slower run presses Cross
before the menu it was meant for. Shake mode's runs (D-1045) and the triage (D-1043) need walks that press at the same
point of the game however fast it runs.

- **Anchors** (pspocket/hle/pad_script.hpp): `cross@flip:2200` presses at the 2200th frame;
  `cross@after:call:cellSaveDataAutoSave2+2s` 2 s after the game's first call of that library function (any linked
  function by name; "after:" may be left out); `cross@play+5s` 5 s after the game is in play. "+Ns" (with an 's') is
  the offset; a plain "+N" stays the repeat, ":H" the hold: `start@flip:100+2s+10:0.5`. The old seconds keep working
  unchanged (the tests of D-069 pass as they were).
- **wait: steps** in a press file: `wait:play`, `wait:flip:N`, `wait:call:NAME+2s` make the presses after it that give
  plain seconds count from that anchor; `wait:boot` goes back to the boot.
- **Play** (hle::PlayDetector): for 3 s, frames at 20 fps or more while the game reads the controller 10 times a second
  or more (cellPadGetData's calls). A loading screen that does both counts too (GTA V's: "in play" at 3 s, frame 86);
  scripts that need a precise point use a flip or call anchor.
- pspocket-boot resolves the anchors every 20 ms while presses are scheduled (250 ms otherwise, for the milestones) and
  logs each ("milestone at 0.39 s, frame 7: presses from call:cellSaveDataAutoLoad2"); the milestones go into the
  summary (D-1043).
- Tests: tests/hle/test_pad_script.cpp (the forms, bad texts, resolution as the anchors happen, wait steps, the play
  detector over a loading screen and then play).

## D-1043 · 2026-10-16 · The run watchdog on the Mac too (freeze, deadlock, livelock), a summary on every exit, triage.py

A run on the Mac that stopped making progress ran on to its timeout (128 s, 330 s) and said what the threads waited on
only then; a fault or a fatal error left no summary (gate.sh: "no summary: the run died"); the phone's freeze watcher
(D-135) was the app's own.

- **runtime/loader watchdog** (pspocket/loader/watchdog.hpp), shared by pspocket-boot and the app (game.mm's watcher
  now is it, with its minute's PPU landings save on the watchdog's poll): every half second a sample (the flips, every
  PPU thread's state from the thread report's snapshot, the SPU threads' and the RSX thread's CPU time from the host,
  the frames' hashes) and three checks (StallJudge): a **freeze**, frames then none for 10 s (--freeze S); a
  **deadlock**, every PPU thread that counts (started, not exited, not an interrupt thread or an attached host thread)
  blocked without a timeout on the same wait for 5 s (--deadlock S) while the SPU threads together and the RSX each
  used under 5% of a core: it needs no frame and no 10 s; a **livelock** (--livelock S, off by default), frames that
  keep flipping with the same picture (a 16x9 thumbnail's hash, top 4 bits a channel, of the Metal captures: a frame a
  second when nothing else captures), with how often the controller changed meanwhile. Each stall once (again after
  progress), with the thread report, logged and kept; --stop-on-stall ends the run there (its exit names the stall).
- **The summary on every exit path**: pspocket-boot writes --summary at its timeout, the game's exit, a guest or host
  fault (from the fault handler, after the thread report, under its 5 s alarm), a fatal error (the log sink, before
  the abort) and a stall stop. New fields: exit_detail (the fault's line, the fatal message, the stall), the
  unimplemented functions and the stubs called (name, NID, calls), the PPU interpreter's instructions by owner, the SPU
  interpreter's, the waker-first waits (D-1041), the milestones (the first frame, play, each press anchor, each stall)
  and the stalls with their reports; shake mode's points and hits (D-1045).
- **scripts/triage.py** [--summary FILE] [LOG...] [--json]: a summary and logs (pspocket-boot's run.log, the phone's
  game-*.log) sorted into buckets, the most serious first, each with its evidence and next action: fault, fatal,
  deadlock, freeze, livelock, unimplemented, RSX failures, SPU or PPU code interpreted, stubs, slow, no summary, clean.
  The phone's GTA IV log (game-153115.log): "fault: SIGBUS: guest access to 0x00000400 ..." and "unimplemented:
  cellGcmSys::? (0xb70b4ad3)" (D-1040). scripts/phone_session.py also counts the deadlock and livelock lines.
- lv2's thread snapshot says which threads are interrupt threads; core's thread_cpu_times() gives every host
  thread's CPU time without the status line's state.
- Tests: tests/hle/test_watchdog.cpp (the freeze once per freeze and none before the first frame; the deadlock only
  with every thread blocked for good and the SPUs idle; the livelock and its presses; the thumbnail hash; two lv2

## D-1045 · 2026-10-16 · Shake mode: seeded perturbations where the threads meet, two families, shake.sh

The races of D-999 showed in 2 of 36 runs side by side, and only under a 2 ms sleep after each send in most; the
phone found them first. Shake mode makes such races show in a few runs on the Mac (the plan's P1a).

- **runtime/core chaos** (pspocket/core/chaos.hpp): a mask of enabled points, one relaxed load at each point when off
  (chaos::on); PSPOCKET_SHAKE="seed=N;legal|all|adversarial;S3=PPM:MAXUS;-S15" sets it at the kernel's creation.
  Every decision comes from the calling thread's own stream (xorshift128+ seeded from the seed and the thread's name:
  "PPU 0x1000003 worker" draws the same in every run of a seed); every injection is counted by point and logged (the
  first 65,536: microseconds, the thread's stream, the point, a detail), PSPOCKET_SHAKE_LOG=FILE at exit.
- **The points** (rate per million and largest delay by default):
  S1 syscall entry (2%, 200 us), S2 library function entry (2%, 200 us), S3 the waker after its call (10%, 500 us),
  S4 the woken thread before it goes back (10%, 500 us), S5 a new thread before its first instruction (50%, 2 ms),
  S6 a usleep's end and the lv2 timer thread late (10%, 1 ms), S8 a conditional store (stwcx., stdcx., PUTLLC) that
  fails for no reason (1%), S9 an SPU's channel read that would wait, delayed first (2%, 100 us), S10 SPURS's choice
  among workloads of one priority shuffled (5% of the selections), S11 the RSX thread between batches (2%, 1 ms),
  S12 a file read (20%, 5 ms), S13 a message dialog's answer and each save data callback later (always, 200 ms),
  S14 cellAudio's period late (2%, 2 ms) — the **PS3-legal** family: a PS3 does these too (an interrupt or a more
  urgent thread, the architecture's spurious reservation loss, a slow disc), so a game must survive them;
  S7 the timebase 0.99 to 1.01 of its rate, chosen anew every quarter second (continuous, monotonic), S15 busy host
  threads (half the cores, bursts up to 20 ms), S16 the woken thread overtaking its waker (20%: D-999 and D-1041
  skipped) — the **host-adversarial** family: what the PS3 never does; a failure there only is pspocket's robustness
  gap, not necessarily the game's.
- The guest's random numbers (sys_get_random_number, sys_ss_random_number_generator, the crypto engine's, cellRudp's
  generator) come from the shake stream while shaking (chaos::random32), so a seed repeats them.
- **scripts/shake.sh gta5|ac**: the gate's prologue walk or Assassin's Creed's install and garden (a fresh hdd0 copy a
  run, removed after), N seeds (--seeds, --from, --seed), --spec, each run with --stop-on-stall --livelock 60 and
  triaged (D-1043): a table of seed, ending, median fps, buckets, ok/FAIL. --rerun S --times K says how often a seed
  fails; --ddmin S delta-debugs the points (halves that still fail, then complements, each test up to K runs).
  pspocket-boot prints the points' injections at the end and the summary has them (shake).
- Tests: tests/core/test_chaos.cpp (off by the mask, the configuration's forms and refusals, a rate, the same stream
  for a seed and a thread name, another for another seed, S8's failures counted and logged and none once off, S7's
  timebase monotonic over four threads and within 3% of the true rate).
- **First runs** (GTA V's gate walk, 128 s, scripts/shake.sh gta5): seeds 1 to 3 "legal", all to their timeout,
  triaged clean, median 29.6, 29.4 and 29.8 fps; seed 1's injections: S1 21,101 (2.1 s of delays), S2 205,326
  (20.5 s), S3 4,121, S4 28,038 (7.0 s), S5 12, S6 2,676, S8 165,601 conditional stores failed, S10 707,852
  selections shuffled, S11 2,215, S12 2,015 reads (5.1 s), S13 7 save data callbacks (0.9 s), S14 490; S9 none (GTA V's
  SPU programs never wait on a channel the host has to fill: its SPURS workers poll). Seeds 11 and 12 "adversarial"
  (S7, S15, S16: 510 rate changes, about 10,000 woken threads overtaking their wakers a run): clean, 29.8 and 28.4 fps.
  Nothing found in GTA V's prologue yet. Assassin's Creed's install path under shake mode (the run that found D-999's
  races) is the next to run: not run here, the disk under 10 GB free (each run copies hdd0 and installs 1.3 GB).
- The frame trace also names conditional-rendering skips (`Backend::draw_skipped`), the RSX's NV0039 and NV3089 copies,
  FIFO jumps, calls and returns, ZPASS enables, clears and each GET_REPORT with its count (waited for, in the traced
  frame only) (`Backend::trace_note`), and each draw's fragment program hash, depth test and write, stencil state,
  polygon offset, cull face and whether it is counted by an occlusion query.
- The trace also names every SET_BEGIN_END, a draw the front end leaves out (no vertices), SET_RENDER_ENABLE, and the
  probe a depth buffer's stencil. `PSPOCKET_RSX_ZPASS_AT_LEAST=N`: every occlusion count at least N (all visible).
- `PSPOCKET_SKIP_VTF_FP_AT=EA`: draws with the fragment program at EA that sample a vertex texture are skipped;
  `PSPOCKET_RSX_TRACE_ZALWAYS_FP=HASH`: in a traced frame, draws with that fragment program pass the depth test and
  write their depth, so the probe shows where and how deep they land.

## D-1029 · 2026-10-16 · The exact mode, a reference on the Mac (PSPOCKET_RSX_EXACT=1)

- **What it is**: the RSX's ordering kept where the fast backend trades it for speed, so a glitch that goes away in the
  exact mode is the fast paths' and one that stays is the translation's (shaders, formats, the game's own logic).
- **Labels, semaphores, the reference, reports and notifies land after the GPU's work before them**, and the targets
  that work drew go into guest memory **on the GPU** with it: at each such write the backend lays every target drawn
  since it was last written back over guest memory with D-137's overlay kernels, straight into no-copy buffers over
  RSX local memory (16 MB windows, or a target's own pages), commits the command buffer and queues the write behind it
  (a D-107 Deferred): nothing waits, and a CPU that sees a label sees what the RSX drew before it. (A first version
  waited for the GPU at every label, `sync_on_label`, and wrote targets back in `sync()`: 1.5 fps on the skyfall route,
  too slow to reach the sea.)
- **A new target starts with what memory holds** when nothing GPU-newer is under it (`upload_surface_from_guest`;
  carried as D-1025 otherwise).
- **The A/B**: `--summary` has the run's draw signature (`MetalBackend::draw_signature`: draws by fragment program hash
  at the last 300-frame report); `scripts/rsx_ab.py FAST.json EXACT.json` compares the per-frame rates of two runs
  of a route and lists the programs one draws and the other does not.
- Test: metal e2e "the exact mode has what the GPU drew in guest memory when a label lands" (a triangle in memory with
  no flush and no readback; a depth buffer made over the target starts with its bytes).
- First A/B (the gate's prologue walk on the flip clock, fast 140 s against exact 1,200 s): the exact run reached
  8,700 flips to the fast run's 3,900 (the prologue runs at 8 to 30 fps there), so the two covered different scenes and
  25 of 125 programs differ by more than half (636 against 565 draws a frame); the exact run's alarms: conditional
  draws decided while pending 0 (fast: 2,732). A per-window signature over the same flips is what a real comparison
  needs (left to the capture and replay tool, E3/E4).

## D-1071 · 2026-10-16 · Signed blending also waits while the pipeline compiles

D-1026 made a draw with a signed blend equation wait for its programs instead of the shader interpreter drawing it as
add. The gate still failed its test ("blend equation 0xf006/0xf006 (signed) drawn as add (the shader
interpreter's draw)"): with the programs compiled and the pipeline state still compiling, the draw went to the
interpreter through the pipeline's own fallback, which D-1026 did not cover, and it counted as a shader-blended draw.
That path now waits too (skip reason "signed blending waits for the pipeline"), the interpreter's draws never count
as shader-blended, and shader_blend_draws counts only draws made (found reading the code; the phone, compiling slowly
all the time, takes this path more often than the Mac).
- The gate's failures themselves were not load: ctest runs every "metal e2e" case a second time with the interpreter
  forced (test_rsx_metal_interpreted, PSPOCKET_RSX_INTERPRETER=1), where a draw that must not use the interpreter
  cannot pass. D-1026's case is left out of that run, as D-948's signed blending is.

## D-1031 · 2026-10-16 · GTA V's black block over the near sea: what it is, what it is not (open)

- **What it is** (trace-on-black runs tob1-tob17, zal1-2, zq1, tobq1, D-1028's tools): just before the skydiver
  reaches the sea, a square region of the near water (the extent of the 128x128 VTF height field around the camera)
  is black (grey in some frames). In that region the G-buffer pass's water depth pre-pass (fragment program
  e46f5d4e84de56cf, colour mask 0, LESS with depth write, vertex texture X32_FLOAT heights at 0xc27a/bf700 from guest
  memory) writes depth, and **no draw writes colour**: the water surface strips (1fe44ba35deefc05, 17 to 28 draws in
  block 0's query) and the near quads (da1f859167474ef4) do not cover it even with the depth and stencil tests forced
  to pass (PSPOCKET_RSX_TRACE_ZALWAYS_FP), and the game's FIFO has no draw between the begin and end of the water
  queries of blocks 1 to 3 (2 KB of state each, no BEGIN_END): the game itself leaves the near patch undrawn.
- **What it is not**: the early "ready" reports (D-1021 removes them; the block stays), the occlusion counts (every
  count forced to at least 100,000: stays, runs vis1-2), the CPU reading GPU-drawn targets late (every target up to
  4 MB mirrored into memory each flip, D-1030: stays), the positions' invariance between programs (positions
  `[[invariant]]` with preserveInvariance, translation 10: stays; reverted, it recompiles every shader), the stencil
  (07 there, the surface's test passes).
- **Resolved by D-1034** (2026-10-17): not the game's decision but render to vertex buffer; the near patch's draws read
  their attributes from targets the GPU had drawn, through stale guest memory. What follows was the plan before that.
- **Next**: the decision is the game's PPU (its water renderer choosing which patches to draw, from the camera, the
  water heights the SPU or the GPU computes, or the game's GPU timer that D-1021 now feeds with completion times). The
  exact mode (D-1029) would tell whether any RSX ordering feeds it, but on the flip clock its 2 to 8 fps took the route
  elsewhere: it needs presses anchored on game events (D-1042's steps).

## D-1046 · 2026-10-16 · cellGcmSetPrepareFlip as libgcm_sys: a full flip ring refused, the slot answered

D-1044 left the full flip ring: pspocket wrote the flip and dropped the oldest queued slot, where the brief said
libgcm_sys returns an error. Read in Sony's libgcm_sys (cellGcmSetPrepareFlip's entry at 0x2514; cellGcmSetFlip at
0x23b4 wraps it): an id over 7 is CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE; then the next slot is (write + 1) % 8 (0x10b0); when that
is the oldest slot not yet flipped (the read index) the answer is CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE with nothing written and the
ring as it was (0x2594); otherwise the slot takes the id (0x25b4, 0x25b8) before the command is written (0x18bc), and
the answer is the slot (r31), not the id as RPCS3's gcmSetPrepareFlip has it. Comparing it on a context the RSX never
runs crashed in Sony's flush of that context (its callback 0), so the full ring is taken from the code; the answer on
the default context is compared.

- runtime/hle/src/cellGcmSys.cpp set_prepare_flip: the slot reserved first (a full ring: CELL_GCM_ERROR_FAILURE, a
  warning, nothing written), then room, the command and put as before; cellGcmSetPrepareFlip answers the slot,
  cellGcmSetFlip CELL_OK or the failure. A callback that fails still answers its own result (RPCS3's; Sony's 0x18bc
  not read further).
- Tests: tests/hle/test_gcm_sys.cpp (the slots; on a game's own context seven flips queue, the eighth and a
  cellGcmSetFlip are refused with the context unchanged, the ring's buffers by index); tests/hle/test_gcm_compare.cpp
  "flips: cellGcmSetPrepareFlip's answer" (three flips, an id of 8 and a cellGcmSetFlip on the default context, the
  answers as Sony's; not the driver information there: pspocket's RSX runs its own GCM_FLIP_COMMAND, which queues the
  buffer on head 1 first, RPCS3's way, flip flags 0xc0000001, where Sony's words leave 0x80000000). An argument value
  kCtxArg in a compare step is the default context's address.
