## D-1047 · 2026-10-17 · The transient allocator kept a large upload's own buffer of a chunk's length as a chunk (Assassin's Creed's garden leak); --max-footprint

Assassin's Creed's first install into the garden (games/ac1/bench install-garden) died on main at a 56 GB footprint:
from the garden's first seconds (about 105 s in) it grew about 1 GB a second, together with D-1025's alarm line ("7.00
targets a frame started with the bytes of those under them"). A/B with the run stopped at a 6 GB footprint:
PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_CARRY=1 stayed at 0.45 to 1.10 GB to its 300 s; with the carry, 0.99 GB then 4.27 GB and stopped at 6 GB
at 108 s. vmmap at the burst: the IOAccelerator (graphics) regions 198, 582, 849, 1,331 in four seconds (about 3.5 MB
each). PSPOCKET_RSX_MEMTRACE=1 (new: a line a flip with the GPU's allocated memory, surfaces, pools, textures, deferred
actions and the transient allocator's chunks) found it: the free list of transient chunks grew by four a flip (151, 331,
571, 811 free) while the frame used 13.

- **The cause** (runtime/rsx/metal/src/metal_backend.mm, TransientAllocator): an allocation over half a chunk (2 MB) gets
  a buffer of its own, kept with the chunks of the command buffer until it completes; there every buffer whose length
  was a chunk's (4 MB) went back to the free list for reuse. A large upload of exactly 4 MB (a 1024x1024 or 1280x819
  A8R8G8B8 target's staging copy or texels, a carry's) is one: it was kept as a chunk, never used again (large uploads
  take buffers of their own), and the next frame's carries made new ones. Four 4 MB carries a frame at 60 fps: the 1 GB
  a second.
- **The fix**: the large uploads' own buffers are kept apart from the chunks and released when their command buffer
  completes, whatever their length; the free list keeps 128 chunks (512 MB) at most and gives a larger peak back.
  Assassin's Creed's run again (carry on, 330 s): to its timeout, footprint 0.45 to 1.30 GB, the GPU's memory 411 to 465
  MB, the garden at 56 to 60 fps.
- **--max-footprint GB** (pspocket-boot): the run stops once the process's footprint passes it, checked four times a
  second; its summary's exit is "footprint" (scripts/triage.py's bucket of that name). A leak no longer fills the swap
  and the disk (the Mac was at 6.7 GB free with 43 GB of swap).
- Tests: tests/rsx/test_transient.mm (frames of four large uploads of exactly 4 MB, of 4 MB less a page, of 6 MB and
  six small ones: the free list and the GPU's memory stay where they were after 200 frames; a command buffer of 150
  chunks gives back all but 128). With the old allocator the free list reached 841 chunks and the test fails.
- Found on the way: the test thread needs an autorelease pool for Metal's own objects to go (as the backend's draw,
  clear and flip have); and Assassin's Creed's two 5 s windows at 2.2 and 0.8 fps of 2026-10-16 (D-1041) are not this
  leak (the footprint was 0.5 GB then); one window at 5.8 fps showed in this run at about 200 s, still to look at.

## D-1051 · 2026-10-17 · The waker rule's guard: Assassin's Creed's boot under D-999's race recipe, every night

D-1050 found D-999's registry race again with shake mode when the woken thread overtakes its waker (S16). A guard
that keeps the rule from regressing unseen: `scripts/shake.sh ac --guard [--times K]` boots Assassin's Creed (a fresh
install, as D-1050's runs) K times (8) for 8 s, each boot with its own seed and "S3=500000:2000": the waker held up to
2 ms after half its wakes, D-999's PSPOCKET_LV2_SEND_DELAY_US=2000 for every kind of wake. It passes when no boot
fails (fault, fatal, stall, footprint). Not S16 itself: S16 is the rule switched off (the woken thread going first at
once), so with it a boot crashes whatever lv2 does; the guard keeps the race's timing and leaves the rule to hold it.
`--guard-control` runs the same with the rule off (PSPOCKET_LV2_SENDER_FIRST=0) and passes when a boot crashes: that
the guard still reaches the race on this build and data.

- Measured: the guard, 8 boots then 16, none failed (75 s for eight); the control, 8 boots, 4 crashed twice over
  (SIGBUS reading 0x0b0000f8 in the registry's sys_lwmutex_trylock, 0.8 s in), so eight boots miss a broken rule about
  one time in 200.
- scripts/nightly-bench.sh runs the guard after the bench (when inventory/BLES00158 has the disc and the bench made its
  library; not on a night the bench skipped), its line in the night's waker-guard.txt; a failure fails the night.
- Found by the control: two threads faulted at once (the registry race faults the saver and the main thread) and the
  run ended with no summary, both fault handlers writing their reports. pspocket-boot's fault handler now writes the
  summary first, right after the fault's line and call site (the memory dump and the thread report take locks and can
  hang), and a second faulting thread writes its line and waits for the first to end the process; the control's
  crashes now have summaries (exit "fault", the first fault's line).

## D-1053 · 2026-10-17 · RSX capture and replay; scripts/rsx_bisect.py

The plan's net 2 (E3, E4): a frame that shows wrong becomes a folder the RSX and its backend can run alone, again and
again, with the fast paths switched off one by one.

- **Capture** (pspocket/rsx/capture.hpp, runtime/rsx/src/capture.cpp; `pspocket-boot --rsx-capture DIR
  --rsx-capture-from FLIP --rsx-capture-frames N --rsx-capture-max-mb MB`, Metal): at the first step boundary of the
  RSX thread after flip FLIP with no packet, call or wait open, the backend writes back what only the GPU holds
  (Backend::flush_memory over every region), then every non-zero page of local memory, the RSX's context memory and
  the IO-mapped main memory goes into the image (each content once, content-addressed, in blobs.bin), the register file
  and vertex program state into state.bin, the layout, IO map, display buffers, FIFO location, get and put into
  manifest.txt; the pages are watched through the write tracker (blocks of four pages). Then before each step of the
  RSX thread a record: the words processed, put, every watched page a store reached and whose bytes changed, and the
  flips asked for outside the FIFO and the FIFO resets the step takes; the FIFO's words are memory, so jumps, calls and
  returns replay as they ran. It ends at the step after its N-th flip, or at the size cap (manifest "incomplete"; the
  IO map changing ends it too); the size is logged.
- **Replay** (replay_capture; the tool `rsx-replay DIR [--frames DIR] [--draws FILE] [--describe N]`): the regions
  committed, the image and state restored, then per record its pages, put, flip requests and resets, and the RSX run
  for as many words as the capture's (Rsx::run_until_idle); a record that ends at other words is a deviation. The RSX's
  own outputs (notifies and reports) are not overwritten by the records after the image: the replay's GPU writes
  them. It prints a hash of each presented frame, the RSX alarms and the deviations; --frames saves PNGs, --draws a
  hash of each colour target after each draw and clear (written back: slow), --describe what a draw had bound.
- **scripts/rsx_bisect.py CAPTURE**: mode A (as the environment is) against B (PSPOCKET_RSX_EXACT=1), with --draws:
  the frames, A's own determinism over two runs, the first draw whose targets differ (described), and each of the
  backend's switches added to A (NO_CARRY, NO_SURFACE_POOL, NO_PASS_MERGING, WRITE_BACK_TARGETS, STRICT_FEEDBACK,
  INTERPRETER, NO_DEPTH_CLAMP, EARLY_REPORTS, UNINIT_TARGETS) and whether it makes A match B from there.
- **GTA V's gate walk, flips 2400 and 2401**: 4 regions, 16,610 pages in the image (255 MB), 139 records, 2,757 pages
  written, 298 MB in all, the run's CPU unchanged otherwise. Replays: 0 deviations, 565,248 words, 12 s; the frames
  as the game's (the bank's lobby). Exact mode: the same two frames every run; the interpreter's: the same every run;
  the fast mode: frame 2 the same every run, frame 1 one of a few (26 pixels, at most 7 levels apart), with the
  replay's alarm conditional_pending 2: two conditional draws decided while their reports were in flight, a race the
  fast path has in the game too (the exact mode waits for them). No switch removes it (rsx_bisect's runs).
  rsx_bisect there: A and B present the same frames with --draws (its write-backs after each draw settle the GPU), the
  first target hash that differs is draw 2's (a 2x multisampled 128x128 depth pre-pass, colour mask 0: the target's
  write-back, not its pixels); no switch changes it.
- Tests: tests/rsx/test_metal.mm (two frames captured after a first one, the CPU changing the triangle's colours
  between frames: two replays present the same pixels as the capture's frames, no deviation; a capture past its cap:
  incomplete, its manifest says so).
- Not in a capture: EDGE's GPU work items (they come from SPU jobs, not RSX memory): capture with PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=0.

## D-1054 · 2026-10-17 · RSX captures that replay GTA V's skyfall: put before pages, the replay's own writes first, a glitch trigger

What the first skyfall captures showed (D-1053's capture, GTA V's skyfall-sea route, `PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=0`): the
replays stalled. One parked on a jump to itself after 163 of 363 records and presented 7 of 15 frames; another blocked
on a semaphore acquire after 611 of 999. The causes and the changes:

- **Put is read before the pages.** The record took the pages written since the last step boundary, then read put.
  The CPU writes commands and then moves put, so a put it moved between the two named commands whose words reached
  the replay a record late (a record whose step ran 1679 words of stale commands, then the replay went elsewhere). Put
  is now read first: every command before it is in the pages harvested after it.
- **Pages are watched again before they are read.** A page made writable by its first fault takes later stores
  without a fault, so a store between the read and the new watch would never have been recorded. The block is now
  watched again first and read after it.
- **The replay's own deferred writes land before each record's pages** (`run_deferred(true)`). Labels and semaphores
  released behind the GPU (D-1029) were in the capture's memory before the CPU wrote what the record holds. In the
  replay, the RSX's release of 0 at semaphore 0x40300470 landed over the CPU's 1, and the acquire after it never passed.
- **The next record's pages come early.** A step the capture's RSX ran on through something it saw during the step
  (an SPU job's PUT over the jump-to-self it was coming to, commands put moved past) has those stores only in the next
  record. When the replay blocks or idles short of the capture's words, it lets its deferred writes land and runs on.
  If it is still short, it writes the next record's pages and put and runs to the words the capture processed.
- **Stores with no fault.** `PSPOCKET_RSX_CAPTURE_CHECK=1` hashes the pages around the FIFO's get at every step
  boundary and records (and logs) any that changed with no store seen: 1 to 9 a capture on the skyfall. The GPU's
  target overlays (D-1027) write guest memory after their `notify_write`, so a page read between the two is stale until
  the next store. Such a page is the replay's own GPU output, except where the FIFO reads it.
- `rsx-replay` reports the early records, says where the RSX stopped at the first deviation (get, put, the capture's
  next get, the semaphore or jump it is blocked on), counts records that end at another FIFO position with the same
  words ("path deviations"), and takes `--verbose` (each early try).
- Result: the 40-frame capture from flip 5410 (996 records, 1.16 GB) replays all 40 flips with 0 deviations and 1 early
  record. 47 records end a word or two off the capture's get, all after early pages. Two fragment programs the live run
  never decoded are reported, from those early pages.
- `pspocket-boot --rsx-capture DIR --rsx-capture-on KIND` (with `--summary`; KIND is a frame detector's kind, D-1064:
  partly-black, flicker, hitch, frozen, flagged). The capture waits for the first such event at or after
  `--rsx-capture-from`, then starts at the next step boundary (`CaptureOptions::armed = false`,
  `CaptureWriter::arm(flip)`, once only). The manifest's `from_flip` and the summary give the flip it started after.
- Route runs for a capture use `PSPOCKET_PRESS_CLOCK=flips` (D-1028). A capture slows the game, and on the wall clock the
  route then presses elsewhere: the morning's skyfall cheat at 125 s fell in shader-compile windows of 10-15 fps and
  never took. On flips the skyfall starts at flip 3960, the near sea's black block comes at 5430-5446 (5 %, then 14 %,
  of the frame), and the player drowns from 6200.
- **The block and the capture.** Without a capture (a control on the flips clock, frames every 2), the block starts at
  flip 5428 (4 % of the frame), grows to 62 % by 5472 and is gone by 5500. The bench's r6 (5160) and fix3 (5430/5460)
  saw it too. It showed in none of three runs whose capture started at 5410 or 5426. In the triggered run the capture
  started at 5447, inside the block, and the block was gone by 5450. A capture's start writes back every target the
  GPU holds (7665 readbacks, a 0.5 s hitch), and that takes the block away. So the block's bytes come from somewhere
  that reads memory where a GPU-held target was never written back, or from the timing the hitch changes; the
  write-back is the likelier of the two. A capture as it stands cannot hold the block: its start removes it.
- The Metal e2e fixture's present hook read each frame back in a completion handler. That handler indexed
  `present_pixels` while a later frame's `emplace_back` could move it, and it ran after the fixture was gone when a
  test did not sync: a finished test's pixels were written into freed heap and crashed the next test's
  `MetalBackend::init` inside the driver's pipeline compile (4 runs in 30, in one random order). The handlers now fill
  their place under a mutex, and `~E2E` waits for any still pending: 0 crashes in 30.
- Test: "rsx capture: an unarmed capture waits for its trigger, then records the frames after it". Two frames pass
  unrecorded, then arm(0); the next frame is captured from flip 2 and replays to its pixels, and a second arm is
  refused. The capture's races are between the CPU, the SPUs and the RSX thread: no synthetic test reproduces them.

## D-1055 · 2026-10-17 · Which target's write-back removes the skyfall's black block: 0xc2820000, read as vertices

- `PSPOCKET_RSX_WRITEBACK_AT=FLIP[:EA-EA,...]` (debugging): after flip FLIP, at the first step boundary with no packet
  or call open, the backend writes back what only the GPU holds over the ranges given. Each range writes back every
  target overlapping it, so `A-A+1` selects the target at A. With no ranges it writes back everything a capture's
  start does (local memory, the context memory, the IO-mapped main memory). No capture is made.
- The readback log line now gives the target's format, pitch, bytes and the flip it was last drawn or sampled at.
- `PSPOCKET_SPU_WATCH=LO-HI:get` logs SPU reads from the range as well as writes, with the SPU program's name.
- Bisection on GTA V's skyfall-sea route (`PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=0`, `PSPOCKET_PRESS_CLOCK=flips`, write-back at flip
  5436, the block counted in frames 5440-5484 at 10 % dark or more; inventory/work/wb_try.sh, wb_bisect.sh):
  - no write-back: the block grows from 4 % at 5428 to 62 % at 5472;
  - all 59 targets: gone from 5440;
  - targets 0-29 by address: gone. Targets 30-58: block as without. 15-22: gone. 15-18: gone. 15-16: block. 17
    alone: gone.
  - The target: **0xc2820000, 128x128, surface format 0x10, pitch 0x200, 64 KB**, drawn every frame.
  - The block can come back around flip 5488 in any run, the full write-back's too: the target is drawn again and
    read the same way.
- The reader (h1's trace): the RSX's own vertex fetch. GTA V draws the water's near patch with attribute 10 from local
  0x2820000 (X32 float, stride 4) and attribute 9 from 0x2830000: render to vertex buffer. The Metal backend copied a
  draw's vertex arrays from guest memory with no check for GPU-newer targets over them. Textures have had the overlay
  since D-137; vertex arrays had nothing, so the patch's heights were last frame's memory, or zero. h1 fixes the
  vertex path (D-1034).
- Test: "PSPOCKET_RSX_WRITEBACK_AT writes back the targets over its ranges after its flip, and no others". A range over
  the target puts its first frame in memory after flip 1; a range elsewhere leaves memory as it was.
## D-1034 · 2026-10-17 · Render to vertex buffer: targets the GPU drew are laid over a draw's vertex arrays (GTA V's near-sea black block)

- **The cause of D-1031's block**: GTA V's water simulation draws into 128x128 targets in local memory (surface format
  F_X32, pitch 0x200, at 0x2810000, 0x2820000 and 0x2830000, drawn every frame), and the near water patch reads two of them
  as vertex attributes: attribute 9 (X32 float, stride 4) from 0x2830000 and attribute 10 (stride 4) from 0x2820000
  (trace: indexed draws of 576 vertices, fragment program b54d5f7b9b5313f4, after VERTEX_DATA_ARRAY_OFFSET[9] = 0x2830000).
  The Metal backend copied vertex arrays from guest memory with no look at targets (textures have had D-137's overlay
  since early on, vertex arrays never had one). Guest memory held whatever the CPU last saw there, never what the GPU
  drew, so the patch's vertices were wrong and it drew off the screen; the G-buffer kept the depth pre-pass's depth and
  no colour, which looked black. Which target matters was found by h2's write-back bisection (D-1055: writing back
  0x2820000 alone at flip 5436 removes the block) and by the trace (reader: the RSX's vertex fetch, not the PPU or an
  SPU). It is not EDGE (run edgel1, EDGE lifted: block stays), the occlusion counts, the exact mode's ordering, or
  depth clamping (D-1031, D-1033).
- **The fix**: before a draw's vertex spans are copied, the targets the GPU holds newer that overlap them are found
  (MetalBackend::Impl::vertex_targets). After the copy, each one is laid over the spans it covers with the overlay
  kernels, oldest first, on the render buffer before the draw's pass (overlay_vertex_targets, encode_overlay), as
  store_readback would have written it. With overlay_targets off (PSPOCKET_RSX_WRITE_BACK_TARGETS), such a target is
  written back before the copy's allocation, because a submit can reuse an allocation made before it. The
  BackendStats::vertex_overlays counter counts these overlays; they also count in the frame report's "targets laid
  over memory".
- **Runs** (skyfall-sea route, PSPOCKET_EDGE_GPU=0, flip clock, frames every 6 flips, share of black pixels):
  - Control (vctl1, the D-1033 build): 1% at 5424, rising to 63% at 5472-5478, gone by 5484 (as h2's sky7).
  - Fix (vfix2): 0% in every frame from 5394 to 5556, with the same scene (the parachute over the sea).
- **Cost** (same runs, 300-frame windows):
  - Laying the targets ends a pass about 8 to 10 more times a frame where the water is drawn: in the city, 107 to 109
    passes against 97 to 99, and 24 against 16 passes ended by target overlays.
  - GPU time per frame moved within the runs' noise: city 10.0 to 10.8 ms against 11.1 to 11.4; over the sea 8.3 to
    9.0 against 7.4 to 9.1.
  - A later saving: one overlay per target generation, shared by every draw that reads it (several draws a pass read
    the same two targets).
- Test: tests/rsx/test_metal.mm "vertex arrays over a target read what the GPU drew there". A target is cleared on the
  GPU while its memory holds stale colours, and a triangle takes its vertex colours from that memory. It is checked
  with the overlay and with the write-back.

## D-1056 · 2026-10-17 · Every read of guest memory a GPU-held target may be newer over: audited; the stale_gpu_reads alarm

After the skyfall's vertex-fetch miss (D-1055, fixed in D-1034), every path where the Metal backend or the RSX front
end reads guest memory was checked for what it does about a target the GPU drew since memory last held it:

| Path | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertex arrays | copied from memory, no check | D-1034: GPU-newer targets laid over the copy (written back without overlays; one neither can write counts the alarm) |
| Index arrays | `before_access` only (queued copies) | written back first (`sync_gpu_held`): the indices are scanned on the CPU |
| Textures, linear, the same pitch | laid over (D-137, D-214) | as before |
| Textures over a target of another pitch, or swizzled; swizzled, cube or volume textures over targets not at their start; vertex textures (D-093) through the same bind | left: memory alone (D-214, after run 132) | live targets written back first; old ones left (below) |
| Compressed textures over a target | left; `dead_overlays` counts one at the start | as before: the GPU cannot draw DXT, so the memory was reused |
| Display buffer shown from memory (no target at its start) | decoded from memory alone | targets inside it written back first |
| NV0039 / NV3089 copies, NV308A writes | `flush_memory` / `flush_memory_later` / `copy_on_gpu` over source and destination (D-107, D-110) | as before |
| Reports and zcull (conditional rendering, GET_REPORT) | the backend writes them whole at completion; `report_pending` (D-1021) | as before |
| Inline arrays, immediate data, transform constants and program | in the FIFO, not memory | n/a |
| Fragment program bytes and constants | read from memory each draw | n/a: no game draws into its shaders |
| A target reloaded from memory the CPU wrote (`cpu_newer`) over other targets | carry (D-1025), `targets_lost` | as before (who wrote last is not known there) |
| EDGE inputs | read by the SPU job (its DMA), not the backend | out of the backend: a CPU or SPU read of a GPU-held target is plan F5 (the mirror, D-1030) |

- `Impl::sync_gpu_held(addr, size, why, handled)`: the surfaces' byte ranges, sorted with a running end (rebuilt when
  surfaces are made or removed), give the targets over a read in a binary search. A target counts when it is
  GPU-newer, not CPU-newer (`check_cpu_writes`), not in `handled` (what the path laid over), and has pixel bytes in
  the range, not only the gaps of a wider pitch. A live one (drawn or sampled in the last two flips: the GPU wrote
  that memory last, as the RSX's writes reach memory) is written back. An older one is left and counted in
  `stale_left`: its memory is taken as reused, the run-132 case. The D-214 test now has both: the live target is
  written back, the old one is left.
- **Alarm `stale_gpu_reads`**: a read under a live GPU-held target that was not brought over (a format the write-back
  does not support, or `PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_STALE_SYNC=1`, the A/B switch that only counts). games/gta5/gate.json limits it
  to 0. Stats: `stale_synced` and `stale_left`. Each write-back is in the readback log, "for an index array", "for a
  texture" or "for a display buffer shown from memory".
- Tests (Metal e2e, each with the sync and with `PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_STALE_SYNC=1`, where the alarm counts):
  - an index array in a target's memory is written back before its indices are read;
  - a display buffer shown from memory gets a target drawn over its lower half;
  - a linear texture of half the pitch inside a target is written back when the target is live, left when it is old
    (D-214's test).
- Not measured on a game yet (no game runs until h1's D-1034 is gated). The cost is one binary search per index
  array, texture bind and memory flip, and a write-back only where a live target lies under the read. The gate's
  readback limits will show a path that does it every frame.

## D-1035 · 2026-10-17 · The vertex arrays' targets from D-1056's range index; a read keeps a target live

- `Impl::gpu_held_over(addr, size, out)` is D-1056's lookup, moved out of `sync_gpu_held`: the GPU-newer targets with
  pixel bytes in a range, found in the sorted range index. `sync_gpu_held` and D-1034's `vertex_targets` both use it.
  `vertex_targets` no longer walks every surface on every draw.
- The vertex path takes D-1056's rule: a target neither drawn nor read in the last two flips is memory the game has
  reused (`stale_left`). A vertex read keeps its target live (`last_frame`, as a sampled target is). Without that,
  the rule broke the fix: with the rule alone, the skyfall's block came back for a frame at flip 5496 (run vfix3,
  52% black). At the water's edge the game draws the simulation's targets less often than its patch reads them.
  With the read counted, every frame from 5400 to 5560 is clean, in steps of 6 flips (vfix4) and of 2 flips (vfix5,
  81 frames).
- Test: "vertex arrays over a target read what the GPU drew there" also reads the target over five flips with no new
  drawing into it, and still gets the GPU's bytes. Without the read counted, the reads after the second flip get the
  stale memory.

## D-1058 · 2026-10-17 · Conditional rendering decided on the GPU (plan F6); a capture's replay loads its new targets

- **The race.** NV4097_SET_RENDER_ENABLE mode 2 decided on the CPU from the report's word when the method ran. A count
  the GPU had not delivered yet rendered the draws (D-115) and counted `conditional_pending`, once a frame or so on the
  gate walk (2,423 in its 128 s). Which way a decision went depended on the GPU's timing, so fast-mode replays of one
  capture differed (D-1053).
- **Now** the backend decides (`Backend::predicate_on_gpu(value_addr)`, `end_predicate()`), whenever it knows the
  report's counters (the last `report_zpass` at that address), whether the count has arrived or not. The decision
  then does not depend on timing. The pass open ends (Metal writes a pass's counters when it ends). A blit copies the
  report's counters together, and a kernel (`rsx_predicate`) runs before the draws. The draws under the predicate are
  indirect draws whose arguments sit in a region of the render buffer, 32 bytes apart. The kernel sets their instance
  counts to 0 when the counters sum to zero, reading at run time how many the RSX thread wrote (it writes them before
  the commit). A predicate that lasts into a new render buffer, or fills its 1,024 places, is armed again there.
  Fallbacks, each counting `conditional_pending`:
  - an EDGE draw, whose arguments come from the EDGE kernels;
  - a full region.

  The exact mode waits for the count as before (D-1029). `PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_GPU_PREDICATE=1` decides on the CPU, for A/B
  (also in scripts/rsx_bisect.py's switches). The 300-frame alarms line gives predicates and draw calls under them a
  frame.
- **Measured on the gate walk** (two runs back to back, the same build; on vs `PSPOCKET_RSX_NO_GPU_PREDICATE=1`):

  | | GPU predicates | CPU (old) |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `conditional_pending` | 0 | 2,423 |
  | fps median / slowest window | 29.8 / 29.6 | 29.8 / 29.0 |
  | render passes a frame (worst) | 83.1 | 83.1 |
  | RSX ms a frame / µs a draw (from 70 s) | 9.16 / 9.01 | 8.92 / 8.99 |
  | GPU ms a frame | 6.7-7.3 | 6.9-7.8 |

  games/gta5/gate.json now limits `conditional_pending` to 0.
- **Replays.** The skyfall capture (40 frames, D-1054) replays to the same 40 frames in each of three fast runs, with no
  `conditional_pending`; before, each fast replay counted 15 to 17. The gate walk's capture (flips 2400-2401) counts
  none now, but its first frame still comes out one of two ways (7 runs of 10 one, 3 the other). The two differ in one
  pixel by 1 level, from the G-buffer's third target at row 317. That difference is not the reports': it stays:
  - with the reports written early (`PSPOCKET_RSX_EARLY_REPORTS=1`);
  - with every fast path off (pass merging, the feedback cache, both pools, carrying, the scratch reuse);
  - with copies made in memory and synchronously;
  - with transient memory zeroed, and with new targets loaded.

  Frame traces of the two kinds of run are identical, draw by draw (the same binds and decisions). The difference goes
  away with a GPU wait (`--sync`) anywhere in the G-buffer pass up to about draw 230, and in the exact mode (which
  waits at every label). It is open (next in docs/improve.md's list): a GPU-side order between that pass and work
  queued with it, not a decision of the backend's.
- `rsx-replay` gains:
  - `--pages FILE`: hashes of local memory's pages at each flip, written back first;
  - `--sync A-B`: a GPU wait after draws A to B;
  - `--trace 1`: the backend's frame trace from the first command. `trace_frame = 1` now starts at the first
    command (no flip begins frame 1).
  - A replay's new targets start with what memory holds (`MetalBackendConfig::load_new_targets`, as in the exact mode):
    the capture wrote the targets back when it started. `PSPOCKET_REPLAY_UNDEFINED_TARGETS=1` leaves them undefined, as
    in a fast run.
- Tests (Metal e2e):
  - the D-115 test, rewritten: in fast and exact mode, with the query's draw visible or scissored away, the draw under
    the report shows exactly when its count is non-zero, against a wrong older count in memory; fast mode decides on
    the GPU (one predicate, no CPU skip, no alarm) before and after the count arrives, exact mode on the CPU;
  - the occlusion test: its conditional draws are decided on the GPU with the same pixels.
## D-1036 · 2026-10-17 · The draw log: light per-draw records for glitches that last one frame

A glitch that lasts one frame (GTA V's grey wedge across the sky) is over before a detector can start a frame trace,
and a capture's start writes every target back, which changes the scene (D-1054). The draw log records every draw
cheaply, so a bad frame found afterwards can be compared with the frames around it.
- Each draw gets a fixed-size record, filled where the frame trace formats its line and formatted only when written:
  - program: fragment program hash, vertex program start;
  - targets: colour and depth targets with format and size, colour mask;
  - state: depth, stencil, blend and cull state, whether occlusion is counted;
  - up to 20 textures, each with its address, format, size and source (memory, target, converted, laid, written
    back, corner, depth);
  - for an indexed draw, a hash of the index bytes it copied, and a hash of the vertex bytes;
  - a skipped draw, with the reason.
- `PSPOCKET_RSX_DRAWLOG=FROM-TO:FILE` keeps frames FROM to TO in memory and writes them to FILE once TO is reached
  (one pause after the window, none inside it). `PSPOCKET_RSX_DRAWLOG_RING=N` keeps the last N frames.
  `MetalBackend::dump_drawlog` writes the ring, and pspocket-boot calls it for each FrameWatch glitch into the
  summary's folder (`drawlog-<kind>-<flip>.txt`). On the rain-street route the range takes about 0.2 KB a draw and
  76 MB for 360 frames.
- Test: "the draw log's ring holds each frame's draws" (three frames, a ring of two: frames 2 and 3, each with its
  draw and its target).
- First use, GTA V's sky wedge on rain-street:
  - A one-frame flat grey polygon across the sky, in front of the sky and behind the trees. It comes at the same
    point of the route, flips 3770 to 3772 (runs dl1, dlb5, dlh2, skyd-on2), and also at 3712 and 3747. About one
    run in two has one.
  - The bad frame's draws (dlh2 3772) against 3771 and 3773: every program is there, and four occlusion probes
    (abd449a846bf6eb0) and four 128x128 shadow-map draws (64450bf999d9b9e3) are missing, which is the game's own
    choice for that frame.
  - No static draw's index or vertex bytes differ from both neighbours. The wedge's draw is not found yet; next is a
    capture from flip 3700 replayed with --draws.

  3800, with PSPOCKET_RSX_CAPTURE_CHECK=1 (cap4: the wedge at 3715 and 3758). The replay is deterministic: 0
  deviations and the wedge in replay frame 15.
  - The frame trace's pixel probe at (150,150): the sky's draws (32a1caebabc80f48, then the clouds 2eec694992dc3eed
    and 5e1988ea5b9667e3) never reach that pixel. Before them, a draw of fragment program f0de183c8cd8dbd3 (the
    far-LOD meshes, 3231 indices, stencil written 0) covers it flat grey, and the sky's stencil test (EQUAL 7) then
    leaves it.
  - The mesh is in frame 15 only (not in 14 or 16). Its vertex program divides by w itself (RCP R0.w, then o[0].w =
    1, o[0].z near the far plane), with c[8..11] as the transform. Its vertices are finite and in range, but their w
    crosses 0 (about -1137 to +2238 over the mesh). Part of the mesh is behind the camera, the division flips it, and
    it spans the sky.
  - The replay draws the same frame with every backend switch: exact mode, the shader interpreter, no carry, no
    surface pool, no pass merging, write-back targets, strict feedback, uninitialised targets. The game-run A/B agrees:
    the exact mode from flip 3600 also shows the wedge (run ex4, 3713 and 3721). So the backend draws what the game
    sends.
  - The cause is upstream, in the game's choice to draw that far LOD for one frame with the camera inside it, most
    likely while the detailed models that replace it were not ready yet (streaming timing) or because of a
    visibility decision. Open: which game system picks the LOD, and whether our file and decompression timing, or a
    lifted function, makes it fall back.
